## From the Kularnava Tantra
### (The Ocean of the Kula Tradition)

"...men deride; let the King punish; but I shall be steadfast, O Supreme Deity I shall serve and ever serve Thee. With mind, speech, body and actions I shall not leave Thy law". Such a man whose faith and devotion are unshakeable even in the midst of all adversity, is verily adored by the Gods and over there he shall become <term>Śiva: The Supreme Being or the state of pure consciousness</term>.

->O <term>Śive: The Goddess, feminine form of Śiva</term>! Though constantly afflicted by disease, poverty and misery, the man who waits yet upon you, the Divine Mother, with ardour, attains the highest State. (56)<-
<note>original: "रोगदारिद्र्यदुःखैः पीडितोऽप्यनिशं शिवे। यस्त्वामुपास्ते भक्त्या स नरः सद्गतिमाप्नुयात्।। ५६।।"</note>

->Whether one receives praise or blame, whether wealth stays with him or leaves, whether death comes today or at the end of the <term>Yuga: A vast cosmic era</term>, he should never leave the <term>Kula: The sacred lineage and its spiritual path</term>. (57)<-
<note>original: "जनाः स्तुवन्तु निन्दन्तु लक्ष्मीर्गच्छतु तिष्ठतु। मृतिरद्य युगान्ते वा कुलं नैव परित्यजेत्।। ५७।।"</note>

->One should never leave the Kula under any circumstance either due to greed, anger, enmity, maliciousness, sensuousness, or fear. (58)<-
<note>original: "नापि लोभाच्च क्रोधान्न द्वेषाच्च मत्सरात्। न कामाच्च भयाद्वापि कुलधर्मं परित्यजेत्।। ५८।।"</note>

->Taking shelter of <term>Kuladharma: The law or duty of the Kula path</term>, one who does not worship you, the Divine Mother, is tortured as soon as born by the enemies of the Self in the form of elemental beings. (59)<-
<note>original: "यो जन्तुर्नार्चयेत्त्वान्तु कुलधर्मसमाश्रितः। क्लिश्यते जातमात्रेण भूतारिणात्मशत्रुणा।। ५९।।"</note>

->Those who are averse to the <term>Kaula: A practitioner or the path itself</term> are like an empty grain among grains, a moth among <term>Jivas: Living beings</term>, or a bubble in water. (60)<-
<note>original: "पुलाका इव धान्येषु पतङ्गा इव जन्तुषु। बुद्बुदा इव तोयेषु ये कौलविमुखा हि ते।। ६०।।"</note>

->The trees live, birds and animals also live; but only he lives meaningfully whose mind is settled in the laws of Kula. (61)<-
<note>original: "तरवोऽपि हि जीवन्ति जीवन्ति मृगपक्षिणः स जीवति मनो यस्य कुलधर्मे व्यवस्थितम्।। ६१।।"</note>

->For him who is away from the Kuladharma, days come and pass; like the bellows of a blacksmith he heaves but does not truly live. (62)<-
<note>original: "कुलधर्म विहीनस्य दिनान्यायान्ति यान्ति च स लोहकारभस्त्रेव श्वसन्नपि न जीवति।। ६२।।"</note>

## Second Illumination

->Whether moving, sitting, waking, or sleeping,<-
->O <term>Kuleśvarī: The Supreme Goddess as sovereign of the Kula path</term>, the life of one who is ignorant of the Kula is like that of an animal. (63)<-
<note>original: "गच्छतस्तिष्ठतो वापि जाग्रतः स्वपतोऽपि वा। कुलेश्वरि कुलाज्ञस्य तत् पशोरिव जीवितम्।। ६३।।"</note>

->*One who is ignorant of Kula-dharma lives like an animal:*<-

O Goddess! A man who does not know the Kula, though he may be moving, sitting, waking, or sleeping, spends his life just like an animal.

->Whether he is an erudite scholar or a fool, religious or irreligious,<-
->whether he adheres to religious observances or not, if a person is averse to the <term>Kaula: The spiritual path centered on the Kula tradition</term> way, (64)<-
->they are merely born into the world as creatures. Only those who live according to<-
-><term>Kula-dharma: The sacred duties and way of life of the Kula</term>, O Goddess, are truly living; the rest are like donkeys tied at a doorway. (65)<-
<note>original: "विद्वानपि च मूर्खोऽसौ धार्मिको वाप्यधार्मिकः। व्रतस्थोऽप्यव्रतस्थो वा यः कौलविमुखो जनः।। ६४।। जातास्त एव जगति जन्तवः साधु जीविनः। कुलधर्मपरा देवि शेषाश्च द्वारगर्दभाः।। ६५।।"</note>

Whether he is a great scholar or an uneducated man, whether he follows traditional morality or not, whether he keeps vows or ignores them—if he turns away from the Kula path, he has no spiritual foundation. His existence is as aimless as a donkey tied outside a house. Only those dedicated to the Kula way of life are considered to be living a truly pious life.

->Only he is called a "man" by the wise who is devoted to Kula-dharma.<-
->Another is, in truth, merely a heap of bones covered with skin. (66)<-
<note>original: "स पुमानुच्यते सद्भिः कुलधर्मपरायणः। अपरस्तु परं सत्यमस्थिकूटत्वचावृतः।। ६६।।"</note>

->*Only he is a man who follows Kula-dharma:*<-

Among the wise, only that person who follows the Kula path deserves to be called a human being. Others are nothing more than skeletons wrapped in skin.

->One who knows the four <term>Vedas: The most ancient and authoritative scriptures of Hinduism</term> but is ignorant of Kula is lower than an outcast, O Beloved.<-
->An outcast who knows the Kula is superior even to a <term>Brahmin: A member of the priestly and scholarly caste</term>. (67)<-
<note>original: "चतुर्वेदी कुलाज्ञानी श्वपचादधमः प्रिये। श्वपचोऽपि कुलज्ञानी ब्राह्मणादतिरिच्यते।। ६७।।"</note>

->*Scholars of the Vedas who are ignorant of Kula are inferior even to <term>Cāṇḍālas: Historically, people outside the four-fold caste system, often performing "unclean" tasks</term>:*<-

Even a scholar who has mastered all four Vedas is considered lower than a <term>Cāṇḍāla</term> if he lacks the Kula wisdom. Conversely, if a person from the lowest social class possesses Kula knowledge, they are spiritually superior to a high-caste Brahmin.

->One who is endowed with the Grace of the <term>Guru: Spiritual teacher</term>,<-
->whose sins are washed away by <term>Dīkṣā: Ritual initiation</term>,<-
->and who delights in the worship of the Kula, O Goddess—he is the true Kaula, and none other. (68)<-
<note>original: "गुरुकारुण्ययुक्त स्तु दीक्षानिर्धूतपातकः। कुलपूजारतो देवि सोऽयं कौलो न चेतरः।। ६८।।"</note>

->*A worshipper of <term>Śakti: The Divine Feminine power</term> alone is a True Kaula:*<-

The true follower of this path is the one who has received the Guru’s compassion, has been purified of their past sins through sacred initiation, and finds joy in the worship of the Divine Power (Śakti). No one else can claim this title.

->That practitioner who does not see, find, or worship<-
->the Kula-wisdom—shame on him! His life is like that of a crow. (69)<-
<note>original: "यः कौलिकः कुलज्ञानं न पश्यति न विन्दति। न पूजयति धिक् तस्य तत् काकस्येव जीवितम्।। ६९।।"</note>

A <term>Kaulika: A practitioner of the Kula path</term> who fails to recognize or honor the sacred power of the Kula is to be pitied. His life is as insignificant and wretched as that of a crow.

## Kularnava Tantra

->Blessed are they, the performers of virtuous deeds, the true saints and the yogis,<-
->in whose minds, O Goddess, the Kula-wisdom shines forth by the power of good fortune. (70)<-
<note>original: "ते धन्याः पुण्यकर्माणस्ते सन्तस्ते च योगिनः। येषां भाग्यवशादेवि कुलज्ञानं प्रकाशते।। ७० ।।"</note>

O Goddess! Those in whose minds the knowledge of the Kula shines—granted by destiny—are truly praiseworthy. They are the righteous ones, the true holy men, and the accomplished <term>Yogis: Practitioners of spiritual disciplines aimed at union with the Divine</term>.

->They are venerable, they are great souls, they have fulfilled their life's purpose, and are the best of men,<-
->in whose hearts arises the Kula-wisdom that has been spoken by Me. (71)<-
<note>original: "ते वन्द्यास्ते महात्मानः कृतार्थास्ते नरोत्तमाः। येषामुत्पद्यते चित्ते कुलज्ञानं मयोदितम्।। ७१ ।।"</note>

Those who harbor this Kula-wisdom in their hearts—the very wisdom I have revealed—are worthy of worship. They are noble souls who have reached the pinnacle of human existence and achieved the ultimate goal of life.

->The vision of all deities, the bathing in all sacred waters,<-
->and the performance of every sacrifice are all contained within entering the Kula-dharma. (72)<-
<note>original: "सर्वप्रकाशगमनं सर्वतीर्थावगाहनम्। यत् सर्वयज्ञाचरणं कुलधर्मप्रवेशनम्।। ७२ ।।"</note>

To enter the <term>Kula-dharma: The sacred spiritual path and obligations of the Kula tradition</term> is equivalent to seeing every radiant god, making pilgrimages to every holy site, and conducting every possible religious ritual.

->Those virtuous men who truly enter the Kula-dharma,<-
->certainly never enter a mother’s womb for birth again. (73)<-
<note>original: "प्रविशन्ति कुलं धर्मं ये वै सुकृतिनो नराः। ते पुनर्जननीगर्भं न विशन्ति कदाचन।। ७३ ।।"</note>

Pious individuals who find their way into the Kula-dharma are liberated from the cycle of reincarnation; they are never again subject to the pains of being born into the physical world.

->Even if someone mentions "Kula, Kula" merely by chance,<-
->that mention becomes purifying, O Goddess, through Your grace.<-
->O Queen of the Kula, for one who has Kula-wisdom, there is no need for any other religion. (74)<-
<note>original: "प्रसङ्गेनापि यः कश्चित् कुलं कुलमितीरयेत्। कुलं तत् पावनं देवि भवति त्वदनुग्रहात्। कुलज्ञानस्य कुलेशानि नान्यधर्मैः प्रयोजनम्।। ७४ ।।"</note>

O Goddess! Even a casual or accidental mention of the word "Kula" carries such power that it purifies the speaker through Your divine favor. O <term>Kuleśānī: The Sovereign Goddess of the Kula path</term>, for the person who possesses this inner wisdom, all other religious paths and duties become unnecessary.

->O Queen of the Kula! To the great-souled Kaulikas who are devoted to the Kula,<-
->I bestow the Supreme Knowledge at the time of their death—of this there is no doubt. (75)<-
<note>original: "कुलेशि कुलनिष्ठानां कौलिकानां महात्मानम्। ददामि परमं ज्ञानं चान्तकाले न संशयः।। ७५ ।।"</note>

O Lady of the Kula! For those <term>Kaulikas: Initiated followers of the Kaula tradition</term> who remain steadfast and devoted, I personally grant the highest spiritual illumination at the moment of their passing. This is an absolute certainty.

->People often desire paths that require long effort for very little reward.<-
->Alas! Who would ever abandon the Kula, which easily provides every possible fruit? (76)<-
<note>original: "चिरायासाल्पफलं काङ्क्षन्ते समयं जनाः। सुखेन सवफलं कुलं कोऽपि त्यजत्यहो।। ७६ ।।"</note>

It is a wonder that people seek out religious systems that demand years of grueling labor only to yield minor spiritual results. Who in their right mind would turn away from the Kula path, which brings every blessing and the ultimate reward with such ease?

<summary>This page extols the virtues of the Kula path, asserting that Kula-wisdom is the highest achievement of human life, superior to all other rituals and pilgrimages, and a direct guarantee of liberation from rebirth.</summary>
<keywords>Kularnava Tantra, Kula-dharma, Kaulika, liberation, reincarnation, Kuleśānī, spiritual wisdom, Shiva, Devi</keywords>

# Page 29

## Chapter Two: The Greatness of Kula-dharma

->One who knows the Kula is all-knowing, even if they have abandoned the study of the Vedas and the scriptures.<-
->However, one who is learned in the Vedas, scriptures, and traditional texts, yet is ignorant of the Kula, is truly ignorant indeed. (77)<-
<note>original: "कुलज्ञो हि च सर्वज्ञो वेदशास्त्रोज्झितोऽपि वा । वेदशास्त्रगमज्ञोऽपि कुलाज्ञस्त्वज्ञ एव हि ।। ७७ ।।"</note>

A <term>Kulajña: One who possesses the direct, experiential realization of the 'Kula' or the divine family/totality</term> is considered omniscient. In this tradition, spiritual experience outweighs the intellectual mastery of the <term>Vedas: The oldest and most sacred Hindu scriptures</term>, the <term>Shastras: Law books and philosophical treatises</term>, or the <term>Agamas: Traditional doctrines or manuals of worship</term>.

->O Goddess! Only Your devotees know the glory of the Kula, not others;<-
->just as only the Chakora bird knows the splendor of the moon, and no other. (78)<-
<note>original: "जानन्ति कुल माहात्म्यं त्वद्भक्ता एव नापरे । चकोरा एव जानन्ति नान्ये चन्द्रगतां रुचिम् ।। ७८ ।।"</note>

The <term>Devi: The Divine Mother or Goddess</term> is told that the secret beauty of this path is reserved for her followers. The <term>Chakora: A mythical bird in Indian literature said to live solely on moonbeams</term> serves as a metaphor for the specialized, refined "taste" required to appreciate spiritual truth.

->Only one who knows the Kula derives happiness from hearing its story, O Beloved;<-
->does the moonlight cause small rivers to swell as it does the great ocean? (79)<-
<note>original: "कुलज्ञा एव तुष्यन्ति श्रुत्वा कुलकथां प्रिये । स्वल्पा नद्यो विवर्द्धन्ते ज्योत्स्नया किं समुद्रवत् ।। ७९ ।।"</note>

Just as the tide only rises significantly in the vast sea and not in minor streams, only a heart expanded by Kula-wisdom can truly respond to its profound teachings.

->The followers of the Kula, who know the essence, pay no heed to other paths;<-
->just as the black bee, enjoying the fragrance of the coral tree, seeks no other flower. (80)<-
<note>original: "नान्यधर्ममवेक्षन्ते कौलिका: सारवेदिन: । भृङ्गा: पुष्पान्तरं लुब्धा मन्दाराामोदसेविन: ।। ८० ।।"</note>

A <term>Kaulika: A practitioner of the Kula tradition</term> who has tasted the "essence" of reality is not distracted by lesser religious systems. The <term>Mandara: The celestial coral tree, one of the five trees of paradise</term>, represents the intoxicating and superior nature of this wisdom.

->Those who know the essence cherish the Kula-dharma, while others do not;<-
->Shiva carries the moon upon His forehead, yet the demon Rahu seeks only to devour it. (81)<-
<note>original: "मानयन्ते हि सारज्ञा: कुलधर्मं न चेतरे । शिव: शिरसि धत्तेऽब्जं सैंहिकेया गिलत्यहो ।। ८१ ।।"</note>

This verse highlights the difference in perspective between the enlightened and the ignorant. <term>Shiva: The supreme deity of this Tantra</term> treats the moon (symbolizing wisdom/Kula) as a crown, whereas the demon <term>Rahu: The shadow planet in Vedic astrology responsible for eclipses</term> tries to consume it.

->Only the wise understand the Kula philosophy, not the ignorant;<-
->can a crane separate milk from water in the way a swan does? (82)<-
<note>original: "अभिज्ञा एव जानन्ति नाभिज्ञा: कुलदर्शनम् । जलमिश्रपय:पानं बक: किं वेत्ति हंसवत् ।। ८२ ।।"</note>

The <term>Jnani: A person of true spiritual knowledge</term> is compared to the legendary swan (*Hamsa*), which is said to have the ability to drink only the milk from a mixture of milk and water—a metaphor for discerning the eternal truth from the temporary world.

->The world is composed of Shiva and Shakti; within this world, the Kula-dharma is established.<-
->Therefore, the Kula path is the highest of all; how could it ever be considered ordinary? (83)<-
<note>original: "शिवशक्तिमयो लोको लोके कौलं प्रतिष्ठितम् । तस्मात् सर्वाधिकं कौलं सर्वसाधारणं कथम् ।। ८३ ।।"</note>

The universe is viewed as the union of <term>Shiva: Consciousness</term> and <term>Shakti: Primordial Energy</term>. Because the <term>Kula-dharma: The spiritual duty and path of the Kula tradition</term> is rooted in this fundamental cosmic reality, it is presented as the most exalted of all spiritual disciplines.

<summary>This page uses a series of poetic analogies—such as the swan separating milk from water and the moon on Shiva's brow—to argue that the Kula-dharma is a supreme, essential wisdom that surpasses mere academic study of the Vedas.</summary>
<keywords>Kula-dharma, Shiva, Shakti, Kaulika, spiritual discernment, Chakora bird, Rahu, Hamsa swan, religious essentialism</keywords>

While the previous page established that experiential knowledge of the Kula path surpasses mere scholarly study of the Vedas, this page reconciles the two. It argues that the various philosophical systems are not rivals but are actually different parts of the Divine body, unified within the Kula tradition through their practical, immediate results.</meta>

# Page 30

### In the Kularnava Tantra

->The six systems of philosophy are My limbs: My feet, My belly, My hands, and My head.<-
->Whoever creates division among them cuts My very limbs. (84)<-
<note>original: "षड्दर्शनानि मेऽङ्गानि पादौ कुक्षिः करौ शिरः। तेषु भेदन्तु यः कुर्यान्ममाङ्गं च्छेदयेत् सः॥ ८४॥"</note>

The <term>Darshanas: The six classical systems of Indian philosophy (Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa, and Vedanta)</term> are described here as the physical body of the Divine. Shiva explains that these various intellectual paths are not contradictory but are integral parts of a single organic whole. To favor one while attacking another is to dismember the deity.

->Indeed, these same six systems constitute the six limbs of the Kula.<-
->Therefore, O Beloved, know the Kula-based scriptures to be of the very essence of the Vedas. (85)<-
<note>original: "एतान्येव कुलस्यापि षडङ्गानि भवन्ति हि। तस्माद्वैदात्मकं शास्त्रं विद्धि कौलात्मकं प्रिये॥ ८५॥"</note>

Similarly, O My Beloved! These six philosophies (deriving from the <term>Vedas: The foundational sacred scriptures of Hinduism</term>) constitute the six limbs of the <term>Kula: Literally 'family' or 'totality,' referring here to the Tantric path that integrates all reality</term>. Therefore, the teachings of the Kula are not a departure from ancient tradition, but its fulfillment.

->Across all philosophies, there is but one Deity who grants the fruit of practice.<-
->In this Kula, it is the same Divine that grants both worldly enjoyment and ultimate liberation to mankind, O Beloved. (86)<-
<note>original: "दर्शनेष्वखिलेष्वेकं फलदं चैकदैवतम्। भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं नृणां कुलेऽस्मिन् दैवतं प्रिये॥ ८६॥"</note>

There is one Divine reality that yields results in diverse schools of thought. In the Kula path, this Divine specifically provides <term>Bhukti: Worldly enjoyment or prosperity</term> and <term>Mukti: Spiritual liberation or release from the cycle of rebirth</term>, showing that the path does not require one to abandon the world to find the spirit.

->O Beloved, Queen of the Perfected Yogis! Even if it seems contrary to worldly customs,<-
->The Kula is proven authentic because it yields immediate, perceptible results. (87)<-
<note>original: "लोकधर्मविरुद्धश्च (ह्वोऽपि) सिद्धयोगीश्वरि प्रिये। कुलं प्रमाणतां याति प्रत्यक्षफलदं यतः॥ ८७॥"</note>

*The authenticity of the Kula-scriptures is inherent in their ability to provide immediate results:*

<term>Siddha Yogis: Perfected masters of yoga who possess supernatural powers</term> are dear to the Lord. Even if the Kula path appears to go against <term>Loka-dharma: Conventional social or religious morality</term>, its validity is proven by "immediate fruit"—meaning the practitioner experiences the benefits in this lifetime, not just in an afterlife.

->Direct perception is the preferred proof for all living beings, O Beloved.<-
->By the power of such direct attainment, all false reasoners are defeated. (88)<-
<note>original: "प्रत्यक्षञ्च प्रमाणाय सर्वेषां प्राणिनां प्रिये। उपलब्धिवालात्तस्य हताः सर्वे कुतार्किकाः॥ ८८॥"</note>

Direct proof is loved by all <term>Jivas: Individual living souls</term>. Those who use "false reasoning" or dry logic to attack the Kula are silenced by the undeniable reality of the spiritual experiences and successes the path provides to its followers.

->Who can truly know what is unseen, or what will happen to whom in the future?<-
->Therefore, that which gives immediate results is the highest philosophy. (89)<-
<note>original: "परोक्षं को नु जानीते कस्य किं वा भविष्यति। यद्वा प्रत्यक्षफलदं तदेवोत्तम दर्शनम्॥ ८९॥"</note>

The text argues for a spiritual pragmatism. Since the distant future and the afterlife are "unseen," the most trustworthy path is the one that transforms the practitioner's reality here and now.

->Knowing this Kula-dharma, all men are liberated.<-
->Recognizing this, O Supreme Goddess, I have "hidden" the Kula through deprecation. (90)<-
<note>original: "कुलधर्ममिमं ज्ञात्वा मुच्यन्ते सर्वमानवाः। इति मत्वा महेशानि मया कौलं विगर्हितम्॥ ९०॥"</note>
<note>The Sanskrit word 'vigarhitam' usually means condemned or censured. In Tantric contexts, the Deity often "censures" or speaks ill of the path to keep it secret and hidden from those who are not ready for its power, ensuring only the truly devoted will seek it out.</note>

<summary>This page defines the Kula path as the harmonious synthesis of all philosophical systems and justifies its validity through the pragmatic "immediate fruit" of spiritual and worldly success. Shiva explains that while the path may seem unconventional, its efficacy is the ultimate proof of its Vedic authority.</summary>

<keywords>Darshanas, limbs of Shiva, Kula-dharma, Bhukti, Mukti, direct perception, immediate results, spiritual pragmatism, Veda-shastra</keywords>

It explains why some are naturally drawn to the truth while others are led astray by lesser scriptures.</meta>

# Second Chapter

->For those deprived of Your compassion and those who oppose the knowledge of the Kula,<-
->the Kula tradition is something to be reviled by these ignorant "bound souls." (61)<-
<note>original: "त्वत्कारुण्यविहीनानां कुलज्ञानविरोधिनाम्। पशूनामन्भिज्ञानां कुलधर्मो विगर्हितः।।"</note>

->One whose heavy bonds of sinful actions from previous lives remain,<-
->will never attain the Grace of the Guru or the knowledge of the Kula. (62)<-
<note>original: "यस्य जन्मान्तरे पापकर्मबन्धोऽधिको भवेत्। न तस्य गुरुकारुण्यं कुलज्ञानं जायते।।"</note>

### *Knowledge of the Kula is not for Sinners:*

The knowledge of <term>Kuladharma: The sacred path or duty of the 'Family' (Kula) of practitioners</term> is condemned by those who are deprived of Your Grace, or who actively oppose the Kula path. This wisdom remains outside the understanding of "bound souls"—the <term>pashus: Literally 'cattle' or 'animals,' referring here to uninitiated individuals bound by worldly instincts and social conventions</term>—who live in the ordinary world. Nor is it intended for those whose actions in past births have forged strong chains of sin. For such individuals, there is no Grace from the <term>Guru: The spiritual teacher</term> nor the dawning of Kula knowledge.

->Just as a blind man cannot see the Sun which illuminates everything,<-
->so those deluded by Your illusion do not recognize the Kula. (63)<-
<note>original: "यथान्धा नैव पश्यन्ति सूर्य सर्वप्रकाशकम्। तथा कुलं न जानन्ति तव मयाविमोहिताः।।"</note>

Just as a blind person cannot perceive the all-illuminating Sun, so too do people who are deluded by Your <term>Maya: The divine power of illusion that makes the world appear separate from the Divine</term> fail to see the truth of the Kula.

->Even if people devotedly follow philosophies like Shaivism, Vaishnavism, and Solar worship,<-
->if they do so every day, their efforts may result in nothing but wasted labor. (64)<-
<note>original: "शैववैष्णवसौरादि दर्शनान्यपि भक्तितः। भजन्ते मानवा नित्यं वृथायासफलानि च।।"</note>

Though people may constantly worship according to other philosophies—such as <term>Shaivism: Worship of Shiva</term>, <term>Vaishnavism: Worship of Vishnu</term>, or <term>Saura: Worship of the Sun</term>—without the deeper Kula connection, their efforts often become a source of exhaustion without yielding the desired spiritual fruit.

->The Vedas, the legal texts, and the scriptures all teach the same path to worldly enjoyment and liberation;<-
->yet alas, the fools condemn Your philosophy, which is so dear to Me! (65)<-
<note>original: "वेदशास्त्रागमैः प्रोक्तं भोगमोक्षैकसाधनम्। मूढा निन्दन्ति हा हन्त मत्प्रियं तव दर्शनम्।।"</note>

The <term>Vedas: The foundational sacred scriptures of Hinduism</term>, the <term>Shastras: Scholarly or legal texts</term>, and the <term>Agamas: Revealed Tantric scriptures</term> all describe the same essential means of attaining <term>Bhoga: Worldly enjoyment</term> and <term>Moksha: Final spiritual liberation</term>. But alas! The foolish condemn Your philosophy, My Beloved, even though it is the path most dear to Me.

->O Goddess, I have confused the "bound souls" with millions of different scriptures;<-
->boasting of their useless knowledge, they remain ignorant of the Kula path. (66)<-
<note>original: "भ्रामिता हि मया देवि पशवः शास्त्रकोटिषु। कुलधर्म न जानन्ति वृथा ज्ञानाभिमानिनः।।"</note>

### *Scriptures for the Bound are propagated to mislead the evil-minded:*

O Goddess! I have led these "bound souls" through a maze of millions of different scriptures. They remain ignorant of the Kuladharma, instead filled with a false and hollow pride in their academic knowledge.

->Indeed, I myself have spoken all these "bound" scriptures,<-
->assuming different forms specifically to delude the wicked-hearted. (67)<-
<note>original: "पशुशास्त्राणि सर्वाणि मयैव कथितानि हि। मूर्त्त्यन्तरन्तु गत्वैव मोहनाय दुरात्मनाम्।।"</note>
->Because of the great sins of these men, a desire for those scriptures arises in them;<-
->they shall not find the True Path even in hundreds of millions of cosmic ages. (68)<-
<note>original: "महापापवशन्नृणां तेषु वाञ्छभिजायते। तेषाञ्च सदगतिर्नास्ति कल्पकोटिशतैरपि।।"</note>

To mislead those who are wicked, I Myself—assuming other forms—have enunciated all the <term>Pashu-shastras: Doctrines intended for the uninitiated or 'animal-natured' who are not ready for the highest truth</term> to fulfill their limited desires. However, because they are involved in great sins, these men are unable to attain a state of true spiritual goodness even in a thousand <term>Kalpas: An immense period of time in Hindu cosmology, representing a single 'day' of the creator god Brahma</term>.

<summary>This page explains that the Kula path is hidden from the sinful and the uninitiated through divine illusion. Lord Shiva reveals that he created lesser scriptures specifically to preoccupy those with "animal natures," preventing them from reaching the highest truth until their karma is purified.</summary>
<keywords>Kuladharma, Pashu, Maya, spiritual blindness, Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Bhoga and Moksha, Pashu-shastras, Kalpa, divine delusion</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Second Chapter of the Kularnava Tantra, following the discussion on how those burdened by past sins or lacking divine grace are unable to perceive the truth of the Kula. While the previous page established that the Kula tradition is the essence of all wisdom, this page explores the rarity of true practitioners and the tragic tendency of humanity to choose worldly distraction over spiritual liberation.</meta>

# In the Kularnava Tantra

->Even when urged, the sinful soul does not enter the Kula path;<-
->even when forbidden, the virtuous soul clings to the Kula alone. (66)<-
<note>original: "प्रेर्यमाणोऽपि पापात्मा कुले नैव प्रवर्तते। वार्यमाणोऽपि पुण्यात्मा कुलमेवाभिलम्बते।।"</note>

Despite active persuasion, those with a darkened mind do not take to the <term>Kuladharma: The sacred duty or "way" of the Kula (divine family) tradition</term>. Conversely, even if one tries to discourage them, the pious and pure-hearted will never forsake this sacred path.

->By the Kula Path, the Gods attained their divinity;<-
->the Sages and the lords of Yogis have reached the highest perfection. (100)<-
<note>original: "कुलधर्मेण देवत्वं देवाः सम्प्रतिपेदिरे। मुनियोगीश्वराद्याश्च सुसिद्धिं परमां गताः।।"</note>

Through the practice of the Kula way, the Gods themselves achieved their divine status. Likewise, the great <term>Munis: Ancient silent sages</term> and master <term>Yogis: Practitioners of spiritual disciplines</term> have attained the supreme state of spiritual success.

### *The Condition of the Kula Path Among the Ignorant:*

->Hypocrites devoted to the rituals of the "bound souls" are easy to find on earth;<-
->those who serve the Kula path alone are great and extremely rare. (101)<-
<note>original: "पशुव्रतादिनिरताः सुलभा दाम्भिका भुवि। ये कौलमेव सेवन्ते ते महान्तोऽति दुर्लभाः।।"</note>

To the hypocrites, who remain caught up in the external observances of the <term>Pashus: Literally 'cattle'; refers to uninitiated souls bound by social convention and worldly instinct</term>, only the mundane world is accessible. However, those who truly serve the Kula path attain a greatness that is rarely found.

->Many are the humans who claim to know false truths;<-
->but rare, O Supreme Goddess, is the one skilled in the reality of the Kula. (102)<-
<note>original: "मानवा बहवः सन्ति मिथ्यातत्त्वार्थवेदिनः। दुर्लभोऽयं महेशानि कुलतत्त्वविशारदः।।"</note>

There are many humans who believe they understand the nature of reality but are actually following false paths. But O <term>Maheshani: A title for the Goddess meaning 'Supreme Mistress'</term>! Those who are truly expert in the <term>Kulatattva: The essential truth or reality of the Kula</term> are very few.

->Just as some diseased men, O Empress of the Kula,<-
->do not take the divine medicine that destroys great illnesses, (103)<-
->but instead use bad medicines and improper food that increase their pain,<-
->so too do they perform worldly actions born of birth and death. (104)<-
->Deprived of Your compassion, they act thus continually;<-
->they do not worship the Kula path, which grants release from worldly bonds. (105)<-
<note>original: "यथा रोगातुरः केचिन्मानवाः कुलनायिके... न भजन्ते कुलं धर्मं भवबन्धविमोचनम्।।"</note>

O <term>Kulanayike: The Leader or Mistress of the Kula</term>! Just as a person suffering from a disease might fail to take a divine medicine capable of destroying the most terrible of ailments, choosing instead harmful foods and ineffective treatments that only worsen the condition; so too do people, when lacking Your grace, spend their entire lives from birth to death chasing worldly activities. They fail to worship the Kula path, which is the only true <term>Bhavabandha-vimochana: Liberation from the bonds of worldly existence</term>.

->Just as people, out of delusion, O Empress of the Kula,<-
->eagerly ask merchants for wild-grown black pepper, (106)<-
->but no one asks for priceless gems;<-
->in the same way, they seek the scriptures of the "bound" which only result in the chains of action. (107)<-
<note>original: "यथा चारण्यजातांस्तु मरीचादीन् वणिग्जनान्... तथैव पशुशास्त्राणि कर्मपाशफलानि च।।"</note>

People are often like deluded shoppers who eagerly seek out common forest-grown black pepper from merchants because it is familiar, while no one thinks to ask for the priceless jewels that are also available. In the same way, most people seek out the <term>Pashu-shastras: Scriptures intended for the uninitiated</term>—teachings that only result in more <term>Karmapasha: The "noose" or bonds created by one's actions</term>—rather than the liberating truth.

<summary>This page contrasts the scarcity of true spiritual seekers with the abundance of "bound souls" who prefer familiar worldly rituals over the liberating but rare Kula path. It uses metaphors of sick men refusing divine medicine and shoppers choosing common pepper over jewels to illustrate human spiritual ignorance.</summary>

## Second Chapter

->So the fools, deluded by Your illusion, ask these questions;<-
->they do not ask about the sacred Duty of the Kula, which grants both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (108)<-
<note>original: "इति पृच्छन्ति मूर्खास्ते तव मायाविमोहिताः। कुलधर्मं न पृच्छन्ति भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदम्।।"</note>

Just as deluded men seek only wild black pepper and fail to ask for the valuable gem, so, O <term>Kulanayika: The "Mistress of the Kula," a title for the Goddess</term>, those deluded by Your <term>Maya: The divine power of illusion that makes the temporary world seem like the only reality</term> desire only the <term>Pashu-shastras: Scriptures intended for "bound souls" or the uninitiated</term>. These scriptures lead them only to being bound by the results of their actions; they do not seek the <term>Kuladharma: The sacred way of the Kula tradition</term> which provides both the enjoyment of life and final emancipation.

->Mistaking musk for mud, or camphor for salt;<-
->mistaking sugar for common gravel, and a gem for mere glass; (109)<-
->the ignorant do not recognize the reality of what is placed right in their hand;<-
->similarly, those deprived of Your grace do not recognize the Kula. (110)<-
<note>original: "कस्तूरीं कर्दमधिया कर्पूरं लवणेच्छया। शार्करं शर्कराभ्रान्त्या मणिं काचमनीषया।। यथादृष्टं न मन्यन्ते करस्थमपि पामराः। तथा कौलं न जानन्ति त्वत्प्रसादविवर्जिताः।।"</note>

->Oh, how great is the power of the delusion born of Your illusion!<-
->O Goddess of Gods, if it deludes even the immortals, what can be said of the ignorant? (111)<-
<note>original: "अहो मोहस्य माहात्म्यं त्वन्मायाजनितस्य च। किमज्ञानपि देवेशि मोहयेदमरानपि।।"</note>

->Drinking the wine, eating the meat, and gazing at the face of the Beloved—<-
->this very conduct is the prayer that leads to the Supreme State. (112)<-
->This Kula vision is attained through the compassion of the Guru;<-
->Your devotees alone know that this Kula provides both enjoyment and liberation, and none others. (113)<-
<note>original: "पेयं मद्यं पलं खाद्यं समालोक्य प्रियामुखम्। इत्येवाचरणं जाप्यं परिप्राप्यं परम्पदम्।। गुरुकारुण्यसँलभ्यमीदृशं कुलदर्शनम्। त्वद्भक्ता एव जानन्ति नेतरे भुक्तिमुक्तिदम्।।"</note>
<note>The text here describes the "Left-Hand" path of Tantra, where worldly pleasures like wine and meat are ritualized and transformed into spiritual tools to reach the "Supreme State."</note>

->There are some who claim to be "Great Ones" while lacking the Guru’s instructions;<-
->already deluded themselves, they now delude all people. (114)<-
<note>original: "गुरूपदेशरहिता महान्त इति केचन। मोहयन्ति जनान् सर्वान् स्वयं पूर्वविमोहिताः।।"</note>

->Certain wicked people, devoted to evil actions, even try to preach;<-
->but as the master is, so shall his followers be. (115)<-
<note>original: "दुराचारपराः केचिद्विद्याचयन्ति च पामराः। कथं भूतो भवेत् स्वामी सेवकाः स्युस्तथाविधाः।।"</note>

<summary>This page uses metaphors of misidentified valuables to illustrate how spiritual ignorance (Maya) prevents people from recognizing the Kula path. It asserts that the Kula tradition, characterized by the ritual transformation of sensory experiences and guided by a true Guru, is the only way to achieve both worldly success and spiritual freedom.</summary>

It clarifies that the path is not a license for hedonism but a disciplined spiritual undertaking.</meta>

# Kularnava Tantra
### Page 34

->Many who mimic the Way of the Kula are merely deceivers possessed of false knowledge.<-
->Deprived of the sacred <term>Guru-Shishya: The lineage-based tradition of teacher and student</term> tradition, they invent their own notions of this spiritual duty through their own limited intellect. (116)<-
<note>original: "बहवः कौलिकं धर्मं मिथ्याज्ञानविडम्बकाः। स्वबुद्ध्या कल्पयन्तीत्थं पारम्पर्यविवर्जिताः।।"</note>

Beguiled by the false knowledge so propagated, certain persons, deprived of the Teacher-Student tradition, imagine the nature of the <term>Kuladharma: The sacred duty or path of the Kula tradition</term> according to their own intellect.

->If a human could truly attain <term>Siddhi: Spiritual perfection, fulfillment, or miraculous powers</term> simply by drinking wine,<-
->then every base drunkard would surely reach perfection. (117)<-
<note>original: "मद्यपानेन मनुजो यदि सिद्धिं लभेत वै। मद्यपानरताः सर्वे सिद्धिं गच्छन्तु पामराः।।"</note>

->If merely partaking of flesh could lead to a holy state,<-
->then all the carnivores in the world would surely possess great merit. (118)<-
<note>original: "मांसभक्षणमात्रेण यदि पुण्या गतिर्भवेत्। लोके मांसाशिनः सर्वे पुण्यभाजो भवन्ति हि।।"</note>

->If liberation were ensured by the mere act of sexual union,<-
->then every creature in the world would be liberated through companionship with the female. (119)<-
<note>original: "शक्तिसम्भोगमात्रेण यदि मोक्षो भवेत् वै। सर्वेऽपि जन्तवो लोके मुक्ताः स्युः स्त्रीनिषेवनात्।।"</note>

->O <term>Mahadevi: "Great Goddess," the consort of Shiva and the recipient of these teachings</term>! It is not the path of the Kula that I have ever condemned.<-
->On the other hand, those who lack proper <term>Achara: Sacred conduct, discipline, or established rules of behavior</term> are the ones to be denounced, and no others. (120)<-
<note>original: "कुलमार्गो महादेवि न मया निन्दितः क्वचित्। आचाररहिता येऽत्र निन्दितास्ते न चेतरे।।"</note>

->The conduct I have prescribed for the Way of the Kula is one thing,<-
->but O Goddess, the fools who imagine themselves to be wise wander in an entirely different direction. (121)<-

->One may walk upon the sharp edge of a sword; one may hold the neck of a tiger;<-
->one may even wrap a serpent around one's body; yet truly following the Way of the Kula is far more difficult. (122)<-
<note>original: "कृपाणधारागमनात् व्याघ्रकण्ठावलम्बनात्। भुजङ्गधारणान्नूनमशक्यं कुलवर्त्तनम्।।"</note>

->Drinking for its own sake, O Goddess of the Gods, is called "vain drinking."<-
->Know this to be a "great sin," as established in the <term>Vedas: The ancient, foundational scriptures of Hindu tradition</term> and other sacred texts. (123)<-

**Drinking denounced by Vedas:**

O Goddess! Vain is the drink—drinking wine as an end in itself. It is a great sin forbidden to men by the Vedas.

<summary>This page refutes the idea that the Kula path is a simple excuse for indulgence, emphasizing that ritual elements like wine, meat, and sex do not grant liberation without the proper tradition and internal discipline. Shiva warns that the true Tantric path is more dangerous and difficult than taming a tiger or walking on a sword.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Second Chapter of the Kularnava Tantra. While the previous page warned against the superficial imitation of Tantric rites by the uninitiated, this page explicitly outlines the strict prohibitions placed upon the "Paśu" (those in the state of limited, animal-like consciousness) and the rigorous penances required for those who violate these codes. It contrasts the ordinary social laws with the specialized practice of the Kaulika.</meta>

## Second Chapter
### Page 35

->For those in the limited state of consciousness, wine and meat are not to be smelled, seen, touched, or drunk.<-
->However, for the <term>Kaulikas: Advanced practitioners of the Kula path</term>, these very things yield the greatest spiritual fruit. (124)<-
<note>original: "अनाघ्रेयमनलोक्यमस्पृश्यञ्चाप्यपेयकम्। मद्यं मांसं पशूनान्तु कौलिकानां महाफलम्।।"</note>

Partaking of flesh and drinking of wine—even their smell, touch, and sight—is strictly prohibited for the seeker still in the <term>Paśu-bhāva: The "animal state," referring to the ordinary, uninitiated soul bound by social conventions and instincts</term>. However, for a perfected Kaulika, these elements are transformed into instruments that bestow the highest spiritual success.

->There are eleven types of wine deemed impure for the twice-born classes.<-
->But the twelfth is the "Great Wine," which is the most supreme of all. (125)<-
->Indeed, ordinary wine is the impurity of grains, and sin itself is called impurity.<-
->Therefore, the priest, the warrior, and the merchant should never drink such wine. (126)<-
<note>original: "अमेध्यानि द्विजातीनां मद्यान्येकादशैव तु। द्वादशन्तु महामद्यं सर्वेषामुत्तमोत्तमम्।। सुरा वै मलमन्नानां पाप्मा तु मलमुच्यते। तस्माद्ब्राह्मणराजन्यौ वैश्य न सुरां पिबेत्।।"</note>

**The eleven prohibited wines for the Twice-born:**
For the <term>Dvijas: "Twice-born," referring to the three higher social classes (Brahmin, Kṣatriya, and Vaiśya) who have undergone spiritual initiation</term>, there are eleven varieties of wine considered unfit for sacred use. However, there is a twelfth variety known as the "Great Wine," which is considered the best of all; only this may be approached under specific conditions. Because ordinary wines are derived from the fermentation of grains, they are viewed as containing the "impurity" of the food and are considered a root of sin. Consequently, the <term>Brahmins: Priestly class</term>, <term>Kṣatriyas: Warrior/ruling class</term>, and <term>Vaiśyas: Merchant/artisan class</term> are forbidden from drinking them.

->By merely sighting wine, one should gaze upon the Sun.<-
->By merely smelling it, one should perform three breath-regulations. (127)<-
->For touching wine, one must submerge themselves up to the knees in water and fast for the day.<-
->If the wine is touched above the navel, the rule is a fast of three nights. (128)<-
->If one drinks wine intentionally, they must pour the liquid, boiling hot, into the mouth.<-
->Once the mouth is thus purified by heat, they may regain their purity. (129)<-
->Such are the traditional methods of penance for the faults of touching wine and the like.<-

**Penances for the sighting or contact with wine:**
For the uninitiated, even the sight of wine is considered a spiritual blemish that must be cleared by looking at the Sun. To remove the stain of smelling wine, one must perform three <term>Prāṇāyāmas: Sacred breath-control exercises</term>, stand in knee-deep water, and fast for an entire day. To cleanse the sin of touching wine, one must fast for three nights while submerged to the navel in water. If an uninitiated person drinks wine deliberately, the traditional <term>Prayashchitta: Atonement or penance</term> is extreme: they must endure the burning of the tongue with boiling liquid. These are the severe methods prescribed to atone for the improper handling or consumption of intoxicants.

->O Beloved, he who slays animals in an unlawful manner for his own sake (130)<-
->will dwell in a terrifying hell for as many days as there are hairs on that animal's body.<-
->Even after death, that wicked person is reborn into the wombs of animals. (131)<-
<note>original: "अविधानेन यो हन्यादात्मार्थं प्राणिनः प्रिये। निवसेन्नरके घोरे दिनानि पशुरोमभिः। स मृतोऽपि दुराचारस्तिर्यग्योनिषु जायते।।"</note>

**Penance for the meaningless killing of life:**
My Beloved! Anyone who kills animals for selfish reasons and without following the sacred law will suffer in a horrific hell for a duration equal to the number of hairs on the slaughtered animal's hide. Furthermore, such a person—having acted contrary to divine order—will be reborn in the lower forms of the animal kingdom.

<summary>This page outlines the strict prohibitions and severe penances regarding meat and wine for the uninitiated (Paśu), contrasting these with the "Great Wine" used by Kaulika adepts. It emphasizes that outside of sacred Tantric ritual, these substances and the act of killing animals lead to spiritual impurity and rebirth in hell or as an animal.</summary>

<keywords>Paśu-bhāva, Kaulika, wine prohibitions, Dvija classes, penance, Prayashchitta, Prāṇāyama, animal sacrifice, karma, spiritual purity</keywords>

It defines the "eight kinds of killers" to demonstrate that anyone involved in the chain of meat consumption shares in the karma, unless the act is performed through the purifying lens of ritual "Vidhi" (prescribed rule).</meta>

## Second Chapter
### Page 36

<header>In the Kularnava Tantra</header>

The one who permits, the one who lures, the one who slaughters, the buyer, the seller, the dresser, the one who serves, and the one who eats—these are the eight kinds of killers. (132)
<note>original: "अनुमन्ता विश्वसिता निहन्ता क्रयविक्रयी। संस्कर्त्ता चोपहर्त्ता च खादिताऽष्टौ च घातकाः।।"</note>

->*Eight kinds of animal-killers:*<-

**The Authorized Killer** (one who decides upon the animal to be killed), **The Deceiver** (one who takes the animal into their confidence), **The Slayer** (the actual killer), **The Traders** (both the purchaser and the seller), **The Dresser** (the one who prepares the carcass), **The Provider** (the one who brings the meat to the table), and **The Eater** (those who consume the flesh)—all eight are considered participants in the act of killing.

The seller kills through the desire for wealth; the eater kills through the act of enjoyment; the executioner kills through the act of binding and slaying. Thus, slaughter is of three kinds. (133)
<note>original: "धनैर्विक्रयिको हन्ति खादिता चोपभोगतः। घातको वध बन्धाभ्यां इत्येष त्रिविधो वधः।।"</note>

->*Three kinds of slaughter:*<-

Selling an animal for money, consuming flesh for personal enjoyment, and the physical slaughter of a tethered animal are the three distinct ways one incurs the sin of killing.

Upon seeing flesh, one should behave as if seeing wine (performing a penance of purification). Therefore, one should never consume <term>Māmsa: Meat</term> or <term>Madya: Wine</term> unless it is done according to the prescribed ritual rules. (134)
<note>original: "मांससन्दर्शनं कृत्वा सुरादर्शनवच्चरेत्। तस्मादविधिना मांसं मद्यं न सेवते क्ववचित्।।"</note>

->*The five <term>Makāras: The "Five Ms," or ritual substances (wine, meat, fish, parched grain, and sexual union)</term> should be resorted to only in the prescribed manner:*<-

O Goddess, if these are consumed according to the sacred rules, You are pleased. But if one partakes of them without such knowledge, O Fair-faced One, they truly lead to the destruction of one’s spiritual progress. (135)
<note>original: "विधिना सेव्यते देवि तरसा त्वं प्रसीदति। नाशयस्यपरिज्ञानात् सत्यमेव वरानने।।"</note>

One should never break even a blade of grass without following the ritual rules. Conversely, if done according to the provisions of the <term>Śāstras: Sacred scriptures and ritual codes</term>, there is no sin even in the killing of a bull or a <term>Brahmin: A member of the priestly class</term>. (136)
<note>This verse emphasizes the absolute authority of "Vidhi" (ritual law). In the context of Tantra, it suggests that the spiritual intent and scriptural injunction transcend worldly morality; an act that is normally a "great sin" is transfigured if it is a ritual necessity.</note>

What more is there to say, My Beloved! Listen to the one essential truth. The method for attaining <term>Jivanmukti: Liberation while still living</term> is a joy hidden within the Kula scriptures. (137)
<note>original: "बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन सारमेकं शृणु प्रिये। जीवन्मुक्तिसुखोपायं कुलशास्त्रेषु गोपितम्।।"</note>

That which is the ultimate goal for one seeking liberation, O Goddess, is as rare as the fragrance of gold. Even among those famous for their knowledge of the Kula path, this supreme knowledge is the most excellent. (138)

->*Vedic proof in favor of <term>Kuladharma: The path and duty of the Kula tradition</term>:*<-

Why say more, O My Beloved! Listen to one fundamental conclusion. The method of Liberation from life is hidden in the...

### Page 37

<header>Second Chapter</header>

The <term>Kula-śāstra</term> <note>The sacred scriptures of the Kula tradition</note> is like fragrance added to gold; it is the ultimate fruit for those who desire <term>Emancipation</term> <note>Moksha; liberation from the cycle of rebirth</note>. Even among those who possess the knowledge of Kula, the wisdom of those known for the <term>Urdhvāmnāya</term> <note>The "Upper Tradition" or highest lineage of Tantric teaching</note> is considered superior.

->All the Kula scriptures were spoken by me alone, O Pārvati.<-
->They are indubitable proofs and must not be refuted by logic. (139)<-
<note>original: "कुलशास्त्राणि सर्वाणि मयैवोक्तानि पार्वति । प्रमाणानि न सन्देहो न हन्तव्यानि हेतुभिः ॥ १३९ ॥"</note>

O Pārvati! I Myself have pronounced all the <term>Kulaśāstras</term>, therefore they are the primary evidence of their own authenticity. They are beyond doubt and should not be challenged by mere intellectual reasoning.

->For the Gods and the Ancestors, the wind blows sweet like honey.<-
->With the most delicious and intoxicating wine, milk, ghee, and honey-water. (140)<-
<note>original: "देवताभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च मधु वाता ऋतायते । स्वादिष्ठया मदिष्ठया क्षीरं सर्पिर्मधूदकम् ॥ १४० ॥"</note>

The wine intended for offering to the Gods and the <term>Pitṛs</term> <note>The ancestral spirits or "Fathers"</note> becomes like nectar. It is deeply nourishing and as pleasant to the taste as rice cooked in milk and clarified butter.

->Holding golden purifying vessels, they bound the male animal.<-
->One should undergo initiation; the Vedas are the proof, my Dear. (141)<-
<note>original: "हिरण्यपावाः खादिश्च अबध्नन् पुरुषं पशुम् । दीक्षामुपैयादित्याद्याः प्रमाणं श्रुतयः प्रिये ॥ १४१ ॥"</note>

If the flesh of a sacrificed male animal is placed in a golden vessel and received as a gift from the Gods according to the prescribed <term>Vedic</term> <note>Ancient Indian scriptures (Śruti) regarded as divine revelation</note> procedures, it immediately washes away all sins and grants the "Knowledge of the Essence."

->Thus I have told you a little of the glory of the Kula, O Mother.<-
->In brief, O Queen of the Kula, what more do you wish to hear? (142)<-
<note>original: "इत्येतत् कथितं किञ्चित् कुलमाहात्म्यम्बिके । समासेन कुलेशानि किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ १४२ ॥"</note>

O <term>Ambike</term>! I have described the greatness of the Kula path to you in this concise way. O <term>Kuleśāni</term> <note>Mistress of the Kula</note>! What else do you desire to learn?

->Thus ends the Second Chapter, titled "The Declaration of the Greatness of the Kula,"<-
->contained within the Upper Tradition Tantra, in the Great Secret of the<-
->Path to Liberation and Nirvana, the highest of all Agamas,<-
->in the one-hundred-and-twenty-five-thousand verse Kularnava. (2)<-
<note>original: "इति श्रीकुलार्णवे निर्वाणमोक्षद्वारे महारहस्ये सर्वागमोत्तमोत्तमे सपादलक्षग्रन्थे पञ्चमखण्डे ऊर्ध्वाम्नायतन्त्रे कुलमाहात्म्यकथनं नाम द्वितीय उल्लासः ॥ २ ॥"</note>

# Chapter Three

## The Great Goddess said:

->O <term>Kuleśa</term> <note>Lord of the Kula; a title for Shiva as the head of the spiritual family</note>! I desire to hear of the <term>Dharma</term> <note>Sacred law or duty</note> which is the most excellent of all.<-
->Speak to me, O Lord, of the <term>Urdhvāmnāya</term> <note>The "Upper Tradition"; the highest and most secret of the five or six directions of Tantric revelation</note>, its sacred <term>Mantra</term>, and its majestic glory. (1)<-
<note>original: "कुलेश श्रोतुमिच्छामि सर्वधर्मोत्तमोत्तमम्। ऊर्ध्वाम्नायश्च तन्मन्त्रं माहात्म्यं वद मे प्रभो।। १।।"</note>

## The Holy Lord said:

->Listen, O Goddess! I shall speak clearly of that which you have asked Me.<-
->By the mere hearing of this, the deities become perfectly pleased. (2)<-
<note>original: "शृणु देवि प्रवक्ष्यामि यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि। तस्य श्रवणमात्रेण देवता सुप्रसीदति।। २।।"</note>

->Never before have I spoken of this to anyone, O <term>Kuleśvarī</term> <note>Mistress of the Kula; a title for the Goddess</note>.<-
->Because of the love I bear for You, I shall tell of the Upper Tradition; listen, my Dear. (3)<-
<note>original: "न कदाचिन्मया प्रोक्तमितः पूर्वं कुलेश्वरि। कथयामि तव स्नेहादूर्ध्वाम्नायं शृणु प्रिये।। ३।।"</note>

->The <term>Vedas</term>, the technical treatises, and the ancient histories are fit for public exposition, O Kuleśvarī.<-
->All the <term>Śaiva</term> and <term>Śākta</term> <term>Āgamas</term> <note>Scriptures revealed by Shiva or the Goddess</note> are declared to be secret. (4)<-
<note>original: "वेदशास्त्रपुराणानि प्रकाश्यानि कुलेश्वरि। शैवशाक्तागमाः सर्वे रहस्याः परिकीर्तिताः।। ४।।"</note>

->The Kula scriptures, O Pārvatī, are the secrets among secrets.<-
->And this, O Mother, is the deepest secret of even those secrets of secrets. (5)<-
<note>original: "रहस्यातिर्रहस्यानि कुलशास्त्राणि पार्वति। रहस्यातिर्रहस्यानां रहस्यमिदमम्बिके।। ५।।"</note>

->The essence of the Upper Tradition is indeed the Supreme <term>Brahman</term> <note>The absolute, infinite reality or the Ultimate Consciousness</note> in its fullness.<-
->Though it has been carefully hidden by Me with great effort, it is now being revealed to You. (6)<-
<note>original: "ऊर्ध्वाम्नायस्य तत्त्वं हि पूर्णब्रह्मात्मकं परम्। सुगोपितं मया यत्नादिदानीन्तु प्रकाश्यते।। ६।।"</note>

<summary>In this opening of Chapter Three, the Goddess requests a discourse on the Urdhvāmnāya (Upper Tradition), and Shiva agrees to reveal this "secret of secrets," identifying it as the essence of the absolute reality (Brahman).</summary>
<keywords>Urdhvāmnāya, Kuleśa, Kulaśāstra, secrecy, Brahman, Shiva and Parvati, revelation, Āgamas</keywords>

--- Page 48 ---
<meta>This page continues the Third Chapter. The previous page ended with the Lord promising to reveal the most secret "Upper Tradition" (Urdhvamnaya) to the Goddess out of love for her. This page details the emergence of the five traditions from Shiva's five faces.</meta>

...of all the Secrets because it is the Supreme Essence in the form of <term>Purna Brahman</term> <note>The Absolute Reality in its complete and perfect form</note>. I have kept it a closely guarded secret but now I am telling it to You.

->From my five faces, the five <term>Amnayas</term> <note>Sacred traditions or "streams" of scriptural revelation</note> have emerged.<-
->The East, the West, the South, and the North;<-
->And the Upper Tradition—these five are celebrated as the paths to liberation. (7)<-
<note>original: "मम पञ्चमुखेभ्यश्च पञ्चाम्नायाः समुद्गताः। पूर्वश्च पश्चिमश्चैव दक्षिणश्चोत्तरस्तथा। ऊर्ध्वाम्नायश्च पञ्चैते मोक्षमार्गाः प्रकीर्तिताः।। ७।।"</note>

### Origin of the Five Traditions from the Five Faces of Shiva
I have produced the five <term>Amnayas</term> from the five faces of Shiva:
I have produced the five <term>Amnayas</term> (Great Traditions) from My five faces, namely: the <term>Purva</term> (Eastern) tradition, the <term>Pashcima</term> (Western) tradition, the <term>Dakshina</term> (Southern) tradition, the <term>Uttara</term> (Northern) tradition, and the <term>Urdhva</term> (Upward or highest) tradition. These are the five traditions, and all five are famous as the paths for Emancipation.

->Many traditions exist, but they are not equal to the Upper Tradition.<-
->This is the truth, O <term>Vararohe</term> <note>A name for the Goddess meaning "one with a beautiful form"</note>; there is no need for a second thought about it. (8)<-
<note>original: "आम्नाया बहवः सन्ति नोर्ध्वाम्नायेन ते समाः। सत्यमेतद्वरारोहे नात्र कार्या विचारणा।। ८।।"</note>

### Superiority of the Upper Tradition
Traditions are many, but none equals the <term>Urdhvamnaya</term>. O Beautiful One, this is the truth and there is no use in doubting it.

->Many secret traditions have arisen from the divisions of the four cardinal traditions.<-
->O <term>Kulanayike</term> <note>Mistress of the Kula lineage</note>, I have previously explained them in this <term>Tantra</term>. (9)<-
<note>original: "आम्नाया बहवो गुप्तश्चतुराम्नायभेदजाः। अस्मिस्तन्त्रे समाख्याताः पूर्वं ते कुलनायिके।। ९।।"</note>

O Mistress of the Kula! Many profound traditions have been born out of the four cardinal traditions. In this <term>Tantra</term> <note>A sacred text or system of practice</note> I will first of all give their summary.

->There are many who know the four traditions, O <term>Kamini</term> <note>Affectionate name for the Goddess</note>.<-
->But those who know the truth of the Upper Tradition are rare, O You who are worshipped by heroes. (10)<-
<note>original: "चतुराम्नाय वेत्तारो बहवः सन्ति कामिनि। ऊर्ध्वाम्नायस्य तत्त्वज्ञा विरला वीरवन्दिते।। १०।।"</note>

### Origin of the Traditions from the portions of Gods, Sakti and Siva
O Beloved! There are many scholars of the four cardinal traditions; but, O Goddess worshipped by the heroic seekers! Rare are the scholars who truly know the Upper Tradition.

->As many as there are grains of dust upon the earth, so many are the mantras.<-
->The <term>Mantras</term> born from each tradition grant both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (11)<-
<note>original: "यावन्तः पांसवो भूमेस्तावन्तः समुदीरिताः। एकैकाम्नायजा मन्त्रा भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदाः।। ११।।"</note>

The <term>Mantras</term> <note>Sacred sound-formulas or prayers</note> leading to Fruition and Emancipation, belonging to one or the other of the traditions to be repeated, are as many as there are dust particles on the earth.

<summary>This page explains the cosmic origin of the five sacred traditions (Amnayas) from the five faces of Shiva, identifying the cardinal directions and the "Upper Tradition." Shiva emphasizes that while many know the four cardinal paths, the Upper Tradition is the most secret and superior path to liberation.</summary>
<keywords>Shiva, Amnaya, Urdhvamnaya, five faces of Shiva, liberation, Mantras, Brahman, Kula tradition, Tantra</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Third Chapter of the Kularnava Tantra. Following the previous page’s introduction of the five traditions (Amnayas) emerging from Shiva's five faces, this section elaborates on the divine origin of mantras and specifically defines why the "Upper Tradition" (Urdhvamnaya) is considered the most supreme path to liberation.</meta>

# In the Kularnava Tantra

->So many subsidiary Mantras, which bestow the essence, have been proclaimed. I Myself have spoken them out of a desire to bless the world. (12)<-
<note>original: "उपमन्त्राश्च तावन्तः सारदाः समुदाहृताः। मयैव कथितास्ते तु लोकानुग्रहकाङ्क्षया।। १२।।"</note>

Similarly, there are infinite subsidiary Mantras of all the <term>Amnayas</term> <note>Sacred traditions or "streams" of scriptural revelation</note> which I Myself have pronounced for the benefit of the World.

->The deities of all these Mantras, who grant their respective results, have emanated from portions of both of Us, O Lady of the beautiful smile! (13)<-
<note>original: "सर्वेषामपि मन्त्राणां देवतास्तत्फलप्रदाः। आवयोरंशसम्भूताः समुद्दिष्टाः शुचिस्मिते।। १३।।"</note>

O Lady of beautiful smile! The <term>Devatas</term> <note>Deities or divine beings</note> of all these Mantras have emanated from both of Us and they all bestow definite results.

->I alone know all the Mantras; no one else knows them. Among tens of millions of humans, someone might know them only through My grace. (14)<-
<note>original: "सर्वमन्त्रानहं वेद्मि नान्यो जानाति कश्चन। मत्प्रसादेन यः कश्चिद्वेत्ति मानवकोटिषु।। १४।।"</note>

Only I know all the Mantras, none else. Out of tens of millions of men, due to My kindness hardly a few know them.

### The Fruits of Knowing the Sacred Traditions

->He who knows even a single tradition is undoubtedly liberated. What then can be said of one who knows all four traditions? Such a person becomes Shiva Himself. (15)<-
<note>original: "एकाम्नायश्च यो वेत्ति स मुक्तो नात्र संशयः। किं पुनश्चतुराम्नायवेत्ता साक्षाच्छिवो भवेत्।। १५।।"</note>

*Fruits of the knowledge of Āmnāyas:*
Whoever knows even one of the Āmnāyas becomes undoubtedly Emancipated. What to say about one who knows four Āmnāyas as he becomes the very <term>Shiva</term> <note>The Supreme Being representing pure consciousness</note> himself.

->Beyond the knowledge of the four traditions is the Upper Tradition, O Dear One! Therefore, one should seek to know that if they desire their own spiritual perfection. (16)<-
<note>original: "चतुराम्नायविज्ञानादूर्ध्वाम्नायः परः प्रिये। तस्मात्तदेव जानीयाद् यदीच्छेत् सिद्धिमात्मनः।। १६।।"</note>

But higher than the Knowledge of all the four Āmnāyas put together is the Knowledge of <term>Urdhvamnaya</term> <note>The "Upward Tradition," considered the highest and most secret path in this lineage</note>, which should, therefore, be known by those desirous of Self-attainment.

### The Meaning of the Upper Tradition

->Because it is the highest of all spiritual paths, the Upper Tradition is praised. Because it raises up those who are situated below, it is called the "Upper Tradition." (17)<-
<note>original: "ऊर्ध्वत्वात् सर्वधर्माणामूर्ध्वाम्नायः प्रशस्यते। ऊर्ध्व नयत्यधःस्थश्च ऊर्ध्वाम्नाय इति स्मृतः।। १७।।"</note>

*Meaning of Urdhvāmnāya:*
Because it is High (Urdhva) among all the <term>Dharmas</term> <note>Spiritual duties, laws, or paths</note> the Urdhvamnaya is superior to all. Because it raises upwards those who are below, therefore, it is so called.

->Because its essence is supreme, O Lady of the Kula, and because it destroys the ocean of worldly existence and is the sole service of the higher worlds, it is remembered as the Upper Tradition. (18)<-
<note>original: "ऊर्ध्वतत्वात् कुलेशानि ध्वस्तसंसार सागरात्। ऊर्ध्वलोकैकसेव्यत्वादूर्ध्वाम्नाय इति स्मृतः।। १८।।"</note>

O <term>Kuleshani</term> <note>A title for the Goddess as the Mistress of the Kula or divine family</note>! Its essence is high, it destroys the world ocean, and the higher worlds wait in its service, hence it is called Urdhvāmnāya.

### The Superiority of the Upper Tradition

->Therefore, O Goddess, know this to be the direct and only means for liberation. The Upper Tradition, higher than the highest, yields greater fruit than all other traditions combined. (19)<-
<note>original: "तस्माद्देवेशि जानीहि साक्षान्मोक्षैकसाधनम्। सर्वाम्नायाधिकफलमूर्ध्वाम्नायं परात् परम्।। १९।।"</note>

*Superiority of Urdhvāmnāya proved through example:*
O <term>Deveshi</term> <note>Goddess of the gods</note>! Know the Urdhvāmnāya as the direct single means for Emancipation yielding a greater Fruit than all others and better than the best of them.

<summary>This page explains that all mantras and their deities originate from Shiva and Shakti, but the knowledge of these traditions is rare. It specifically highlights the "Upper Tradition" (Urdhvamnaya) as the most effective path to liberation, surpassing the four cardinal traditions.</summary>

<keywords>Amnaya, Urdhvamnaya, Mantras, Shiva, Shakti, Kuleshani, liberation, spiritual traditions, Kularnava Tantra</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Third Chapter of the Kularnava Tantra. Following the previous discussion on the divine origin of various Mantras, Shiva now focuses on the supreme status of the Urdhvamnaya (the Upper Tradition), placing it at the pinnacle of all spiritual systems.</meta>

### Third Chapter

->Just as I am worshiped by everyone in all worlds, O Beloved, so is the <term>Urdhvamnaya</term> <note>The 'Upper Tradition' or zenith stream of revelation, considered the most secret and powerful in Tantra</note> the most worshipful among all the sacred traditions, O <term>Shive</term> <note>An address to the Goddess as the feminine form of Shiva</note>. (20)<-
<note>original: "सर्वलोकेषु सर्वेभ्यो ह्यहं पूज्यो यथा प्रिये। आम्नायेषु च सर्वेषु ऊर्ध्वाम्नायस्तथा शिवे।। २०।।"</note>

->As <term>Vishnu</term> <note>The preserver deity</note> is among the gods, as the Sun is among the luminaries; as <term>Kashi</term> <note>Modern-day Varanasi, the holiest city in Hinduism</note> is among the <term>Tirthas</term> <note>Sacred crossing places or pilgrimage sites</note>, and as the Celestial River <note>The Ganges</note> is among the rivers; (21)<-
<note>original: "देवतानां यथा विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां भास्करो यथा। तीर्थानान्तु यथा काशी स्वर्णदी सरितां यथा।। २१।।"</note>

->As Mount Meru is among the mountains, and as Sandalwood is among the trees; as the <term>Ashvamedha</term> <note>The "Horse Sacrifice," the most prestigious of ancient royal rituals</note> is among the sacrifices, and as the Gem is among the stones; (22)<-
<note>original: "पर्वतानां यथा मेरुस्तरूणां चन्दनं यथा। अश्वमेधः क्रतूनाञ्च पाषाणानां यथा मणिः।। २२।।"</note>

->As sweetness is among the tastes, and as gold is among the metals; as the cow is among the four-legged animals, and as the swan is among the birds; (23)<-
<note>original: "यथा रसानां माधुर्यं धातूनां काञ्चनं यथा। चतुष्पदां यथा धेनुर्यथा हंसस्तु पक्षिणाम्।। २३।।"</note>

->As the wandering ascetic is among the stages of life, and as the <term>Brahmin</term> <note>The priestly and intellectual class</note> is among the social classes; as the King is among men, and as the head is among the limbs of the body; (24)<-
<note>original: "आश्रमाणां यथा भिक्षुर्वर्णानां ब्राह्मणो यथा। मनुष्याणां यथा राजाऽवयवानां यथा शिरः।। २४।।"</note>

->As musk is among fragrances, and as the city of <term>Kanchipuri</term> <note>Kanchipuram, one of the seven sacred cities of India</note> was among the cities of old—so, O Beloved, is the Upper Tradition the most excellent among all religions and duties. (25)<-
<note>original: "आमोदानाश्च कस्तूरी यथा काञ्चीपुरी पुराम्। तथैव सर्वधर्माणामूर्ध्वाम्नायोऽधिकः प्रिये।। २५।।"</note>

->Through the arising of the fruits of limitless meritorious deeds earned across many births, one may come to know the Upper Tradition; it cannot be known otherwise, O <term>Viravandite</term> <note>An epithet for the Goddess meaning "She who is worshiped by heroes"</note>. (26)<-
<note>original: "नानाजन्मार्जितापारपुण्यकर्मफलोदयात्। ऊर्ध्वाम्नायं विजानीयान्नान्यथा वीरवन्दिते।। २६।।"</note>

->*The Basis of the Knowledge of the Upper Tradition:*<-

->That man is blessed who, among hundreds of thousands of people, knows the <term>Kuladarshana</term> <note>The philosophy or "vision" of the Kula tradition, a central path in Tantra</note>; but among hundreds of thousands of such people, there is hardly one who truly understands the Upper Tradition. (27)<-
<note>original: "धन्यो मनुष्यलक्षेपु जानाति कुलदर्शनम्। तेषां लक्षेषु यः कश्चिदूर्ध्वाम्नायं प्रवेत्ति च।। २७।।"</note>

<summary>In this passage, Shiva uses a series of poetic superlatives—comparing the Upper Tradition (Urdhvamnaya) to the Sun, the Ganges, and Mount Meru—to establish it as the supreme path of spiritual wisdom. He explains that attaining this knowledge is an extremely rare event, possible only through the accumulated merit of many lifetimes.</summary>

<keywords>Urdhvamnaya, Kularnava Tantra, Kula tradition, spiritual hierarchy, Kashi, Meru, Ashvamedha, merit, liberation, Kuladarshana</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Third Chapter of the Kularnava Tantra, where Shiva is extolling the virtues of the Urdhvamnaya (the Upper Tradition). The previous page compared this tradition to the highest peaks and the most sacred rivers, establishing its supremacy over all other paths. This section focuses on the necessity of a Guru to access this knowledge and the divine status of one who attains it.</meta>

<page-num>42</page-num>
<header>From the Kularnava Tantra</header>

->Not by the <term>Vedas</term> <note>The most ancient sacred scriptures of India</note>, nor by the <term>Agamas</term> <note>Revealed tantric scriptures</note>, nor by the <term>Shastras</term> <note>Philosophical and legal treatises</note>, nor by the extensive <term>Puranas</term> <note>Ancient encyclopedic collections of myth and lore</note>; (28)<-
<note>original: "न वेदैर्नागमैः शास्त्रैर्न पुराणैः सुविस्तरैः।"</note>

->Neither by sacrifices, nor by austerities, nor by millions of pilgrimages and vows; (28)<-
<note>original: "न यज्ञैर्न तपोभिर्वा न तीर्थव्रतकोटिभिः।।"</note>

->Nor by any other means, O Goddess of the gods, such as <term>Mantras</term> <note>Sacred chants or sound-formulas</note> and medicinal herbs, is the <term>Urdhvamnaya</term> <note>The "Upper Tradition" or zenith-stream of revelation, considered the most secret and powerful in the Tantric system</note> known, except through the mouth of the glorious <term>Guru</term> <note>The spiritual teacher who provides direct initiation and oral instruction</note>. (29)<-
<note>original: "नान्यैरुपायैर्देवेशि मन्त्रौषधिपुरःसरैः। आम्नायो ज्ञायते चोर्ध्वः श्रीमद्गुरुमुखं विना।।"</note>

### *The Upper Tradition can be known only from the mouth of the Guru:*

Neither through the Vedas, Agamas, Shastras, and Puranas, however exhaustive they may be, nor through sacrifices, austerities, and visits to millions of places of pilgrimage, nor even through Mantras and herbs, can one know about the Urdhvamnaya. It can be known only through the mouth of the Guru.

->One should seek him there—the omniscient one, a treasure-house of compassion, endowed with all auspicious signs, and an expert in the meaning of the Urdhvamnaya. (30)<-
<note>original: "तमेवान्वेषयेत्तत्र सर्वज्ञं करुणानिधिम्। सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नं ऊर्ध्वाम्नायार्थकोविदम्।"</note>

->Therefore, O Goddess of the gods, O <term>Kuleshvari</term> <note>Mistress of the Kula, or the divine family/lineage</note>, one should learn of the Urdhvamnaya from him. (30)<-
<note>original: "तस्माद्देवेशि जानीयादूर्ध्वाम्नायं कुलेश्वरि।।"</note>

Therefore, look for that compassionate and all-knowing Guru endowed with all the auspicious signs, who may be knowing the Truth of Urdhvamnaya. From him, O Devi Kuleshvari, one should receive the knowledge of Urdhvamnaya.

->O Goddess, the man who knows this tradition in its true essence obtains his desired <term>Siddhi</term> <note>Spiritual power, perfection, or success</note>. This is the truth, the absolute truth, O <term>Varanane</term> <note>A poetic address meaning "One with a lovely face"</note>! (31)<-
<note>original: "आम्नायं यो नरो देवि विजानाति च तत्त्वतः। लभते कांक्षितां सिद्धिं सत्यं सत्यं वरानने।।"</note>

### *The knower of the Upper Tradition is blessed and liberated from worldly life:*

O Devi! One who knows the <term>Amnayas</term> <note>The sacred traditions or streams of revelation</note> in their essence obtains the desired attainments. This is, O Lovely-faced One, truly the truth.

->He who knows the Urdhvamnaya perfectly from the mouth of the glorious Guru, according to the path of the scriptures—that man is, without a doubt, a <term>Jivanmukta</term> <note>One who is liberated while still inhabiting a physical body</note>. (32)<-
<note>original: "ऊर्ध्वाम्नायं विजानाति यः सम्यक् श्रीगुरोर्मुखात्। शास्त्रमार्गेण स नरो जीवन्मुक्तो न संशयः।।"</note>

One who obtains the appropriate knowledge of Urdhvamnaya from the mouth of the Guru obtains liberation in this very life according to the mode of the Scriptures.

->O Goddess, he who knows such a tradition in its true essence is venerable, he is a true Guru, he is to be worshiped, he is an astrologer, and he is a master of mantras. (33)<-
<note>original: "आम्नायमीदृशं देवि विजानाति च तत्त्वतः। स वन्द्यः सद्गुरुः सोऽर्च्यः स दैवज्ञः स मान्त्रिकः।"</note>

->He is to be served, he is to be praised, he is to be seen, and he is full of <term>Sattva</term> <note>The quality of light, purity, and harmony</note>. He is the keeper of vows, the ascetic, the performer of rituals, and the worshiper. (34)<-
<note>original: "स सेव्यः स च संस्तुत्यः स द्रष्टव्यः स सात्त्विकः। स व्रती स तपस्वी च सोऽनुष्ठाता स पूजकः।"</note>

->He is a master of all sciences, including the Vedas, Agamas, and Shastras. He is the <term>Acharya</term> <note>The spiritual preceptor or teacher of conduct</note>, the wise one, the ascetic, and the <term>Kaulika</term> <note>A practitioner of the Kula path</note>. (35)<-
<note>original: "स वेदागमशास्त्रादिसर्वविद्याविशारदः। स आचार्यः स मतिमान् स यतिः स च कौलिकः।"</note>

->He is the sacrificer, the pure-souled, the chanter of mantras, and the practitioner. He is the <term>Yogi</term>, the one who has accomplished his goal, the hero, and the most excellent. (36)<-
<note>original: "स यज्वा स च पूतात्मा स जापी स च साधकः। स योगी स कृतार्थस्तु स वीरः स च उत्तमः।"</note>

->He is the virtuous soul, the all-knowing, the liberated, and indeed, he is <term>Shiva</term> <note>The supreme consciousness or Godhead</note> himself, O Beloved. (36)<-
<note>original: "स पुण्यात्मा स सर्वज्ञः स मुक्तः स शिवः प्रिये।।"</note>

Who knows thus the Amnayas in essence, O Devi, is:

<vocab>Urdhvamnaya: The highest or "Upper" stream of Tantric revelation; Kularnava Tantra: A primary text of the Kaula school of Tantra; Guru: A spiritual teacher; Agama: Traditional Tantric scriptures; Purana: Ancient mythological texts; Veda: The oldest Sanskrit scriptures; Jivanmukta: One liberated while alive; Kuleshvari: A title for the Goddess as mistress of the Kula path.</vocab>

<summary>This page emphasizes that the Urdhvamnaya (the highest spiritual tradition) cannot be learned through intellectual study or ritual alone, but only through the direct oral instruction of a qualified Guru. It concludes by describing the practitioner who possesses this knowledge as being equivalent to Lord Shiva himself, embodying all spiritual virtues and achieving liberation while alive.</summary>

<header>THIRD CHAPTER</header>
<note>original: "तृतीय उल्लासः"</note>

...venerable, a <term>Sadguru</term> <note>A true or realized spiritual teacher</note>, adorable, knower of the Deities and <term>Mantras</term> <note>Sacred sound-syllables</note>, deserves service and obeisance. He is worth seeing, of pure conduct, devout, ascetic, performer of religious rituals, a worshipper, scholar of all the sciences of <term>Vedas</term>, <term>Agamas</term> and <term>Shastras</term>, an <term>Acharya</term> <note>A spiritual preceptor or authority</note> and a <term>Kaulika</term> <note>One who follows the path of the 'Kula' or spiritual family</note>. He is a performer of sacrifices, purified in self, reciter of Mantras and a <term>Sadhaka</term> <note>A disciplined spiritual practitioner</note>. He is a <term>Yogi</term>, a satisfied person, a <term>Vira</term> <note>A 'heroic' practitioner who has conquered their passions</note> and the best. He is pious, all-knower, emancipated and himself <term>Shiva</term> <note>The Supreme Reality or the Auspicious One</note>.

> ->That family is made sacred, O Goddess; that mother is considered blessed.<-
> <note>original: "तत्कुलं पावनं देवि धन्या तज्जननी स्मृता।"</note>
> ->That father becomes successful in his goals, and his ancestors are liberated, my dear.<-
> <note>original: "तत्पिता च कृतार्थः स्यान्मुक्तास्तत्पितरः प्रिये।"</note>
> ->All born in his lineage are meritorious, and his friends and kinsmen are purified. (37)<-
> <note>original: "पुण्यास्तद्वंशजाः सर्वे पूतास्तन्मित्रबान्धवाः।।"</note>

His family is sacred; his mother, O Devi, is blessed; his father receives the fulfilment of all his desires and his forefathers are all liberated; even his entire lineage, fraternity and his friends are all purified.

> ->Why say more here regarding those devoted to the Upper Tradition?<-
> <note>original: "बहुनेह किमुक्तेन चोर्ध्वाम्नायपरस्य च।"</note>
> ->Remembering, singing praises, seeing, or even bowing to him,<-
> <note>original: "स्मरणं कीर्तनं वापि दर्शनं वन्दनं तथा।"</note>
> ->as well as conversing with him, produces a fruit greater than the Rajasuya sacrifice. (38)<-
> <note>original: "सम्भाषणञ्चकुरुते राजसूयाधिकं फलम्।।"</note>
> <note>Rajasuya: An ancient royal consecration ritual of immense power and complexity</note>
> ->Wherever he resides, O Goddess, there Prosperity and Victory shall be.<-
> <note>original: "स यत्र वसते देवि तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भवेत्।"</note>
> ->Health, abundance of food, good rainfall, and freedom from disturbances prevail there. (39)<-
> <note>original: "अनामयं सुभिक्षञ्च सुवृष्टिर्निरुपद्रवम्।।"</note>

### *Eulogy of the knower of the Upper Tradition:*
<note>original: "Urdhvāmnāya"</note>

Why to say much, one who remembers, sings eulogies, praises, sees and converses with the knower of the Upper Tradition obtains greater fruit than the performance of a <term>Rajasuya</term> sacrifice. Wherever such a person lives, there reside Goddess <term>Lakshmi</term> <note>The Goddess of wealth and prosperity</note> and victory. That place, rid of all diseases, becomes full of grains, receives good rainfall, is free of disturbances and peace reigns there.

> ->Therefore, that best of men who, by the grace of the Guru,<-
> <note>original: "तस्माद् गुरुप्रसादेन ऊर्ध्वाम्नायं नरोत्तमः।"</note>
> ->knows the Upper Tradition in its true essence, O Goddess, becomes most dear to Me. (40)<-
> <note>original: "यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतो देवि स मे प्रियतमो भवेत्।।"</note>

Therefore, that best of men, who knows the <term>Urdhvamnaya</term> by the Grace of the Guru, becomes, O Devi, My favourite.

> ->The Eastern Tradition is the form of Creation; the Southern is the form of Maintenance.<-
> <note>original: "पूर्वाम्नायः सृष्टिरूपः स्थितिरुपश्च दक्षिणः।"</note>
> ->The Western is Destruction, O Goddess; the Northern becomes Compassion/Grace. (41)<-
> <note>original: "संहारः पश्चिमो देवि उत्तरोऽनुग्रहो भवेत्।।"</note>

### *Distinction of the Traditions based on Creation, etc:*
<note>original: "Amnās"</note>

The Central Truth of the Eastern Tradition <note>original: "Purvāmnāya"</note> is <term>Srishti</term> (Creation), of the Southern <note>original: "Dakṣiṇa"</note> is maintenance (<term>Sthiti</term>), of the Western <note>original: "Paścima"</note> is Destruction (<term>Samhara</term>), and that of the Northern <note>original: "Uttara"</note> is Compassion (<term>Anugraha</term>).

<summary>This page describes the divine status of a Sadguru who knows the Urdhvamnaya, noting that their presence brings prosperity to the land and liberation to their entire lineage. It also categorizes the four cardinal spiritual traditions (Amnayas) by their cosmic functions: creation, maintenance, destruction, and grace.</summary>
