<header>IN THE KULARNAVA TANTRA</header>

->They know <term>Mantra Yoga</term> <note>The path of spiritual union through sacred sound</note> to be the Eastern tradition, and <term>Bhakti Yoga</term> <note>The path of devotion</note> the Southern;<-
->The Western is <term>Karma Yoga</term> <note>The path of selfless action</note>, and <term>Jnana Yoga</term> <note>The path of wisdom and knowledge</note> is the Northern. (42)<-
<note>original: "मन्त्रयोगं विदुः पूर्वं भक्तियोगश्च दक्षिणम्। पश्चिमं कर्मयोगश्च ज्ञानयोगं तथोत्तरम्।। ४२।।"</note>

### *Distinction of Traditions based on Paths:*

The Path of the East (<term>Purva</term>) is Mantra Yoga, the South (<term>Dakshina</term>) is Bhakti Yoga, the West (<term>Pashcima</term>) is Karma Yoga, and the North (<term>Uttara</term>) is Jnana Yoga.

->Twenty-four <term>Sanketas</term> <note>Principles or symbolic codes</note> are declared for the Eastern tradition;<-
->Twenty-five <term>Sanketas</term> are declared for the Southern tradition. (43)<-
<note>original: "पूर्वाम्नायस्य सङ्केताश्चतुर्विंशतिरीरिताः। दक्षिणाम्नायसङ्केताः पञ्चविंशतिरीरिताः।। ४३।।"</note>
->Thirty-two <term>Sanketas</term> are proclaimed for the Western tradition;<-
->Know that there are thirty-six <term>Sanketas</term> in the glorious Northern tradition. (44)<-
<note>original: "पश्चिमाम्नायसङ्केता द्वात्रिंशत् समुदाहृताः। विदुः षट्त्रिंशदाम्नाये सङ्केताः श्रीमदुत्तरे।। ४४।।"</note>

### *Distinction of Traditions based on the number of Principles:*

The principles of the <term>Purva-amnaya</term> <note>Eastern Tradition</note> are twenty-four, those of the <term>Dakshina-amnaya</term> <note>Southern Tradition</note> are twenty-five, those of the <term>Pashcima-amnaya</term> <note>Western Tradition</note> are said to be thirty-two, and know that those of the <term>Uttara-amnaya</term> <note>Northern Tradition</note> are thirty-six.

->O <term>Kulanayike</term> <note>Mistress of the Kula (spiritual family)</note>! None of these exist in the <term>Urdhvamnaya</term> <note>The Upper or Highest Tradition</note>;<-
->Because it is the direct form of <term>Shiva</term> <note>The Supreme Reality</note>, no ritual action remains within it. (45)<-
<note>original: "ऊर्द्ध्वाम्नायस्य चैतानि न सन्ति कुलनायिके। साक्षाच्छिवस्वरूपत्वान्न किञ्चित् कर्म विद्यते।। ४५।।"</note>

### *In the Upper Tradition there is an absence of all the above:*

O Mistress of the spiritual family! These [numerical divisions] do not exist in the Upper Tradition. Since it is essentially identical to Shiva himself, there is no need for the performance of rites or karmas.

->I alone know the greatness of the Upper Tradition, and no one else;<-
->Out of My love for You, You also know it—this is the truth, O <term>Varanane</term> <note>Beautiful-faced one</note>. (46)<-
->Thus have I told You the greatness of the Upper Tradition.<-
<note>original: "ऊर्द्ध्वाम्नायस्य माहात्म्यमहं वेद्मि न चापरः। मत्स्नेहात्त्वञ्च जानासि सत्यमेतद्वरानने।। ४६।। ऊर्द्ध्वाम्नायस्य माहात्म्यमिति ते कथितं मया।"</note>

O Beautiful-faced One! The glory of the Upper Tradition is known only to Me and no other. Because of My affection for You, You also know this truly. I have thus described to you the majesty of the Upper Tradition.

->In brief, O <term>Kuleshani</term> <note>Goddess of the Kula</note>, the greatness of the <term>Mantra</term> is now being told; (47)<-
->Before this, O <term>Parvati</term> <note>The Goddess, daughter of the mountains</note>, I have never spoken of this to anyone;<-
->I tell it to You out of love; listen, O Beloved of the <term>Mantrarnava</term> <note>The ocean of Mantras</note>. (48)<-
<note>original: "समासेन कुलेशानि मन्त्रमाहात्म्यमुच्यते।। ४७।। इतः पूर्वं मया नोक्तं यस्य कस्यापि पार्वति। तद्वदामि तव स्नेहाच्छृणु मन्त्राणवल्लभे।। ४८।।"</note>

### *Glory of the Holy Prasada-Para Mantra in the Form of Shiva-Shakti:*

O Goddess of the Kula! I am now telling You the Great Mantra. O Parvati! I have never before revealed this to anyone. Now, O Beloved of My Life, I am telling it only out of love; please listen.

It concludes with Shiva beginning to reveal a secret, "Great Mantra" to Parvati that has never been shared before.</summary>

<header>THIRD CHAPTER</header>

->The supreme <term>Prasada Mantra</term> <note>A foundational sacred sound, often identified with the Hamsa or "breath" mantra</note> presides over the <term>Urdhvamnaya</term> <note>The "Upper Tradition," regarded as the highest and most secret of the five or six spiritual directions</note>.<-
->This Mantra is the ultimate form of both of Us <note>The divine union of Shiva and Shakti</note>. One who realizes this is Shiva Himself. (49)<-
<note>original: "श्रीप्रासादपरमन्त्रमूर्ध्वाम्नायमधिष्ठितम्। आवयो: परमाकारं यो वेत्ति स स्वयं शिव:।। ४९।।"</note>

The *Śrī-Prāsāda-Parā* <note>The "Supreme Palace" mantra</note> (i.e., the <term>Hamsa Mantra</term>)¹ is the Mantra presiding over the Upper Tradition. This Mantra is the full form of Both of Us. One who knows it thus is Shiva Himself.

->From Shiva down to the smallest worm, within the breath-path of all living beings,<-
->This Mantra exists in the form of every exhalation and inhalation, O Beloved. (50)<-
<note>original: "शिवादिक्रिमपर्यन्तं प्राणिनां प्राणवर्त्मना। निश्वासोच्छ्वासरूपेण मन्त्रोऽयं वर्तते प्रिये।। ५०।।"</note>

*The whole world is inherent in this Prāsāda Mantra:*
From Shiva to a <term>Krimi</term> (the tiniest worm), all organisms keep on repeating this Mantra in the form of Expiration and Inspiration of breath.

->Just as clouds do not drift in the sky without the wind,<-
->So this world cannot exist without this <term>Para-Prasada Mantra</term>, O Beloved. (51)<-
<note>original: "अनिलेन विना मेघो यथाकाशे न वेहते। पराप्रासादमन्त्रेण विना लोकस्तथा प्रिये।। ५१।।"</note>

Just as clouds do not stay in the sky without wind, so this world cannot exist without this <term>Para-Prasada Mantra</term>.

->The entire mobile and immobile creation is woven through with the <term>Para-Prasada Mantra</term>.<-
->Essentially, the two are inseparable, O Goddess, just as the wind is to a hand-fan; (52)<-
->As the sprout is within the seed, oil within sesame, heat within fire, and radiance within the sun; (53)<-
->As moonlight is in the moon, fire in wood, fragrance in a flower, and liquidity in water;<-
->As meaning is in a word, <term>Shakti</term> <note>Divine Energy</note> is in Shiva, butter is in milk, and flavor is in a fruit; (54)<-
->As sweetness is in sugar, and coolness is in camphor;<-
->As the power of restraint or grace is in a mantra, and divinity is in a statue;<-
->As a reflection is in a mirror, and movement is in the breeze—<-
->In the same way, this entire universe is situated within the <term>Para-Prasada Mantra</term>. (55)<-
<note>original: "पराप्रासादमन्त्रेण स्यूतमेतच्चराचरम्... पराप्रासादमन्त्रेऽपि प्रपञ्चोऽयं तथा स्थित:।। ५२-५५।।"</note>

The whole mobile and immobile creation is pervaded by the <term>Para-Prasada Mantra</term>. Essentially the two are inseparable. Just like:

---

1. In this Mantra, the syllable *Ha* stands for <term>Shiva</term>, the <term>Purusha</term> or the Male Principle; *Sa* stands for <term>Shakti</term>, the <term>Prakriti</term>, or the Female Principle. Both together make creation and are so present in each form in creation. The outgoing breath, the expiration, sounds like *Ha* and incoming breath, the inspiration, sounds like *Sa*. This automatic repetition of *Ha-Sa* during the continuous movement of breathing of the <term>Jivas</term> <note>individual souls</note> is called <term>Ajapa Japa</term>, i.e., repetition without effort. It is said that the number of times during one day and night one repeats this <term>Hamsah Mantra</term> is 21,600. <note>original Sanskrit quote: "With the sound 'Ham' it goes out, with the sound 'Sah' it enters again. The individual soul always repeats this supreme mantra, Hamsa."</note> See also the *Niruttara Tantra* IV. 20 and the *Dhyanabindupanishad*, 61-64.

<summary>This page describes the Para-Prasada (Hamsa) Mantra as the supreme force presiding over the Upper Tradition, illustrating how it is biologically inherent in the breath of all living things and woven into the very fabric of the universe through a series of poetic analogies.</summary>

### CHAPTER THREE

Whoever, O <term>Maheshani</term> <note>Great Goddess; a title for Parvati</note>, knows the <term>Para-Prasada Mantra</term> <note>The "Supreme Palace" mantra, the core secret invocation of this lineage</note> received through proper <term>initiation</term> <note>original: "Diksha"</note> and according to the unbroken line of tradition, undoubtedly becomes Myself <note>Shiva is the speaker here</note>. (77)

All these fourteen worlds, along with every moving and unmoving being within them, always reside within the body of the one who knows the Supreme Palace Mantra. (78)

Wherever the knower of the Supreme Palace Mantra resides, O Goddess, that place and the entire area for ten <term>yojanas</term> <note>An ancient Indian measure of distance, roughly 8 to 9 miles or 13 kilometers</note> in every direction is declared to be a Divine Territory. (79)

O <term>Kulanayike</term> <note>Mistress of the Kula, or spiritual family/lineage</note>! Even the gods and demons worship the one who knows the essential truth and meaning of the Supreme Palace Mantra—what then need be said of mere human beings? (80)

O <term>Parvati</term> <note>The Goddess, daughter of the mountains</note>! Wherever the knower of the Supreme Palace Mantra stays is considered by the company of sages and gods to be my own <term>Siddha</term> place <note>A place of spiritual power or perfection</note>. (81)

**The knower of the Para-Prasada Mantra possesses the knowledge of all other mantras, such as those of Shiva:**
The knower of the Supreme Palace Mantra knows all the mantras belonging to the traditions of <term>Shaiva</term> <note>Followers of Shiva</note>, <term>Vaishnava</term> <note>Followers of Vishnu</note>, <term>Shakta</term> <note>Followers of the Goddess Durga</note>, <term>Saura</term> <note>Sun-worshippers</note>, <term>Ganapatya</term> <note>Followers of Ganesha</note>, and <term>Chandra</term> <note>Followers of the Moon</note>. (82)

**The Prasada-Para Mantra is the bestower of all fruits:**
On the tip of whose tongue the Holy Supreme Palace Mantra resides, by his mere sight even a <term>shvapacha</term> <note>Literally "one who cooks dogs," referring to those traditionally considered outside the social order</note> is liberated from worldly bondage. (83)

# THIRD CHAPTER

->This Para-Prasada mantra is the soul of all; therefore, it becomes the essence of everything. (61)<-

### The Para-Prasada Mantra is the Unity of All Forms

This Para-Prasada mantra <note>original: "parā-prāsāda-mantra"</note> is the unity of all forms:

O <term>Kuleshvari</term> <note>Mistress of the Kula, a title for the Goddess</note>! This Supreme Reality is formless, reachable only through the feeling of faith. It is the <term>Para Brahma</term> <note>the Absolute or Ultimate Reality</note>, devoid of parts, stainless, eternal, beyond all qualities, and like the infinite sky. (62)

It is the infinite, imperishable Truth, beyond the reach of mind and speech. The true meaning of this Para-Prasada mantra shines forth only through deep concentration. (63)

Therefore, O Goddess! This mantra is named <term>Para-Prasada</term> <note>literally "Supreme Palace" or "Supreme Grace"</note> because it is the very form of the Supreme Reality, characterized by <term>Sat, Cit, and Ananda</term> <note>Existence, Consciousness, and Bliss</note>. (64)

Because it consists of the union of <term>Shiva and Shakti</term> <note>the masculine and feminine principles of divinity</note>, it grants both worldly enjoyment and spiritual liberation. Though it appears involved in action, it is actionless; though it possesses attributes, it is beyond all attributes. (65)

This <term>Shri-Prasada-Para</term> mantra is the crest-jewel of all mantras. One who recites it undoubtedly obtains both <term>Bhukti</term> <note>material enjoyment</note> and <term>Mukti</term> <note>final liberation</note>. (66)

### Eulogy of the Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra

What is the use of speaking at length? Listen, O my Beloved! To the essence of all: there is no mantra equal to the Shri-Prasada-Para mantra. (67)

This alone is the supreme knowledge; this alone is the supreme penance.
This alone is the supreme meditation; this alone is the supreme worship. (68)

This alone is the supreme initiation; this alone is the supreme recitation.
This alone is the supreme Truth; this alone is the supreme vow. (69)

This alone is the supreme sacrifice; this alone is that which is higher than the highest.
This alone is the supreme good; this alone is the supreme fruit. (100) <note>Note: The verse numbering follows the original manuscript's jump from 69 to 100.</note>

This alone is the supreme <term>Brahman</term> <note>the Absolute</note>; this alone is the supreme goal.
This alone is the supreme secret; this is the truth, the truth, without a doubt.
O Dear One! Knowing this to be the best of mantras, one should always remain devoted to it. (101)

<summary>This page defines the Para-Prasada mantra as the formless, eternal Absolute (Brahman) that encompasses both worldly success and spiritual liberation. It concludes with a rhythmic series of verses declaring the mantra to be the ultimate substitute for all other religious rites and knowledge.</summary>

# THE KULARNAVA TANTRA

It is the essence of everything. There is no Mantra equal to the <term>Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra</term> <note>The "Supreme Mantra of Divine Grace," considered the core mantra of this lineage</note>. This is the Supreme Knowledge, this is supreme Austerity, this is supreme Concentration, this is supreme Worship, this is supreme Initiation, this is supreme Recitation (<term>Japa</term>), this is supreme Truth, this is supreme Observance (<term>Vrata</term>), this is supreme Sacrifice, this is supreme Beyond, this is supreme Blessedness; this is supreme Fruit, this is supreme Brahman <note>the ultimate reality</note>, this is supreme Goal, this is supreme Mystery, indubitably the Truth of Truths. Knowing it thus, men should always remain dedicated to it.

->Following the method laid down by the sacred traditions, and beginning with the prescribed order of worship,<-
->one should recite the Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra one hundred and eight times.<-
->By doing so, one is liberated from the five "great sins," including the killing of a priest. (102)<-

### *Method of Recitation of the Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra:*

Following the method laid down by the <term>Agamas</term> <note>the collection of authoritative tantric scriptures</note>, and beginning with the prescribed way of worship, one should recite this Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra one hundred and eight times. This provides liberation from the five great sins, including <term>Brahmanicide</term> <note>the sin of killing a Brahmin or a person of high spiritual knowledge</note>, and others.

->O Goddess, whoever recites the Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra two hundred times,<-
->is freed from the traces of actions accumulated across eighty-four hundred thousand types of births,<-
->including those from previous lives, whether in old age, youth, or childhood; and whether in the waking, dreaming, or deep sleep states.<-
->Whether committed through action, mind, or speech, and whether done with knowledge or in ignorance,<-
->one is liberated from the "great sins" and millions of "lesser sins." O Beautiful-Faced One! There is no doubt about this; it is the truth. (103–105)<-

One who recites it two hundred times becomes liberated from all groups of sins, whether committed by mind, action, or speech, either intentionally or unintentionally. This applies to sins from childhood, youth, and old age; during the states of waking, sleeping, and dreaming; and from all previous births within the <term>8,400,000 species</term> <note>In Indian cosmology, this is the total number of possible forms of life through which a soul can reincarnate</note>. O <term>Varanane</term> <note>original: "varānane," meaning "Beautiful-Faced One," an affectionate address to the Goddess</note>! There is no doubt about it.

->O Goddess, whoever recites the Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra three hundred times,<-
->attains the merit found in all ritual sacrifices and the rewards of all charitable acts,<-
->the holiness of all sacred vows and the benefits of visiting every holy pilgrimage site.<-
->One obtains all these rewards, O Goddess; there is no need for further deliberation on this. (106–107)<-

One who recites it three hundred times obtains the merits of all kinds of sacrifices, the fruits of all kinds of charities, the merits of all sacred vows (<term>Vratas</term>), and the rewards of visiting all sacred pilgrimage places. That one receives all these benefits is true, and there is no reason for a second thought about it.

<summary>This page details the transformative power of the Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra, asserting that specific counts of its recitation can purify a practitioner of even the most severe sins across lifetimes. It positions this single mantra as a comprehensive spiritual practice that yields the combined benefits of all other rituals, charities, and pilgrimages.</summary>

->The Holy Goddess said:<-

### The Holy Lord Said:

->Listen, O Goddess! I shall proclaim that which you have asked. By merely hearing it, one becomes identical in form to <term>Shiva</term>. (2)<-

**The Holy Lord said:**

Listen, O Goddess! I am telling you what you have asked. By merely hearing it, one takes on the form of the Divine.

->Prior to this, I have never revealed this mantra to anyone. Out of My love for You, I will speak it today. Listen, O Beloved of the Mantras. (3)<-

I have never told this Mantra to anyone prior to this moment. Out of My love for You, I will now tell it. O Beloved of My life, listen.

->Infinite-Moon-Abode <note>original: "Ananta-Candra-Bhuvana"</note> joined with the pair of Lunar-Dots <note>original: "Indu-Bindu-Yuga"</note>; this is the Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra, which bestows the fruits of both enjoyment and liberation. (4)<-

->O <term>Kuleshvari</term> <note>original: "Kuleśvarī"; Sovereign Goddess of the Kula</note>, the Supreme Grace Mantra <note>original: "Parā-prāsāda-mantra"</note> is said to begin with the letter 'Sa'.<-

*Extraction of the Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra:*

<note>Tantric texts often "hide" mantras in code. Here, "Infinite Moon" refers to the nasal sound (Nada-Bindu), "Abode" refers to the vowel 'Au', "Dot" refers to the letter 'Ha', and "Lunar-Dot Pair" refers to the letter 'Sa'.</note>

Infinite Moon Abode is the Nasal Sound ( ँ ), Abode is the vowel 'Au' ( ौ ), Dot is the letter 'Ha' ( ह ), and the Lunar-Dot Pair is the letter 'Sa' ( स ). Thus, the <term>Shri-Prasada-Para Mantra</term> is **Hsauṃ** ( ह्सौँ ). It is the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and spiritual emancipation. O Sovereign Goddess! The Supreme Grace Mantra is said to begin with 'Sa'—that is, it is **Shauṃ** ( सौँ ).

# In the Kularnava Tantra

->Because it is won over by a peaceful heart, because it defines well-known truths,<-
->because it pacifies past sins and destroys the suffering of those seeking refuge,<-
->and because it quickly bestows grace <note>original: "prasāda"</note>, it is called the **Prasada Mantra**. (6)<-

->**Word-meaning of the Grace (Prasada) Mantra:**<-

Being of the form of the **Bliss of Light** <note>original: "Prakāśānanda"</note>, due to yielding direct results, being captivated by a pleasant mind, due to explaining the famous meaning, due to pacifying former sins, due to destroying the pains of those who resort to it, and being pleased very soon, this Mantra has been called *Prasada* (Grace).

->Because it is the essence of the Supreme Truth, because it reveals the Supreme Self,<-
->because it generates Supreme Bliss and demonstrates the Supreme Dharma <note>the universal law or path</note>, (7)<-
->because it grants transcendental results and is the cause of supreme sovereignty,<-
->and because it is superior <note>original: "parattvāt"</note> to all other mantras, it is called the **Para Mantra** <note>The Supreme or "Beyond" Mantra</note>. (8)<-
->This is the **Kula Mantra**, O Goddess; now listen, I shall describe its **Nyasa** <note>the ritual placement of the mantra's sounds on the body</note> to you.<-

Being of the form of Truth Beyond, due to throwing light on the Self Beyond, due to providing the Bliss Beyond, due to expounding the Dharma Beyond, due to providing transcendental results, being the cause of Affluence Beyond, and being beyond comparison with other Mantras, this has been called the **Para** (Beyond) Mantra. This is the **Kula Mantra**. Now listen to its ritual placement.

->First, rising early in the morning, one should meditate upon the **Guru**. (9)<-
->Focusing the mind on the root-center <note>original: "kandamūla"; a psychic center at the base of the spine</note>, one should perform the calls of nature.<-
->Cleaning, washing the mouth, bathing, and performing the twilight prayers and offerings should follow. (10)<-
->In solitude, one should worship the entrance, remove the three types of obstacles <note>original: "vighnatraya"; typically categorized as divine, atmospheric, and terrestrial</note>,<-
->enter the place of worship, and take one’s proper seat. (11)<-

->**Delineation of Duties prior to Ritual Placement:**<-

First of all, rising in the morning, one should concentrate upon the Teacher. Then, after remembering the Kula-Mantra, one should relieve himself of nature's call etc. After that, washing of the mouth, bathing, morning prayer and presentation of libations of water <note>original: "arpanam"</note> should be done. Thereafter, performing the door-worship in an isolated manner and driving away all the three obstacles (Divine, atmospheric, and terrestrial), one should enter into the place of worship and occupy the proper seat.

# Fourth Chapter

->Meditation on the house of the Goddess’s worship, saluting Shiva and the Guru,<-

->Binding the directions, the two pairs of limbs, and the Mother-letters according to the rules,<-
->the ten-fold types of elements, the script called the Tortoise. (14)<-

After the ritual of Binding the Directions <note>original: "Digbandha"</note>, two rituals of placing sounds on the limbs <note>original: "Aṅga-nyāsas"</note>, and ten rituals involving the Mother-letters <note>original: "Mātrkā-nyāsas"</note> should be performed. These ten include: 
1. Internal placement of the Mother-letters; 
2-4. The three external placements (representing the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe); 
5. The placement of the Arts <note>original: "Kalā"</note>; 
6. The placement of the "Illustrious Neck" <note>original: "Srīkaṇṭha"</note>; 
7. The placement of Krishna <note>original: "Keśava"</note>; 
8-10. The placements of the seed-syllables of Modesty <note>original: "Lajjā"</note>, Fortune <note>original: "Ramā"</note>, and Desire <note>original: "Kāma"</note>. 

After that, the ritual placement of the Sages and others for the **Mantra of the Supreme Grace-Palace** <note>original: "Śrī-parā-prāsāda Mantra"</note> should be performed.

->The Sage of this is the Supreme Shambhu, the Meter is the Unmanifest,<-
->and the Deity here is the Supreme Goddess of All Mantras. (15)<-

->The root joined with the three long vowels is the Seed, the Power, and the Stake.<-
->With the root seed joined with the six long vowels, perform the six-limbed ritual, O Daughter of the Mountain! (16)<-

**Ritual Placement of the Sages for the Mantra of the Supreme Grace-Palace:**

O Daughter of the Mountain <note>original: "Pārvati"</note>! The Sage <note>the ancestral seer</note> of this Mantra is the Supreme Shambhu <note>Shiva</note>, the poetic Meter is the Unmanifest <note>original: "Avyaktā"</note>, and the Deity is the Supreme Goddess of All Mantras. The Seed <note>original: "Bīja"</note>, the Power <note>original: "Śakti"</note>, and the Stake <note>original: "Kīlaka," the pin that unlocks the mantra</note> are the Root Seed-syllables combined with three long vowels (namely: Seed: *Hsam*; Power: *Hsim Shim*; Stake: *Hsum Shum*). Thereafter, the ritual placement on the six limbs <note>original: "Ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa"</note> should be performed using the Root Seed-syllables with long vowels.

**The Ritual Application <note>original: "Viniyoga"</note>:** Om. Of this, the mantra of the Supreme Grace-Palace, the Sage is the Supreme Shambhu; the Meter is the Unmanifest Gayatri; the Deity is the Supreme Goddess of All Mantras; the Seed is *Hsam Snham*; the Power is *Hsim Snhim*; the Stake is *Hsum Snhum*. This application is performed for the purpose of attaining the grace of the Supreme Goddess of All Mantras.

**Placement of the Sage and Others <note>original: "Ṛṣyādi-nyāsa"</note>:**
To the Sage Supreme Shambhu, salutations (touching) the head. 
To the Meter Unmanifest Gayatri, salutations (touching) the mouth. 
To the Deity Supreme Goddess of All Mantras, salutations (touching) the heart. 
To the Seed *Hsam Snham*, salutations (touching) the genitals. 
To the Power *Hsim Snhim*, salutations (touching) the navel. 
To the Stake *Hsum Snhum*, salutations (touching) the phallus. 
To the application for the purpose of attaining the grace of the Supreme Goddess of All Mantras, salutations (touching) the two feet.

**Ritual Placement in the Hands:** <note>original: "Karanyāsa"</note>
With the seed-sounds *Hrām Hrām*, homage to the two thumbs. 
With the seed-sounds *Hrīm Hrīm*, homage to the two forefingers. 
With the seed-sounds *Hrūm Hrūm*, homage to the two middle fingers. 
With the seed-sounds *Hraim Hraim*, homage to the two ring fingers. 
With the seed-sounds *Hraum Hraum*, homage to the two little fingers. 
With the seed-sounds *Hasaḥ Hraḥ*, homage to the two palms and the backs of the hands.

**Ritual Placement in the Six Limbs:** <note>original: "Ṣaḍaṅganyāsa"</note>
With the seed-sounds *Hrām Hrām*, homage to the heart. 
With the seed-sounds *Hrīm Hrīm*, may the offering go to the head. 
With the seed-sounds *Hrūm Hrūm*, may the offering go to the topknot <note>original: "śikhā"</note>. 
With the seed-sounds *Hraim Hraim*, to the armor <note>symbolized by the shoulders</note> of the soul. 
With the seed-sounds *Hraum Hraum*, to the three eyes <note>the two physical eyes and the eye of wisdom</note>. 
With the seed-sounds *Hasaḥ Hraḥ*, to the "weapon" <note>original: "astra," a protective gesture made by snapping fingers</note>.

->One should place the forms of the five aspects of Shiva: Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Sadyojāta, and the Self,<-
->first into the five fingers, and then place those forms upon the faces of the deity. (17)<-
->One should perform the placement of the limbs into the five sacred powers <term>Brahmans: the five primary manifestations of Shiva</term> in the same way.<-
->Beginning with the Power of the Foundation <note>original: "Ādhāra-śakti"</note> and ending with the Mantra of the Seat, O Mother! (18)<-
->O Queen of the Kula! One should perform the "Minor Six-fold Placement" according to the path previously described.<-

*The Minor Six-fold Placement:* <note>original: "Alpa-ṣoḍhā-nyāsa"</note>

O Mother <note>original: "Ambikā"</note>! The ritual placement <note>original: "Nyāsa"</note> using the five fingers should be performed for the five aspects of Shiva: the Lord <note>Īśāna</note>, the Supreme Person <note>Tatpuruṣa</note>, the Non-Terrifying <note>Aghora</note>, the Quickly-Born <note>Sadyojāta</note>, and the Self <note>Ātmā</note>. Similarly, this placement should be performed respectively on the crown of the head, the face, the heart, the private region, and the feet <note>original: "pāda-deśa"</note> using the five fingers starting with the thumb. These placements should begin with the Power of the Foundation and conclude with the Seat-Mantra. Thus, O Queen of the Kula! one should perform the Minor Six-fold Placement.

The whole process should be as follows:

**Placement of the Forms:** <note>original: "Mūrtinyāsa"</note>
*Om Aim Hrīm Śrīm Hraum Hraum Hroḥ* — Homage to the Lord <note>Īśāna</note> — on the two thumbs. 
*Om* [repeated six times] *Haim* — Homage to the Supreme Person <note>Tatpuruṣa</note> — on the two forefingers. 
*Om* [six times] *Hum* — Homage to the Non-Terrifying <note>Aghora</note> — on the two middle fingers. 
*Om* [six times] *Him* — Homage to the Beautiful Deity <note>Vāmadeva</note> — on the two ring fingers. 
*Om* [six times] *Ham* — Homage to the Quickly-Born <note>Sadyojāta</note> — on the two little fingers.

Similarly, one should perform this placement on the crown, face, heart, private region, and feet with the thumb and other fingers.

Thereafter, in the same order, the ritual placement should be performed in the directions of the faces: Upward, Front, South, North, and West, using the thumb and other fingers.

After that, the Six-Limb Placement should be performed with the syllables *Hsām Hsīm* etc., and then again with the syllables *Shām Shīm* etc.

Then, the Six-Limb Placement should be performed in the following manner:

*Om Aim Hrīm Śrīm Hraum Hraum* — Homage to the All-Knowing <note>original: "Sarvajña"</note> — on the two thumbs. 
*Om* [six times] — To the Nectar-like, Garlanded with Radiance, and Eternally Content — homage on the two forefingers. 
*Om* [six times] — To the head of Brahma; may the offering go to the blazing fire of the topknot; homage to the Eternal Knowledge — on the two middle fingers. 
*Om* [six times] — To the Wielder of the Thunderbolt, with the Thunderbolt in hand, to the Independent One — homage on the two ring fingers. 
*Om* [six times] *Saum Vīm Haum* — Homage to the One whose Power is Eternally Undiminished — on the two little fingers. 
*Om* [six times] *Śrīm Śrīm* — To the bound soul <note>original: "paśu"</note>, may the weapon strike, homage to the One of Infinite Power — on the two palms.

# In the Kulārṇava Tantra

### *The Great Sixteenfold Ritual Placement:*

Now, for the attainment <term>Siddhi: spiritual perfection or success in ritual</term> of the divine state <term>Devatā-bhāva: the internal realization of one's own divinity</term>, one should perform the Great Sixteenfold Ritual Placement <term>Mahā-ṣoḍhā-nyāsa: a practice of "depositing" sixteen categories of sacred energy into the body</term> according to the rules. This Ritual Placement should not be shared with just anyone. I am revealing it to You out of My love for You. This Ritual Placement should be performed with respect to: 1. The Phenomenal World <note>original: "Prapañca"</note>; 2. The Worlds <note>original: "Bhuvana"</note>; 3. The Divine Form <note>original: "Murti"</note>; 4. The Sacred Sound <note>original: "Mantra"</note>; 5. The Deity <note>original: "Daivata"</note>; and 6. The Mother-Letters <note>original: "Mātṛkā"</note>. In relation to these, this Great Sixteenfold Ritual Placement is the highest of all such practices.

### *The Ritual Placement of the Phenomenal World*

O Supreme Goddess <note>original: "Parameśāni"</note>! First of all, I am telling You the Ritual Placement of the Phenomenal World <note>original: "Prapañca Nyāsa"</note>. This should be performed for the various forms of the Goddess Lakshmi—Fortune, Illusion, the Lotus-One, the Beloved of Vishnu, She who holds the Lotus, Daughter of the Ocean, Mother of the World, Dweller in the Lotus, Indira, Illusion, Rama, Padma, Beloved of Narayana, Siddha-Lakshmi, Raja-Lakshmi, and Maha-Lakshmi—corresponding respectively to the sixteen categories: the physical world, islands, oceans, mountains, cities, sacred seats, fields, forests, hermitages, caves, rivers, crossroads <note>Note: The Sanskrit 'gahvara' or 'catvara' refers to clearings or squares</note>, those born of seeds, those born of sweat, those born of eggs, and those born of the womb. These Powers <note>original: "Śaktis"</note> are the presiding Deities of the Vowels <note>original: "Svaras"</note> in this Ritual Placement.

In the beginning of each of the following Prayers <note>original: "Mantra"</note>, the seed sounds *Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsauṃ* <note>These are "Bija" or seed-mantras representing various divine energies like wisdom, power, and prosperity</note> and at the end of each, *Srhouṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ* should invariably be added.

**Aṃ** <note>original: "अं"</note>: To the Goddess of Fortune <note>original: "Śriyai"</note> in the form of the manifested world, homage; **at the head.** 
**Āṃ** <note>original: "आं"</note>: To the Goddess of Illusion <note>original: "Māyāyai"</note> in the form of the islands, homage; **at the circle of the face.** 
**Iṃ** <note>original: "इं"</note>: To the Lotus-One in the form of the oceans, homage; **at the right eye.** 
**Īṃ** <note>original: "ईं"</note>: To the Beloved of Vishnu in the form of the mountains, homage; **at the left eye.** 
**Uṃ** <note>original: "उं"</note>: To the Holder of the Lotus in the form of the cities, homage; **at the right ear.** 
**Ūṃ** <note>original: "ऊं"</note>: To the Daughter of the Ocean in the form of the sacred seats, homage; **at the left ear.** 
**Ṛṃ** <note>original: "ऋं"</note>: To the Mother of the World in the form of the sacred fields, homage; **at the right nostril.** 
**Ṝṃ** <note>original: "ॠं"</note>: To the Dweller in the Lotus in the form of the forests, homage; **at the left nostril.** 
**Lṛṃ** <note>original: "लृं"</note>: To Indira in the form of the hermitages, homage; **at the right cheek.** 
**Lṝṃ** <note>original: "लॄं"</note>: To the Goddess of Illusion in the form of the caves, homage; **at the left cheek.** 
**Eṃ** <note>original: "एं"</note>: To Rama in the form of the rivers, homage; **at the upper lip.** 
**Aiṃ** <note>original: "ऐं"</note>: To Padma in the form of the crossroads, homage; **at the lower lip.** 
**Oṃ** <note>original: "ओं"</note>: To the Beloved of Narayana in the form of plant life <note>original: "Udbhija" (born of seeds/sprouting)</note>, homage; **at the upper row of teeth.** 
**Auṃ** <note>original: "औं"</note>: To Siddha-Lakshmi in the form of those born of sweat <note>Referring to insects or small organisms believed to arise from heat and moisture</note>, homage; **at the lower row of teeth.** 
**Aṃ** <note>original: "अं"</note>: To Raja-Lakshmi in the form of those born of eggs, homage; **at the root of the tongue.** 
**Aḥ** <note>original: "अः"</note>: To Maha-Lakshmi in the form of those born of the womb, homage; **at the tip of the tongue.**

The Ritual Placement <term>Nyāsa: the practice of "placing" or "depositing" sacred syllables and deities into specific parts of the body to sanctify it</term> in the different parts of the body should be performed with the consonants Ka to Ma. Here the Presiding Deities Āryā, Umā, Caṇḍikā, Durgā, Śivā, Aparṇā, Ambikā, Satī, Īśvarī, Śāmbhavī, Īśānī, Pārvatī, Sarvamaṅgalā, Dākṣāyaṇī, Haimavatī, Mahāmāyā, Maheśvarī, Mṛḍānī, Rudrāṇī, Sarvāṇī, Parameśvarī, Kālī, Kātyāyanī, Gaurī and Bhavānī [take] the forms of Moment, Split-second, Fraction, Minute fraction, Blink, Breath, 24-minute period, 48-minute period, Three-hour watch, Day, Twilight, Night, Lunar day, Weekday, Lunar mansion, Astrological union, Half-lunar day, Fortnight, Month, Zodiac sign, Season, Half-year, Year, Eon and Dissolution respectively. These are twenty-five in number. Their Ritual Placement should be performed according to the rules, from the root of the right arm to the heart.

The specific sounds and the bodily parts in which the "Placement" has to be performed are as follows. However, the syllables *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsauḥ* <note>original: "Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Hsauḥ"; these are seed-syllables (bīja-mantras) representing the Goddess and the power of the Self</note> should invariably be added at the beginning of each of these formulas.

*Aṃ Āṃ I*: To the Mother Goddess who is the Power of the Support <note>original: "Adhāra-śakty-ambā-devyai"</note>, joined with a billion deities known as the "Secret Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Atala** <term>Atala: the first of the seven lower worlds</term>, I bow; this is placed on the **feet**.

*Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ*: To the Mother Goddess of Infinite Power, joined with a billion deities known as the "More Secret Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Vitala**, I bow; this is placed on the **ankles**.

*Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Lṛṃ*: To the Mother Goddess of Inconceivable Power, joined with a billion deities known as the "Highly Secret Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Sutala**, I bow; this is placed on the **shanks**.

*Lṛṃ Eṃ Aiṃ*: To the Mother Goddess of Independence, joined with a billion deities known as the "Greatly Secret Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Mahātala**, I bow; this is placed on the **knees**.

*Oṃ Auṃ*: To the Mother Goddess of the Supreme Secret Will, joined with a billion deities known as the "Mystery Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Talātala**, I bow; this is placed on the **thighs**.

*Aṃ Aḥ*: To the Mother Goddess of Knowledge, joined with a billion deities known as the "Mystery Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Rasātala**, I bow; this is placed in the **genital region**.

The five letters starting with *Ka* <note>The consonants ka, kha, ga, gha, and ṅa</note>: To the Mother Goddess of Action, joined with a billion deities known as the "Most-Secret-of-Mysteries Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Pātāla**, I bow; this is placed in the **Root Center** <term>Mūlādhāra: the chakra at the base of the spine</term>.

The five letters starting with *Ca*: To the Mother Goddess Ḍākinī, joined with a billion deities known as the "Highly Secret Yoginis" who dwell in the world of the **Earth** <term>Bhūrloka: the physical plane</term>, I bow; this is placed in the **Self-Base Center** <term>Svādhiṣṭhāna: the sacral chakra</term>.

The five letters starting with *Ṭa*: To the Mother Goddess Rākinī, joined with a billion deities known as the "Great-Mystery Yoginis" who dwell in the world of the **Atmosphere** <term>Bhuvarloka</term>, I bow; this is placed in the **navel**.

The five letters starting with *Ta*: To the Mother Goddess Lākinī, joined with a billion deities known as the "Supreme-Mystery Yoginis" who dwell in the world of the **Heavens** <term>Svarloka</term>, I bow; this is placed in the **heart**.

The five letters starting with *Pa*: To the Mother Goddess Kākinī, joined with a billion deities known as the "Hidden Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Maharloka** <term>the fourth of the seven upper worlds</term>, I bow; this is placed at the **root of the palate**.

The four letters starting with *Ya*: To the Mother Goddess Śākinī, joined with a billion deities known as the "Hidden-Wandering Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Janaloka**, I bow; this is placed in the **Command Center** <term>Ājñā: the "third eye" between the eyebrows</term>.

The four letters starting with *Śa*: To the Mother Goddess Hākinī, joined with a billion deities known as the "Highly Hidden Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Tapoloka**, I bow; this is placed on the **forehead**.

*Laṃ Kṣaṃ*: To the Mother Goddess Yākinī, joined with a billion deities known as the "Greatly Hidden Yoginis" who dwell in the world of **Satyaloka** <term>the highest spiritual plane</term>, I bow; this is placed at the **Opening of Brahma** <term>Brahmarandhra: the crown of the head</term>.

*Aṃ* [through] *Kṣaṃ*: To the Supreme Mother Goddess, the sovereign of the fourteen worlds, I bow; this is a pervasive placement across **all the limbs of the body**.

> Having thus performed the Placement of the Planes, one should then perform the Placement of the Forms <term>Mūrti-nyāsa</term>.
> The forms are: Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, Govinda, and Viṣṇu; [52]
>
> Madhusūdana, Trivikrama, and the two known as Vāmana and
> Śrīdhara; as well as Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha, and Dāmodara;
> Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha. [53]
> <note>These are the sixteen traditional names and forms of the god Viṣṇu used in purification rituals</note>
>
> Akṣotkā, Indrāṇī, Iśānī, Ugrā, Dhanayanā,
> Ṛddhi, Rūpiṇī, Lṛkā, the leader who is the sole guide for faults, [54]
>
> Aiṣariṇī, Oghavatī, she who has the radiance of all desires,
> and she who wears a garland of bones—these are declared to be the Vowel-Deities. [55]
>
> Bhava, Śarva, Rudra, Paśupati, and Ugra;
> Mahādeva, Bhīma, Īśāna, and the one called Tatpuruṣa;
>
> Aghora, Sadyojāta, and Vāmadeva—these are the ones spoken of. [56]
> <note>These represent the various aspects of the god Śiva, often associated with the elements and directions</note>

# Fourth Chapter

Karabhadrā, Khagacalā, and she who grants the fruit of powers like Garimā <note>original: "Garimādiphalapradā"; Garimā is the yogic power of becoming infinitely heavy</note>;
Ghaṇṭādharā, the fierce-eyed Ugranayanā, and then Candradhartrī (Bearer of the Moon);
The goddess composed of meters, Chandomayī, she who abides in the universe, Jagatsthānā, and then Jvalattārā (Blazing Star); || 57 ||
She who bestows wisdom, Jñānadā, she who holds the chisel, Taṅkadharā, and Dhṛti (Fortitude)—these are said to be the twelve.
These are the presiding deities of the letters starting from *Ka* and *Bha* and ending with *Ṭha* and *Ḍa*. || 58 ||
Brahmā, Prajāpati, Vedhās, Parameṣṭhī, Pitāmaha (the Grandfather),
Vidhātā, Viriñci, Sraṣṭā (the Creator), and Caturānana (the Four-Faced);
Including Hiraṇyagarbha, these are said to be the ten forms of Brahmā in order. || 59 ||
Yakṣiṇī, Rañjinī, Lakṣmī, Vajriṇī, Śaśidhāriṇī (Bearer of the Moon),
Dhaḍādhāralayā, Sarvanāyikā (the Universal Leader), Hasitānanā (Smiling-Faced),
Lalitā, and Kṣamā (Patience)—these are the deities of the letters beginning with *Ya*. || 60 ||
At the end of the root mantra and the three sacred sounds <note>original: "tritāra"; referring to the three bīja mantras Om, Hrīṃ, Śrīṃ</note>, one should place the vowels and the Viṣṇus along with their respective Powers <term>Śakti: the feminine creative energy of a deity</term>.
Using the fourth case <term>Dative case: the grammatical form used for "salutations to..."</term> and the word "Namah" (salutation), one should place them on the **head** and the **face**. || 61 ||
O Supreme Goddess, one should then place them on the **shoulders, sides, waist, thighs, knees, shanks, and feet**,
moving from the right side across to the left. || 62 ||
The practitioner should place the forms of Śiva <note>original: "Bhavādīn"; referring to Bhava and other aspects of Śiva</note> together with their Powers, joined with the letters starting with *Ka* and *Bha*,
on the **feet, sides, arms, neck, and the five faces**.
One should place Brahmā and the others, joined with the Powers of the *Ya* group, upon the **ten supports**. || 63 ||
At the end of the root mantra and the three sacred sounds, one should say "The Mother Goddess of the Three Forms" <note>original: "Śrī-trimūrty-ambikā"</note>.
With the word "Namah," one should perform the "pervasive placement" <term>Vyāpaka Nyāsa: a ritual gesture where the hands pass over the entire body to distribute divine energy</term> to the Primal Mother Goddess.

After performing the Placement of the Spheres <term>Bhuvana Nyāsa</term> in the aforesaid manner one should perform the Placement of the Forms <term>Mūrti Nyāsa</term>. The formula for each Placement and the parts of the body where the Placement is to be performed should be as follows. Here also, *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsauḥ* should be prefixed to each of the Mantras.

*Aṃ*: Salutations to Keśava and Akṣara-Śakti; on the **forehead**.
*Āṃ*: Salutations to Nārāyaṇa and the First Power; on the **right side of the face**.

*Ṛṃ*: Salutations to Trivikrama and Ṛddhi (Prosperity); on the **right shank**.
*Ṝṃ*: Salutations to Vāmana and Rūpiṇī; on the **right foot**.
*Lṛṃ*: Salutations to Śrīdhara and Luptā; on the **left foot**.
*Lṝṃ*: Salutations to Hṛṣīkeśa and Lūnadoṣā (Destroyer of Blemishes); on the **left shank**.
*Eṃ*: Salutations to Padmanābha and Ekanāyikā (Sole Leader); on the **left knee**.
*Aiṃ*: Salutations to Dāmodara and Aiṅkāriṇī; on the **left thigh**.
*Oṃ*: Salutations to Vāsudeva and Odhavatī; on the **left side of the torso**.
*Auṃ*: Salutations to Saṅkarṣaṇa and Sarvakāmā (All-Desiring); on the **left shoulder**.
*Aṃ*: Salutations to Pradyumna and Añjaprabhā; on the **left side of the face**.
*Aḥ*: Salutations to Aniruddha and Asthimālā-dharā (Bearer of the Bone-Garland); on the **left side of the head**.
*Ka* and *Bha*: Salutations to Bhava and Karabhadrā; on the **right foot**.
*Kha* and *Ba*: Salutations to Śarva and Khagabalā; on the **left foot**.
*Ga* and *Pha*: Salutations to Rudra and she who grants the fruit of powers like Garimā; on the **right side**.
*Gha* and *Pa*: Salutations to Paśupati and the Pacifier of Dharma; on the **left side**.

*Cha* and *Da*: Salutations to Bhīma and she who is composed of meters; on the **neck**.
*Ja* and *Tha*: Salutations to Īśāna and the Abiding-Place of the Universe; on the **upward face**.

# In the Kularnava Tantra

*Taṃ*: Salutations to the "Supreme Person" (Tatpuruṣa) and the "Blazing Star" (Jvalattārā) in the **eastern face**.
*Jaṃ* and *Ṇaṃ*: Salutations to the "Fearless One" (Aghora) and the "Giver of the Fruit of Wisdom" (Jñānaphalapradā) in the **southern face**.
*Ṭaṃ* and *Ḍhaṃ*: Salutations to the "Born-at-Once" (Sadyojāta) and the "Bearer of the Chisel" (Taṅkadharā) in the **western face**.
*Ṭhaṃ* and *Ḍaṃ*: Salutations to the "Handsome Lord" (Vāmadeva) and the "Terrifying Sounding One" (Ṭaṅkāra-Ḍāmarī) in the **northern face**.

*Yaṃ*: Salutations to Brahmā and the Yakṣiṇī <note>A class of nature spirits or minor goddesses associated here with the creative force</note> in the **root center** (Mūlādhāra).
*Raṃ*: Salutations to the "Lord of Progeny" (Prajāpati) and the "Delighting One" (Rañjinī) in the **sacral center** (Svādhiṣṭhāna).
*Laṃ*: Salutations to the "Creator" (Vedhās) and Lakṣmī in the **navel center** (Maṇipūra).
*Vaṃ*: Salutations to the "Supreme Abode" (Parameṣṭhī) and the "Wielder of the Thunderbolt" (Vajriṇī) in the **heart center** (Anāhata).
*Śaṃ*: Salutations to the "Grandfather" (Pitāmaha) and the "Bearer of the Moon" (Śaśidhāriṇī) in the **throat center** (Viśuddhi).
*Ṣaṃ*: Salutations to the "Ordainer" (Vidhātṛ) and the "Six-fold Support" (Ṣaḍādhārā) in the **third eye center** (Ājñā).
*Saṃ*: Salutations to the "Creator" (Viriñci) and the "Universal Leader" (Sarvanāyikā) in the **moon center** (Indu).
*Haṃ*: Salutations to the "Creator" (Sraṣṭṛ) and the "Smiling-faced One" (Hasitānanā) in the **point center** (Bindu).
*Laṃ*: Salutations to the "Four-faced One" (Caturānana) and the "Playful One" (Lalitā) in the **sound center** (Nāda).
*Kṣaṃ*: Salutations to the "Golden Womb" (Hiraṇyagarbha) and "Patience" (Kṣamā) in the **end-of-sound center** (Nādānta).

From *Aṃ* to *Kṣaṃ*: Salutations to the Supreme Mother Goddess (Parāmbā Devī), whose nature is the Triple Form <note>The Trimūrti: the union of Hari (Viṣṇu), Hara (Śiva), and Brahmā</note>, pervading **all the limbs**.

> Having performed the placement of the forms (*Mūrti Nyāsa*) in this way, one should then perform the placement of the mantras (*Mantra Nyāsa*). || 64 ||
>
> The root of the three sacred sounds <note>Tritāra: likely the syllables Om, Hrīṃ, and Śrīṃ</note>, from *Aṃ*, *Āṃ*, to *Iṃ*, numbering one hundred thousand and ten million;
> With various distinctions starting from the single-syllabled soul of all mantras. || 65 ||
>
> Then, for the presiding deity, let there be the "Giver of All Fruits."
> One should say: "Salutations to the Supreme Mother Goddess, the Lady of the Single Peak" <note>Ekakūṭeśvarī; 'Kūṭa' refers to a group of secret syllables in a mantra</note>. || 66 ||
>
> With *Īṃ*, *Uṃ*, *Ūṃ* etc., and the "Swan" (Haṃsa) etc., is the "Double Peak," as before.
> With *Ṛṃ*, *Ṝṃ*, *Lṛṃ* etc., and the "Fire" (Agni) etc., is the "Triple Peak," as before. || 67 ||
>
> With *Lṝṃ*, *Eṃ*, *Aiṃ*, and the "Moon" (Candra) etc., is the "Four-fold Peak," as before.
> With *Oṃ*, *Auṃ*, *Aṃ*, *Aḥ*, and the "Sun" (Sūrya) etc., is the "Five-fold Peak," as before. || 68 ||
>
> With *Kaṃ*, *Khaṃ*, *Gaṃ*, and "Skanda" (the god of war) etc., is the "Six-fold Peak," as before.
> With *Ghaṃ*, *Ṅaṃ*, *Caṃ*, and "Gaṇeśa" (the remover of obstacles) etc., is the "Seven-fold Peak," as before. || 69 ||
>
> With *Chaṃ*, *Jaṃ*, *Jhaṃ*, and "Vaṭuka" (the youthful form of Bhairava) etc., is the "Eight-fold Peak," as before.
> With *Ñaṃ*, *Ṭaṃ*, *Ṭhaṃ*, and "Brahmā" etc., is the "Nine-fold Peak," as before. || 70 ||
>
> With *Ḍaṃ*, *Ḍhaṃ*, *Ṅaṃ*, and "Viṣṇu" etc., is the "Ten-fold Peak," as before.
> With *Taṃ*, *Thaṃ*, *Daṃ*, and "Rudra" (the fierce form of Śiva) etc., is the "Eleven-fold Peak," as before. || 71 ||
>
> With *Dhaṃ*, *Naṃ*, *Paṃ*, and "Vāṇī" (Sarasvatī) etc., is the "Twelve-fold Peak," as before.
> With *Phaṃ*, *Baṃ*, *Bhaṃ*, and "Lakṣmī" etc., is the "Thirteen-fold Peak," as before. || 72 ||
>
> With *Maṃ*, *Yaṃ*, *Raṃ*, and "Gaurī" etc., is the "Fourteen-fold Peak," as before.
> With *Laṃ*, *Vaṃ*, *Śaṃ*, and "Durgā" etc., is the "Fifteen-fold Peak," as before.
> With *Ṣaṃ*, *Saṃ*, *Haṃ*, *Laṃ*, *Kṣaṃ*, and "Tripurā" etc., is the "Sixteen-fold Peak." || 73 ||
>
> To the presiding deity of all the mantras composed of these letters;
> And to the Mother Goddess, the Lady of the Sixteen Peaks, the "Giver of All Fruits." || 74 ||
>
> Salutations to the Mother Goddess. Thus is the placement of the mantras (*Mantra Nyāsa*) declared, O Great Goddess.
> In the root, the genitals, the navel, the heart, the throat, and in the two eyes; || 75 ||
>
> In the "Awakener" (Nibodhikā), the "Half-moon," the "Point" (Bindu), and in the "Level of Arts" (Kalāpada);
> In the "Beyond-Mind" (Unmanā), the "Mouth of Viṣṇu," the "Sound" (Nāda), and the "End of Sound" (Nādānta);
> And in the "Region of the North Star" (Dhruva-maṇḍala), one should place these, O Leader of the Kula. || 76 ||
>
> At the end of the root mantra of the three sacred sounds, with the phrase "The Soul of All Mantras,"
> One should place the Supreme Mother Goddess, pervading the **heart**. || 77 ||

# Fourth Chapter

### *Sacred Placement of Mantras (Mantra Nyāsa):*

After the Placement of the Forms (Murti Nyāsa) is complete, the Sacred Placement of Mantras (Mantra Nyāsa) should be performed next in the following manner. Here also, the seed syllables <note>original: "Bīja Mantras"</note> *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsauḥ* should be prefixed to each Mantra.

**Aṃ, Āṃ, Iṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the single-syllable mantra <term>Praṇava; the sacred sound Om</term>, existing in one trillion <note>original: "eka-lakṣa-koṭi," literally one hundred thousand times ten million</note> variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Single Peak. Placement: **Root center** (Mūlādhāra).

**Īṃ, Uṃ, Ūṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the two-syllable mantra beginning with *Haṃsa* <note>The "Swan" mantra representing the breath</note>, existing in two trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Double Peak. Placement: **Generative center** (Liṅga).

**Ṛṃ, Ṝṃ, Lṛṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the three-syllable mantra beginning with *Vahni* <note>Fire</note>, existing in three trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Triple Peak. Placement: **Navel center** (Nābhi).

**ॡं, Eṃ, Aiṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the four-syllable mantra beginning with *Candra* <note>The Moon</note>, existing in four trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Quadruple Peak. Placement: **Heart center** (Hṛdaya).

**Oṃ, Auṃ, Aṃ, Aḥ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the five-syllable mantra beginning with *Sūrya* <note>The Sun</note>, existing in five trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Quintuple Peak. Placement: **Throat center** (Kaṇṭha).

**Kaṃ, Khaṃ, Gaṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the six-syllable mantra beginning with *Skanda* <note>The deity of war and son of Shiva</note>, existing in six trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Sextuple Peak. Placement: **Mouth** (Mukhe).

**Ghaṃ, Ṅaṃ, Caṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the seven-syllable mantra beginning with *Gaṇeśa*, existing in seven trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Septuple Peak. Placement: **Eyes** (Netrayoḥ).

**Chaṃ, Jaṃ, Jhaṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the eight-syllable mantra beginning with *Baṭuka* <note>A form of Bhairava or the youth-protector</note>, existing in eight trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Octuple Peak. Placement: **Brow center** (Ājñā).

**Añ, Ṭaṃ, Ṭhaṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the nine-syllable mantra beginning with *Brahmā*, existing in nine trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Nonuple Peak. Placement: **Moon center** (Indu).

**Ḍaṃ, Ḍhaṃ, Ṇaṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the ten-syllable mantra beginning with *Viṣṇu*, existing in ten trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Decuple Peak. Placement: **Point center** (Bindu).

**Taṃ, Thaṃ, Daṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the eleven-syllable mantra beginning with *Rudra*, existing in eleven trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Eleven-fold Peak. Placement: **Digit center** (Kalā).

**Dhaṃ, Naṃ, Paṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the twelve-syllable mantra beginning with *Sarasvatī*, existing in twelve trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Twelve-fold Peak. Placement: **Center of Transcendent Mind** (Unmanī).

**Phaṃ, Baṃ, Bhaṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the thirteen-syllable mantra beginning with *Lakṣmī*, existing in thirteen trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Thirteen-fold Peak. Placement: **Circumference of the head** (Śirovṛtta).

**Maṃ, Yaṃ, Raṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the fourteen-syllable mantra beginning with *Gaurī*, existing in fourteen trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Fourteen-fold Peak. Placement: **Sound center** (Nāda).

**Laṃ, Vaṃ, Śaṃ, Ṣaṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the fifteen-syllable mantra beginning with *Durgā*, existing in fifteen trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Fifteen-fold Peak. Placement: **End of Sound center** (Nādānta).

**Saṃ, Haṃ, Laṃ, Kṣaṃ**: Salutations to the Goddess whose essence is the sixteen-syllable mantra beginning with *Tripurā*, existing in sixteen trillion variations. Salutations to the Presiding Deity of all Mantras, the Giver of all Fruits, the Mother Goddess of the Sixteen-fold Peak. Placement: **Opening of Brahma** (Brahmarandhra).

**Aṃ... Kṣaṃ**: Salutations to the Supreme Mother Goddess, who is the essence of all mantras. This should be performed as a **pervasive placement over all limbs**.

# In the Kularnava Tantra

<meta>This page continues the ritual instructions following the Matrika Nyasa (the ritual placement of the letters of the alphabet). ### Fourth Chapter

O Great Goddess <note>original: "Maheśāni"</note>! One must perform the ritual placement of the letters of the alphabet <note>original: "Mātṛkā Nyāsa"</note> in this way with a concentrated mind. **107**

Having thus established the letters upon the body, O Goddess, one should meditate upon the Lord with a focused mind: In the middle of the Ocean of Nectar <note>original: "Amṛtārṇava"</note>, upon a beautifully adorned Island of Gems <note>original: "Maṇi-dvīpa"</note>, **108**

Inside a pavilion of rubies and precious stones <note>original: "Maṇḍapa"</note> situated within a forest of wish-fulfilling trees <note>original: "Kalpavṛkṣa"</note>. On a glorious lotus-throne composed of the nine precious jewels, **109**

Seated within a triangle, shining with the radiance of ten thousand suns and moons combined. He is joined with the Mother <note>original: "Ambikā"</note> as half of His own body, with his ornaments and decorations divided between the two halves. **110**

Possessing the beauty of ten million gods of love <note>original: "Kāma Deva"</note>, and appearing eternally as a sixteen-year-old youth. His lotus-like face bears a gentle smile; He has three eyes and the moon as His crest-ornament. **111**

Clad in divine garments and flower-garlands, His body is anointed with celestial pastes and adorned with divine jewelry. In His hands, He holds a drinking vessel <note>original: "pāna-pātra"</note>, the gesture of consciousness <note>original: "Cinmudrā"</note>, a trident <note>original: "Triśūla"</note>, and a book. **112**

Granting the perfect attainment of sacred knowledge <note>original: "Vidyā"</note>, His eyes and face radiate eternal bliss. He is served by the entire host of deities described in the ritual of the Great Sixteen-fold Path <note>original: "Mahāṣoḍhā"</note>. **113**

One should thus meditate upon the Lord who is Half-Woman <note>original: "Ardha-nārīśvara"</note>, the Auspicious One <note>original: "Śiva"</note>, within the lotus of the heart.

### Meditation on the Lord who is Half-Woman <note>original: "Ardha-Nārīśvara Dhyāna"</note>:

O Great Goddess! After performing with a concentrated mind the ritual placement of the alphabet <term>Mātṛkā Nyāsa: The practice of mentally or physically "placing" the sacred sounds of the Sanskrit alphabet onto parts of the body to sanctify it.</term> as described above, the meditation <note>original: "Dhyāna"</note> of the Lord who is Half-Woman <note>original: "Ardha-nārīśvara"</note> should be performed. One should, in the lotus of the heart, first contemplate the Auspicious Lord who is Half-Woman in the following manner: 

In the middle of the Ocean of Nectar, embellished, there is a raised Island. On it, in the woodland of wish-fulfilling trees <note>original: "Kalpa-vṛkṣas"</note>, there is a beautiful canopy <note>original: "Maṇḍapa"</note> made of nine rubies. In that canopy, there is a throne embellished with nine jewels. On that throne, on a triangular seat in the center of the lotus, is seated Lord Shiva decorated with the moon and sun, and the Goddess Mother <note>original: "Ambikā"</note> forming half of His body. The respective ornaments of both are glittering on their bodies separately. 

Beautiful as tens of millions of gods of love <note>original: "Kāma Devas"</note> and always young as a sixteen-year-old, the lotus-face of the Lord who is Half-Woman is in a mildly smiling pose. He has three eyes, and the moon decorates His crest of hair. He is putting on divine clothing, ornaments, and flower-garlands, and His body is smeared with sandal-paste. Three of His four hands are holding a drinking vessel <note>original: "pāna-pātra"</note>, a trident <note>original: "Triśūla"</note>, and a book <note>original: "Pustaka"</note>, and the fourth is in the gesture of consciousness <term>Cinmudrā: A symbolic hand gesture where the thumb and index finger touch, representing the union of individual and universal consciousness.</term>. 

Accompanied by sacred knowledge <note>original: "Vidyā"</note> and spiritual powers <note>original: "Siddhis"</note>, He is always blissful. Innumerable gods mentioned above in the Great Sixteen-fold ritual <note>original: "Mahāṣoḍhā"</note> are waiting in His service. One should contemplate upon such a form of the Lord who is Half-Woman, the Auspicious One, in the lotus of the heart.

### In the Kularnava Tantra
<note>The Kularnava Tantra is a major text of the Kaula school of Tantra, focusing on ritual, yoga, and the path to liberation.</note>

->One may remember the divine form as male, O Goddess, or reflect upon it as female. 114<-
->Alternatively, one may meditate upon the formless <note>original: "niṣkala"</note>, characterized as Being, Consciousness, and Bliss <note>original: "Saccidānanda"</note>. He consists of all radiance, O Goddess, and His body contains the entire creation, both moving and unmoving. 115<-

*Contemplation in Masculine, Feminine, or Formless Aspect:*
One can contemplate upon the deity as the Half-Female Lord <note>original: "Ardha-Nārīśvara," a form of Shiva and Parvati joined as one</note> either in a Masculine or in a Feminine form, or in the Attributeless Form of Being-Consciousness-Bliss, which is full of radiance and contains all the mobile and immobile creation.

->Then, O Supreme Goddess, one should display the ten ritual hand gestures <note>term: "Mudrās" (symbolic hand positions used in ritual to channel energy)</note>.<-
->The Womb <note>original: "Yoni"</note>, the Phallus <note>original: "Liṅga"</note>, the Cow of Plenty <note>original: "Surabhi"</note>, and the four gestures of Weapons <note>original: "Heti"</note>. 116<-

*Contemplation of the Holy Teacher:*
After exhibiting the hand gestures, one should contemplate the Holy Teacher in the crown of the head as a form of Shiva in the following manner: *He resides in the thousand-petaled lotus, shining with the cool radiance of the moon. His face and eyes are serene, and he is the embodiment of all gods.*

O Parvati! Whoever performs the ritual placement of energy in the manner described becomes like the Supreme Shiva Himself. A practitioner <note>original: "Sādhaka"</note> who performs this "Sixfold Great Placement" every day obtains the power of both restraint and kindness; all the gods salute him, and truly, I also salute him.

### Fourth Chapter
<note>original: "चतुर्थ उल्लासः" (Chaturtha Ullāsaḥ)</note>

->Wherever this Great Sixfold Ritual <note>term: "Mahāṣoḍhā Nyāsa" (A complex ritual where mantras are 'placed' on the body to divinize the practitioner)</note> is performed, O Mountain-Daughter <note>original: "Pārvatī"</note>,<-

->O Goddess! After performing this ritual placement, wherever a person goes,<-

O <term>Devi</term> <note>Goddess</note>! After performing this <term>Nyāsa</term> wherever a <term>Sādhaka</term> <note>spiritual practitioner</note> goes he obtains victory, benefits, honour and splendour.

->Whoever performs this ritual, known by the name 'Adamantine Cage,'<-
<note>The name "Vajra-pañjara" implies an impenetrable spiritual shield.</note>

One who performs this <term>Nyāsa</term>, from his fear all the fierce <term>Bhūtas</term> <note>spirits</note>, <term>Vetāls</term> <note>vampire-like beings</note>, <term>Devas</term> <note>gods</note>, <term>Rākṣasas</term> <note>demons</note>, and <term>Grahas</term> <note>planetary spirits or seizors</note> who reside in the Divine <term>Lokas</term> <note>worlds</note>, in the atmosphere, on the earth and mountains, in water and forests. All these, O <term>Kuleśvarī</term> <note>Sovereign Goddess of the Kaula tradition</note>! fear his very sight.

# Chapter Five

->The Holy Goddess said:<-

I wish to hear about the characteristics of the supporting vessels <note>original: "ādhāra-pātra"</note> and the ritual meats; the preparation of the sacred Kula substances <note>term: "Kula-dravya" (The specific physical materials, such as wine, meat, and fish, used in Tantric worship to represent and activate divine energies)</note>, their various types, and their spiritual glory. 1

O Ocean of Compassion <note>original: "Karuṇānidhe"</note>, tell me all of this: the sin that arises from acting without following the rules, and the fruit that is gained by acting according to the sacred injunctions. 2

*Question regarding the supporting vessels and other materials:*

The Holy Goddess said: O Lord of the Kula Tradition <note>original: "Kuleśa"</note>! I want to hear about the characteristics of the supporting vessels and the meat; the method of making the sacred substances, their varieties and their majesty; the sins arising from performing the ritual improperly and the rewards of performing them properly. O Ocean of Compassion! Tell me about all these things.

->The Lord said:<-

Listen, O Goddess, and I shall explain what You have asked of Me. Merely by hearing this, one attains equality with the thirty gods <note>original: "tridashaiḥ" (A traditional term for the Vedic pantheon/gods)</note>. 3

*The Necessity of Supporting Vessels:*

The Holy Lord said: Listen, O Goddess! I am telling you what You have asked. Merely by hearing it, one becomes like the Gods.

Without a support <note>original: "ādhāra" (The ritual base or stand upon which a vessel is placed)</note>, there is a spiritual fall, and the Mother Spirits <note>term: "Mātaraḥ" (The Matrikas or Mother Goddesses who govern the ritual and must be satisfied through proper offerings)</note> are not satisfied. Therefore, O Sovereign of the Tradition <note>original: "Kulanāyikā"</note>, one should prepare the support according to the rules. 4

Absence of supporting vessels is considered a fault and the Mother Spirits do not accept the offering. Therefore, O Sovereign of the Kula! One should prepare the vessels according to the rules.

The masters say the support may be three-legged, six-legged, or four-legged; or, O Goddess, one may make it in a beautiful circular shape. 5

O Devi! The vessels should be made beautifully. They can be three-sided, four-sided, six-sided, or circular.

It may be crafted from gold, silver, stone, the shell of a tortoise, a skull, wood <note>original: "āla"</note>, or clay; or it may be born of a coconut, a conch shell, copper, or a pearl-oyster shell. 6

# 76

### In the Kularnava Tantra

->A wise person should fashion a ritual vessel from a sacred tree.<-
->One should avoid vessels that are too thin, too thick, cracked, or broken. 7<-

*Metals for the construction of the vessels:*

Vessels may be crafted from gold, silver, stone, the shell of a tortoise, a skull, a gourd, earth, coconut, conch-shell, copper, pearl, oyster-shell, or the wood of sacred trees. One should not use vessels that are too large or too small, nor those that are damaged or shattered.

->Gold, silver, and copper vessels grant all spiritual perfections.<-
->A stone vessel is used for rites of pacification, and an earthen one for immobilization. 8<-
->A coconut vessel is used for subjugation, and one of tortoise shell for malevolent magic.<-
->A conch shell bestows knowledge, and an oyster shell provides the grace of the Goddess. 9<-
->Vessels made of skull and gourd grant perfection in Yoga,<-
->and those made from sacred trees destroy all sins.<-
->O Goddess! One should select a single vessel from among these materials. 10<-

*Kinds of Vessels according to the desires to be fulfilled:*

Gold, silver, and copper provide all results. In rites of pacification <note>original: "shantika" (rituals to remove disease or bad omens)</note> and immobilization <note>term: "stambhana" (the ritual power to paralyze or halt an opponent's actions)</note>, stone vessels are useful. Coconut vessels are used in rituals of subjugation <note>original: "vashya" (the act of attracting or controlling others)</note>, tortoise shell in charms, and conch-shells in works providing knowledge. Pearl or oyster-shell vessels bestow the love of the Mother Goddess. Vessels made of human skulls or gourds provide *Yoga-siddhi* <note>term: "Yoga-siddhi" (spiritual perfections or supernatural powers attained through disciplined practice)</note>, and those from sacred trees destroy all sins. O Goddess! A practitioner should select their vessel from any of these materials based on their intent.

->I shall now describe the sacred substances of the Kula tradition; listen with a focused mind, O Goddess.<-
->Take twelve measures of water and half a measure of buttermilk; 11<-
->Four measures of rice and two measures of boiled grain;<-
->along with a handful of sprouts, these should all be combined in a single jar. 12<-

*Name of the Kula-substances:*

Now I am telling you of the *Kula-dravyas* <note>term: "Kula-dravya" (the specific physical materials, such as wine or fermented grains, used as offerings in Kula rituals)</note>. Listen to them with a concentrated mind. Twelve *prasthas* <note>term: "prastha" (a traditional unit of volume, roughly equal to 750ml or a quart)</note> of water, half a *prastha* of buttermilk <note>original: "takra"</note>, four *prasthas* of rice, and two *prasthas* of grain/food, along with a bundle of grass sprouts (a quantity that fits within one's grip), should all be placed together in a large earthen jar.

->This vessel should be kept in a place free from cold for two days.<-
->Then, place it over a fire and cook it until the mixture becomes like a thick paste. 13<-

This vessel should be placed for two days in a location protected from the cold. Thereafter, it should be set upon a fire and cooked until all the combined materials reach the consistency of a thick sludge or paste <note>original: "jambala-sadṛśam" (literally: "resembling mud")</note>.

# Chapter Five

->Afterward, it should be removed from the fire and allowed to reach a cool state. Then, a wise practitioner should grind a quarter-measure <term>prastha: a traditional unit of volume, approximately 750 milliliters</term> of this substance and mix it thoroughly by hand. 14<-

After the initial preparation is heated, it must be cooled. A learned person then takes a quarter-measure of the finely ground material and blends it manually to ensure a smooth consistency.

->One should add half a measure of rice and take it up again the next day. After grinding the whole mixture well with buttermilk, one should stir it to combine. This is known as the grain liquor <term>Paiṣṭī: a sacred spirit distilled from meal or fermented husks</term>, and it is honored by both gods and demons. 15<-

To the existing paste, add half a measure of rice and allow the mixture to rest for one full day. On the following day, the preparation is ground again and mixed with buttermilk <note>original: "takra"</note> to create a fine paste. This substance is famously known as *Paiṣṭī*; it is considered so sacred that it is worshipped by all celestial and chthonic beings.

->O Goddess of the Kula lineage <note>original: "Kuleśāni"</note>, for the molasses liquor <term>Gauḍī: a spirit made from treacle or unrefined sugar</term>, take ten measures of water prepared with the bark of the white acacia and the rose-apple tree. 16<-
->Add one measure of the auspicious flowers of the fire-flame bush <note>original: "dhātakī"</note> or coconut blossoms. Then add eight coins' weight <term>niṣka: a historical unit of weight, roughly 4 grams in medical contexts</term> each of yellow myrobalan and the fruit of the nut-grass. 17<-
->One should also add one weight each of leadwort <note>original: "vahni"</note> and the "Three Bitters" <term>trikaṭu: a medicinal blend of ginger, long pepper, and black pepper</term> individually. Mix all of these with eighty weights of molasses in a single earthen jar. 18<-
->One should stir it thoroughly with the hand, moving both clockwise and counter-clockwise, for one hundred and eight rotations, three times a day, every day. 19<-
->The fermentation is complete in twelve days, and one should filter it on the thirteenth. This is called the molasses liquor, and it is the means for achieving union with Shiva. 20<-

To prepare the *Gauḍī* liquor, the practitioner uses a base of water infused with the bark of the White Acacia and the Rose-Apple tree. Various botanical ingredients are added, including *Dhātakī* flowers, coconut blossoms, and medicinal fruits like *Harītaki*. The mixture is fortified with the "Three Bitters" (ginger and two types of pepper) and a significant amount of molasses. The ritual of preparation requires active physical engagement: the jar must be stirred 108 times, both clockwise and counter-clockwise, during the three transitions of the day (dawn, noon, and sunset). After fermenting for twelve days, the liquid is filtered on the thirteenth day. This potent brew is said to facilitate *Sāyujya*, or the ultimate absorption of the soul into the Divine.

->One should add twice the amount of water to flower-nectar <term>makaranda: the sweet juice of flowers or honey</term> in a jar. The fermentation takes twelve days, and the rest of the process is as previously described.<-

->This is designated as the honey-wine, which brings delight to the deities. 21<-

Place honey in a vessel and add double that quantity of water. Leave the mixture to ferment for twelve days. The remainder of the procedure follows the previously described methods. This preparation is called *Mādhvī* <term>Mādhvī: a sacred liquor derived from honey, often associated with sweetness and divine favor</term> and it bestows the love of the gods upon the practitioner.

->One part dry ginger, two parts bark, and three parts pepper;<-

->Mixed with eighty parts of molasses, the rest as previously told;<-
->This is a delightful substance, the highest drink for the Yoginīs. 23<-

Mix one part of dry ginger <note>original: "Śuṇṭhī"</note>, two parts of the bark of a lemon tree, three parts of black pepper <note>original: "Marīca"</note>, four parts of the fire-flame bush <note>original: "Dhātakī"; used as a fermenting agent</term>, five parts of flowers, six parts of honey, and eighty parts of unrefined sugar <note>original: "Guḍa"</note> or molasses. The rest of the preparation follows the earlier instructions. This creates a pleasant liquor considered excellent for the consumption of the *Yoginīs* <term>Yoginīs: powerful female spirits or advanced female practitioners in the Tantric path</term>.

->One and a half measures of buffalo curd, and one measure of clarified butter;<-
->With a hundred unripe bananas, this combination makes a glorious wine. 24<-
->Mixing these together, one should cook them in a thick bamboo tube;<-

->Taking it out, one should dry it thoroughly in the sun’s rays;<-
->When it reaches a hardened state, the person should store it. 26<-
->A portion the size of a berry, when mixed well with water;<-
->Fills the cup as desired, granting supreme bliss. 27<-
->This too is a supreme substance, O Beloved, dear to all the gods;<-
->These are the sources of intoxication; other wines may also be made. 28<-

Combine twelve *Tolās* <term>Tolā: a traditional Indian unit of weight, approximately 12 grams</term> of buffalo milk curd <note>original: "Dadhi"</note>, one *prastha* <term>prastha: a volume roughly equivalent to 750 milliliters</term> of clarified butter (ghee), and one hundred unripe bananas <note>original: "Kadalī"</note>. This mixture creates a most auspicious wine. These ingredients must be blended thoroughly and sealed inside the hollow cavity of a thick bamboo stalk. The bamboo is then buried for forty-eight days to mature in the nutrient-rich mud of a pond where lotuses grow. Afterward, it is removed and left to dry in the heat of the sun. Once the substance hardens, the practitioner <note>original: "Sādhaka"</note> takes a small amount—about the weight of a single *Ratti* seed <note>original: "Guñjā-phala"</note>—and dissolves it in a vessel of water. This creates a liquor that provides supreme spiritual pleasure. Lord Shiva addresses the Goddess, saying, "O My Beloved! This substance <note>original: "dravya"</note> is loved by all the deities." These described here are the primary base liquors, which can be further blended to create many other varieties.

->Jackfruit, grape, honey-tree, date, palm, and sugarcane;<-
->Honey-based, rum, mead, spiced wine, and that of the coconut. 29<-
