### The Eleven Varieties of Wine

->These eleven wines bring both worldly enjoyment and spiritual liberation.<-

*The Names of the Eleven Kinds of Wine:*

<term>Pānasa</term> <note>Jackfruit wine</note>, <term>Drākṣā</term> <note>Grape wine</note>, <term>Mādhūka</term> <note>Wine made from the Madhuka flower, Bassia latifolia</note>, <term>Khārjūra</term> <note>Date wine</note>, <term>Tāla</term> <note>Palm wine or toddy</note>, <term>Aikṣaṇa</term> <note>Sugarcane wine</note>, <term>Madhu</term> <note>Honey wine</note>, <term>Ucchiṣṭa</term> <note>A wine made from fermented grain or specific ritual residues</note>, <term>Mādhvīka</term> <note>A sweet wine derived from flowers</note>, <term>Maireya</term> <note>A spiced herbal wine</note>, and <term>Nārikela</term> <note>Coconut wine</note> are the eleven kinds of wine which provide both Enjoyment <note>original: "Bhukti"</note> and Emancipation <note>original: "Mukti"</note>.

->The twelfth wine, however, is Sura; it is the best of all, O My Beloved! 30<-

*The Twelfth Wine, Surā: Its Kinds and Qualities:*

The twelfth wine is called <term>Surā</term> <note>The most sacred or "distilled" spirit in Vedic and Tantric traditions</note> and it is, O My Beloved, the best of all.

->Surā should be known as being of three kinds: Paiṣṭī, Gauḍī, and Mādhvī.<-
->Paiṣṭī bestows all spiritual attainments; Gauḍī provides enjoyment. 31<-
->Mādhvī should be known to provide liberation; Surā is beloved by the Gods.<-

<term>Surā</term> should be known to be of three types: <term>Paiṣṭī</term> <note>made from grain or flour</note>, <term>Gauḍī</term> <note>made from molasses or unrefined sugar</note>, and <term>Mādhvī</term> <note>made from honey</note>. The <term>Paiṣṭī</term> variety bestows all Attainments <note>original: "Siddhis"; supernatural powers or successes</note>, <term>Gauḍī</term> gives worldly Enjoyment, and the <term>Mādhvī</term> gives Emancipation. Thus, know these <term>Surās</term> as the favorites of the deities.

->Sugarcane wine provides learning; grape wine provides a kingdom. 32<-
->Palm wine is excellent for immobilization; date wine destroys enemies.<-
->Coconut wine gives wealth, and jackfruit wine brings auspiciousness. 33<-
->Madhuka wine provides wisdom, and Madhvika wine destroys diseases.<-
->O Queen of the Kula, the wine named Maireya always destroys sins. 34<-

<term>Aikṣavī</term> <note>Sugarcane wine</note> provides Learning; <term>Drākṣī</term> <note>Grape wine</note> provides a kingdom; <term>Tālajā</term> <note>Palm wine</note> is famous for providing Immobilization <note>original: "Stambhana"; the magical power to paralyze or stop an opponent</note>; <term>Khārjūrī</term> <note>Date wine</note> destroys enemies; <term>Nārikela</term> <note>Coconut</note> wine gives wealth and <term>Pānasī</term> <note>Jackfruit wine</note> is auspicious. <term>Madhūkajā</term> wine <note>from Madhuka flowers</note> provides knowledge, and <term>Mādhvīkā</term> destroys all diseases. O <term>Kuleśāni</term> <note>Lady of the Kula/Clan, a title for the Goddess</note>, the wine named <term>Maireya</term> is the perpetual destroyer of sins.

->Wine born from milky trees, or produced from bark;<-
->Wine born from Madhuka flowers, or liquor from rice. 35<-

Wines made from <term>Kṣīra-vṛkṣas</term> <note>milky-sap trees such as the Banyan or Peepal</note>, from the barks of trees, from <term>Madhūka</term> (*Bassia latifolia*) flowers, and the fermented water of cooked rice <note>original: "Tandulodbhavam"</note> are the various other kinds.

->That wine which offers pure joy and a delightful fragrance—<-
->That wine is superior, O Goddess, and brings pleasure to the gods. 36<-

That wine is considered superior which provides faultless pleasure and beautiful entertainment. O Goddess <note>original: "Devi"</note>, such wines are always loved by the Gods.

### Page 80

One should fill the vessel as much as the heart desires; it increases supreme bliss. O Beloved! This intoxicating substance <note>original: "dravya"</note> is dear to all the gods. 37

*Qualities of Good Wines:*

One should fill his glass with wine according to his heart's satisfaction in order to enhance his supreme pleasure. O My Beloved! such entertaining substances <note>original: "dravyas"</note> are loved by all the Gods.

By the mere sight of the sacred spirit <term>Surā</term>, all sins are destroyed. Smelling its fragrance alone bestows the merit of performing one hundred Vedic sacrifices <note>original: "śatrakratu-phalam," referring to the Ashvamedha or horse-sacrifices</note>. 38

The touch of wine provides fruits equivalent to visiting millions of <term>Tirthas</term> <note>sacred places of pilgrimage</note>, and O Goddess! by drinking it one directly obtains the four-fold Emancipation <note>the four states of liberation: Salokya, Samipya, Sarupya, and Sayujya</note>. 39

*Desire and other Powers (Shaktis) in the Sacred Spirit:*

->In the fragrance of the spirit resides the Power of Will; in its essence is the Power of Knowledge.<-
->In its taste is the Power of Action, and in its exhilaration resides the Supreme Power. 40<-

*Methods of taking wine:*

Wine is said to lead towards the Absolute <note>original: "Brahmagā"</note> and is a means for purifying the mind. Therefore, one of the above-mentioned wines should be brought in any case for the rituals of worship. 41

A wise practitioner should take <term>Madya</term> <note>wine</note>, <term>Māṁsa</term> <note>meat</note>, fish, and <term>Vijayā</term> <note>an intoxicating substance, usually hemp or cannabis</note>, and mix them well with the eight sacred fragrances <term>Aṣṭa-gandha</term>. <margin>The eight fragrances vary by deity. For the Goddess (Shakti), these are: sandalwood, aloe wood, camphor, cora, saffron, rochana, spikenard, and kapi.</margin> Having ground these and formed them into a ritual pill, he should keep them ready. If wine is unavailable, he should offer the libation by mixing this pill with water. 42

One may also offer the libation using buttermilk mixed with molasses and honey, or with sour barley-gruel <note>original: "sauvīra"</note>. One must never omit this ritual. If it is omitted through negligence, one will incur the curse of the deities. 43

...means of obtaining Attainments <term>Siddhis</term> <note>supernatural powers or spiritual realizations</note>. This has been expounded by Kula Philosophy and also by Great Bhairava <note>a fierce manifestation of Shiva and the primary deity of this Tantra</note>.

If by performing an action there is a lapse of that action, then that action is performed by seventy million superior Sages.

->O Beloved, one should strike the animal with this mantra after consecrating it,<-
->having worshipped it with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken rice; otherwise, one goes to hell. 50<-

*Mantra for Animal-sacrifice:*
One should worship the animal with fragrances, flowers, and rice-grain. Thereafter, sanctifying it by the following <term>Mantra</term> <note>a sacred utterance or prayer</note> (Verse 51) it should be sacrificed:

->"This body is cut by Shiva; therefore, you have attained the state of Shiva."<-
->"Realize that, O animal! For you are not a beast; you are indeed Shiva Himself." 51<-
<note>original: "shivottkṛttamidaṃ piṇḍamatastvaṃ shivatāṃ gataḥ / tad budhyasva pasho tvaṃ hi mā shivastvaṃ shivo'si hi"</note>

"Your body is being cut by Shiva; hence you will obtain <term>Shivatva</term> <note>the state of being one with Shiva; divinity</note>. O animal! You should know this. For me you are Shiva, as Shiva is for you."

->Brahma resides in the meat, Vishnu in the fragrance, and Rudra in the juices.<-
->The Supreme Soul resides in the bliss thereof; therefore, O Beloved, this should be consumed. 52<-

*Existence of Brahma etc., Gods in various Ingredients of Flesh:*
There resides Brahma <note>the Creator</note> in the water of flesh; Vishnu <note>the Preserver</note> in the smell of flesh; Rudra <note>the Destroyer</note> in the <term>Rasa</term> <note>the essence or juice</note> of flesh, and the Supreme Spirit in the pleasure of flesh. Hence, O My Beloved! it is worth taking.

->In the absence of meat, one should take garlic, fresh ginger, or dried ginger;<-
->taking these, O Goddess, one should worship, otherwise the ritual becomes fruitless. 53<-

*Things to be offered in the absence of Flesh:*
In the absence of flesh, one should worship the Devi with garlic or ginger; otherwise the worship becomes useless. <note>In certain Tantric traditions, pungent plants like garlic and ginger are considered ritual equivalents to meat because of their "heating" properties.</note>

->One should not offer libations with wine alone, if fish and meat are lacking.<-
->Nor should one perform worship with fish and meat without the presence of wine. 54<-

*Inter-relationship of Fish, Meat, and Wine:*
Without <term>Māṃsa</term> (flesh) and <term>Matsya</term> (fish) one should not offer libations with <term>Madya</term> (wine) alone. Similarly, without wine one should not perform worship with fish and meat alone. <note>The text emphasizes the synergy between the "Five M's" or ritual ingredients; they must be used in conjunction to be effective.</note>

->By offering a piece of meat the size of a sesame seed, or half that size with a drop of wine,<-
->by that single act of libation, one obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices. 55<-

By offering libations with meat equal to even a <term>Tila</term> <note>a sesame seed</note> and a drop of wine equal to half of a sesame seed, one gets the fruit of all the sacrifices.

->There is no merit in the three worlds equal to Kula-worship.<-

<note>original: "kulapūjāsamṃ nāsti puṇyamanyajjagattraye / tasmād yaḥ pūjayedbhaktyā bhuktimuktyoḥ sa bhājanam"</note>

*Sins of non-performance of Kula-worship:*

In the three worlds there is no merit equal to the <term>Kulapūjā</term> <note>the central ritual worship of the Kaula tradition</note>. Hence, one who performs this worship with devotion obtains both <term>Bhukti</term> <note>worldly enjoyment</note> and <term>Mukti</term> <note>spiritual liberation</note>.

->Even if unlearned and ignorant of the scriptures, one who is devoted to the Guru and firm in vows,<-
->who is intent on Kula-worship, becomes most dear to Me. 57<-

Even if an illiterate or one ignorant of the <term>Śāstras</term> <note>sacred legal and theoretical treatises</note> performs Kulapūjā with devotion to his <term>Guru</term> <note>spiritual teacher</note> and with firm determination, he is most loved by Me.

->O Goddess! This worship bestows desired fruits when performed by any of the four classes,<-
->or the four stages of life, whether they be men, women, or of the third gender. 58<-
<note>original: "caturṇāmapi varṇānāshramāṇāmapīshvari / puṃstrīnapuṃsakānāntu pūjiteṣṭaphalapradā"</note>

O <term>Īśvarī</term> <note>the Divine Feminine/Goddess</note>! On being worshipped by all the men, women and people of third gender of the four <term>Varṇas</term> <note>social classes: Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra</note> and of the four <term>Āśramas</term> <note>stages of life: student, householder, forest-dweller, and renunciant</note>, You bestow the desired fruits on them.

->When worshipped, You grant rewards in this world and the next, like a virtuous wife;<-
->but un-worshipped, O Queen of the Gods, You bring misery like a quarrelsome wife. 59<-
->The evil-minded person who acts without performing Kula-worship<-
->goes to a terrible hell along with twenty-one generations of his lineage. 60<-

If worshipped, You like a good lady give the desired fruits, and if not worshipped, You torment like a bad lady. An evil-minded person who without Kula-pūjā behaves thus (i.e., ignores Your worship), goes to Hell with his twenty-one previous ancestors.

->Therefore, with every effort, one should be intent on Kula-worship.<-
->He attains all spiritual powers; of this there is no doubt. 61<-

Hence with all his efforts one should devote himself to Kulapūjā. Thus he indubitably attains all <term>Siddhis</term> <note>extraordinary spiritual powers or perfections</note>.

->If one is unable to perform the adoration, one should provide the materials for the ritual.<-
->He who is unable to even give should simply witness the performance of the worship. 62<-

*Duties of those incapable of performing Kula-pūjā:*

One who is incapable of performing Kula-pūjā should offer to others materials connected with Kula-pūjā. One who is unable to give even these materials should witness the <term>pūjā</term> <note>ritual worship</note> where it is being performed.

<summary>This page describes Kulapūjā as the highest form of merit, accessible to all people regardless of gender, social class, or education level. It warns that neglecting this worship leads to spiritual downfall for oneself and one's ancestors, while even witnessing the ritual brings benefit to those unable to perform it.</summary>

--- Page 95 ---
<meta>This page continues the "Fifth Flash" or chapter of the Kularnava Tantra. While the previous page used the metaphor of a lamp to describe how the Self (Atma) is revealed, this page moves into the specific tantric theology of the "Five Ms" (Makaras), specifically wine and meat. It redefines these physical substances as symbolic embodiments of the divine union between Shiva and Shakti, arguing that their ritual use is not for mere intoxication but for manifesting the inherent bliss of the Absolute within the human body.</meta>

<page-num>86</page-num>
<header>In the Kularnava Tantra</header>

->Wine is Power <note>Shakti</note> and meat is the Great Lord <note>Shiva</note>; the one who partakes of them is the Divine Consciousness <note>Bhairava</note> Himself.<-
->The bliss arising from the union of these two is called Liberation. 79<-

*Symptoms of Emancipation:*

Wine represents the Goddess (<term>Shakti</term>) and Meat represents the God (<term>Shiva</term>). The practitioner who ritualistically consumes both realizes themselves as the Supreme Reality (<term>Bhairava</term>) personified. The spiritual ecstasy that results from the "union" of these two substances—mirroring the cosmic union of the divine masculine and feminine—is identified as true spiritual freedom or <term>Moksha</term>.

->Bliss is the very form of the Absolute, and it is situated within the body.<-
->Wine is the catalyst that manifests that bliss; therefore, it is drunk by the Yogis. 80<-

Divine Joy (<term>Ananda</term>) is the essential nature of the ultimate reality (<term>Brahman</term>). This joy is not external; it is already present within the physical body of the seeker. Ritual wine (<term>Madya</term>) is used by practitioners of yoga as a tool to "unlock" or manifest this internal state of bliss.

->Holding the water-pot, the conch-shell, and the skull-cup, all filled with the "honey" <note>Wine</note>,<-
->Does the world not see in him the presence of the Creator, the Preserver, and the Destroyer? 81<-

When a practitioner holds the ritual vessels—the ascetic's water-pot (<term>Kamandalu</term>), the sacred conch, and the skull-cup (<term>Kapala</term>)—filled with consecrated wine, they are seen as an embodiment of the Great Trinity: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva <note>original: "Brahma-Vishnu-Maheshvaran"</note>.

->Free from doubt, free from fear, heroic, without shame or idle curiosity,<-
->Having mastered the meaning of the Vedas and Scriptures, he should drink the boon-providing Wine. 82<-

A "Heroic Seeker" (<term>Vira Sadhaka</term>) is one who has transcended social inhibitions and mental hesitations. Armed with deep scriptural knowledge and a focused mind, he partakes of the ritual wine—referred to here as <term>Varuni</term> <note>originally a Vedic goddess associated with water and later the "spirit" of the wine</note>—to receive its spiritual blessings.

->O Goddess! Through the drinking of the nectar purified by sacred chants,<-
->A divine state of being is born that releases one from the bonds of worldly existence. 83<-

Addressing the Goddess <note>Parvati</note>, the text explains that when the substance is consecrated through <term>Mantras</term> (sacred sound formulas), it ceases to be mere alcohol and becomes "nectar" (<term>Amrita</term>). Drinking this transforms the seeker's consciousness into a divine state, breaking the cycle of birth and death.

->For the Priest, it may be drunk always; for the Warrior, at the approach of battle;<-
->For the Merchant, at the time of sacrifice; and for the Laborer, during the final rites. 84<-

*Time of Drinking by the Brahmin etc. classes:*

The text provides a ritual framework for the four traditional social classes (<term>Varnas</term>): The <term>Brahmins</term> (priests/scholars) may use it constantly in their rites; <term>Kshatriyas</term> (warriors) use it to summon courage before war; <term>Vaishyas</term> (merchants/farmers) use it during specific animal sacrifices <note>original: "golambhane," often interpreted as the ritual handling of cattle or specific agricultural rites</note>; and <term>Shudras</term> (laborers) use it during funeral ceremonies.

->Having worshipped the Gods and the Ancestors according to the scriptural path,<-
->Remembering the Teacher and drinking wine and eating meat, one incurs no sin. 85<-

Provided that the consumption is done within a sacred context—after honoring the deities, the spirits of the ancestors (<term>Pitras</term>), and the spiritual lineage/teacher (<term>Gurudeva</term>)—the act of eating meat and drinking wine is considered a holy sacrament rather than a vice or a sin.

<summary>This page provides a theological justification for the ritual use of wine and meat in Tantric practice, defining them as physical manifestations of Shiva and Shakti. It outlines how these substances, when purified by mantras, catalyze a state of divine bliss and liberation for practitioners of all social classes.</summary>

<header>Fifth Flash</header>

->For the satisfaction of the ancestral spirits <note>Pitras</note> and the gods, and to remain steady in meditation on the Absolute <note>Brahman</note>,<-
->one should partake of ritual wine <note>Madya</note> and meat <note>Mamsa</note>. If one consumes them out of mere thirst, they are a sinner. 86<-

One should take ritual wine and meat only for the satisfaction of the Divine and the ancestors, and to help the mind concentrate on the essence of the Absolute. However, if a person consumes these substances simply to satisfy their own hunger or thirst, they commit a spiritual offense.

->For the sake of revealing the inner meaning of sacred chants <note>Mantra</note>, for the stability of the mind,<-
->and to obtain release from the bonds of worldly existence, one should practice the ritual drinking of wine. 87<-

The ritual use of wine is intended to spark an enlightenment regarding the power of sacred sounds, to steady the flickering mind, and to help the soul break free from the cycle of worldly attachment.

->One who partakes of wine and other ritual substances for their own pleasure is a sinner.<-
->Free from personal desire, one should consume them solely for the pleasure of the deities. 88<-

Anyone who drinks wine for the sake of sensory enjoyment is considered a sinner in this path. The practitioner must be entirely devoid of personal craving, partaking in the substance only as an offering to please the gods.

->The consumption of fish, meat, wine, and other intoxicants<-
->is declared a fault, My Beloved, at any time other than during a ritual sacrifice. 89<-

**The prohibition of ritual substances outside of sacred timing:**
The Teacher addresses the Goddess, saying: "O My Beloved! Consuming intoxicants—including fish, meat, and wine—at any time other than during a formal ritual sacrifice <note>Yaga</note> is considered a sin."

->Just as the drinking of the sacred nectar <note>Soma</note> is ordained for the priests during Vedic sacrifices,<-
->so too should the drinking of wine be done at the prescribed time, for it bestows both worldly enjoyment and spiritual liberation. 90<-

In the same way that ancient priests were required to drink the sacred <term>Soma</term> during Vedic rites, the Tantric practitioner is directed to use wine at specific, sacred times. When done correctly, this practice grants both <term>Bhukti</term> (worldly enjoyment/fulfillment) and <term>Mukti</term> (spiritual liberation).

->Only after properly understanding the inner purpose from the mouth of the Teacher and the scriptures of the Tradition,<-
->should one engage with the Five Ritual Substances; otherwise, one will meet their downfall. 91<-

One must not attempt these practices alone. Only after receiving a deep understanding of the <term>Kula-Shastras</term> (the scriptures of this tradition) from a qualified Teacher <note>Guru</note> should one use the <term>Five Mudras</term> (the five ritual components: wine, meat, fish, parched grain, and sexual union). Without this guidance, the practitioner will experience a spiritual fall.

->Without worshipping the lineage of Teachers, the protective deities, and the Boy-God,<-
->even a "Heroic" practitioner who drinks wine in vain will receive the curse of the gods. 92<-

**Useless drinking is prohibited even for an advanced practitioner:**
Even a <term>Vira-Sadhaka</term> (a practitioner on the "heroic" path) must not drink wine pointlessly. If they fail to first worship the lineage of Gurus and the protective deity <term>Batuka</term> (a guardian form of Shiva), the act of drinking becomes empty and invites a divine curse rather than a blessing.

Devoid of the purifying rites of initiation <note>Diksha</note>, one who leads an arbitrary life does not obtain liberation even through physical austerities, visits to holy sites, or religious observances.

*Impure "Five Ms" <note>Madya (wine), Mamsa (meat), etc.</note> are prohibited:*
One who drinks unconsecrated ritual substances, takes meat only for his own taste, or commits sexual violence goes to the Raurava Hell <note>a specific hell in Hindu cosmology described as a place of great suffering</note>.

<header>Fifth Flash</header>

If Kaulas <term>Kaula|a practitioner of the Kula path of Tantra</term> follow the restricted vows of the uninitiated <note>original: "Pasu-vratasya"; the behavior of 'pasus' or 'bound souls' who follow standard social conventions instead of Tantric liberty</note>, they become mockers of both paths. They shall remain in the Raurava Hell for as many years as there are hairs on their bodies. 100.

*Adhering to the ways of ordinary men, even a Kaula goes to Hell:*

If a Kaula takes to the ways of ordinary men, then he is ridiculed by both the Kaula path <note>original: "Kaulacara"</note> and the path of the uninitiated <note>original: "Pasvacara"</note> and lives in the Raurava Hell for as long a period as there are hairs on his body.

One who adheres to other philosophies but resorts to the ritual substances of the Kula <term>Kula-dravyas|sacred materials used in Tantric ritual, such as wine or meat</term> will be born among the lower spirits <note>original: "Bhuta-yonis"</note> for as many lives as there are hairs on his body. 101.

Adhering to other faiths, one who resorts to the ritual substances takes as many births among the lower spirits as there are hairs on his body.

One whose soul <note>original: "Atma"</note> is clouded by intoxication knows nothing at all. He knows neither contemplation, nor austerity, nor worship, nor religious duty, nor good actions. 102.
He knows neither the Divine, nor the Guru, nor the inquiry into the self <note>original: "Atma-vichara"</note>. He is not a true practitioner <note>original: "Kaulika"</note>, but is merely addicted to his own sensory pleasures. Such a person undoubtedly meets his downfall. 103.

*A wine-addict meets his downfall:*

One whose soul is concealed due to the drinking of wine does not possess knowledge of Contemplation, Austerity, Worship, Religion, Good actions, God, Guru, or his own soul. He is not a practitioner of the path, but is addicted to his own sensual pleasures. Such a person indubitably meets his downfall.

One who is addicted to wine, eats meat, and indulges in women, but is devoid of the secret teachings of the Kula path <note>original: "Kaulopadesha"</note>, goes to an eternal hell. 104.

Devoid of the teachings of the Kaula, one who remains addicted to wine, woman, and flesh lives perpetually in Hell.

O Goddess of the Kula! <note>original: "Kuleshi"; a title for the Divine Mother</note> Even if one is engrossed in the Absolute <term>Brahman|the ultimate, formless reality</term>, if he resorts to the five ritual substances <term>Pancha Mudra|the "five signs" or ingredients used in Tantric ritual</term> without the proper consecrating rites <note>original: "Asamskari"</note>, he falls into condemnation. 105.

O Goddess! Even if one is engrossed in the Absolute, if he resorts to the Five Ingredients without the proper rituals, he stands condemned.

One who knows the distinction between the three sacred symbols <term>Lingas|three specific energy points in the subtle body: Svayambhu, Bana, and Itara</term> and has pierced through the six energy centers <term>Chakras|the energy vortices of the subtle body</term> should reach the sacred seats <note>original: "Pitha-sthanas"</note> and wander into the Great Forest of the Lotus <note>original: "Maha-padma-vanam"; a poetic term for the Sahasrara or crown chakra</note>. 106.

Hence a Yogi who knows the three signs <note>the Svayambhu, Bana, and Itara Lingas</note>, and has penetrated the Six Centers, should come to the Sacred Seat and roam in the forest of the Great Lotus <note>the Thousand-Petaled Lotus at the crown of the head</note>.

-> Traveling from the root support <term>Mūlādhāra|the foundational energy center at the base of the spine</term> to the gateway of the divine <term>Brahmarandhra|the 'aperture of Brahma' located at the crown of the head</term> repeatedly; the arising of the bliss of equilibrium between the coiled energy <term>Kuṇḍalinī Śakti|the latent spiritual power within a person</term> and the moon of pure consciousness. 107. <-

-> He who remains filled with the joy of the union between the Supreme Energy and the Self—that is "sexual union" <term>Maithuna|spiritual union of the individual and universal</term>. Others are merely frequenters of women. 112. <-

***Reality of Union <note>original: "Maithuna"</note>:***
The Power <note>original: "Śakti"</note> of ordinary men with animal feelings remains asleep, but the Power of a Kaula is wide awake. One who serves this Power (the Power which is awake) is the real server of Power. One who experiences the Bliss arising out of the union of Supreme Power and his own Self is the real knower of Union. Others are just enjoyers of women.

O Lady of the Kula! Knowing thus the purport of the Five Gestures (the Five M’s, namely: Wine, Meat, Fish, Union, and Parched Grain) from the mouth of the Teacher, one who devotes himself to spiritual practice <note>original: "Sādhanā"</note>, becomes Released.

# The Sixth Flash

<br/>

-> Pure in soul, avoiding excessive accumulation, free from anger and greed; <-
-> averse to the vows of the "animal" state <note>original: "pashu-vrata," referring to the lower, uninitiated spiritual path</note>, and of happy countenance—such a person should worship, O Beloved. || 6 || <-

Pure of heart, devoid of anger and greed, superbly joyous, averse to the inferior observances of ordinary men, and with a cheerful countenance, a practitioner <term>Sadhaka|one who follows a specific spiritual discipline</term> should engage himself in worship.

After a long time, when due to My grace, love and lasting devotion arise in a practitioner, then O My Beloved! he should offer to the Deity libations of ritual substances prescribed by the Lord in accordance with the instructions of a teacher. Otherwise, he will meet his downfall.

O Goddess! He should worship the sacred wheel with the union of mantras. Only then, accompanied by You, I accept that worship with distinction.

-> Realizing "I am the Lord" <note>original: "Bhairavo'ham"</note> and endowed with qualities like omniscience, <-

"I am the Lord," with this realization and equipped with qualities like knowledge of everything, a superior practitioner should engage himself in the Kula worship.

-> Endowed with these characteristics, the follower of the Kula path <note>original: "Kaulika"</note>, steady in his vows, <-
-> who worships You, O Goddess, becomes a vessel for both worldly enjoyment and spiritual liberation. || 11 || <-

Possessing the above qualities and following the prescribed rules, when a follower of the Kula path worships You, O Goddess! only then he becomes eligible for enjoyment and emancipation.

<br/>

-> In a secluded, lonely forest, in a place free from disturbances, <-
-> seated in a comfortable posture, facing either East or North— || 12 || <-

->*Place and Seat for Kula-pūjā:*<-

The worshipper should seat himself in a comfortable position which gives stability, and face either North or East, at an isolated place or in a forest or at a place which may be free from disturbances.

# The Kularnava Tantra

<br/>

### The Visualization of the Sacred Island

-> One should contemplate the ruby pavilion, shining with walls of gems, <-
-> situated beneath the Wish-Fulfilling Trees <term>Kalpavṛkṣas|mythological trees that grant all desires</term> on the Island of Jewels in the center of the Sea of Nectar. || 13 || <-
-> This pavilion is adorned with canopies of flower-garlands, enclosed by secret curtains, <-
-> illumined by camphor lamps, and fragrant with the sweet scent of incense. || 14 || <-
-> Meditating upon oneself as seated within that pavilion with a calm and steady mind, <-
-> one should perform the Kula-worship <term>Kula-pūjā|the specific ritual practice of the Kula lineage</term>, O Goddess, by the command of the spiritual teacher. || 15 || <-

<br/>

### The Five Purifications

-> Purification of the self, the place, the mantra, the materials, and the deity; <-
-> let these be the five purifications. || 16 <note>original: "pañca-śuddhi"</note> || <-

Until the practitioner <term>Mantrī|one who uses mantras; a practitioner</term> performs these five, how can there be any true worship of the Divine?

-> O Beloved! Purification of the self is said to be achieved through a good bath, <-
-> the purification of the elements <term>Bhūta-śuddhi|a meditative process of dissolving the physical body into its primal elements and rebuilding it in a divine form</term>, breath control <term>Prāṇāyāma|disciplined breathing exercises</term>, <-
-> and the various ritual placements of sound upon the body <term>Nyāsa|the practice of "layering" or "touching" divine energy onto specific parts of the body</term>. || 17 || <-

<br/>

### Purification of the Space and Mantra

-> Cleaning, anointing, and making the area as clear and bright as the surface of a mirror, <-
-> then decorating it with canopies, incense, lamps, and flower-garlands, <-
-> and drawing designs with powders of five colors—this is called purification of the place. || 18 || <-

Cleaning, wiping, and anointing the place of worship so that it shines like a mirror, and then decorating it with flowers, garlands, incense, camphor, lights, and five colors is called purification of the place of worship.

-> Intertwining the letters of the Root Mantra <term>Mūla-mantra|the primary, foundational sound-syllable of the deity</term> with the letters of the sacred alphabet <term>Mātṛkā|the "mother" sounds of the Sanskrit alphabet</term>, <-
-> twice through in both forward and reverse order, is called purification of the Mantra. || 19 || <-

<br/>

### Sixth Flash

<br/>

-> One who knows the ritual method should sprinkle the materials of worship, <-
-> and show the Cow Gesture <term>Dhenu Mudrā|a hand gesture symbolizing the flowing of divine nectar from a cow's udder</term>; this is called the purification of materials. || 20 <note>original: "dravya-śuddhi"</note> || <-

The purification of the materials of worship is achieved by sprinkling water on them while reciting the "Root-Weapon" Mantra <note>original: "Mūla-astra," often identified as 'Mūlaṁ phaṭ'</note> and then performing the Cow Gesture.

-> Having established the Deity upon the sacred seat and making the Deity whole, <-
-> the wise practitioner <term>Sādhaka|a spiritual adept or seeker</term>, with an illumined soul, <-
-> should sprinkle the Deity three times with the water of the materials sanctified by ritual placement. <-
-> This is called the purification of the Deity. || 21 <note>original: "deva-śuddhi"</note> || <-

By invoking life into the Deity on the ceremonial seat <term>Pīṭha|a sacred stool or platform</term> and visualizing Him in His complete form—with all limbs and attributes—the practitioner sprinkles the Deity thrice with water that has been consecrated through the ritual placement of energy <term>Nyāsa|the practice of touching parts of the body while reciting mantras to "place" divine power there</term> while chanting the primary mantra <term>Mūla Mantra|the core "root" mantra of the deity</term>.

-> After performing the five purifications in this way, one should then perform the worship. <-
-> That worship is said to be fruitful; otherwise, it becomes useless. || 22 || <-

Only after completing these five essential purifications—self, place, mantra, materials, and deity—should the practitioner begin the actual ritual. Only such worship bears fruit; without these steps, the effort is in vain.

-> O Beloved! Worship is said to be fruitless without a sacred diagram. <-
-> Therefore, one should draw a sacred diagram according to the rules and worship there. || 23 <note>original: "maṇḍala"</note> || <-

**The Necessity of Sacred Diagrams in Worship:**

O My Beloved! Ritual worship is considered ineffective if performed without a sacred diagram <term>Maṇḍala|a geometric map of the cosmos used as a focal point for deities</term>. Therefore, these diagrams must be drawn according to traditional law, and the worship must be conducted within them.

-> Pervading the Universe exists the shape of an unbroken circle. <-
-> That which adorns the three worlds is the sacred diagram, which is eternally Shiva himself. || 24 <note>original: "Sadā-Śiva"</note> || <-

The shape of the unbroken circle <note>original: "akhanda-mandala-akaram"</note> exists everywhere, pervading the entire universe. The sacred diagram that circumscribes the three realms of existence is the very form of the Eternal Shiva.

-> Uḍḍīyāna is a square; Kāmarūpa is a circle; <-
-> Jālandhara is a half-moon; and Pūrṇagiri is a triangle. || 25 || <-
-> After honoring the sacred diagram, one should establish the supports in their proper order. <-

The four great seats of power <note>referring to the four primary Śākta Pīṭhas or centers of energy</note> are associated with specific shapes: the **Uḍḍīyāna** seat is a four-sided square; the **Kāmarūpa** seat is a circle; the **Jālandhara** seat is a semi-circle or crescent; and the **Pūrṇagiri** seat is a triangle. Once these diagrams are honored, the physical supports for the ritual should be placed in their correct sequence.

<meta>This page continues the Sixth Flash (Ṣaṣṭha Ullāsaḥ) of the Kularnava Tantra. Following the five purifications (Pañca-śuddhi) described on the previous page, the text now details the specific ritual vessels and the quality of the substances used within them.</meta>

### In the Kularnava Tantra

<br/>

-> The five vessels: the Common, Fortune, Guru, Enjoyment, and Sacrifice vessels. || 26 || <-

*The Common Vessel and others, being the five Vessels <note>original: "pātras"</note>:*

The common vessel for offering water <term>Sāmānya-arghya-pātra|the primary vessel used for general libations</term>, the Vessel of Fortune <note>original: "Śrīpātra"</note>, the Teacher’s Vessel <note>original: "Guru-pātra"</note>, the Vessel of Enjoyment <note>original: "Bhoga-pātra"</note>, and the Vessel of Sacrifice <note>original: "Bali-pātra"</note> constitute the five ritual containers.

-> One should not use only two vessels, or three, or just one. <-
-> Arranging them from his right to his left, <-
-> the practitioner should worship them and fill them with ritual liquor. || 27 || <-
-> O Goddess of the Kula, one who knows the placement should fill them <-
-> while reciting the Root Mantra. <-
-> There, one should drop fish and meat, <-
-> each in the quantity of a single bean. || 28 || <-

A practitioner <term>Sādhaka|a spiritual seeker or adept</term> must avoid using an incorrect number of vessels, such as one, two, or three, as the ritual requires the full set. After arranging the vessels in a line from right to left, they are filled with consecrated liquor <term>Āsava|a fermented ritual beverage</term> while chanting the deity's primary sacred sound <term>Mūla-Mantra|the "root" mantra unique to the specific deity being worshipped</term>. Small portions of fish <note>original: "matsya"</note> and meat <note>original: "māṁsa"</note>, each about the weight of a single black-gram bean <term>Māṣa|a traditional unit of weight based on a seed</term>, are then added to the vessels.

-> Materials that are ruined, stale, leftover, <-
-> foul-smelling, or lacking any scent— <-
-> or ritual liquids held in another's vessel— <-
-> make the libation completely fruitless. || 29 || <-

*Determining the proper materials <note>original: "dravyas"</note> for Libations:*

Offerings that are spoiled, old, already tasted by others, or have an unpleasant or absent odor are forbidden. Additionally, using the ritual wine <term>Hetu or Madya|technical terms for the consecrated alcohol used in Tantric rites</term> that belongs to or is contained in another person's vessel will render the ceremony ineffective.

-> O Goddess of the Kula, one should not fill the vessels with such unpleasant things! <-
-> With materials that are delicious, fragrant, and delightful, <-
-> resembling the nectar of immortality, O Great Queen— <-
-> only then does the libation become successful. || 30 || <-

The Goddess <note>original: "Kuleśvari"</note> is told that only the highest quality ingredients should be used. The offerings must be pleasing to the senses and resemble the divine nectar <note>original: "amṛta"</note> to ensure the spiritual goals of the ritual are met.

-> Unconsecrated wine brings sin, strife, disease, and sorrow. <-
-> It destroys lifespan, fortune, fame, luck, wealth, and grain. || 31 || <-

*Uncultured or unconsecrated wine <note>original: "Surā"</note> is prohibited:*

Wine that has not undergone the proper tantric "culturing" or consecration is considered dangerous. Rather than providing spiritual liberation, it leads to social and physical ruin, depleting both the practitioner's merit and their worldly prosperity.

-> Therefore, one must duly consecrate the ritual substance before worshipping it. <-
-> Otherwise, both the giver and the consumer will go to hell; of this, there is no doubt. || 32 || <-

Every ritual substance <term>Kula-dravya|the sacred materials, such as wine, used within the Kula tradition</term> must be purified according to the prescribed rites. Failure to do so results in severe spiritual consequences for everyone involved in the offering.

<summary>This page defines the five specific ritual vessels (pātras) required for ceremony and emphasizes the strict necessity of using high-quality, consecrated materials—including fish, meat, and wine—while warning of the spiritual and worldly ruin caused by using unpurified substances.</summary>

# Sixth Flash

<br/>

-> Without the proper ritual consecration <note>original: "dravya-ādivāsena"</note> of substances, one should neither perform silent recitation <term>Japa|the meditative repetition of a mantra</term> nor meditate <note>original: "smaret"</note>, O Beloved! <-
-> Those foolish people who do so suffer at every step. || 33 || <-

Without the proper consecration of ritual substances <term>Dravyas|the materials used in Tantric ritual, such as wine, meat, or grain</term>, one should neither perform Japa nor Dhyāna <term>Dhyāna|focused meditation or visualization</term>. O My Beloved! Those who do so suffer pain at every step.

-> Without ritual liquor <note>original: "āsava"</note>, the sacred sound is not a mantra; without the mantra, the liquor is merely mundane. <-
-> Because of this mutual contradiction, how can worship be correctly performed? || 34 || <-
-> If there is any doubt regarding this, one should clarify it from the mouth of a Teacher. <-

Without ritual liquor <note>original: "Āsava"</note>—here referring to *spiritous liquor* used in a sacred context—the Mantra is not a Mantra, and without the Mantra, the liquor remains unsanctified and useless. How can there be worship when there is such mutual contradiction? If there is any doubt in this connection, it should be clarified by the words of a Teacher <note>original: "Guru"</note>.

-> Through gazing, sprinkling, meditation, and purification by mantra and gesture, <-
-> the substance becomes fit for offering libations, bringing joy to the Deity. || 35 || <-

Substances <note>original: "Dravyas"</note> purified by specific ritual acts—beholding <note>original: "Vikṣaṇa"</note>, sprinkling with water <note>original: "Prokṣaṇa"</note>, meditation <note>original: "Dhyāna"</note>, the recitation of sacred sounds <note>original: "Mantra"</note>, and ritual hand gestures <term>Mudrā|symbolic or ritual gestures used to channel energy</term>—are fit for offering libations because such consecrated substances please the Deity.

-> Through the twenty-four mantras of Fire, Sun, Moon, Brahma, Indra, Vishnu, Rudra, and Sadasiva, <-
-> the liquor indeed becomes the Supreme Nectar. || 36 || <-

With the twenty-four Mantras of the divine powers—Agni (Fire), Sūrya (Sun), Indu (the Moon), Brahmā (the Creator), Indra (the King of Gods), Viṣṇu (the Preserver), Rudra (the Destroyer), and Sadāśiva (the Eternal Shiva)—the ritual liquor <note>original: "Madya"</note> is transformed into Supreme Nectar <note>original: "Parāmṛtam"</note>.

-> Amrita, Manada, Pusha, Tushti, Pushti, Rati, Dhriti, <-
-> Shashini, Chandrika, Kanti, Jyotsna, Shri, Priti, Angada, <-
-> Purna, and Purnamrita—thus they are called, O Queen of the Kula. || 37 || <-
-> These sixteen peaceful, desire-fulfilling energies arise from the vowels. || 38 || <-

-> *Sixteen desire-fulfilling phases of the Moon <note>original: "Candra-kalā"</note> originating from the Vowels <note>original: "Svaras"</note>:* <-

Amṛtā (The Immortal), Mānadā (The Giver of Honor), Pūṣā (The Nourisher), Tuṣṭi (Contentment), Puṣṭī (Abundance), Rati (Delight), Dhṛti (Fortitude), Śasinī (The Moon-like), Candrikā (Moonlight), Kānti (Radiance), Jyotsnā (Illumination), Śrī (Prosperity), Prīti (Affection), Aṅgadā (Bestower of Limbs/Strength), Pūrṇā (The Full), and Pūrṇāmṛtā (The Full Nectar) are the sixteen desire-fulfilling phases <note>original: "Kalās"</note> of the Moon <note>original: "Candramā"</note>, which originate from the sixteen Vowels of the Sanskrit alphabet.

-> Tapini, Tapini, Dhumra, Marichi, Jvalini, Ruchi, <-
-> Sushumna, Bhogada, Vishva, Rodhini, Dharini, Kshama; <-
-> These twelve solar energies, beginning with the 'Ka-Bha' group and ending with 'Tha-Da', give wealth. || 39 || <-

-> *Twelve wealth-giving phases of the Sun <note>original: "Saura-kalās"</note> associated with the consonant groups 'Ka-Bha' to 'Tha-Da':* <-

Tapinī (The Burning), Tāpinī (The Inflaming), Dhūmrā (The Smoky), Marīci (The Ray of Light), Jvālini (The Blazing), Ruci (The Lustrous), Suṣumnā (The Very Gracious), Bhogadā (The Giver of Enjoyment), Viśvā (The Universal), Rodhinī (The Obstructing), Dhāriṇī (The Supporting), and Kṣamā (The Forbearing) are the twelve wealth-giving Solar phases <note>original: "Saura-kalās"</note> which are mapped to specific groups of Sanskrit consonants <note>beginning with the "Ka-Bha" group and ending in the "Tha-Ḍa" group</note>.

## Sixth Flash

> Cessation, Foundation, Knowledge, and Peace;
> Kindling, Illuminating, Emptying, Liberating, and the Supreme;
> Subtle, the Subtle Nectar, the Nectar of Wisdom, and the Nectar;
> The Nourishing, the Pervasive, and the Sky-formed. These are the sixteen energies born of the vowels.

### *Sixteen energies of grace <term>Anugraha-kalās|specific divine powers or "phases" that bestow spiritual favor and transformation</term> originating from Subtle Sound <note>original: "Nāda"</note> and born out of the Ever-Auspicious One <note>original: "Sadāśiva"</note>:*

Nivṛtti <note>Cessation</note>, Pratiṣṭhā <note>Foundation</note>, Vidyā <note>Knowledge</note>, Śānti <note>Peace</note>, Indhikā <note>Kindling</note>, Dīpikā <note>Illuminating</note>, Recikā <note>Emptying/Breathing out</note>, Mocikā <note>Liberating</note>, Parā <note>Supreme</note>, Sūkṣmā <note>Subtle</note>, Sūkṣmāmṛtā <note>Subtle Nectar</note>, Jñānā <note>Wisdom</note>, Amṛtā <note>Nectar/Immortality</note>, Āpyāyanī <note>Nourishing</note>, Vyāpinī <note>Pervasive</note>, and Vyoma-rūpā <note>Sky-formed/Ethereal</note> are the sixteen energies of grace originating from the primordial vibration and born of the highest state of Shiva.

> First is the "Swan" mantra of nature; then the "Behold Vishnu" mantra;
> The "Three-Eyed One" is the third; the fourth begins with "That state of Vishnu";
> "May Vishnu prepare the womb" is the fifth in the sequence of creation.
> These ninety-four mantras grant the perfection of the deity's state. || 47–48 ||

### *Mantras for the Purification of Elements:*

After the worship of the energies of the Creator <note>original: "Brahma-kalā"</note> with the *Hamśaḥ* <note>original: "I am He/The Swan"</note> mantra, etc.; then the worship of the energies of the Preserver <note>original: "Viṣṇu-kalās"</note> with the *Pratadviṣṇu* <note>original: "Behold Vishnu"</note>, etc., mantra; then the worship of the energies of the Destroyer <note>original: "Rudra-kalās"</note> with the *Tryambakaṃ* <note>original: "The Three-Eyed One"</note>, etc., mantra; then another worship of the Destroyer's energies with the *Tad Viṣṇoḥ* <note>original: "That [highest step] of Vishnu"</note>, etc., mantra; and finally the worship of the energies of the Ever-Auspicious One <note>original: "Sadāśiva-kalās"</note> with the *Viṣṇuryoni* <note>original: "May Vishnu [prepare] the womb"</note>, etc., mantra should be performed. By worshipping with these ninety-four mantras, the perfections <term>Siddhis|attainments or supernatural powers</term> of the mantra, the individual self <note>original: "Ātmā"</note>, and the state of the deity are obtained.

> The chanting of the mantras is declared, as is the praise of the Self with five verses.
> O Queen of the Clan! These are the five mantras declared here. || 49 ||

O Queen of the Clan! <note>A title for the Goddess, the recipient of these teachings.</note> These are the five aforementioned mantras. After the ritual recitation <note>original: "Japa"</note> of these mantras, one should invite the First Element with the following verses (50-52).

> In this vessel of the supreme nectar, which is a mine of the joy of one unbroken essence,
> O Form of the Absolute, place here your spontaneous radiance. || 50 ||
> O Form of Nectar residing in the Absolute, O Supreme One who grants the knowledge of perfection,
> Bestow the state of immortality upon this fluid substance. || 51 ||
> Having achieved a state of one-ness with that essence, O Form of Reality,
> Become the supreme nectar and awaken the flash of consciousness within me. || 52 ||
> The syllable of the origin of speech is at the side; the Earth and nourishment are joined with the moon;
> Stability is adorned with the moon for the sake of the grace of fire. || 53 ||

# In the Kularnava Tantra

->Joined with the steady "i", "e", and the crescent moon; the white one joined with the two dots of light;<-
->Then one should speak the word "Nectar," and after that "Born of Nectar." || 54 ||<-
->Having then said "Goddess of Nectar," followed by "Showerer of Nectar,"<-
->One should say "Flow the Nectar" twice; ending with the fire-mantra <note>original: "dviṭhā" referring to "Svāhā"</note>, it purifies the ritual substances.<-
->The mantra of the Nectar-Goddess is declared to consist of thirty-five syllables. || 55 ||<-

### *The Nectar-Goddess Mantra <term>Amṛteśī Mantra|A powerful invocation used to transform ritual offerings into "Amṛta" or the nectar of immortality</term>:*

Now, the repetition <note>original: "Japa"</note> of the thirty-five-lettered Mantra named the Nectar-Goddess should be performed. The expanded form of this Mantra is:

->Aiṃ Plūṃ Srauṃ Jūṃ Saḥ <note>These are seed-syllables representing speech, stability, and life-force</note> O Nectar, O Thou born of Nectar, O Goddess of Nectar, O Showerer of Nectar, flow the nectar, flow the nectar, Svāhā! <note>Hail / May the offering be made</note><-

->The seed of speech <note>Aiṃ</note>, the word "Speak" twice, then "Speaker of Speech," then the seed of speech again;<-
->Then the seed of the King of Desire <note>Klīṃ</note>, then "O Moist One," "O Drencher," and "Drench!"; || 56 ||<-
->Then "Grant great liberation," the word "Grant" twice, followed by the seed of the King of Desire;<-
->Thirdly, after the word "Liberation," one should say "Grant" twice; || 57 ||<-
->Finally, the seed of Grace <note>Srauṃ</note> should be at the end, making thirty-seven syllables.<-
->This is called the Illuminating Mantra <note>original: "Dīpanī-manur"</note>, O Beloved, which grants all spiritual perfections. || 58 ||<-

After this, the repetition of the thirty-seven-lettered Mantra named the Illuminator should be performed, which provides all the perfections <note>original: "Siddhis"</note>. The expanded form of the Mantra is:

->Aiṃ Speak, speak, O Speaker of Speech, Aiṃ Klīṃ O Moist One, O Drencher, Drench! Grant great liberation, grant, grant! Klīṃ Hsrauṃ grant liberation, grant, grant! Hsrauṃ Srauṃ!<-

->These energies, the Mother-letters of the alphabet, the "Unique Whole" mantra and those following,<-
->The Nectar-Goddess, the Illuminator, and the Root Mantra in their proper order; || 59 ||<-
->One, two, three, four, five, and eight times respectively, O Mother,<-
->Having remembered them and worshipped the vessel, one should honor it with the Cow Gesture. || 60 ||<-

### Method of Vessel Purification:

Now the mantras of (i) the Divine Energies <note>Kalā</note>, (ii) the Mother-letters <note>Mātṛkā</note>, (iii) the "Fragment of the Universe" mantra <note>Akhaṇḍaika-mantra</note>, (iv) the Nectar-Goddess, (v) the Illuminator, and (vi) the Root Mantra <note>Mūla-mantra</note> should be meditated upon in sequence, repeated one, two, three, four, five, and eight times respectively. After this, the ritual worship of the vessels should be performed and the Cow Gesture <term>Dhenu Mudrā|A ritual hand position that resembles the udder of a cow, used to signify the flowing of divine milk or nectar</term> should be shown to them.

->Born from the fragments of the cosmic egg, filled with all the world's essences,<-
->O Great Vessel, now full, bring forth the essence of the nectar of immortality. || 61 ||<-

### *Mantra for Vessel purification:*

The vessels should be purified by this prayer (Verse 61).

# Sixth Flash

->With those same purified substances—with incense, flowers, and unbroken rice—<-
->and with all the mantras prescribed for ritual placement <term>Nyāsa|The practice of 'placing' mantras into the body by touching specific points, turning the physical body into a divine vessel</term>, one should worship one's own self, O Beloved. || 62 ||<-
->In the crown of the head, one should worship the lines of the Holy Teachers <note>original: "Śrī-guru-paṅktī"</note>, and in the root-center <term>Mūlādhāra|The 'root-support' energy center located at the base of the spine</term>, one should worship the sandals <note>original: "pādukā," representing the feet/authority of the teacher</note>.<-

Thereafter, O My Beloved! With the ritual substances <note>original: "Dravyas"</note> purified in the manner described before, using incense, flowers, and unbroken rice <note>original: "Akṣata"</note>, and also with all the Mantras used for ritual placement, one should worship himself. The entire lineage of Teachers should be worshipped in the head, and the Holy Sandals should be worshipped in the root-center.

->In the Divine Lineage <term>Divyaugha|The 'Lineage of the Gods,' the highest tier of teachers consisting of primordial deities</term> are the First Lord <note>original: "Ādinātha"</note> and His Power <note>original: "Śakti"</note>; the Eternal Śiva; || 63 ||<-

### *The Line of Gurus called the Divine, the Perfected, and the Human:*

**The Divine Lineage <note>original: "Divyaugha"</note>:**
1-2. The Primordial Lord <note>Ādinātha</note> and His Power <note>Śakti</note>; 3-4. Eternal Śiva <note>Sadāśiva</note> and His Wife; 5-6. The Lord <note>Īśvara</note> and His Wife <note>Bhāryā</note>; 7-8. The Howler <note>Rudra</note> and His Bride <note>Vadhū</note>; 9-10. The Pervader <note>Viṣṇu</note> and His Beloved; 11-12. The Creator <note>Brahmā</note> and his Wife—these are the twelve Divine Teachers.

->In the Lineage of the Perfected <term>Siddhaugha|The 'Lineage of the Perfected ones,' semi-divine sages who attained liberation through yoga and tantra</term> are Sanaka, Sanandana, and Sanātana;<-
->Sanatkumāra, Sanatsujāta, and the one born of Ṛbhukṣa <note>Ṛbhukṣaja</note>; || 65 ||<-
->Dattātreya, Raivataka, and thereafter Vāmadeva;<-
->Then Vyāsa and Śuka—these eleven are proclaimed. || 66 ||<-

**The Perfected Lineage <note>original: "Siddhaugha"</note>:**
1. Sanaka, 2. Sanandana, 3. Sanātana, 4. Sanatkumāra, 5. Sanatsujāta, 6. Ṛbhukṣaja, 7. Dattātreya, 8. Raivataka, 9. Vāmadeva, 10. Vyāsa, and 11. Śuka are the eleven Perfected Teachers.

->In the Lineage of Humans <term>Mānavaugha|The 'Lineage of Men,' historical or human gurus who transmitted the secret teachings</term> are the Man-Lion <note>Nṛsiṁha</note>, the Great Lord <note>Maheśa</note>, and the Sun <note>Bhāskara</note>;<-
->The King of Gods <note>Mahendra</note>, the Lord of Fortune <note>Mādhava</note>, and Viṣṇu—these six are celebrated. || 67 ||<-

**The Human Lineage <note>original: "Mānavaugha"</note>:**
1. Nṛsiṁha, 2. Maheśa, 3. Bhāskara, 4. Mahendra, 5. Mādhava, and 6. Viṣṇu are the six Human Teachers.

->One should add the word "Salutations" <note>original: "Namaḥ"</note> at the end, O Goddess; Supreme Śiva in the Divine Lineage;<-
->Great Śiva in the Perfected Lineage; and Eternal Śiva in the Human Lineage. || 68 ||<-

One should always add "Salutations" <note>Namaḥ</note> and "Supreme Śiva" <note>Parama Śiva</note> at the end of each name of the Divine class; "Salutations" and "Great Śiva" <note>Mahāśiva</note> at the end of each name of the Perfected class; and "Salutations" and "Eternal Śiva" <note>Sadāśiva</note> at the end of each name of the Human class.

### In the Kularnava Tantra

Then, after worshipping the sacred pedestal <term>Pīṭha|The ritual seat or base upon which the deity is established</term>, one should invoke the Goddess, O Beloved.

<note>original: "ततः पीठं समभ्यर्च्य देवीमावाहयेत् प्रिये।"</note>

"O Mother who dwells within the great forest of lotuses, the very embodiment of the bliss of the ultimate cause, the well-wisher of all beings—come here, O Supreme Goddess! O Goddess of gods, easily reached through devotion, accompanied by all Your surrounding attendants; for as long as I worship You here, please remain steady and present." || 69-70 ||

<note>original: "महापद्मवनान्तःस्थे कारणानन्दविग्रहे। सर्वभूतहिते मातरेहोहि परमेश्वरि।। देवेशि भक्तिसुलभे सर्वावरणसंयुते। यावत्त्वां पूजयामीह तावत्त्वं सुस्थिरा भव।।"</note>

**Mantra for the Invocation of Devi:**

Then, after worship of the **Pīṭha**, one should invoke the Devi with this sacred chant <term>Mantra|A sacred sound or phrase used as a spiritual tool</term> (the verses beginning "Residing in the great forest of lotuses..." through "remain steady," Verses 69-70).

Invoking Her with this mantra, one should worship the Goddess with a single-minded focus. Meditating upon Her and showing the ritual hand-gestures <term>Mudrā|Symbolic hand positions used to evoke specific energies or states of mind</term>, one should offer perfume, flowers, and unbroken rice <term>Akṣata|Whole, unpolished rice grains used in offerings to represent purity and completeness</term>, and other such items. || 71 ||

<note>original: "मन्त्रेणानेन चावाह्य यजेद्देवीमनन्यधीः। ध्यात्वा मुद्रां प्रदर्श्यार्चत् गन्धपुष्पाक्षतादिभिः।।"</note>

Invoking the Goddess with the above **Mantra**, one should contemplate upon the Goddess, show **Mudrā** and worship Her with incense, flowers, and **Akṣata**, etc.

Though the Supreme Reality <term>Brahman|The ultimate, formless reality or world-soul</term> is composed of pure consciousness, is immeasurable, without qualities, and without a physical body, a form is imagined for the benefit of spiritual seekers <term>Sādhakas|Practitioners who follow a disciplined path toward a goal</term>. || 72 ||

<note>original: "चिन्मयस्याप्रमेयस्य निर्गुणस्याशरीरिणः। साधकानां हितार्थाय ब्रह्मणो रूपकल्पना।।"</note>

**Imagination of the Form of Brahman:**

Although Bodiless, consisting of Pure Intelligence, Immeasurable and Attributeless, yet the Form of **Brahman** has been imagined for the benefit of the **Sādhakas**.

The pillar-symbol <term>Liṅga|The iconic, non-anthropomorphic representation of Shiva</term>, the ritual altar <term>Sthaṇḍila</term>, the sacred fire <term>Vahni</term>, water <term>Jala</term>, a winnowing fan <term>Sūrpa</term>, a pot <term>Kumbha</term>, a cloth or painting <term>Paṭa</term>, a ritual circle <term>Maṇḍala</term>, a wooden plank <term>Phalaka</term>, and within one's own head or heart—these ten locations are celebrated. || 73 ||
In these places, O Goddess of gods, those devoted to ritual action worship the Supreme Goddess, giving a form to the Formless. || 74 ||

<note>original: "लिङ्गस्थण्डिलवह्न्यम्बुसूर्पकुम्भपटेषु च। मण्डले फलके मूर्ध्नि हृदि वा दश कीर्त्तिताः।। एषु स्थानेषु देवेशि यजन्ति परमां शिवाम्। अरूपां रूपिणीं कृत्वा कर्मकाण्डरता नराः।।"</note>

**Ten places for the worship of Devi:**

**Liṅga** (symbol), **Sthaṇḍila** (altar), **Vahni** (fire), **Jala** (water), **Vastra** (garments/cloth), **Sūrpa** (winnowing fan), **Maṇḍala** (ritualistic circles), **Phalaka** (plank), **Mūrdhni** (head), and **Hṛdaya** (heart) are the ten places where, imagining a Form of the Formless, a **Sādhaka** engrossed in ritualistic practices, should worship the Supreme Shiva <note>original: "Paramā Śivā," here referring to the Goddess as the feminine aspect of the Supreme</note>.

Just as milk, though it pervades the entire body of a cow, only flows out from the teats of her udder; in the same way, the Divine, though all-pervading, shines forth most clearly in sacred images and other ritual objects. || 75 ||

<note>original: "गवां सर्वाङ्गगं क्षीरं स्त्रवेत् स्तनमुखाद् यथा। तथा सर्वगतो देवः प्रतिमादिषु राजते।।"</note>

**Reason for the Worship of a Symbol:**

Just as milk pervades the whole body of a cow, but it flows out only through the teats of her udder; in the same way the Divinity though all-pervading exists only in the Image and the like.

It explains that while the Divine is formless and all-pervading, practitioners use ten specific "locations" (like fire, water, or icons) to focus their devotion, just as milk is gathered from a specific part of a cow.</summary>

### Sixth Flash: Page 103

->The presence of the Divine is attained through the beauty of the image, the excellence of the ritual worship, and above all, the unwavering faith of the practitioner <term>Sādhaka|An aspirant or practitioner of a spiritual discipline</term>. || 76 ||<-
<note>original: "आभिरूप्याच्च बिम्बस्य पूजायाश्च विशेषतः । साधकस्य च विश्वासात् सन्निधौ देवता भवेत् ।।"</note>

->Clarified butter <term>Ghṛta|Ghee, or clarified butter, used in rituals and as a concentrated source of energy</term> exists within the body of a cow, yet it does not nourish the cow’s limbs while it remains in that state. Only when it is extracted through the proper process and then consumed does it provide nourishment. || 77 ||<-
<note>original: "गवां सर्पिः शरीरस्थं न करोत्यङ्गपोषणम् । स्वकर्मरचितं दत्तं पुनस्तामेव पोषयेत् ।।"</note>

->In the same way, O Goddess, the Supreme Sovereign <term>Parameśvarī|The female aspect of the Divine or the Great Goddess</term> dwells within all bodies like ghee in a cow. However, without dedicated worship <term>Upāsanā|Systematic devotion or "sitting near" the divine</term>, She does not bestow the fruits of spiritual practice upon humanity. || 78 ||<-
<note>original: "एवं सर्वशरीरस्था सर्पिर्वत् परमेश्वरी । विना चोपसनां देवि न ददाति फलं नृणाम् ।।"</note>

->One must unify the divine vital breaths <term>Prāṇa|The vital life-force or breath</term>, awaken the senses <term>Indriya|The faculties of perception and action</term>, and establish the deity’s life-force within the image. Only then should one perform the worship, O Goddess; otherwise, the rite remains fruitless. || 79 ||<-
<note>original: "सकलीकृत्य तत्प्राणान् समुद्दीपेन्द्रियाणि च । प्रतिष्ठाप्यार्चयेद्देवि चान्यथा निष्फलं भवेत् ।।"</note>

### *Importance of Adhering to Rules :*

->Should there be deficiencies in the sacred chants <term>Mantra|A sacred sound or syllable used as a spiritual tool</term>, the ritual actions, or the prescribed procedures, the practitioner should perfect all those missing parts and steps by seeking the forgiveness of the Deity <term>Devatā|The specific form of the Divine being worshipped</term>. || 80 ||<-
<note>original: "मन्त्रहीनं क्रियाहीनं विधिहीनञ्च यद् भवेत् । क्षमया साधयेत् सर्व हीनमङ्गं पदं तथा ।।"</note>

->Whatever action one performs in violation of the rules yields no fruit at all due to the error in sequence. || 81 ||<-
<note>original: "नियमादतिरेकेण यद् यत् कर्म करोति यः । न किञ्चिदप्यस्य फलं सिध्यति क्रमदोषतः ।।"</note>

->Actions that are either insufficient or excessive never bear fruit; only those virtuous deeds performed exactly as prescribed truly yield results. || 82 ||<-
<note>original: "न्यूनातिरिक्तकर्माणि न फलन्ति कदाचन । यथाविधि कृतानीह सत्कर्माणि फलन्ति हि ।।"</note>

<summary>This page uses the analogy of ghee in a cow to explain that while the Divine is omnipresent, ritual worship and faith are necessary to manifest that presence and receive spiritual benefits. It also emphasizes the importance of following ritual procedures precisely, while allowing for the correction of errors through a plea for divine forgiveness.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Sixth Flash of the Kularnava Tantra. While the previous page established that the Divine presence is invoked through faith and the animation of an image, this page specifies the technical necessity of the Yantra (sacred diagram) as the specific "body" or vessel for the Deity during ritual worship.</meta>

### From the Kularnava Tantra

->Ritual actions performed during chanting <term>Japa|The meditative repetition of a mantra or divine name</term>, fire offerings <term>Homa|A consecrated fire ritual where offerings are made to the deities</term>, and worship, when done according to the prescribed rules, please the Deity and grant the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and spiritual liberation. || 83 ||<-
<note>original: "तद्विधानकृतं कर्म जपहोमार्चनादिषु। देवताप्रीतिदं भूयाद् भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदम्।।"</note>

->For those who do not understand how the Mantra pervades the Deity—who is essentially formed of the Mantra itself—all efforts at worship and prayer become useless, O Shambhavi <term>Śāmbhavī|A title for the Goddess, referring to her as the consort of Shambhu or Shiva</term>! || 84 ||<-
<note>original: "देवस्य मन्त्ररूपस्य मन्त्रव्याप्तिमजानताम्। कृतार्थनादिकं सर्वं व्यर्थं भवति शाम्भवि।।"</note>

**The Unity of the Deity, the Mantra, and the Sacred Diagram**

->The Sacred Diagram <term>Yantra|A mystical geometric diagram used in Indian religions for focal points in worship and meditation</term> is said to be composed of Mantras, and the Deity is of the same nature as the Mantra. Therefore, O Goddess, when the Deity is worshipped within the Yantra, She is pleased immediately. || 85 ||<-
<note>original: "यन्त्रं मन्त्रमयं प्रोक्तं देवता मन्त्ररूपिणी। यन्त्रे सा पूजिता देवि सहसैव प्रसीदति।।"</note>

**The Origin of the word "Yantra"**

->Because it restrains and controls <term>Niyantraṇa|The act of governing, binding, or restraining</term> all the suffering born from faults such as desire and anger, it is called a "Yantra." The Deity is satisfied when worshipped within this instrument. || 86 ||<-
<note>original: "कामक्रोधादिदोषोत्थसर्वदुःखनियन्त्रणात्। यन्त्रमित्याहुरेतस्मिन् देवः प्रीणाति पूजितः।।"</note>

->Just as the physical body is for the soul <term>Jīva|The individual living being or soul</term>, and as oil <term>Sneha|Literally "oil" or "grease," but also implying the lubricating power of affection</term> or clarified butter is for a lamp, so too is the consecrated Yantra established as the foundation for all Deities. || 87 ||<-
<note>original: "शरीरमिव जीवस्य दीपस्य स्नेहवत् प्रिये। सर्वेषामपि देवानां तथायन्त्रं प्रतिष्ठितम्।।"</note>

->Therefore, after drawing the Yantra or meditating upon Shiva with His attendants, and having learned everything from the mouth of the Guru <term>Guru|A spiritual teacher who transmits sacred knowledge</term>, one should perform the worship according to the rules, O Beloved. || 88 ||<-
<note>original: "तस्माद् यन्त्रं लिखित्वा वा ध्यात्वा सावृत्तिकं शिवम्। ज्ञात्वा गुरुमुखात् सर्वं पूजयेद्विधिना प्रिये।।"</note>

**The Proper Method for Worshipping the Yantra**

->If one performs the worship of different deities on a single altar <term>Pīṭha|A sacred seat, pedestal, or platform for a deity</term> without using their specific Yantras, then by ignoring the relationship between the spirit and its form, that practitioner <term>Sādhaka|An aspirant or dedicated spiritual practitioner</term> incurs the curse of the Deities. || 89 ||<-
<note>original: "एकपीठे पृथक्पूजां विना यन्त्रं करोति यः। अङ्गित्वं परित्यज्य देवताशापमाप्नुयात्।।"</note>

<summary>This page defines the Yantra as the essential "body" of the Deity and the "restrainer" of worldly suffering, warning that worship is ineffective or even harmful without the proper geometric diagram and a teacher's guidance.</summary>

# Sixth Flash

->In a single sacred seat <term>Pītha|A consecrated altar or ritual space</term>, O Queen of the Kula, one should worship the deities along with their retinues separately in their respective mystical diagrams <term>Yantra|Geometric diagrams that serve as the body of the deity</term>, according to the specific rules. || 60 ||<-
<note>original: "एकपीठे कुलेशानि स्वे स्वे यन्त्रे पृथक्पृथक्। यजेदावरणोपेता देवतास्तद्विधानतः।।"</note>

->If a practitioner <term>Mantrin|One who utilizes mantras; a ritualist</term> of unstable mind invokes one deity but then proceeds to worship another, he receives a curse from both deities. || 61 ||<-
<note>original: "आवाह्य देवतामेकां पूजयेदन्यदेवताम्। उभाभ्यां लभते शापं मन्त्री चञ्चलमानसः।।"</note>

->O Beloved! Knowing these principles from the Teacher <term>Guru|The spiritual preceptor who initiates the student</term> and from the scriptures, one should perform the worship correctly; then the Deity is fully pleased. || 62 ||<-
<note>original: "इत्यादिलक्षणं ज्ञात्वा गुरुतः शास्त्रतः प्रिये। विधिनाभ्यर्चयेत् सम्यग्देवता सुप्रसीदति।।"</note>

->One should worship the benevolent Lord <term>Shiva|The auspicious one; the supreme deity of the Tantras</term> along with his various limbs and retinues using the sixteen types of offerings <term>Upacāra|Specific services offered to a deity, such as water, flowers, or incense</term>, the primary mantra <term>Mūla Mantra|The 'root' or principal mantra of the deity</term>, scents, flowers, and consecrated grains <term>Akṣata|Whole, unhusked rice grains used in ritual</term>. || 63 ||<-
<note>original: "षोडशैरुपचारैस्तु साङ्गं सावरणं शिवम्। पूजयेन्मूलमन्त्रेण गन्धपुष्पाक्षतादिभिः।।"</note>

->O Goddess of Shambhu! One should worship all the members of the divine family mentioned in the Great Sixfold Rite <term>Mahāṣoḍhā|A complex ritual arrangement of various groups of deities</term> by calling their individual names, starting with the sacred syllable 'Om' <term>Praṇava|The cosmic primordial sound</term> and ending with 'Salutations' <term>Namaḥ|A term of obeisance or bowing</term>. || 64 ||<-
<note>original: "महाषोढोदिताशेषपरिवाराम्श्च शाम्भवि। प्रणवादिन्मोऽन्तेन तत्तन्नाम्ना समर्चयेत्।।"</note>

### **The Method for Offering Libations**

->Following the path revealed in the scriptures, one should offer libations with drops of the consecrated ritual fluid <term>Ali-bindu|Literally 'bee-drops'; a tantric term for consecrated wine or ritual nectar</term>. || 65 ||<-
<note>original: "आगमोक्तेन मार्गेण तर्पयेदलिबिन्दुभिः।"</note>

->Using the thumb and the ring finger <term>Anāmikā|Literally 'the nameless finger'; the fourth finger</term>, with the nails turned upward, let the fluid flow from your own vessel according to the rules, O Queen of the Kula. || 65 (cont.) ||<-
<note>original: "अङ्गुष्ठानामिकाभ्याञ्च नखै निःसृतमूर्ध्वतः। स्वापात्रस्पन्दनिष्यन्दं विधिवत् कुलनायिके।।"</note>

->After offering libations once, chanting the root mantra and the sacred lineage mantra <term>Pādukā|Literally 'sandals'; referring to the mantra of the Guru's feet/lineage</term>, and awakening the internal spiritual power, one should offer libations to the deities residing within the body. || 66 ||<-
<note>original: "सकृत्तर्पणमुत्सृज्य जप्त्वा मूलञ्च पादुकाम्। अन्तःशक्ति समुत्थाप्य तर्पयेद्देहदेवताः।।"</note>

->The thumb represents the God <term>Bhairava|The fierce and transformative aspect of Shiva</term> and the ring finger represents the Goddess <term>Caṇḍikā|A fierce form of the Mother Goddess</term>. By joining the thumb and ring finger together, one should offer libations to the entire lineage of the Kula. || 67 ||<-
<note>original: "अङ्गुष्ठो भैरवो देवो अनामा चण्डिका प्रिये। अनामाङ्गुष्ठयोगेन तर्पयेत् कुलसन्ततिम्।।"</note>

<summary>This page details the ritual precision required in Tantric worship, emphasizing that deities must be worshiped in their specific Yantras and that libations must be offered using a specific mudra (thumb and ring finger) to honor the union of Bhairava and Chandika.</summary>
<keywords>Yantra, Upacara, Mula Mantra, Libation, Tarpana, Bhairava, Chandika, Ritual Protocol, Kularnava Tantra</keywords>

# In the Kularnava Tantra

One should offer libations <term>Tarpaṇa|A ritual offering of liquids, literally meaning 'to satisfy'</term> using the thumb and the ring finger for rituals of captivation <term>Vaśya|The magical act of attracting or enchanting others</term>. For rituals of magical charms <term>Abhicāra|Rituals intended to influence or harm others</term>, one should offer libations by joining the index finger with the thumb. O Beloved! For rituals of immobilization <term>Stambhana|The power to freeze or stop the actions or speech of an opponent</term>, one should offer libations by joining the little finger and the thumb. || 68 ||
<note>original: "अङ्गुष्ठानामिकाभ्याञ्च वश्यकर्मणि तर्पयेत्। तर्जून्यङ्गुष्ठयोगेन तर्पयेदभिcharके। कनिष्ठाङ्गुष्ठयोगेन स्तम्भने तर्पयेत् प्रिये।।"</note>

***

### The Worship of the Guru Lineage

O Queen of the Gods! Having thus offered libations according to the rules using the sacred substances <term>Kula-dravya|Specific substances used in Tantric ritual, such as consecrated wine or meat</term>, one should worship the lineage of Teachers <term>Guru-pāṅkti|The sequential line of spiritual preceptors through whom the tradition is transmitted</term> in front of the Deity. One should do this with an undistracted mind, having correctly understood the sequence of the three lines of Teachers. || 69 ||
<note>original: "एवं सन्तर्प्य देवेशि कुलद्रव्यैर्यथाविधि। देवतापुरतो देवि गुरुपङ्क्तीश्च पूजयेत्। पङ्क्तित्रयक्रमेणाथ ज्ञात्वा सम्यगनन्यधीः।।"</note>

One should worship the lineage of Teachers in their traditional order, holding the gesture of consciousness <term>Cinmudrā|A hand gesture where the thumb and index finger touch, symbolizing the union of the soul with the absolute</term> and a human skull cup <term>Nṛkapāla|A ritual vessel made from a cranium, common in left-handed Tantric paths</term> in their hands. They shine like molten gold, are anointed with red flower paste, and wear red garments. Their side-long glances are full of compassion, their eyes and matted hair have a reddish hue, and they are surrounded by the throngs of perfected beings <term>Siddha|Beings who have achieved spiritual perfection and magical powers</term>. || 100 ||
<note>original: "कराभ्यां चिन्मुद्रां समधृनृकपालञ्च दधतीम्। द्रुतस्वर्णप्रख्यामरुणकुसुमालेपवसनाम्। कृपापूर्णापाङ्गीमरुणनयनाम्बरजटा। मुपेतां सिद्धौघैर्यजतु गुरुपङ्क्तिं क्रमगतिम्।।"</note>

***

### Final Offerings

Having performed the meditations in this way, a practitioner <term>Sādhaka|An aspirant following a specific spiritual discipline</term> should offer incense, a ritual lamp, and food offerings. One should present spiritous liquor <term>Āsava|A fermented ritual drink</term> together with meat <term>Piśita|Flesh or meat</term>, various types of edible snacks, fruits such as bananas, and betel leaves. || 101 ||
<note>original: "एवं संपूज्य धूपश्च दीपं नैवेद्यमेव च। आसवं पिशितोपेतं भक्ष्याणि विविधानि च। कदल्यादिफलान्येव ताम्बूलञ्च समर्पयेत्।।"</note>

Thus, O Goddess, I have described to you the characteristics of the Kula path <term>Kulācāra|The specific conduct and tradition of the Kula sect</term>, the preparation of ritual substances, their purification, and the like. What else do you wish to hear? || 102 ||
<note>original: "इति ते कथितं देवि कुलाचारस्य लक्षणम्। द्रव्यसंस्कारशुद्ध्यादि किमन्यत् श्रोतुमिच्छसि।।"</note>

->Thus ends the Sixth Flash,<-
->named 'The Description of the Rules for the Consecration of Substances,'<-
->in the Upper Tradition of the Tantra,<-
->the fifth section of the 125,000-verse text,<-
->the Great Secret and Doorway to Liberation,<-
->the Illustrious Kularnava, the highest of all scriptures. || 6 ||<-
<note>original: "इति श्रीकुलार्णवे निर्वाणमोक्षद्वारे महारहस्ये सर्वागमोत्तमोत्तमे सपादलक्षग्रन्थे पञ्चम-खण्डे ऊर्ध्वाम्नायतन्त्रे द्रव्यसंस्कार-विधानकथनं नाम षष्ठ उल्लासः।"</note>

# The Seventh Flash

***

## The Divine Mother Spoke

->O Lord of the Clan <term>Kuleśa|A title for Shiva as the sovereign of the Kula, the spiritual 'family' or lineage</term>! Kindly tell me about the ritual offerings <term>Bali|A sacrificial offering or oblation presented to spirits or secondary deities</term> intended for the Youthful Guardian <term>Baṭuka|A fierce manifestation of Shiva, often appearing as a young boy, who protects the ritual space</term> and others, and the defining characteristics of the Feminine Power <term>Śakti|In this ritual context, the term refers to the female practitioner or the divine energy embodied in the ceremony</term>.<-

->O Ocean of Compassion! Tell me also about the proper acceptance of those ritual substances. || 1 ||<-
<note>original: "कुलेश बटुकादीनां बलिश्च शक्तिलक्षणम् । तद्रव्यस्यैव स्वीकारं वद मे करुणानिधे ।।"</note>

***

## The Lord Spoke

->Listen, O Goddess, for I shall explain what You have asked of Me. By the mere act of hearing this, the knowledge of ultimate reality <term>Tattva-jñāna|True spiritual insight into the nature of the universe and the self</term> shines forth. || 2 ||<-
<note>original: "शृणु देवि प्रवक्ष्यामि यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि । तस्य श्रवणमात्रेण तत्त्वज्ञानं प्रकाशते ।।"</note>

->O Queen of the Clan <term>Kuleśvarī|The female counterpart to Kuleśa; a title for the Goddess</term>! As long as the offering is not given to the Youthful Guardian, none of the deities are satisfied, even through meditation or acts of worship. || 3 ||<-
<note>original: "यावन्नो बटुके दत्तात्तावन्नैव कुलेश्वरि । तृप्यन्ति देवताः सर्वाः स्मरणाद् यजनादपि ।।"</note>

->Therefore, one should worship the Youthful Guardian and the other spirits with perfumes, flowers, spirituous liquor <term>Āsava|A type of fermented ritual drink</term>, and meat <term>Māṁsa|Meat used as a consecrated substance in Tantric ritual</term>. Through the specific rules and sacred sounds <term>Mantra|A sacred sound or syllable used as a tool for the mind in ritual</term> assigned to them, the Deity attains satisfaction. || 4 ||<-
<note>original: "बटुकादीन् यजेत्तस्माद् गन्धपुष्पासवामिषैः । तत्तन्मन्त्रविधानेन देवता प्रीतिमाप्नुयात् ।।"</note>

->Whatever collection of substances has been brought for the purpose of worship and enjoyment, O Queen of the Clan, should be offered with devotion to the Guardians of the Sacred Fields <term>Kṣetrapālas|Deities who protect specific sacred territories or ritual grounds</term>. || 5 ||<-
<note>original: "यत्किञ्चिद्द्रव्यसंघातं पूजार्थं भोगहेतुना । आनीतं दीयते भक्त्या क्षेत्रेभ्यः कुलेश्वरि ।।"</note>

->I shall now speak of the sacred sounds for the Youthful Guardian; listen, O Leader of the Clan <term>Kulanāyikā|Another title for the Goddess as the head of the lineage</term>. By merely performing worship with these, all obstacles and disturbances are destroyed. || 6 ||<-
<note>original: "बटुकमन्त्रान् वक्ष्यामि शृणुष्व कुलनायिके । यैः समर्चनमात्रेण सर्वे नश्यन्त्युपद्रवाः ।।"</note>

***

<summary>This page marks the beginning of the Seventh Flash, where Shiva begins explaining the essential role of secondary guardian deities like Baṭuka and the Kṣetrapālas in Tantric ritual. He emphasizes that the main deities cannot be satisfied until these guardians are properly honored with specific offerings of wine and meat.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Seventh Flash of the Kularnava Tantra.
