### In the Kularnava Tantra

> Three syllables of the sacred sound <note>original: "tāra-trayaṃ", referring to the Oṃ syllable</note>, followed by the words "Son of the Goddess" and "Youthful Guardian."
> Then "Lord," and "Resplendent with a mass of tawny matted hair." || 7 ||
>
> Then the word "Three-eyed," followed by the word "Fire-mouthed."
> Then "Take, take this worship and offering," ending with the Beloved of the Fire-God <note>original: "pāvakavallabhā", a ritual term for the word "Svāhā"</note>.
> This Baṭuka Mantra is thus declared to consist of forty-four letters. || 8 ||
>
> Satisfied by the ritual offering <term>Bali|A sacrificial gift of food or other substances presented to spirits</term>, the Youthful Guardian grants all spiritual successes.
> May he, who is served by spirits and ghouls <term>Vetāla|Spirits that inhabit corpses, often acting as guardians or servants to fierce deities</term>, grant me peace eternally. || 9 ||

*After extracting the components, the Mantra for the Youthful Guardian <term>Baṭuka|A fierce form of Shiva appearing as a young protector</term> runs as follows:*
**Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ! O Son of the Goddess! O Youthful Guardian Lord! O You who shine with a mass of tawny matted hair! O Three-eyed One! O Fire-mouthed One! Take, take this worship and offering! Svāhā!**

This is the Baṭuka Mantra of forty-four letters; reciting this, one should offer the oblations with the prayer: "*By this offering... served by ghouls*" (Verse 9 above).

> After the three sacred sounds, one should say the word "To all the Feminine Powers" <note>original: "sarvayoginībhyaḥ"</note>.
> After that, "To all beings," and "To those presiding over all beings." || 10 ||
>
> Then the word "To those Dakinis," and the word "To those Shakinis" <note>Classes of female spirits or attendants in the retinue of the Goddess</note>.
> Then the word "To those residing in the three worlds," followed by "this." || 11 ||
>
> "Worship and offering," then the double "Take, take," ending with "Svāhā." This is the Mantra of the Feminine Powers <term>Yoginī|Semi-divine female beings representing various aspects of the cosmic energy (Shakti)</term>.
> O Great Goddess <term>Maheśānī|A title for the consort of Shiva</term>! This mantra is said to consist of fifty letters. || 12 ||

*Mantra of Oblation for the Yoginīs:*
*After extraction, the fifty-lettered Yoginī Mantra runs thus:*
**Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ! To all Yoginīs! To all beings! To those presiding over all beings! To the Dakinis! To the Shakinis! To those residing in the three worlds! Take, take this worship and offering! Svāhā!**

> Whichever Yoginī is fierce, gentle, or most terrifying;
> Whether she moves in the sky, on the earth, or in the heavens—may she be pleased with me always. || 13 ||

While offering the ritual gift with the Yoginī Mantra, one should pray with this verse (*Whichever Yoginī... may she be pleased with me always*, Verse 13).

> One should say the three sacred sounds, then "To all beings," indeed.
> Then "To the Lord of all beings," ending with the heart-mantra—this consists of seventeen letters. || 14 ||
> <note>original: "hṛdayataḥ", usually implying the addition of the word "Namaḥ" or "Svāhā"</note>

*Mantra of Oblations for the Lord of All Beings <term>Sarvabhūtapati|A title for Shiva as the master of all created spirits and entities</term>:*
The seventeen-lettered Mantra, after extraction, runs as follows:
**Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ! To all beings! To the Lord of all beings! Svāhā!**

> Beings of various forms—celestial, terrestrial, or those that move in the atmosphere;
> Some residing in the underworld, all of whom are refined through the union with Shiva; || 15 ||
>
> The North Star and others, the speakers of truth, Indra and the other gods established in heaven;
> May they be satisfied, with pleased minds, and accept this offering. || 16 ||

While offering oblations with the above Mantra, one should pray with these words (*Beings of various forms... accept this offering*).

# Seventh Flash

> One should speak the three sacred sounds <note>original: "tāra-trayaṃ", the syllable Oṃ repeated thrice</note>, then say the word "Give" twice, followed by the word "Goddess."
> Then "To the Son, to the Youthful Guardian Lord," and then "to the One who takes the ritual remnants" <note>original: "ucchiṣṭahāriṇe", referring to the deity who consumes the leftovers of a sacrifice</note>. || 17 ||
>
> Then the words "From all obstacles," followed by "destroy" twice.
> Then "Take" twice, then the word "Ruru" <note>A fierce manifestation of Shiva</note>, followed by the word "Guardian of the Field."
> One should say "this worship and offering together with all ritual services."
> This mantra for the Guardian of the Field <term>Kṣetrapāla|The deity who protects a specific physical site or sacred ground</term> ends with "Take, take," O Beloved. || 18 ||
>
> It is declared to consist of sixty-four letters and bestows all spiritual attainments <term>Siddhi|Supranormal powers or spiritual perfections</term>.

### *Mantra of Oblation for the Guardians of the Field:*

The sixty-four-lettered Mantra which bestows all Siddhis, after extraction from the code, runs as follows:

**Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ! Give, give! To the Son of the Goddess, to the Youthful Guardian Lord, to the One who partakes of the ritual remnants! From all obstacles, destroy, destroy! Take, take! O Ruru! O Guardian of the Field! Together with all ritual services, take, take this worship and offering! Take, take! Svāhā!**

> "Whoever dwells in this field and is a servant of the Guardian,
> may he, pleased by this ritual offering <term>Bali|A sacrificial gift of food or other substances presented to spirits</term>, grant me full protection." || 19 ||

While offering oblations with the above Mantra, one should pray with these words (*"Whoever dwells in this field... grant me protection." Verse 19*).

> One should speak the three sacred sounds <note>original: "tāra", the Oṃ syllable</note>, followed by the mantras of the Resplendent Palace and the Supreme Goddess <note>original: "śrī-prāsāda-parā-manu", technical names for specific seed-syllables</note>.
> At the beginning, say "Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ" twice, followed by "To the one presided over by the Terrible One" <note>original: "bhairavādhiṣṭhitāya"</note>. || 20 ||
>
> Then "From the Unshakable Bliss," followed by "Giver of the heart's desires."
> After speaking the word "Realized Aim" <note>original: "siddhārtha"</note>, then the word "Descend" twice. || 21 ||
>
> Then the word "Guardian of the Field," followed by the word "Greatly Peaceful."
> Then the word "Son of the Mother," followed by the word "Son of the Clan." || 22 ||
>
> Then "Son of Success," and then the word "Overlord of the Place."
> Then "To the Overlord of the Village," and then "To the Overlord of the Region." || 23 ||
>
> One should say "Youthful Guardian Lord" <term>Baṭuka-nātha|A fierce form of Shiva appearing as a young protector</term>, followed by "Son of the Goddess."
> Then the word "Thunder-Sound," followed by "Fierce and Terrible." || 24 ||
>
> Then the word "Skull-Bearer," followed by the word "Terrifying."
> Then "To the Overlord of all obstacles," followed by "this worship and offering." || 25 ||
>
> One should say "Take, take," then "Do, do," and then "Remove my [obstacles]" twice.
> One should say "Shine, shine! Blaze, blaze!" and then "All obstacles." || 26 ||
>
> Then "Destroy" twice, then the syllables "Kṣāṃ Kṣeṃ," followed by the word "Wisdom."
> Then "To the Guardian of the Field, Vauṣaṭ Hūṃ." This consists of one hundred and sixty letters. || 27 ||

### *Mantra of Oblation for the King of Kings:*

The one hundred and sixty lettered Mantra, after extraction from the code, runs thus:

### *Places of offering Oblations to the Guardians, etc.*

Worshipping the Youthful Guardian in the West, the Female Spirits in the North, all Earthly Spirits in the East, and the Guardians of the Field in the South, one should, O Leader of the Clan, worship the King of Kings in the Center.

->The offering for the Youthful Guardian is remembered as being made with the thumb and the ring finger.<-
->With the index, middle, ring finger, and thumb, the offering for the Female Spirits is made. || 31 ||<-
->With all the fingers, the offering for the Earthly Spirits is prescribed, O Beloved.<-

### *Determination of Fingers in the Oblations of the Guardians, etc:*

One should offer sacrificial gifts to the Youthful Guardian with the thumb and ring finger; to the Female Spirits with the thumb, index, middle, and ring fingers; to all Earthly Spirits with all the fingers; to the Guardians of the Field with the thumb and index finger; and to the King of Kings with the thumb and middle finger. <note>These hand positions are known as Mudras and are thought to direct the energy of the offering to the specific class of being invoked.</note>

### *Ritual of the Clan Lamp and the Symptoms of Success:*

After worshipping the Youthful Guardians <note>original: Baṭuka</note>, etc., one should show the Clan Lamp. One should, out of well-kneaded light red-coloured flour, prepare nine, seven, or five triangular lamps of the shape of a big hourglass drum <note>original: Ḍamarū</note>. ### *The Order of Ritual Drinking:*

After showing the Clan Lamp, the practitioner <term>Sādhaka|An aspirant or practitioner of the Tantric path</term> should worship the Power <note>original: Śakti</note>.

One should first offer the drink to one’s own partner <note>original: Sva-śakti</note>, or a Heroic partner <term>Vīra-śakti|A woman qualified for the 'Heroic' (Vira) path of Tantra</term> who has been initiated through the path of the teacher. Only after she has drunk should the practitioner drink; this is the firm conclusion of the sacred scriptures <term>Śāstra|Authoritative religious texts</term>. || 37 ||

O Mother <note>original: Ambike</note>! If a woman is uninitiated, the practitioner should immediately perform the purificatory rite for her. She becomes pure through the rules of sacred sound initiation <term>Mantra-dīkṣā|The ritual process of being initiated into a sacred sound or power</term>, and not otherwise. || 38 ||

Therefore, viewing a woman of good characteristics as the Deity herself, one should worship her with incense, flowers, and sanctified unbroken rice <term>Akṣata|Grains of rice used in ritual, symbolizing wholeness</term>, and then offer her the vessel of ritual enjoyment <term>Bhoga-pātra|The cup containing the consecrated ritual drink</term>. || 39 ||

### *Purification of the Disciple’s Body:*

O My Beloved! With a pure heart, he purifies the disciple’s gross body using the twenty-four fundamental principles—from Primal Nature <term>Prakṛti</term> to Earth <term>Pṛthivī</term>—along with the vowels containing the Seed-Syllable of Speech <note>original: "Vāgbhava-bīja" (Aiṁ)</note>, united with the Teacher's own Principle of the Self <term>Ātma-tattva</term>.

->With the seven principles from the Veiling Power <term>Māyā</term> to the Individual Soul <term>Puruṣa</term>, which are both pure and impure,<-
->With the contact-consonants <note>original: "Sparśa-varṇas"; the consonants from ka to ma</note> and the Seed-Syllable of the King of Desire <note>original: "Kāmarāja-bīja" (Klīṁ)</note>, the knower of mantras...<-
->...united with the Principle of Knowledge <term>Vidyā-tattva</term>, should purify the subtle body <term>Sūkṣma-deha|the energetic or mental body</term>. || 73 ||<-

Thereafter, using the seven "purer than pure" principles ranging from the Veiling Power <term>Māyā</term> to the Individual Soul <term>Puruṣa</term> and the Seed-Syllable of the King of Desire <note>original: "Kāmarāja-bīja" (Klīṁ)</note>, united with the contact-consonants, the Guru, using the Principle of Knowledge <term>Vidyā-tattva</term>, purifies the subtle body of the disciple.

->With the five expansive pure principles from the Auspicious One <term>Śiva</term> down to Wisdom <term>Vidyā</term>,<-
->And with the Supreme Seed-Syllable <note>original: "Para-bīja" (Sauḥ)</note> and the Principle of Supreme Shiva, he should purify the transcendental body <term>para-śarīra</term>. || 74 ||<-

Then, with all five pure principles ranging from the Auspicious One <term>Śiva</term> to Wisdom <term>Vidyā</term> and the Supreme Seed <note>original: "Para" (Sauḥ)</note>, united comprehensively with the Principle of Supreme Shiva, he should purify the transcendental body of the disciple.

->Along with the thirty-six principles and the Garlanded Maiden <note>original: "Mālinī Bālā"; a ritual arrangement of the Sanskrit alphabet personified as a goddess</note>, O Beloved,<-
->He should purify the seed that is the refuge of all principles with all the principles themselves. || 75 ||<-

Then, with all thirty-six principles and the Garlanded Maiden, he should purify the "Seed" <term>Bīja</term>—which embodies all other seeds—using the totality of the principles.

->The Guru should provide the ritual wine <term>Ali</term> with the "second element" <note>consecrated ritual meat</note> and utter the word "Purify!"<-
->Receiving the handful <term>Cullū|a cavity formed by joining the palms</term> given by the Guru and saying "I purify all principles,"<-
->The disciple, bowed with devotion, should drink the ritual wine three times without making a sound. || 76 ||<-
->He should then touch his body with both hands, reciting all the principles.<-
->From the head down to the feet, he should contemplate his body as being entirely purified. || 77 ||<-

After this, the Guru provides the disciple with the ritual wine <term>Ali</term> along with the "second element" <note>the meat offering</note> and should utter the command "Purify!" <note>original: "Śodhaya"</note>. The disciple, bowing with devotion, should then drink one palmful <term>Cullū</term> of the ritual wine provided by the Guru without making any sound, while uttering the words "I purify all principles" <note>original: "Sarva Tattvaṁ śodhayāmi"</note>. Then, touching his own body with his hands and reciting the names of all the principles, he should visualize that his entire body, from head to toe, has been made perfectly pure.

This is achieved through the systematic application of thirty-six cosmic principles, sacred seed-syllables, and the ceremonial consumption of consecrated ritual wine.</summary>

# Seventh Flash

->The Principle of the Self <term>Ātma-tattva</term> is limited to the gross body; the Principle of Knowledge <term>Vidyā-tattva</term> falls within the range of the subtle body;<-
->The Principle of Shiva <term>Śiva-tattva</term> extends to the Transcendent. Thus, the entire world is composed of these three principles. || 78 ||<-

*Distinction of the Three Principles of the Self, etc., and the fruit of their Knowledge:*

The Principle of the Self <term>Ātma-tattva</term> is confined to the gross physical body; the Principle of Knowledge <term>Vidyā-tattva</term> is perceptible within the subtle or energetic body; while the Principle of Shiva <term>Śiva-tattva</term> extends to the transcendental state <note>original: "Para-śarīra"</note>. The entire universe is a manifestation of these three fundamental principles.

->One who performs ritual actions after receiving the knowledge of these three principles from the mouth of the Teacher,<-
->becomes liberated even while still living. This is the decree spoken by Lord Shiva <note>original: "Śaṅkara-bhāṣitam"</note>. || 79 ||<-

A practitioner who carries out their spiritual duties with an understanding of these three principles—as transmitted directly by the Teacher <term>Guru</term>—attains liberation in this very life <term>Jīvanmukta</term>. This is the established truth ordained by the sacred scriptures.

->Thereafter, having accepted the consecrated substances, the Teacher should offer the remainder to the disciples.<-
->Taking that which is given by the Teacher, the disciple should drink the ritual wine along with the second element. || 80 ||<-

*Drinking in the presence of the Teacher and others is prohibited:*

After the Teacher <term>Guru</term> has personally partaken of the ritual substances <term>Dravyas</term>, he should distribute the consecrated remnants to his disciples <term>Śiṣyas</term>. The disciples should then consume that ritual wine <term>Āsava</term> accompanied by the "second element" <note>original: "Sadvitīya"; likely referring to the second of the five ritual components (the Makaras), which is fish</note>.

->In the presence of the Holy Teacher, elders, and those worthy of worship, O Queen of the Kula,<-
->one should not sit and drink wine; this is the firm decision of the scripture. || 81 ||<-

It is strictly forbidden to consume wine in the presence of one's Teacher <term>Gurudeva</term> or other senior and venerable practitioners <term>Sādhakas</term>. This rule is a formal decree within the tantric tradition.

->One who acts without knowing the distinctions of the vital breaths, the joy of the results, and the characteristics of proper salutation and posture,<-
->shall find himself in a place of great misfortune. || 82 ||<-
->One should never drink the wine without the sacred mantra; otherwise, a penance is required.<-
->Therefore, O Queen of the Kula, the ritual must be performed according to the rules of the mantras. || 83 ||<-

*The prohibition against drinking without knowledge of the vital breaths and mantras:*

Anyone who engages in these rituals without understanding the various movements of the vital life-force <term>Prāṇa</term>, the spiritual exhilaration that follows, or the correct physical postures and forms of bowing, will encounter hardship. The ritual wine must only be consumed while reciting the appropriate sacred sound <term>Mantra</term>; to do otherwise requires the practitioner to undergo acts of purification or penance. Therefore, O Goddess <term>Kulanāyikā</term>, one must always proceed according to the specific ritual instructions for the mantras as provided below:

# In the Kularnava Tantra

->“I drink this holy nectar, the medicine for the cycle of rebirth, which destroys the fetters of the limited soul <term>paśu-pāśa</term> and was spoken by Lord Bhairava.” || 84 ||<-

->“Because the mind possesses the essence of absolute freedom and consists of the nature of bliss, all things are of that same nature; therefore, all objects are absorbed within this liquid essence <term>rasa</term>.” || 85 ||<-

->“This sweet nectar is drunk to expand the central energy channel <term>suṣumṇā</term>. Therefore, O Goddess Wine <term>surā</term>, being full of the Self, I drink you.” || 86 ||<-

**These are the Mantras for drinking.**

O Goddess, the knower of Mantras should slowly drink the ritual wine <term>ali</term> with a composed mind, reciting the previous verses along with the Root-Mantra <term>mūla-mantra</term>. || 87 ||

*Uttering the above Mantras (Verses 84-86) and the Root-Mantra, one should drink the wine gradually with a composed mind.*

One should offer the consecrated substances <term>dravya</term> with the following mantra into the fire of Pure Intelligence, which takes the form of the Serpent Power <term>kuṇḍalinī</term>, resplendent as millions of suns and situated in the triangle of one's own root center <term>mūlādhāra</term>. || 88 ||

*One should offer the libations of consecrated substances with the following verse (89) into the Pure Intelligence that takes the form of the Kundalini, which is as bright as millions of suns and located in the triangular space of the root chakra.*

->“This supreme nectar of 'this-ness' <note>original: "idantā", referring to objective experience</note> is filled into the vessel of 'great-ness' <note>original: "mahantā"</note>; it is the sign of an offering accepted into the fire of the 'Supreme I-ness' <note>original: "parāhantā"</note>.” || 89 ||<-

*This is the Mantra for offering libations of consecrated substances.*

With the intellect, one should contemplate the oneness of the Teacher <term>guru</term>, the Deity <term>devatā</term>, and the Mantra. One should drink the honey-wine <term>madhu</term> according to the instructions until the point of spiritual exhilaration <term>ullāsa</term>. || 90 ||

### Method of Drinking:

*Assuming the unity of the Teacher, the Deity, and the Mantra, one should continue drinking the wine until a state of spiritual joy is obtained.*

A single handful <term>culluka</term> is said to grant spiritual success <term>siddhi</term>; the 'lamp' of further drinking grants knowledge; and the transition from the state of sin to the supreme state—these three attainments are declared in the Kula system. || 91 ||

*It is said that drinking one handful (the cavity formed by joining the palms) bestows success, and drinking until spiritual enlightenment bestows knowledge. One reaches the Supreme State through this practice. These three achievements are established in the Kula tradition.*

Wine taken after a meal is poison. Similarly, taking a meal after wine is poison. Know that to be the nectar of immortality <term>amṛta</term> when the food is taken together with the wine. || 92 ||

*Drinking at the end of a meal is considered harmful, as is eating only after one has finished drinking. Food is only considered spiritual nectar when it is consumed alongside the consecrated wine.*

<meta>This page continues the Seventh Flash of the Kularnava Tantra. # Seventh Chapter

->“O Beloved, drinking accompanied by food <note>original: "carvaṇena", literally "chewing," referring to the ritual snacks or meat known as Śuddhi</note> is called nectar <term>amṛta</term>. Drinking without food is merely the increase of poison.” || 63 ||<-

O My Beloved! Drinking along with eating is Nectar and drinking without eating alongside increases only poison.

->“Drinking is said to be of three kinds, following the sequence of the Divine, the Heroic, and the Animal.”<-
->“Divine drinking is performed in the presence of the Goddess; Heroic drinking is done while established in the ritual posture <term>āsana</term> and seal <term>mudrā</term>.” || 64 ||<-
->“Drinking according to one’s own arbitrary desire, like a beast, is called Animal drinking.” || 65 ||<-

**Three kinds of Drinking: 1. Divine <term>divya</term>; 2. Heroic <term>vīra</term>; 3. Animal <term>paśu</term>:**

Divine, Heroic, and Animal respectively have been said to be the three kinds of drinking. Drinking in front of the Goddess <note>the Devi or the consecrated altar</note> is called Divine; drinking with the appropriate ritual Posture and Seal is Heroic; and drinking arbitrarily according to one's desire is Animal drinking.

->“The fruit of Divine drinking is both worldly enjoyment <term>bhukti</term> and spiritual liberation <term>mukti</term>; the Heroic drinking leads to enjoyment; and Animal drinking is said to lead to hell.” || 66 ||<-

The fruit of Divine-drinking is both Enjoyment and Emancipation, of Heroic-drinking only Enjoyment, and of Animal-drinking, Hell.

->“One should continue drinking only as long as the sight, mind, speech, and body do not become deluded. Beyond that limit, it is considered Animal drinking.” || 67 ||<-

Unless visual, mental, vocal, and bodily illusions develop, one should keep on drinking. Exceeding this limit is called Animal-drinking.

->“One should drink the ritual wine only as long as the senses are not impaired and the face does not become distorted. Otherwise, a spiritual downfall occurs.” || 68 ||<-

Unless the sense-organs become agitated and unless the mouth becomes deformed, one should keep on drinking. Drinking beyond this limit brings downfall.

->“O Goddess, I now declare the method of drinking for those who have received the Full Initiation <term>pūrnābhiṣikta</term>.”<-
->“Lifting the vessel with both hands, the practitioner should remember the Root-Mantra <term>mūla-mantra</term> and the Guru’s lineage <term>pādukā</term>.”<-
->“The practitioner who drinks the consecrated substance up to the throat is undoubtedly liberated.” || 69 ||<-

**Method of drinking for those who are Fully Initiated <term>Pūrnābhiṣikta</term>:**

O Goddess! I am now expounding the method for drinking by those who are Fully Initiated. Lifting the vessel with both hands, such a seeker <term>sādhaka</term> should remember the Root Mantra and the sacred feet of the Guru <note>original: "pādukā", referring to the lineage of teachers</note>. Drinking up to the throat thereafter, he becomes indubitably Released.

It concludes with the specific protocol for the Fully Initiated practitioner to achieve liberation through the act.</summary>

# Seventh Chapter

->“One should drink, and drink, and drink again, until one falls upon the ground.”<-
->“Rising up and drinking yet again, there shall be no more rebirth for him.” || 100 ||<-

The practitioner should partake of the ritual wine <note>original: "pītvā," referring to the consecrated wine used in Tantric ceremony</note> repeatedly until they reach a state of physical collapse on the earth. If, after rising, they continue this sacred consumption, they attain a state of spiritual perfection that ends the cycle of reincarnation <term>saṃsāra</term>. 

->“The Goddess is satisfied by his bliss; Bhairava himself by his swooning;”<-
->“And all the gods by his vomiting; therefore, one should perform these three.” || 101 ||<-

In this ecstatic ritual, different levels of intoxication serve as offerings: the Goddess <term>Devī</term> is pleased by the practitioner's internal joy; the fierce form of Shiva, Bhairava, is satisfied when the practitioner loses consciousness <note>the "swoon" represents the dissolution of the individual ego into the infinite</note>; and the various deities are honored even through the ritual cleansing or physical purging that may follow. Thus, these three states are embraced as part of the path.

->“The happiness found by the Kula-yogis who are devoted to divine drinking,”<-
->“Is a joy that not even a world-ruling Emperor possesses.” || 102 ||<-

The spiritual bliss experienced by those following the Kula path <term>Kula-yogīs</term> through the consecrated "Divine drinking" <term>divya-pāna</term> far exceeds any worldly pleasure, even the total power and luxury available to a sovereign king of the entire earth.

->“The happiness that comes to those devoted to the Kula tradition from using the ritual materials,”<-
->“That very happiness is truly Liberation. O Beautiful-Faced One! This is the Truth.” || 103 ||<-

O Goddess! <note>original: "Varānane," a title for the Goddess meaning "Lovely-Faced One"</note> The profound joy resulting from the proper use of the ritual substances <term>Kula-dravya</term> is not a distraction from the spirit, but is itself the experience of Emancipation <term>mokṣa</term>. This is an absolute truth.

->“Thus I have described to you briefly the worship of Batuka, the Shaktis, and the rest.”<-
->“O Queen of the Kula! What else do you wish to hear?” || 104 ||<-

O Great Goddess <term>Kuleśānī</term>! I have now summarized the essential rites for honoring the guardian deity Baṭuka and the various Divine Powers <term>Śaktis</term>. What further mysteries do you desire for Me to reveal?

->Thus ends the Seventh Flash, entitled "The Worship of Batuka, the Shaktis, and Others,"<-
->in the Fifth Section of the Great Mystery, the Door to Nirvana and Liberation,<-
->within the venerable Kularnava Tantra, the Best of all Traditions,<-
->consisting of one hundred and twenty-five thousand verses of the Upper Transmission.<-

->**Seventh Chapter || 7 ||**<-

# Eighth Chapter

->**The Goddess said:**<-

->O Lord of the Kula <term>Kuleśa</term>, O Ocean of the Nectar of Compassion! I desire to hear about the distinctions between the stages of spiritual exhilaration <term>Ullāsa</term>, O God of gods, and the transition of the sacred substances <term>dravya</term> and the ritual vessels. || 1 ||<-
->Tell me also, O Supreme Lord, about the time for the ritual union <term>Rati</term> and its conclusion <note>original: "udvāsana-kāla," the time for the ceremonial dismissal or abandonment of the ritual state</note>, the arrangement of the Sacred Circle <term>Śrīcakra</term>, and the conduct of the female powers <term>Kaulika-shaktis</term> belonging to our path. || 2 ||<-

The Goddess asks Shiva for specific instructions on the mechanics of the Tantric ritual, seeking to understand how the internal state of the practitioner changes alongside the physical movement of ritual objects.

->**The Lord said:**<-

->Listen, O Goddess, and I shall explain what You have asked me; by merely hearing this, a divine state of consciousness <note>original: "divya-bhāvanā"</note> is born. || 3 ||<-

*The Seven Exhilarations and their characteristics:*

The Lord said: Listen, O Goddess, I am telling You what you have asked, the mere hearing of which arouses Divine Feeling.

->The Beginning, the Juvenile, the Youthful, and the Mature;<-
->The Post-Mature, the State Beyond Mind, and the seventh, the Heart's Exhilaration. || 4 ||<-

The stages of spiritual exhilaration <term>Ullāsa</term> <note>these refer to the progressive levels of ritual intoxication and spiritual awakening during the ceremony</note> are seven: 
1. **The Beginning** <note>original: "Ārambha"</note>
2. **The Juvenile** <note>original: "Taruṇa"</note>
3. **The Youthful** <note>original: "Yauvana"</note>
4. **The Mature** <note>original: "Prauḍha"</note>
5. **The Post-Mature** <note>original: "Prauḍhānta"</note>
6. **The State Beyond Mind** <note>original: "Unmanā"</note> 
7. **The Heart's Exhilaration** <note>original: "Manollāsa"</note>

->O Queen of the Kula <term>Kulanāyikā</term>, the stage of "Beginning" is said to arise from the three essential principles <term>tattva-traya</term>.<-
->O Mother, the "Juvenile" exhilaration is described as the arising of youthful pleasure. || 5 ||<-

O Queen of the Kula! The stage of **Beginning** is caused by the rise of the three essential principles <note>referring to the three Tattvas: Atma (Self), Vidya (Knowledge), and Shiva</note>. O Mother! The **Juvenile** exhilaration is assumed when the initial, youthful pleasure of the ritual arises.

->O My Beloved! The condition of proper mental exhilaration and steady poise is called the "Youthful" stage;<-
->And when there is a faltering of vision, mind, and speech, it is called "Mature." || 6 ||<-

O My Beloved! The condition of proper mental exhilaration and spiritual stability is called the **Youthful** stage; and when the practitioner experiences a divine "faltering" or loss of mundane control over their vision, mind, and speech, it is known as the **Mature** stage.

# In the Kularnava Tantra

->When the state of spiritual exhilaration <term>Ullāsa</term> has blossomed within the Sacred Circle <term>Cakra</term>, if one wishes to interchange the ritual vessels <term>Pātra-melanam</term>,<-
->One should never do so before the "Mature" stage of exhilaration <term>Prauḍha-samullāsa</term> has been reached.<-
->Even then, the interchanging of vessels must only be performed according to one's spiritual authority <term>adhikāra</term>. || 7 ||<-

*Rules for the Interchange of Sacred Substances <term>Dravyas</term>:*

In the event of reaching a state of spiritual joy during the ritual circle, if a practitioner wishes to share or exchange ritual vessels, they must only do so if they have reached the appropriate level of spiritual maturity and possess the ritual right to do so.

->One should not share or interchange ritual substances <term>Dravya-saṅgati</term> with those who are uninitiated, those of bad conduct, those ignorant of the Tantras, or those without a Chosen Deity <term>Iṣṭa-devatā</term>.<-
->Likewise, avoid those who are fault-finders or those who have fallen from the sacred code of conduct <term>Samayācāra</term>. || 8 ||<-

Those uninitiated persons who behave poorly, who do not understand the technicalities of the Tantras, who lack a personal connection to the Divine, who are prone to guilt or criticism, or who have abandoned their spiritual vows should not be permitted to share in the ritual substances.

->One should not share ritual substances with those who are conceited in their supposed knowledge, those who maintain worldly or deceptive vows,<-
->Those who possess an animalistic consciousness <term>Paśu-bhāva</term> <note>original: "paśubhiḥ," referring to the "bound" or uninitiated soul who lacks spiritual perception</note>, or those who are engaged in mean-spirited actions. || 9 ||<-

The ignorant, the arrogant, the treacherous, and those stuck in a mundane or "animal" state of mind should not participate in the ritual exchange.

->Do not share ritual substances with those who hate women, those cursed by their Gurus, those devoid of devotion, the evil-minded,<-
->Or those who have not received the secret instructions of the Kula path. || 10 ||<-

Haters of women, those who have broken their bond with their teacher, the faithless, and those who lack the inner teachings of the Kula tradition <term>Kuladharma</term> are excluded from this sacred interaction.

->Even if one is a master of grammar <term>pada</term>, logic <term>vākya</term>, and the means of valid knowledge <term>pramāṇa</term>, and is well-versed in the meaning of the Vedas <term>Śruti</term> and Traditional Law <term>Smṛti</term>,<-
->If they are ignorant of the Kula path <term>Kuladharma</term>, one should avoid their company in the ritual. || 11 ||<-

Intellectual mastery of the scriptures and philosophy is not enough; if a person does not understand the specific spiritual path of the Kula, they are to be avoided in this context.

->Even if one is born in a noble family, or is an elder of good character—<-
->If they are averse to Your worship, O Goddess, one should shun their company. || 12 ||<-

Even social standing or high birth cannot substitute for devotion. If someone is opposed to the worship of the Goddess, they have no place in the ritual circle.

->O Pārvatī, listen! Even if they are beloved wives, sons, friends, or close relatives,<-
->If they are ignorant of the Kula conduct <term>Kulācāra</term>, their company must be avoided, O Dear One. || 13 ||<-

Family ties are secondary to spiritual alignment. Shiva instructs Parvati that even the most intimate family members must be excluded from the ritual circle if they have not been initiated into its specific practices.

## The Eighth Stage of Exultation

->One should not interchange ritual substances <term>Dravyas</term> <note>original: "dravya-saṅgatim"</note> with unknown men or those living in distant lands,<-
->unless a connection has been established through the use of secret signs <term>saṅketa</term>. || 14 ||<-

A practitioner should not share or exchange the sacred materials of the ritual with strangers or people from other regions unless they can prove their initiation and belonging to the tradition through specific, coded hand gestures or signs.

->One should not share from a single vessel, even if the Lord of the Kula <term>Kuleśvara</term> Himself were present.<-
->If one does so, the protective Mantras turn their faces away and obstacles appear at every step. || 15 ||<-

Even if the highest spiritual authority is present, the ritual cup is for individual use. Sharing a single cup—outside of specific ceremonial exchanges—is considered a breach of discipline that causes the practitioner's sacred chants to lose their power.

->One should not offer the ritual wine <term>Hetu</term> <note>The word "Hetu," meaning "cause," is a technical term for the wine used in Tantric rites</note> already in one's own vessel to the terrifying form of the Divine <term>Bhairava</term>.<-
->If one does so, O Goddess of the Clan <term>Kuleśāni</term>! one incurs the curse of the deities. || 16 ||<-

->One’s seat, food, ritual vessel, clothing, bed, and similar items<-
->should never be shared with those who are uninitiated; nor should one keep company with such ignorant persons. || 17 ||<-

The practitioner is instructed to maintain strict boundaries regarding personal and ritual items. Sharing these with those who have not undergone the proper initiations <note>original: "anabhijñaiḥ", meaning those who are ignorant or unacquainted with the path</note> is seen as a depletion of spiritual energy.

->A follower of the Kula path <term>Kaulika</term> may exchange vessels according to the distinction of the traditional lineages <term>Āmnāyas</term>.<-
->There is a spiritual compatibility between the East and South lineages, as well as between the North and West. || 18 ||<-

The Tantric tradition is divided into "streams" or "lineages" <term>Āmnāyas</term> associated with the cardinal directions. This verse explains the protocol for which practitioners may share vessels based on their specific spiritual lineage.

->In that ritual, those devoted to the sequential worship <term>Kramārcana</term> should exchange vessels with heroic practitioners <term>Vīras</term> who are their equals,<-
->and with the ritual women <term>Kāminīs</term> across these four lineages. || 19 ||<-

->O Beloved! When a full vessel is provided by male or female adepts <term>Yogīs</term> and <term>Yoginīs</term>,<-
->it should be drunk while reciting the foundational mantra <term>Mūla Mantra</term> and the sacred lineage prayer <term>Pādukā</term> of one's own Mother-Goddess <term>Mātṛkā</term>. || 20 ||<-

->If, by some stroke of divine chance, one receives a vessel of ritual wine <term>Ali-pātra</term> with devotion,<-
->one should accept it, recite the mantras as previously described, and drink while remembering the Guru. || 21 ||<-

# In the Kularnava Tantra

### Rules regarding the partaking of ritual remainders in the Circle

->One should eat the sacred remainders <term>ucchista</term> <note>original: "ucchista"; literally "leftovers," but in a Tantric context, these are substances infused with the spiritual power of the person who consumed them first</note> of the Guru’s female counterpart <term>Shakti</term>, the sons of the Guru, and those senior to oneself.<-
->O Goddess of the Mountain <term>Parvati</term>! One should never consume the remainders of anyone else. || 22 ||<-

O Parvati! One should eat the remainder of only the Guru’s consort, the sons of the Guru, and seniors in the tradition, but not of any other person.

->One should drink the liquid remainder <term>dravya</term> of the female practitioner <term>Shakti</term> and eat the food remainders of a heroic initiate <term>Vira</term>.<-
->One should not give away one's own remainders, nor should one partake of what belongs to another. || 23 ||<-

One should drink the remainder of the ritual fluids belonging to a Shakti and eat the remainder of the food of a Heroic Initiate. One must neither offer their own leftovers to others nor consume the leftovers of outsiders.

->One may consume the remainders of women, but one must never offer their own remainders to them.<-
->O Sovereign of the Gods <term>Deveshi</term>! Even within the ritual circle <term>Cakra</term>, doing otherwise leads to a spiritual fall. || 24 ||<-

The remainders left by women can be eaten, but O Goddess, one should not give them his own remainder, even during the Cakra ritual. If a practitioner does so, he meets his spiritual downfall.

->O Mother <term>Ambike</term>! One should offer their remainders only to their own junior disciples <term>shishyas</term>.<-
->Whoever offers to or takes from others out of affection, they become a dwelling place for misfortunes. || 25 ||<-
->Whether out of delusion, affection, greed, or fear, whoever shares the vessel or the remainder of the ritual wine <term>Asava</term>,<-
->they shall receive the curse of the deities. || 26 ||<-

O Mother! One should offer remainders only to his own junior disciples. Whoever, out of emotional attachment, offers to or takes from others the remainder of the ritual wine or the vessel, receives the curse of the Gods and falls into great difficulties.

### Method of offering Libations to the Dreadful Lord of Remainders

->O Queen of the Clan <term>Kuleshani</term>! During the stage of mature exultation <term>Praudhollasa</term> <note>The fifth of seven stages of spiritual intoxication/joy in the Kula tradition</note>, one should perform the dismissal of the offerings.<-
->This should be done within a triangle <term>trikona</term> either outside the worship room or in another part of the house. || 27 ||<-

O Queen of the Clan! In the state of Mature Exultation, one should draw a triangle either inside or outside the place of worship. One should worship it with incense, flowers, and consecrated grains <term>Akshata</term> <note>original: "akshata"; literally "unbroken," referring to whole grains of rice used in ritual</note> and then meditate upon the Dreadful Lord of Remainders <term>Ucchista-Bhairava</term> using the following description:

->Worship with perfumes, flowers, and consecrated grains, and meditate upon the Lord of Remainders.<-
->He has three eyes and holds a mace, a trident, a drum, and a ritual bowl in his hands.<-
->One should meditate on this dark-complexioned <term>Bhairava</term> as the remover of all obstacles. || 28 ||<-

This verse describes the visualization of the deity Ucchista-Bhairava. He is envisioned with a dark complexion, three eyes, and four hands holding a mace, a trident, a small drum, and a ritual vessel. He is worshipped to ensure that no obstacles remain after the ritual.

# Eighth Chapter

### The Mantra of the Sacred Remainder

Having uttered the three syllables of the pranava <term>Om</term> <note>original: "tara-trayam"; literally "three stars," a technical term for repeating 'Om' three times</note>, one should then invoke Ucchishta Bhairava <note>The "Bhairava of the Sacred Remainder," a fierce form of Shiva who presides over the leftovers of the ritual</note>. Use the word "Come" twice, "Take the offering" twice, followed by the syllable "Phat" and the two-syllabled ending <note>original: "dvitantakah," referring to the word 'Svaha'</note>. || 29 ||

Thereafter, offer a libation with the following Mantra as it stands after extrication:

->**Om Om Om, Ucchishta Bhairava, come, come, take the offering, take the offering, Phat Svaha!**<-

This is the mantra for removing the ritual offering, consisting of twenty-two syllables. After this, one should recite the following Hymn of Peace <term>Shanti-stava</term> (Verses 31 to 54) and offer libations of drops of ritual wine <term>Ali</term> <note>original: "Ali"; literally "bee," a common Tantric code-word for consecrated wine or the "nectar" used in ceremony</note>. || 30 ||

### The Hymn of Peace

I bow to the assembly of sixty-four Yoginis <note>original: "ashta-ashtaka-yogini-ganam"; literally the "eight-times-eight" group of semi-divine female spirits</note>, who worship the lotus-feet of the Lord <term>Shiva</term>—the feet which are a dwelling of grace and the source of the nectar of liberation, and which awaken the realization of infinite truth. || 31 ||

I bow my head to the Lord Bhairava, the beloved of the fierce Goddess, who sits in the center of the circle of Yoginis and is surrounded by the assembly of the Divine Mothers. || 32 ||

Salutations to the holy Lord-Physician <note>original: "Shri-Natha-Vaidya"</note>, the sole destroyer of the darkness of this eternal and terrifying worldly existence, who prepares the medicine of the Tradition <term>Kula</term>. || 33 ||

May all calamities, sins, and diseases arising from the violation of ritual conduct <term>Samayachara</term> be entirely removed through the gathering of this divine ritual circle <term>Chakra</term>. || 34 ||

May longevity, health, prosperity, fame, success, happiness, and victory be granted; may there be enchanting beauty, and may all the deities protect us. || 35 ||

May the Lord of the Tradition <term>Kulesha</term> grant peace to the worshippers, the protectors, the great masters of yoga, the ascetics, the country, the nation, the lineage, and the King. || 36 ||

May the community of practitioners <term>Sadhakas</term> flourish—those who perceive the non-duality of the tradition and the great Shaktas who occupy the ritual throne. May the supreme followers of the path <term>Kaulas</term> rejoice, as well as those who distinguish the various special stages of the path of Shiva <term>Shambhava</term>. || 37 ||

May the perfected Teachers <term>Siddha-Gurus</term> and those who know the lineage-sequence rejoice. May the seniors, the initiated members, the youths <term>Vatukas</term>, and the ritual maidens <term>Kumaris</term> flourish. May those born in the lineage of the excellent Yoginis and Heroes <term>Viras</term> prosper, along with the kings, the cattle, the priests, and all good people. || 38 ||

May they rejoice—those skilled in conduct, those of faultless devotion, the envy-less, the incomparable, and those free from all afflictions. May the Teachers flourish, who are ever devoted to the Stainless One <term>Niranjana</term>, who are free from desire, peaceful, tranquil of mind, and who have destroyed all grief and doubt. || 39 ||

# Kularnava Tantra

### The Benediction of the Community

May those devoted to Yoga rejoice, as well as those united through the practice of the Kula tradition <note>original: "Kula-yoga-yukta"; referring to the specific Tantric path of the Kularnava</note>. May the teachers, those bound by sacred vows, the practitioners, and the spiritual sons <note>original: "Acarya-samayika-sadhaka-putrakas"; these are the four grades of initiation in the Tantric hierarchy</note> all find happiness. May the cows, the twice-born <term>Brahmins</term>, the young women, the ascetics, and the young girls find joy. May all people devoted to the Guru be established in the path of Righteousness. || 40 ||

May the families of practitioners rejoice and be fully established in the Self. May curses fall upon those who hate the sacred pledges <term>samaya</term> made to the Yoginis. May that indescribable Shambhavi state <note>original: "Shambhavi-avastha"; a high state of consciousness in which one perceives the world as identical to Shiva</note> manifest—that state in which the only absolute truth is the lotus-feet of the Guru. || 41 ||

### Invocation of the Indwelling Goddesses

May the Goddesses who reside in the various stages of the wheel-like energy centers <term>chakras</term>, who dwell within the subtle channels <term>nadis</term>, and who inhabit the very pores of the hair on the body rejoice. May those who reside in the physical tissues <note>original: "dhatushu"; the seven fundamental elements of the body like blood, bone, and marrow</note>, who dwell in the waves of the incoming and outgoing breath, and who are intent on consuming the side of the enemy <note>interpretive: 'enemies' here often refers to internal obstacles like ego and passion</note> be pleased when worshipped by the followers of the Kula path. || 42 ||

May all those Goddesses who arise from the Kula lineage—those who walk the earth, those who dwell in the waters, those of celebrated radiance who reside in fire, and those whose home is the wind—grant me peace. May those who are made of the nectar of the lunar mandala in the space of the heart, and who are omnipresent at all times, remain intent on protecting the path of the Kula. || 43 ||

### Protection from All Realms

Whether they are above the cosmic egg <note>original: "Brahmanda"; the universe envisioned as an egg</note>, in the heavens, in the sky, on the earth, or in the lower regions; whether they are in the underworld, in fire, in water, or in the air—wherever they may be stayed; whether they have taken their place in the sacred seats of power <term>Pithas</term> and their secondary sites <term>Upapithas</term>—may those Goddesses, who are worshipped by the heroes <term>Vira</term>, be pleased by our incense, lamps, and auspicious ritual offerings, and forever protect us. || 44 ||

May Brahma, Shri <note>the Goddess Lakshmi</note>, the serpent Shesha, Durga, Guha <note>the war-god Skanda</note>, the groups of Batukas <note>the boy-form of Bhairava</note>, the Bhairavas, and the Lords of the Field <term>Kshetrapalas</term> all protect us. May the ghosts, the sun, the Rudras, the planets, the perfected beings <term>Siddhas</term>, the celestial nymphs <term>Apsaras</term>, and the secret dwellers <term>Guhyakas</term> protect us. May the spirits, the celestial musicians, the holders of wisdom, the seers, the ancestors, the titans, the spirits of the underworld, the masters of Yoga, the celestial wanderers, the horse-headed beings, the great sages, and those who move within the sacred wheels—may they all protect us. || 45 ||

### The Ritual Satisfaction

May all the deities residing within the body—the elephant-headed Ganesha, the Lords of the Field, the Bhairavas, the Yoginis, the Batukas, the spirits of the ancestors, the ghosts, the demons, and the planetary spirits—be satisfied. May all other beings that move on the earth, in the sky, or in the directions—the vampires and the spirits of the hunt—be satisfied as this son of the Kula lineage partakes of the ritual drink and the sacred offering <term>Charu</term> <note>original: "sadeepa-charum"; literally "the offering with the lamp," a specific sacrificial mash</note>. || 46 ||

### The Act of Truth

If it is true that the word of the Guru is supreme; if the ancestors, the gods, and the Yoginis exist; if the Supreme Goddess is pleased; if the Vedas are indeed the ultimate authority; if the Shakta philosophy is true and its commands are unfailing; and if the Kula Dharma is the highest truth—then may victory be mine forever! || 47 ||

May all practitioners rejoice, and may those who defile the Kula lineage be destroyed. May the Shambhavi state dwell within me, and may my Guru be forever pleased. || 48 ||

### Chapter Eight: Page 127

If this be the Goddess Bhairavi, if this be the law of Bhairava, and if this be the sacred Path of the Kula <note>original: "Kula-dharma"; the specific lineage-based spiritual system of this Tantra</note>, then let those who find fault with it perish! || 49 ||

Salutations, forever, to all those Yoginis <note>female semi-divine beings or practitioners with supernatural powers</note> by the power of whose command the three worlds were established. || 50 ||

May all the Mothers <term>Matarah</term> drink; may the most excellent members of the Kula drink; may all the Bhairavas <note>fierce forms of Shiva or high-level practitioners</note> who reside within my very body drink. || 51 ||

May all the Mothers be satisfied, as well as the oceans and the lords of the divine hosts <term>Ganadhipas</term>; may the Yoginis and the Guardians of the Fields <term>Kshetrapalas</term> established within my body be satisfied. || 52 ||

From Shiva down to the very earth, from the creator Brahma down to a blade of grass, and from the Fire of Time <note>Kalagni; the fire that consumes the world at the end of an age</note> up to the highest Shiva—may the entire universe be satisfied by this sacrifice. || 53 ||

Those who stand at the gates of the pavilion of gems, those in the surrounding beautiful Nandana forest, those residing in empty houses, pleasure-groves, caves, monasteries, the open sky <note>original: "vyomni"</note>, or the cremation grounds; those situated at wells, at crossroads, or in the places where messages are sent—may they accept these flowers and offerings and protect us. || 54 ||

This is the **Hymn of Peace** <note>original: "Śānti-stava"</note>.

O Beloved! After reciting this, the Guru should lift the vessel of worship and then, O Leader of the Kula <term>Kulanayike</term>, he should distribute the consecrated offering <term>Prasada</term> to his disciple. || 55 ||

**Behavior of Practitioners within the Sacred Circle:**

O My Beloved! After reciting the **Hymn of Peace** (Verses 31-54), the Guru should lift the vessel of worship and then, O Leader of the Kula, distribute the consecrated food and drink to his disciples.

The performance of one’s own desired actions is described as the "Mature Stage of Joy" <term>Praudha-anta-ullasa</term>. O Goddess! When this Mature Stage is reached, and the circle of practitioners <term>Yogis</term> and <term>Yoginis</term> is gladdened, a state of Bliss is sequentially achieved. || 56 ||

For the Heroes <term>Viras</term> who have ascended to that state, there is no longer a distinction between what should be done and what should not be done. Their very desire is the same as the wealth of the scriptures—this is the command, O Supreme Goddess. || 57 ||

In that state, whatever action is performed—whether it be considered good or bad—it all results in the pleasure of the deity, O Divine Beauty. || 58 ||

The performance of their desired actions by the participant practitioners <term>Sadhakas</term> of the Sacred Circle <term>Cakra</term> is called the **Mature Stage of Joy**. O Goddess! When this stage is achieved, then in that state of ecstasy, there is a shared delight among the groups of male and female practitioners. In such an atmosphere of exhilaration, there is no consideration of worldly propriety among the Heroic practitioners. O Supreme Goddess! In this state, desire alone is the sacred law prescribed by the scriptures. Hence, in this state, whatever auspicious or inauspicious actions are performed, they are, O Divine Beauty, considered to be meant for the pleas<unclear>ure</unclear> of the Deity <term>Devata</term>.

# In the Kularnava Tantra

->Speech is the fruit of mantra recitation <note>original: "japa"</note>, and drowsiness is understood as meditative absorption <note>original: "samadhi"</note>.<-
->Every movement is worship, O Goddess; this is declared the way of Bhairava <note>the fierce form of Shiva</note>. || 59 ||<-
->Liberation is union with the Power <note>original: "Shakti"</note>; hymns are the words spoken at that moment.<-
->The ritual placement of power <note>original: "nyasa"</note> is the touch of limbs; the act of sacrifice <note>original: "havana"</note> is the partaking of food. || 60 ||<-
->Gazing is meditation, O Sovereign Lady; sleeping becomes the act of bowing.<-
->Whatever varied actions are performed in that state of exhilaration <note>original: "ullasa"</note> are considered sacred deeds.<-
->One who judges between what is proper and improper in this state is a sinner. || 61 ||<-

In this state, ordinary conversation achieves the same spiritual merit as the repetitive chanting of mantras; drowsiness is actually a state of deep meditative trance; all physical movements are acts of worship; and union with the feminine divine energy is final liberation. Partaking in the ritual substances is as if they were consumed by the God Bhairava himself, and any spoken word, O Goddess, is considered a sacred hymn of praise. The ritualized touching of body parts is achieved through natural physical contact, the eating of food is the same as pouring offerings into a sacred fire, sight is meditation, and sleep is an act of prostration. In this way, every action performed during this stage of spiritual ecstasy is considered a righteous act. Anyone who attempts to apply mundane logic or moral judgment to these actions is considered a sinner.

->The Heroes <term>Viras</term> present in this ritual circle are to be known as supreme Yogis.<-
->Through them, human beings attain the very form of Bhairava Himself. || 62 ||<-

The practitioners (known as "Heroes" for their courage in facing these intense rituals) who participate in such a ritual circle are exalted spiritual adepts in whom other people should see the manifest form of the God Bhairava.

->Exuberance, supreme bliss, the increase of knowledge, the playing of flutes, lutes <note>original: "vina"</note>, and other instruments, and the composition of poetry— || 63 ||<-
->Weeping, speaking, falling down, rising up, yawning,<-
->Walking, and all other movements, O Goddess, are called Yoga. || 64 ||<-

Feelings of intense joy, the experience of supreme bliss, the sudden expansion of wisdom, playing music on the flute or the stringed lute, composing poetry, weeping, speaking, falling, standing up, yawning, and even simple walking—all these actions, O Goddess, are considered formal yogic practices when performed in this state.

->In this ritual circle, the Heroic Yogis and the Yoginis, slowed by intoxication,<-
->Conduct themselves, O Sovereign of the Gods, according to the inner exhilaration of their hearts. || 65 ||<-

Within this sacred circle, the male and female practitioners <term>Yogis and Yoginis</term>, moving with the heavy grace of ritual intoxication, behave according to the spontaneous joy and exhilaration rising from within their own minds.

->Having forgotten their own intentions, they softly question those beside them;<-
->Holding the ritual cup to their mouths, they remain in a state of quietude. || 66 ||<-

Forgetting their previous thoughts or intentions, they quietly ask questions of the fellow practitioners <term>Sadhakas</term> sitting next to them, and holding the ritual vessel to their lips, they sit in a peaceful, silent state.

<note>Vocabulary: 
**Japa**: meditative repetition of a mantra.
**Samadhi**: a state of intense concentration or meditative absorption.
**Shakti**: the divine feminine creative power.
**Bhairava**: a fierce manifestation of Shiva associated with the Kula tradition.
**Stotra**: a hymn of praise.
**Nyasa**: the ritual practice of touching various parts of the body to instill them with divine power.
**Ullasa**: "Exhilaration" or "Joy"; specifically referring to the progressive stages of ritual intoxication in Tantra.
**Vira**: "Hero"; a practitioner of the "Left-Hand" path who has the spiritual strength to use forbidden substances in ritual.
**Cakra**: "Circle"; a ritual gathering of initiates.
**Vina**: a traditional Indian stringed instrument.
**Sadhaka**: a spiritual practitioner or adept.</note>

### Chapter Eight: The Stages of Exhilaration

Intoxicated by passion and mistaking other men for their own beloveds, the women seek their shelter. Men also, having reached the stage of "Mature Exhilaration" <note>original: "Praudhānta-ullāsa"; the sixth of seven stages of ritual intoxication where ego-boundaries begin to dissolve</note>, behave in exactly the same way. || 67 ||

In this state of total immersion, a man might embrace another man out of delusion, rather than a woman. 

The bewildered woman asks her own husband questions such as: "Who are you? Who am I? Who are these people? || 68 ||

What is our purpose here? Why are we staying in this place? Is this a garden, a house, or perhaps a courtyard?" || 69 ||

Filling their mouths with wine, the women make their beloveds drink directly from them. They place savory snacks <note>original: "upadamsha"; appetizers taken with wine</note> in their own mouths and then transfer them into the mouths of their lovers. || 70 ||

O Goddess <note>original: "Shambhavi"; a name for the Goddess as the consort of Shiva</note>! The practitioners <note>original: "yogis"</note> take food from one another's vessels, and placing the wine-pots upon their heads, they dance around. || 71 ||

Filling their mouths with wine, they make the women drink it from their own mouths. They put pungent items in their mouths and then transfer them to the mouths of their beloveds. <note>Note: The text here repeats the sentiment of verse 70 with a slight variation in roles.</note>

Clapping their hands without conscious direction, singing songs with indistinct words, and moving with stumbling steps, the female ritual partners <note>original: "kula-shaktis"</note> dance about. || 72 ||

The male practitioners, intoxicated with joy, fall upon the laps of the women, and the intoxicated women fall upon the men. || 73 ||

O Sovereign Lady of the Kula <note>original: "kulanayike"</note>! Thus fulfilling each other’s heartfelt desires, they perform various actions of this kind. || 74 ||

->**When the mind is free from distortion and exhilaration arises, the great practitioners attain the state of the Divine.**<-

When one is devoid of mental perversions or worldly distortions and this state of exhilaration takes hold, then the most excellent practitioners achieve the "State of the Deity" <note>original: "devatābhāva"; the realization that the practitioner and the divine are one</note>. || 75 ||

<summary>This page describes the "Praudhānta" stage of ritual intoxication in Tantric practice, where social norms and individual identities dissolve into a state of communal divine ecstasy. It emphasizes that these unconventional behaviors are outward signs of attaining a divine state of consciousness (Devatābhāva) free from mental distortion.</summary>

### From the Kularnava Tantra

->The fool who, in his clouded mind, slanders a Kaulika <note>original: "Kaulika"; a practitioner of the Kula path of Tantra</note> while they are possessed by the spirit of Bhairava <note>original: "Bhairava-aveshan"; a state where the practitioner is seen as the terrifying and ecstatic form of Shiva himself</note>—O Leader of the Kula <note>original: "Kulanayike"; an address to the Goddess</note>, such a person is undoubtedly destroyed by the Yoginis. || 76 ||<-

**The Sin of Showing Disrespect to Kaulikas:**

A fool who reproaches a Kaulika in his Bhairava form is, O Goddess, indubitably destroyed by the semi-divine female spirits known as the Yoginis.

->One should never criticize nor mock those in the ritual circle who are languid with the intoxication of the wine. One must never disclose the private matters of the ritual circle to the outside world. || 77 ||<-

One should neither reproach nor laugh at the practitioners <note>term: "Sadhakas" (those following a spiritual discipline)</note> who become ecstatic under intoxication within a ritual circle <note>term: "Cakra" (a 'circle' or assembly of practitioners for ritual purposes)</note>; and one should never disclose the incidents of the Cakra to those outside the path.

->One should not harbor malice against them, nor perform any harmful act. Instead, one should honor them with devotion and guard their secrets with great effort. || 78 ||<-

One should neither revolt against the practitioners of a ritual circle nor harm them in any manner. On the other hand, honor them with devotion and also take care to keep their secrets.

->Seeing those in the circle overcome by spiritual intoxication, one should meditate upon them as being one with the Deity. He who rejoices and bows with devotion reaches the status of the Yoginis. || 79 ||<-

**The Fruits of Showing Respect to a Kaulika:**

Seeing intoxicated practitioners in a ritual circle, one who develops a reverent feeling towards them—viewing them as divine—and gladly prays to them with devotion, obtains the spiritual status of the Yoginis.

->O Beloved, the Kaulika who views the ritual circle with such devotion obtains the fruit of ten million vows, pilgrimages, austerities, charities, and sacrifices. || 80 ||<-

A Kaulika who thus sees the ritual circle with devotion obtains, O My Beloved, the spiritual merit equivalent to millions of formal religious observances, austerities, acts of charity, and ritual sacrifices.

->In the stage of the "Trans-mental" <note>original: "Unmana"; the state beyond the ordinary mind</note>, there is falling down and rising up, and repeated fainting. In this stage of exhilaration known as the Trans-mental, within the circle where heroes are worshiped, || 81 ||<-
->those two who are devoted to the Supreme Word <note>original: "karmaparaksharau"; likely referring to those dedicated to the ritual action and the imperishable syllable</note> remain for a long time. O Leader of the Kula, they are those who yearn for contemplation of the Supreme Absolute. || 82 ||<-
->This is called the "State of Equilibrium," where one is no longer in control of the body or the senses. In that exhilaration known as Equilibrium, everything becomes equalized. || 83 ||<-

**The Trans-mental Stage, the State of Equilibrium, and the Gesture of Shambhu:**

In the state of the sixth stage of exhilaration <note>term: "Ullasa" (the stages of ritual joy/intoxication)</note> called the Trans-mental, physical actions like falling down, rising up, and repeated swoonings take place. Associated with the desire to know the Supreme Absolute <note>original: "Para Brahma"</note>, these two actions happening for an indefinite time induce a state of equilibrium beyond the control of the physical body and the senses. This state, O Goddess, falls within the domain of the seventh stage of exhilaration.

<summary>This page warns against disparaging practitioners within the sacred ritual circle (Chakra) and describes the intense physical and spiritual symptoms of the sixth and seventh stages of ritual exhilaration (Ullasa).</summary>
<keywords>Kularnava Tantra, Kaulika, Bhairava, Kulanayika, Yogini, Sadhaka, Chakra, Unmana, Para Brahma, Ullasa, spiritual intoxication, ritual secrecy</keywords>

# Chapter Eight

->Assuming the form of the Supreme Mantra <note>original: "Parā Mantra"</note>, the practitioner attains the Supreme Ecstatic Faint <note>term: "Mūrchanā" (a state of spiritual swoon or deep meditative absorption)</note>; for the proximity of this state of absorption is known as the highest root of Liberation <note>original: "Mukti"</note>. || 84 ||<-

**The Shambhavi Mudra:**

->With the gaze fixed externally but the focus directed entirely within, without the closing <note>original: "Nimeṣa"</note> or opening <note>original: "Unmeṣa"</note> of the eyelids—this is the **Shambhavi Mudra** <note>original: "Śāmbhavī Mudrā"; a prestigious yogic gesture named after Shambhu, an epithet of Shiva</note>, which is kept secret in all the Tantras. || 85 ||<-

->This gesture transcends all things, providing a constant sense of "I-ness" <note>original: "Ahantā"; the pure consciousness of the Self</note> and a perfect harmony of essence and form <note>original: "Sāmarasya"; the 'equilibrium of taste' or the union of opposites</note>. The Heroic Practitioners <note>term: "Vira Sadhakas" (advanced adepts who follow the 'path of the hero')</note> who revel in this state are undoubtedly Shiva himself. || 86 ||<-

**The Indescribable Bliss of Meditation:**

->How can ordinary men understand the supreme happiness of those devoted to meditating on the Self? That supreme bliss cannot be expressed in words. || 87 ||<-

->It is experienced within oneself, much like the taste of sugar in a drink of milk; one cannot describe such happiness as being "like this" or "like that." That which is visible through the bristling of body hair <note>original: "Pulaka"; goosebumps or tremors signifying religious ecstasy</note> is called Meditation on the Absolute <note>original: "Brahmadhyāna"</note>. || 88 ||<-

->I cannot describe the supreme pleasure found in meditation, which brings about a divine impulse <note>term: "Avesha" (the descent of divine energy or 'possession' by the deity)</note>; only the awakened one, fully absorbed in it, knows it. || 89 ||<-

->Virtuous men, devoted to the supreme bliss of meditating on the Absolute, feel sorrow if it vanishes for even a moment, as if their inner light has been extinguished. || 90 ||<-

->Such is the great fruit of pleasure obtained by your devotees who have reached the Seventh Stage of Exultation <note>term: "Ullāsa" (the progressive stages of spiritual joy or intoxication in the Kula tradition)</note>.<-

<summary>This page describes the Shambhavi Mudra, a secret yogic technique of internal focus, and the profound, indescribable bliss of the Seventh Exultation, which identifies the practitioner with Shiva.</summary>
<keywords>Shambhavi Mudra, Murchana, Brahmadhyana, Vira Sadhaka, Avesha, Ullasa, spiritual ecstasy, Kularnava Tantra</keywords>

<meta>Continuity: This page transitions from the specific physical techniques of meditation (the Shambhavi Mudra) to the internal signs of spiritual success and the various stages of exultation (Ullāsas) experienced by the practitioner. # The Kularnava Tantra

->Oh Goddess of the Kula <note>original: "Kuleśvari"</note>, eight signs <note>original: "Pratyayas"</note> arise from knowledge of the three divisions of time <note>past, present, and future</note>, and eight physical states beginning with trembling <note>original: "Kampādyā"</note> occur without a doubt. || 61 ||<-

->What more need be said? The eight great attainments <note>term: "Siddhis" (miraculous powers)</note>, beginning with the power of miniaturization <note>original: "Aṇimā"</note>, take the role of doorkeepers and serve in the practitioner's temple for a long time. || 62 ||<-

->Those auspicious qualities belonging to the Supreme Lord in His five-faced form <note>original: "Pañcavaktra-tanu"; an iconic form of Shiva</note> are attained by the knower of the Kula principles <note>term: "Kula-tattva" (the essential truth of the Kula tradition)</note> through the realization of Truth. || 63 ||<-

**The Signs and States of the Seventh Exultation:**

In this seventh stage of exultation <note>term: "Ullāsa" (a level of spiritual joy or progress)</note> are inherent the eight **Signs** <note>original: "Pratyayas"; while the exact meaning here is debated, it likely refers to the Guru, the Deity, the Mantra, the Scriptures, the Lineage, the Disposition, and the Conduct</note> and the eight **States** <note>original: "Avasthās"</note> arising from knowledge of the past, present, and future. These states include:
* **Trembling** <note>original: "Kampana"</note>
* **Horripilation** <note>original: "Romāñca"; a thrill of joy where hair stands on end</note>
* **Throbbing** <note>original: "Sphuraṇa"</note>
* **Tears of love** <note>original: "Premāśru"</note>
* **Perspiration** <note>original: "Sveda"</note>
* **Laughter** <note>original: "Hāsya"</note>
* **Ecstatic dance** <note>original: "Lāsya"</note>
* **Singing** <note>original: "Gāyana"</note>

There is no doubt regarding these. To speak briefly, all the eight **Attainments** <note>term: "Siddhis"; specifically Aṇimā (smallness), Laghimā (lightness), Prāpti (attaining anything), Prākāmya (irresistible will), Mahimā (vastness), Īśitva (lordship), Vaśitva (control), and Kāmāvasāyit (fulfillment of all desires)</note> become like servants, residing in the home of the practitioner <note>original: "Sādhaka"</note> to serve him. All the divine qualities present in the form of the Five-faced Supreme Lord <note>original: "Parameśvara"</note> are gathered by the knower of Truth and Kula-principles.

->The stages are Beginning, Young, Youthful, and Mature <note>original: "Ārambha, Taruṇa, Yauvana, Prauḍha"</note>. At the end of these is the state of Waking. The "Mind-beyond" state <note>original: "Unmanā"</note> is called the Dreaming state. || 64 ||<-

->The "Stable state" <note>original: "Samavasthā"</note> is Deep Sleep, yet it is joined with all three states. Whoever understands these seven stages of exultation is liberated and is a true practitioner of the Kula <note>term: "Kaulika"</note>. || 65 ||<-

**The Five Levels of Exultation and States of Consciousness:**
The stages known as **Beginning**, **Young**, **Youthful**, **Mature**, and **Peaceful** are said to comprise the "Waking" state of consciousness. The sixth stage, the **Mind-beyond** <note>original: "Unmanā"</note>, is the "Dreaming" state. The seventh stage, the **Continuous State** <note>original: "Anvasthā"</note>, corresponds to "Deep Sleep," which paradoxically contains the essence of all three prior states. One who masters these seven levels of exultation is a liberated soul and a true Kaulika.

->When the Circle of the Goddess <note>term: "Bhairavī-cakra" (a sacred ritual gathering of practitioners)</note> is in progress, all social classes are considered high-born <note>original: "dvijātayaḥ"; literally "twice-born"</note>. Once the Circle is concluded, all classes return to their separate stations. || 66 ||<-

**Social Equality within the Ritual Circle:**
All practitioners participating in a *Bhairavī-cakra* are considered equal to the highest priestly class, regardless of their birth. Within this sacred space, caste discrimination is abolished. However, once the ritual concludes and the circle is dissolved, the practitioners return to their respective social orders and the conventional rules of society become effective once again.

<summary>This page details the physical and spiritual signs of advancement (Siddhis and Avasthās) and maps the seven stages of spiritual exultation (Ullāsas) onto states of consciousness, concluding with the ritual suspension of caste distinctions.</summary>
<keywords>Pratyaya, Avasthā, Siddhis, Ullāsa, Unmanā, Kaulika, Bhairavī-cakra, spiritual equality, states of consciousness</keywords>

<meta>Continuity: This page continues from the discussion of the internal spiritual signs (Pratyayas) and physical manifestations of success in the Seventh Exultation. It transitions into the Eighth Exultation, specifically focusing on the radical social equality mandated within the ritual gathering known as the Cakra.</meta>

### Eighth Exultation
<note>original: "Aṣṭama Ullāsaḥ"</note>

->Whether a woman or a man, a person of third gender <note>original: "ṣaṇḍha"</note>, an outcaste <note>term: "Cāṇḍāla" (historically a marginalized social group)</note>, or the highest of the twice-born <note>term: "Dvija" (referring to the Brahmin, Kshatriya, and Vaishya classes; here meaning a high-born person)</note>—there is absolutely no distinction in this ritual circle <note>term: "Cakra" (a sacred communal gathering of practitioners)</note>. Everyone here is considered to be equal to Shiva. || 97 ||<-

->Just as the waters of various streams achieve unity once they reach the Ganges, in the same way, all human beings attain oneness within the Sacred Circle <note>original: "Śrī Cakra"</note>. || 98 ||<-

->Just as water mixed with milk becomes milk itself, in the same manner, caste discrimination <note>original: "jāti-bhedo"</note> does not exist within the Sacred Circle. || 99 ||<-

->Just as in the pious worlds such as Heaven <note>original: "Svarga"</note> there are none other than gods, in the same way, all people in the midst of a Circle are like deities. || 100 ||<-

->There is no caste discrimination in this Circle; all are remembered as equal to Shiva. The Vedas <note>the most ancient and authoritative Hindu scriptures</note> also stand by this, for they declare that everything is indeed the Absolute <note>term: "Brahman" (the ultimate, non-dual reality)</note>. || 101 ||<-

->O Goddess of the Kula <note>original: "Kuleśvari"</note>, why say more? In the midst of a Circle, all men take my form <note>the form of Shiva</note> and all women take your form, my dear. || 102 ||<-

**The Sin of Caste Discrimination in a Circle:**

The fool who maintains caste distinctions in the midst of a Ritual Circle—O Leader of the Kula <note>original: "Kulanāyike"</note>, I swear it by you!—is devoured by the Yoginīs <note>fierce female deities who protect the purity of the ritual and punish the transgressor</note>. || 103 ||

**Method of Seating Men and Women in a Circle:**

In a Circle, men and women may either be seated in separate areas, or they may be seated in pairs <note>original: "mithuna"</note>, arranged sequentially in a row or a circle. || 104 ||

<summary>This page outlines the radical social egalitarianism of the Tantric Cakra ritual, where all participants—regardless of gender, caste, or social standing—are viewed as manifestations of Shiva and Shakti. It warns that maintaining worldly prejudices within this sacred space is a spiritual sin punishable by divine forces.</summary>
<keywords>Cakra, equality, caste-discrimination, Shiva, Shakti, Kuleśvari, Brahman, ritual purity, social hierarchy, Yoginīs</keywords>

<meta>Continuity: This page continues the discourse on the equality of all practitioners within the ritual circle (Cakra), moving from the abolition of caste distinctions to the divine identification of the participants as Shiva and Shakti themselves. It concludes the Eighth Exultation with instructions on ritual union and the purification of intent.</meta>

# In the Kularnava Tantra
<note>original: "Kulārṇava Tantre"</note>

->Whether they are seated in a row or perfectly in a circle, O Beloved! In the midst of that circle, one should worship everyone with the realization that they are Shiva and Shakti. || 105 ||<-

->Just as we two <note>referring to the speakers, Shiva and his consort Parvati</note> are undivided, just as Lakshmi and Narayana <note>the goddess of fortune and the preserver god Vishnu</note> are one, and just as Vani and the Creator <note>original: "Vāṇī-vidhātārau"; the goddess of speech Sarasvati and the creator god Brahma</note> are inseparable, so too is the condition of the Hero <note>term: "Vīra" (an advanced Tantric practitioner who has overcome human passions)</note> with his Power <note>term: "Śakti" (the female partner in ritual, embodying the divine feminine energy)</note>. || 106 ||<-

->O woman of beautiful limbs <note>original: "varārohe"</note>! I am not satisfied by thousands of vessels of wine <note>original: "madhu", literally honey, but contextually ritual wine</note> nor by hundreds of loads of meat, without the nectar arising from the union of the generative symbols <note>original: "bhaga-liṅgāmṛtaṃ"; referring to the "nectar" produced during ritual sexual union</note>. || 107 ||<-

**The World as the form of Shiva and Shakti:**
->This world does not bear the mark of the Discus <note>original: "Cakra"; a symbol of Vishnu</note>, nor the mark of the Lotus, nor the mark of the Thunderbolt <note>original: "Vajra"; a symbol of Indra or Buddhist traditions</note>. In truth, it bears the marks of the male and female generative organs <note>original: "Liṅga" and "Bhaga"</note>. Therefore, the entire world is the very essence of Shakti and Shiva. || 108 ||<-

**Samadhi from the union of Shiva and Shakti:**
->At the moment when the union of Shiva and Shakti occurs, that is the true "twilight prayer" <note>term: "Sandhyā" (the traditional daily prayers performed at dawn, noon, and dusk)</note> for those devoted to the Kula path; that moment is ordained as the state of deep meditative absorption <note>term: "Samādhi"</note>. || 109 ||<-

**Voluptuousness prohibited:**
->A man driven by mere lust should not approach a woman for union if she is uninitiated <note>original: "adīkṣitām"</note>, even if she desires it. He should approach a woman only when she has been purified by the prescribed rituals <note>original: "saṃskāra"</note>. || 110 ||<-

->Thus, the distinctions regarding the three principles <note>term: "Tattvas" (Reality, Soul, and Shiva)</note>, the exultations, and the rules of ritual drinking have been declared in brief. O Lady of the Kula <note>original: "Kuleśāni"</note>! What more do you wish to hear? || 111 ||<-

->Thus ends the eighth exultation, titled "The Discourse on the Three Principles, Ritual Drinking, and Other Distinctions," in the fifth section of the Upper Tradition Tantra, the Great Mystery, the Gateway to Liberation and Nirvana, the Best of all Scriptures, within the illustrious Kularnava [which consists of one hundred and twenty-five thousand verses]. || 8 ||<-
