Alternatively, O Pārvati! If nine beautiful young women who have reached maturity are easily available, the seeker who knows the sacred sounds <term>Mantras</term> should worship them with devotion during the Nine Nights <term>Navaratra</term>. || 34 ||

*Method of Worship of Nine Young Ladies :*
Or, O Pārvati ! If beautiful young nine ladies are easily available, then in the Nine Nights <note>The festival of Navaratra</note> the knower of Mantras should worship them with devotion.

Worshipping them respectively by the names: **Hṛllekhā** <note>The Sacred Vibration of the Heart</note>, **Gaganā** <note>The Sky or Infinite Space</note>, **Raktā** <note>The Red or Passionate One</note>, **Mahocchuṣmā** <note>The Great Fierce One</note>, **Karālikā** <note>The Terrifying One</note>, **Icchā** <note>Will</note>, **Jñānā** <note>Knowledge</note>, **Kriyā** <note>Action</note>, and **Durgā** <note>The Inaccessible</note>; one should also worship two boys representing the protector **Baṭuka** and the Lord of Obstacles **Gaṇeśvara**, satisfying them all with wine <note>original: "Madya"</note> and other ritual offerings as previously described. || 35 ||

*Worshipping them respectively with the names : 1 Hṛllekhā, 2 Gaganā, 3 Raktā, 4 Mahocchuṣmā, 5 Karālikā, 6 Icchā, 7 Jñānā, 8 Kriyā and 9 Durga, one should also worship two boys in the forms of Baṭuka and Gaṇeśvara and satisfy them all with wine, etc., materials as before.*

If those women are satisfied while joined in the bliss of the mature stage of ritual joy <term>Prauḍhānta-ullāsa</term> <note>The penultimate stage of ritual intoxication and spiritual ecstasy in this tradition</note>, O Beloved, then the practitioner <term>Sadhaka</term>, having attained total contentment, shall reside near You. || 36 ||

*Associating with the bliss of the mature stage, if the practitioner is able to satisfy the aforesaid Deities then he resides near You.*

O Devi! Whoever worships in this way every year with a steadfast vow, or every six months, or every three months, or even every month— || 37 ||
Whether worshipping three, five, or seven ladies with the mindset that they are Deities, that person—whose soul is enriched with all divine splendors—becomes a favorite of both of Us. || 38 ||

O My Beloved ! One who either every year or every six months or every three months or every month worships three, five or seven young ladies or girls treating them as Deities <term>Devatas</term>, obtains all splendours and also becomes a favourite of both of Us.

O Goddess of the Kula lineage <note>original: "Kuleśāni"</note>! On Fridays <note>original: "Bhṛguvāra"</note>, one should invite a beautiful, willing young woman who possesses all auspicious signs and is blooming with youth. || 39 ||
O Devi, one should invite a woman from the "Eight Families" <term>Kulāṣṭaka</term> <note>These are eight specific social or ritual lineages: the Outcaste, the Leatherworker, the Bard, the Low-caste, the Dog-cooker, the Butcher, the Fisherman, and the Woman of the World</note> who is in her fertile period. After she has purified her body with an oil bath, one should seat her upon a ritual throne. || 40 ||
The practitioner, knowing the proper rites, should decorate her with fragrance, flowers, and beautiful clothes. Thereafter, O Goddess of the Kula <note>original: "Kuleśvarī"</note>, the practitioner should also adorn himself with fragrance and flowers. || 41 ||

*Method of Śakti-worship on Fridays :*
O Goddess of the Kula ! On Fridays one should respectfully invite any of the beautiful willing young ladies bearing all the auspicious signs and blooming with youth out of the Eight Families (The Outcaste, Leatherworker, Bard, Low-caste, Dog-cooker, Butcher, Fisherman, and Woman of the World are the eight lineages) purify her body with a good bath, seat her properly and embellish her with fragrance, flowers and beautiful clothes. Thereafter, O Goddess of the Kula ! the practitioner also should adore himself with fragrance and flowers.

Then, invoking the Deity in the lady, one should worship her with incense and lamp in the order of ritual mantra placement <term>Nyāsa</term>, show her the lamps of the lineage <term>Kula-dīpaka</term>, and devotedly satisfy her with meat <term>Māṁsa</term>, various eatables, and drinks full of the six traditional flavors <note>Sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent</note>.

Thus, keeping his mind free from impurities, he should perform 1008 repetitions of the mantra. Then, offering the merit of the recitation <term>Japa</term>, he should spend the night with her.

Then, O My Beloved! On three, five, seven, or nine Fridays <note>original: "Bhṛguvāra"</note>, if he worships according to the prescribed rules in the same manner, then the merit he obtains cannot be measured. He also obtains the spiritual fruit of worship at all four major sacred pilgrimage centers <term>Pīṭhas</term> <note>The four primary seats of the Goddess in Tantric geography</note>, and whatever desires he has are indubitably fulfilled.

### *Worship of Nine Couples <term>Mithunas</term>:*

Or, O My Beloved! One should worship couples <term>Mithunas</term> on the days when the Sun transfers into a new zodiac sign <term>Saṁkrānti</term>, specifically in the signs of Cancer <note>Karka</note>, Capricorn <note>Makara</note>, Gemini <note>Mithuna</note>, Libra <note>Tulā</note>, Leo <note>Siṁha</note>, Aries <note>Meṣa</note>, or indeed during any of the Sun's transits.

Gauri and Shiva, Rama and Vishnu, Vani and the Lotus-Seated One <note>Saraswati and Brahma</note>, Shachi and Indra, Rohini and the Moon, Svaha and the Fire-god, Prabha and the Sun, Bhadrakali and Virabhadra, and also Bhairavi and Bhairava. These nine divine couples <term>Mithuna</term> should be worshipped following the path previously described. || 50–51 ||

1. Gaurī-Śiva, 2. Ramā-Viṣṇu, 3. Vāṇī-Brahmā, 4. Śacī-Indra, 5. Rohiṇī-Candramā, 6. Svāhā-Agni, 7. Prabhā-Ravi, 8. Kālī-Vīrabhadra and 9. Bhairavī-Bhairava are the nine couples which should be worshipped as per procedure already described.

The practitioner who knows the ritual procedure should place three 'Taras' <note>The sacred syllable Auṁ</note> at the beginning of each name and the word of salutation <note>original: "Namaḥ"</note> at the end. Between these, the names of the couples should be placed <note>For example: Auṁ Auṁ Auṁ Gaurī-Śivābhyāṁ Namaḥ</note>. A knower of the procedures should place three Tāras (three Āuṁs) in the beginning of each name, Namaḥ at the end, and in-between the names of couples (i.e. Auṁ Auṁ Auṁ Gaurī-Śivābhyāṁ Namaḥ, etc.) and worship them with fragrance, flowers and also satisfy with **Madya**, etc.

One should contemplate these couples while in the state of mature ritual ecstasy <term>Prauḍhānta-ullāsa</term>. O Goddess, when this is done, there is no doubt that the deities of these couples are satisfied; they show their grace and grant all heart's desires. || 53 ||

Thereafter, associated with **Prauḍhānta-ullāsa** remember the Deities in their Couple Form. O Devi! By worshipping thus the Devatā-couples are satisfied, show compassion and indubitably fulfil the desires of the Sādhaka.

He who performs this worship of the divine couples with devotion every year shall dwell in Your realm, endowed with all divine powers and splendors. || 54 ||

One who worships the couples with devotion every year, possessing all the splendours resides in Your world.

Now, O Supreme Goddess <note>original: "Īśvarī"</note>, on the first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha <note>The lunar month corresponding to April-May</note>, one should rise during the auspicious pre-dawn hours <term>Brāhme Muhūrte</term>. After performing the ritual bath and the morning prayers <term>Sandhyā</term>, one should go to a pleasant, secluded place and sit facing the East. The practitioner, knowing the rules, should then adorn himself with fragrances and flowers. || 55–56 ||

### *Worship of the Heart-Chosen Deity <term>Iṣṭa Devatā</term> in the Second Month (Vaiśākha):*

O Īśvarī! Rising at early dawn on the first day of the lighted fortnight of Vaiśākha one should, after a purificatory bath and Sandhyā, etc., and adoring himself with fragrances and flowers as prescribed, sit at a quiet place and face Eastwards.

->Having performed the ritual placements <term>Nyāsas: the practice of touching body parts to install divine energy</term> described earlier, one should dwell in the feeling of being one with the deity.<-

After performing the ritual placements <note>original: "Nyāsas"</note> as described earlier, absorb yourself in the feeling of the Divine. ->Meditating upon that sacred circle of the Goddess,<-

Concentrating on the sacred circle <note>original: "maṇḍala"; some traditions interpret "Stana-maṇḍala" here as the breasts of the Goddess</note> of the Goddess, perform 1,008 recitations <term>Japa</term>. Then, offering the fruits of the recitation, worship the deity and bid her farewell.

->one should daily perform the recitation and worship until the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, O Mother. || 62 ||<-

O Mother <note>original: "Ambike"</note>! In this manner, beginning on the auspicious first day of the waxing moon <term>Śukla-pakṣa</term>, daily perform the recitation and worship up to the fourteenth day of the waning moon <term>Kṛṣṇa-pakṣa</term>.

->Whoever performs this worship at sunrise for one full month,<-

If a practitioner <term>Sādhaka</term> performs this worship at sunrise for one month, then the deities, being pleased with him, fulfill his desires.

->One should worship the Lord at midday and also worship Him in the evening, O Beloved.<-

### **Worship of the Chosen Deity in the month of Māgha**
*(The 11th month of the Hindu Calendar)*:
Fasting on the first day of the waxing moon in the month of Māgha and putting on white clothes after a purifying bath, one should perform worship in the evening.

->Following the path prescribed for Sun-worship, equipped with all necessary materials,<-
->and joined with the exuberance of youth <note>original: "Yauvanollāsa"; a state of ritual joy or vitality</note>, one should meditate on the deity residing in the Moon. || 68 ||<-

Then, equipped with all the ritual items <note>original: "Dravyas"</note> mentioned previously in connection with Sun-worship, and entering a state of ritual exuberance, meditate upon the deity situated within the Moon <note>interpreted here as the seat of the mind</note>.

->Until the Moon sets, one should repeat the mantra with undivided attention.<-
->One should worship in this manner every day until the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight. || 69 ||<-

The seeker should, with a concentrated mind, perform the rhythmic repetition of the mantra <term>Japa</term> until the Moon sets. He should regularly perform this worship every night up to the fourteenth day of the waxing moon.

->On the Full Moon day, one should worship the divine energies and the noble practitioners according to one's capacity.<-
->O Beloved, whoever performs the worship of the bright fortnight with devotion,<-
->becomes a soul purified of all sins, endowed with all lordly powers,<-
->and becomes the sole object of worship for all worlds, living like Shiva upon the Earth. || 70–71 ||<-

On the Full Moon day, the seeker should worship the divine feminine energies <note>original: "Śaktis"</note> and the practitioners of the Kaula path <note>original: "Kaulikas"</note> to the best of their ability. Whoever devotedly performs this worship during the waxing moon becomes free of all sins, purifies their soul, and obtains every form of divine splendor. Such a person is honored by everyone and lives as a manifestation of the god Shiva here on Earth.

->Just as worship in the bright fortnight is fruitful, so it is in the dark fortnight.<-

Worship performed during the dark half of the month <note>original: "Asita-pakshe" — the waning moon</note> is just as effective as that performed during the bright half. Therefore, a practitioner who follows the proper procedures will find all their wishes granted.

### *Worship of the Chosen Deity in Kārtika (Eighth month):*

O Supreme Goddess! On the first day of the waxing moon in the month of Kārtika, the practitioner should take a purifying bath, perform <term>Ācamana: the ritual sipping of water for purification</term>, and execute the <term>Nyāsas: the practice of "placing" the energy of mantras onto different parts of the body</term> as previously instructed.

->When the world of living beings is asleep, with a joyful heart at the Great Night,<-
->following the previously mentioned rules of worship and equipped with all materials... || 75 ||<-

During the "Great Night" <note>original: "Mahānishi" — refers to the powerful spiritual window around midnight</note>, when the rest of the world is asleep, the seeker should joyfully prepare all the necessary <term>Dravyas: ritual substances or offerings</term> according to the established tradition.

->Having lit a wick as thick as the ring finger in clarified butter, O Parvati,<-

O Goddess Parvati! The seeker should light a thick lamp-wick—roughly the width of the ring finger—soaked in <term>Ghee: clarified butter</term>. This should be placed upon a <term>Yantra: a sacred geometric diagram</term> in the shape of an eight-petalled lotus, created using ritual powders of five different colors.

->In a beautiful bronze vessel filled with honey,<-
->having placed the lamp in front while facing the North... || 77 ||<-

A beautiful bronze pot should be filled with <term>Madhu: literally "honey," but in this Tantric context, it often refers to ritual wine</term>. The practitioner should then sit facing North and place the lamp in front of this vessel.

->One should worship the Goddess with Her attendants, meditating on Her within the lamp.<-
->Joined with the exuberance of youth, one should remember the Deity situated in the lamp. || 78 ||<-

The seeker should meditate on the Goddess <note>original: "Devī"</note> and her surrounding retinue of deities as being present within the flame of the lamp. While maintaining a state of <term>Yauvanollāsa: "the exuberance of youth," a specific ritual state of vitality and joy</term>, the seeker should focus their mind entirely on the Divinity residing within that light.

### *Worship of the Eight-by-Eight Group:* <note>original: "Aṣṭāṣṭaka"</note>

If capable, one should perform the worship of the "Eight-by-Eight" group in a single day. Alternatively, O Goddess, one may have it completed over a period of eight, sixteen, thirty-two, or sixty-four days. || 82 ||

This should be performed by a <term>Guru: spiritual teacher</term> who knows the ritual sequence, or by another knowledgeable person. If the practitioner himself knows the sequence, he may perform it himself, provided he is free from <term>Vitta-shāthya: "financial stinginess," or the withholding of resources required for the ritual</term>. || 83 ||

O My Beloved! The "Root Eight" <note>original: "Mūlāṣṭaka"</note> consist of the eight <term>Mātṛkās: Mother Goddesses</term> led by Brāhmī, and the eight <term>Bhairavas: fierce forms of Shiva</term> led by Asitāṅga, along with their auspicious pairs; these are the ones designated by this term. || 84 ||

---

1. Brāhmī, Nārāyaṇī, Maheśvarī, Cāmuṇḍā, Kaumārī, Aparājitā, Vārāhī, and Nārasiṃhī are the eight <term>Kulāṣṭaka: the eight goddesses of the Kula tradition</term>. (Cf. *Bṛhat Tantrasāra* 10th Edition, p. 531). However, elsewhere there is a slight difference in the list of names: Brahmāṇī, Maheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, Aindrī, Cāmuṇḍā, and Mahālakṣmī are mentioned instead (Cf. *Vāmakeśvara Tantrāntargata Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava* I. 169-171).

2. The eight Bhairavas led by Asitāṅga are: Asitāṅga ("Black-limbed"), Ruru ("The Hound"), Caṇḍa ("The Fierce"), Krodha ("Wrath"), Unmatta ("The Mad"), Kapālī ("The Skull-bearer"), Bhīṣaṇa ("The Terrifying"), and Saṃhāra ("The Destroyer") (Cf. *Puraścaryārṇava*, Vol. II, p. 473).

# Tenth Chapter <note>original: "Dashama Ullāsaḥ"</note>

Famous in the scriptures of the <term>Kula tradition: a prominent lineage of Tantric practice</term> <note>original: "Kulāgama"</note> as originating from the "Root Eight" <note>original: "Mūlāṣṭaka"</note>, one should worship the sixty-four divine couples, beginning with the Unshakeable One <note>original: "Akṣobhya"</note> and his consort. || 85 ||

One should worship them according to the procedure mentioned earlier, to the full extent of one's wealth and resources. For the fulfillment of one’s desired goals, there should be no lapse in the proper ritual order. || 86 ||

O Goddess <note>original: "Devi"</note>! With extreme devotion, one should fully satisfy these divine couples with fragrances, flowers, <term>Akshata: whole, unbroken grains of rice used as a sacred offering</term>, fish, meat, and wine, as well as various types of foods and drinks endowed with the six traditional flavors. || 87 ||

O Mother <note>original: "Ambike"</note>! One should worship the <term>Shri Cakra: the "Great Wheel," a sacred geometric map of the cosmos and the Goddess</term> until the stage of "Mature Bliss" <note>original: "Prauḍhānta-ullāsa"</note> is achieved. O Goddess, whoever performs this "Eight-by-Eight" <note>original: "Aṣṭāṣṭaka"</note> worship even once is honored by the high gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Shiva <note>original: "Maheśa"</note>. || 88 ||

If the gods themselves honor such a person, what then of mere humans? In truth, such a <term>Sadhaka: a dedicated spiritual practitioner</term> becomes like another Shiva in person. || 89 ||

By performing this worship, praised by the assembly of sixty-four <term>Yoginis: powerful female deities who represent various aspects of consciousness and energy</term>, the practitioner becomes free from the cycle of rebirth and resides forever in Your presence. || 90 ||

O Supreme Goddess <note>original: "Parameśvarī"</note>! This worship is the source of pleasure for all the deities. There is no worship superior to this; this is the truth, and there is no doubt about it. || 91 ||

O My Beloved! One who views this "Eight-by-Eight" Wheel <note>original: "Cakra"</note> with devotion receives the spiritual merit of ten million sacrifices, acts of charity, austerities, pilgrimages, and sacred observances. || 92 ||

->Without the **Kula-Worship** <note>original: "Kula-pūjā"; the central ritual system of the Kula tradition, focusing on the union of Shiva and Shakti</note>, one has no right whatsoever to participate in the **Sacred Circle** <note>original: "Cakra"; a ritual gathering of initiated practitioners</note>. **Eulogy of Kula-Worship:**

->Therefore, with every effort, in all conditions, and at all times, one should be devoted to Kula-Worship for the successful attainment of one’s desired fruits. || 111 ||<-

->There is no sacrifice greater than Kula-Worship, no vow greater than Kula-Worship, no pilgrimage greater than Kula-Worship, and no austerity greater than Kula-Worship. || 112 ||<-

->There is no righteousness greater than Kula-Worship, no reward greater than Kula-Worship, no meditation greater than Kula-Worship, and no splendor greater than Kula-Worship. || 114 ||<-

->It does not exist, it does not exist—again, it does not exist! I swear to you, O **Chieftainess of the Kula** <note>original: "Kulanāyike"</note>! What is the use of speaking much here? Listen to the secret, **O Daughter of the Mountain** <note>original: "Pārvati"</note>: || 116 ||<-

->Whoever performs Kula-Worship alongside the path prescribed by the **Vedic scriptures** <note>original: "Veda-shāstra"</note>, know that I and You <note>The divine couple Shiva and Shakti</note>, O **Beautiful Lady** <note>original: "Bhāvinī"</note>, reside near him and nowhere else. <header>### Chapter Ten</header>

...no knowledge greater than **Kula-Worship** <note>original: "Kula-pūjā"; the central ritual of the Kula tradition</note>, no greater **Comfort** than Kula-Worship, no greater **Sacred Law** <note>original: "Dharma"</note> than Kula-Worship, no greater **Fruit** than Kula-Worship, no greater **Meditation** <note>original: "Dhyāna"</note> than Kula-Worship, no greater **Radiance** <note>original: "Tejas"</note> than Kula-Worship, no greater **Union** <note>original: "Yoga"</note> than Kula-Worship, no greater **State** than Kula-Worship, no better **Fate** than Kula-Worship, and no greater worship than Kula-Worship. 

O **Leader of the Kula** <note>original: "Kulanāyike"; an address to the Goddess</note>! I swear by You that there is nothing, nothing, and again nothing greater than Kula-Worship. Why speak at length? Listen, O **Parvati** <note>the Goddess, consort of Shiva</note>, to this secret: Know that I sit near him who performs Kula-Worship according to the procedures prescribed in the **Sacred Scriptures** <note>original: "Vedas and Śāstras"</note>. I do not live elsewhere. This is a truth, a veritable truth, and again a truth; there is no doubt about it.

->O Beloved, there are those who move in the sky, on the earth, in the directions, in the waters, on mountains, and in forests.<-
->There are a hundred billion **Goddesses** <note>original: "Yoginīs"</note> and just as many **Fierce Protectors** <note>original: "Bhairavas"</note> as well.<-
->O Devi, I have appointed them specifically for the protection of the Kula. || 118 ||<-
->Day after day, O Parvati, with joyful faces,<-
->they look upon the **practitioners** <note>original: "Sādhakas"</note> with the desire to receive their own worship. || 119 ||<-

For the protection of the Kula path, O Goddess, I have appointed a hundred billion Yoginis and an equal number of Bhairavas who constantly roam the skies, the earth, the cardinal directions, the waters, the mountains, and the forests. O Parvati! All these beings look toward the practitioner daily with joyful countenances, longing to be honored in ritual.

->When unworshipped, they create obstacles, but when well-worshipped, they protect<-
->those devoted to the Teacher, those of good conduct, those who keep the secret teachings, and those who are peaceful like Shiva. || 120 ||<-
->They destroy those lacking devotion, those of wicked conduct, and those who reveal the secrets.<-
->Therefore, O Beloved, one should remember the Yoginis and Bhairavas within the **Sacred Wheel** <note>original: "Śrī Cakra"; a complex geometric diagram used in Tantric worship</note>. || 121 ||<-
->If a foolish-minded person does not remember them, he becomes the **tethered beast** <note>original: "Paśu"; a term for the uninitiated or those bound by worldly ignorance</note> of the Yoginis.<-
->Therefore, one should remember all the **Deities** <note>original: "Devatās"</note> within the Sacred Wheel. || 122 ||<-
->O Mistress of the Gods, they surely bestow grace upon the practitioners; of this there is no doubt.<-

When these spirits are not honored, they hinder progress, but when properly worshipped, they guard the devotees of the Guru, the virtuous, and those who maintain the sanctity of the secret path. Conversely, they bring ruin to those who lack faith, those who behave wickedly, and those who publicize the hidden mysteries. Consequently, O Beloved, one must always keep the Yoginis and Bhairavas in mind while focused on the Sacred Wheel. If a fool neglects this, he falls into a state of spiritual bondage, becoming like cattle to the Yoginis. Therefore, one must honor all the deities within the Sacred Wheel, for they undoubtedly grant their blessings to the practitioner.

# Chapter Eleven

---

->The Auspicious Goddess said:<-

O Lord of the Kula <note>original: "Kuleśa"</note>! I wish to hear about the orderly system of the Kula path <note>original: "Kulācāra-krama"</note>, which is worshipped by all the world. O Lord, O Ocean of Compassion, please describe it to me. || 1 ||

->The Lord Shiva said:<-

Listen, O Goddess! I shall explain what You have asked of me. By the mere act of hearing this teaching, a soul is liberated from the "animal bondage" <note>original: "pashu-pasha"; in Tantric thought, this refers to the limitations of the uninitiated soul, bound like an animal by worldly ties</note>. || 2 ||

If an initiated senior practitioner <note>original: "dikshito jyeshthah"</note> is, for some reason, unable to perform the Kula-worship <note>original: "Kula-pūjā"</note>, then a junior practitioner who knows the proper ritual sequence should perform the ceremony instead. || 3 ||

The junior should approach the senior, saluting him as if he were the Guru itself. After offering everything to the senior, the junior should then consume the remains <note>original: "shesha"; the sanctified remnants of the offering</note>, O Daughter of the Mountain. || 4 ||

If the Guru, a senior initiate, or a venerable person arrives in the middle of a ritual, the practitioner <note>original: "Sādhaka"</note> should offer salutations while remaining in their ritual seat and, after obtaining permission, proceed with the remaining rites. || 5 ||

O Queen of the Kula <note>original: "Kulanāyike"</note>, when seniors and juniors are gathered together in one place, the conduct between them is declared to be exactly as described before. || 6 ||

### In the Kularnava Tantra

->When an unknown practitioner of the Kula path <note>original: "Kaulika"</note> arrives, one should consider the traditional order of precedence.<-
->Remembering one’s own Guru, O Goddess, one should offer water libations according to one’s own specific practice. || 7 ||<-

*In the event of arrival of an unknown follower of the Kula tradition:*

In the event of the arrival of an unknown practitioner, one should observe the traditional formalities and, remembering their Spiritual Teacher <note>original: "Gurudeva"</note>, offer water libations according to one’s own established practice.

->One should perform daily worship during the day and occasional ritual worship at night.<-
->It is the decision of the scriptures <note>original: "Shastra"</note> that both are rituals performed for specific desired results. || 8 ||<-

*Time of Worship:*

Daily worship <note>original: "Nityārcana"</note> should be performed in the daytime, while occasional worship <note>original: "Naimittikārcana"</note> should be performed at night. Both are considered desirable rituals <note>original: "Kamya-karmani"</note>—so has been declared by the sacred scriptures.

->Without bathing, or without sitting on a proper ritual seat, or after eating, or while talking idly,<-
->Or without being adorned with perfumes, flowers, consecrated grains, and appropriate ritual robes,<-
->Or without performing the ritual placement of energy <term>Nyāsa</term> <note>the practice of "placing" sacred sounds or deities upon the body to sanctify it</note> in the body, one should not perform the Kula-worship. || 9 ||<-

*Duties regarding Worship:*

Without bathing or without sitting on a proper seat, or after meals, or while prattling, or without adorning oneself with proper clothing, or without performing the ritual placement of mantras <term>Nyāsa</term> upon the body, one should not perform the Kula-worship <term>Kula-pūjā</term>.

->O My Beloved! Worship without a sacred chant, libations without meat,<-
->And drinking without the presence of the female ritual partners has been declared to be fruitless. || 10 ||<-

O My Beloved! Worship <term>Pūjā</term> without a sacred chant <term>Mantra</term>, libations <term>Tarpaṇa</term> without meat <term>Māṁsa</term>, and anything drunk without the presence of the female ritual partners <term>Śaktis</term> has been said to be fruitless.

->One should perform the worship of the Sacred Circle alone, but should not worship using a single vessel.<-
->One should neither worship with only one hand, nor drink with only one hand. || 11 ||<-

One should neither perform worship of the Sacred Geometric Chart <term>Śrī Cakra</term> alone, nor worship in the same vessel, nor worship with one hand, nor drink with one hand.

->O Goddess, one should not worship with fish, meat, and wine in the presence of an uninitiated person.<-
->One should enter the ritual circle only after bowing, and depart also after bowing. || 12 ||<-

Worshipping with fish <term>Matsya</term>, meat <term>Māṁsa</term>, and wine <term>Āsava</term> should not be performed near an uninitiated person <term>Paśu</term> <note>Literally "animal," referring to those bound by worldly conventions and not yet initiated into these mysteries</note>. The practitioner <term>Sādhaka</term> should enter the ritual circle <term>Cakra</term> only after offering salutations and depart also after offering salutations.

### Eleventh Chapter

->On the Śrī Cakra <note>the sacred geometric diagram representing the cosmos and the Goddess</note>, one should neither remain standing nor sit in the Hero’s Posture <term>Vīrāsana</term> <note>a specific yoga posture where one sits on the heels or with one knee up</note>, O Beloved.<-
->O Goddess! Simply gazing upon the Śrī Cakra destroys the sins committed by the eyes.<-
->If a practitioner of the Kula path <note>original: "Kaulika"</note> does not see it, his two eyes are not truly eyes, but are merely a pair of wounds. || 13 ||<-

O My Beloved! In the presence of the Śrī Cakra, one should neither stand upon the ritual seat nor sit in the Vīrāsana posture. O Devi! The act of seeing the Śrī Cakra itself destroys visual sins. If a Kaulika is unable to see the Śrī Cakra, then his two eyes do not remain eyes and become, as it were, two wounds.

->O Devi! Even the improper behavior of those within the ritual circle—both the female practitioners <note>original: "Śaktis"</note> and the male practitioners—becomes proper conduct.<-
->One should meditate upon them with the mindset that they are the gods Śiva and Gaurī, and they must never be disrespected. || 14 ||<-

Even the improper behavior of Śaktis and Kaulikas sitting in a ritual circle <note>original: "Cakra"</note> becomes proper. O Devi! They should be treated as the divine couple Gaurī and Śiva and should not be disregarded.

->Going to the house of a Kula teacher <note>original: "Kulācārya"</note> with devotion for the purification of sins,<-
->one should request the sacred nectar and food; in its absence, one should drink only water. || 15 ||<-

*Request for nectar in the house of a Kulācārya:*

If one goes to the house of a Kulācārya, he should then, in order to be released from sins, devotedly request for nectar <note>referring to consecrated ritual wine</note> and in its absence drink just water.

->When a vessel is offered with devotion by the Kula teacher or his consort,<-
->one should receive it only after bowing; otherwise, one goes to hell. || 16 ||<-

Saluting the vessel offered by the Kulācārya or his Śakti, one should receive it with devotion, otherwise he will have to go to Hell.

->O Mistress of the Kula! Whether due to a lack of bathing, a lack of devotion, or out of simple greed,<-
->whoever consumes the sacred substances of the Kula will fall into poverty. || 17 ||<-

*Rules regarding drinking of Kula-dravya <note>sacred ritual substances, usually wine, meat, or grain</note>:*

One who resorts to Kula-substance without bathing, without devotion, or out of greed, he, O Kuleśvari, falls to poverty.

->One who is wearing a turban, wearing a tunic, or who is naked, with hair disheveled, or surrounded by a crowd,<-
->or who is distracted, angry, or argumentative, should not consume the Kula-nectar. || 18 ||<-

One wearing a turban or tailored upper garments <note>original: "kañcukī"</note> or who is naked, who has disheveled hair, who is in the company of uninitiated persons, or who is quarrelsome, uneasy, or angry, should not drink the Kula-nectar <note>original: "Kulāmṛta"</note>.

->By spitting out the nectar of union, by exhaustion from the wine-vessel,<-
->or by drinking through an upward pipe <note>such as a straw</note>, one receives the curse of the deities. || 19 ||<-

One who drinks wine from a vessel that has passed through too many hands, or which contains the backwash of others, or from which wine is drunk through a sucking pipe, receives the curse of the Deities <note>original: "Devatās"</note>.

<meta>This page continues the eleventh chapter of the Kularnava Tantra, moving from the internal meditations on the Śrī Cakra to the strict behavioral codes (Acaras) required during the communal ritual. ### In the Kularnava Tantra

->Sitting on a single seat, eating from a single vessel,<-
->and drinking the ritual liquid from the same cup—these lead to Hell, O Beloved. || 20 ||<-

O My Beloved! All those who sit on the same seat, who take food from the same vessel and who drink ritual substances <term>Dravyas</term> <note>original: "dravyas"; refers to consecrated liquids, often wine, used in the ritual</note> from the same pot, go to Hell.

->If a Guru, a knower of the Kula, his son, or a senior teacher of the Kula path lives in the same village,<-
->one should not partake of the ritual substances without their permission, O Great Goddess; otherwise, he goes to eternal Hell. || 21 ||<-

O Great Goddess <note>original: "Maheśāni"</note>! If the Guru or his son or his descendants <note>the lineage of the teacher</note> live in the same village or township where the practitioner <term>Sādhaka</term> <note>one who follows a spiritual discipline</note> is also living, then such a practitioner should partake of the sacred Kula-substances only after their permission. Otherwise the practitioner will have to go to Hell.

->One should not touch the ritual substances while unclean within the circle, O Pārvatī.<-
->After washing one's hands outside, one may then offer the ritual substances. || 22 ||<-

->*Behaviours prohibited in the Cakra* <note>original: "Cakra"; the ritual circle or assembly of practitioners</note>:<-

O Pārvatī <note>the Goddess to whom the text is addressed</note>! In a Kula <note>the Tantric tradition or family</note> one should not touch the ritual substances with unclean hands. Only after washing his hands outside the ritual circle should one give the sacred substances to others.

->One should not fill a vessel by lifting the wine-container, O Beloved.<-
->The drinking vessel should never be dipped into the wine-jar. || 23 ||<-

O My Beloved! A practitioner should not fill the vessel by lifting the wine container and should never dip the vessel he is drinking from into that container <note>this preserves the ritual purity of the source container</note>.

->He who, with a foolish mind, washes his hands and so forth in the midst of the circle,<-
->that foolish soul becomes the very abode of calamities. || 24 ||<-

In order to clean himself one who washes his hands, etc. right in the midst of the ritual circle itself, that fool is overtaken by calamities.

->Spitting, excreting, urinating, or passing gas—<-
->whoever does these in the midst of the Holy Circle becomes a beast of the Yoginīs. || 25 ||<-

One who eases himself, passes urine or farts in the midst of the ritual circle becomes a "beast" <term>Paśu</term> <note>original: "paśu"; a term for an uninitiated or spiritually "bound" individual who lacks higher awareness</note> of the semi-divine female spirits <term>Yoginīs</term>.

->If a jar breaks in the midst of the circle, or a vessel falls to the ground,<-
->or if the lamp is extinguished, one should perform the Holy Circle ritual again for purification, O Beloved. || 26 ||<-

O My Beloved! To pacify the sin incurred in the event of breaking a pot or its falling down on the ground, or the extinguishing of the lamp in the midst of a ritual circle, the Holy Circle <term>Śrī Cakra</term> should be worshipped afresh.

### Eleventh Chapter 177

->The wise, when inspired by the ritual, chant, meditate, offer praise, and bow;<-
->they instruct others, ask sacred questions, and rejoice, O Beloved. || 27 ||<-
->The ignorant, when intoxicated, wander about, roar, laugh, and quarrel;<-
->they weep, lust after women, and speak ill of others, O Beloved. || 28 ||<-

O My Beloved! The wise in the <term>Cakra</term> <note>the sacred ritual circle or assembly of practitioners</note> perform <term>Japa</term> <note>meditative chanting of a mantra</note> and <term>Dhyāna</term> <note>focused meditation</note>, recite <term>Stotras</term> <note>hymns of praise</note>, salute the divine, preach the teachings, show a desire for knowledge, and take delight in the spirit. On the other hand, O My Beloved! the ignorant simply become intoxicated; they roam aimlessly and shout, laugh and fight, cry, feel worldly desire for women, and criticize others.

->Joking, idle chatter, useless debate, and excessive talking,<-
->indifference, fear, and anger should all be avoided within the circle. || 29 ||<-

Joking, useless or excessive talking, sorrow, fear, and anger are strictly prohibited while inside a ritual circle.

->O Great Goddess, one should not wander within the circle with a vessel in hand;<-
->holding a full vessel in his hands, O Beloved, one should not sit indefinitely. || 30 ||<-

O <term>Mahādevi</term> <note>original: "Great Goddess," a title for the consort of Shiva</note>! One must not walk around the ritual circle while holding a drinking pot. O My Beloved! If a person is holding a vessel filled with the ritual wine, they should not remain seated without action for a long period of time.

->One should not speak while holding the vessel, nor should one break the vessel, O Mother;<-
->one should not touch the vessel with the feet, nor let a single drop fall to the ground. || 31 ||<-

O <term>Ambike</term> <note>original: "Mother," another name for the Goddess</note>! While holding the ritual drinking pot, one should not engage in idle talk. The vessel containing the wine should never be broken, nor should it be touched by one’s feet. One must be careful not to spill even a drop of the wine onto the ground.

->It should not be offered with only one hand, nor without the proper ritual gesture, O Beloved;<-
->the vessel should not be moved from its place, nor should one mix up the vessels. || 32 ||<-

The ritual wine container should not be handed to another using only one hand, nor should it be offered without the accompanying <term>Mudrā</term> <note>a symbolic or ritual hand gesture used to consecrate the act</note>. The vessel should not be shifted from its designated spot, and one must ensure that their vessel does not get mixed up with those of others.

->One should not make a sound while drinking, nor while filling the cup;<-
->one should not clink the vessels together, nor let them fall to the ground. || 33 ||<-

One should remain silent and not make gulping sounds while drinking the wine, nor should the act of filling the cup be noisy. The vessels should not be struck against one another, nor should they be allowed to fall.

->One should not lift the vessel with its base, nor set it down without a base;<-
->one should not leave the vessel empty, nor should one spin the vessel, O Beloved. || 34 ||<-

The drinking pot should not be lifted up along with its stand or support, nor should it be placed down where there is no proper support. O My Beloved! The pot should never be left completely empty, nor should it be rotated or spun around.

# Kularnava Tantra

->The wise person should not step over the ritual vessel, nor should they knock it over, O Beloved.<-
->The vessel should be cleaned and then kept hidden; this is the command, O Supreme Goddess. || 35 ||<-

O My Beloved! One should neither skip over the pot nor lift it up <note>or "displace/overturn" it</note>. It should be well hidden after cleaning. O <term>Parameśvari</term> <note>original: "Supreme Goddess," a title for the Goddess to whom Shiva is speaking</note>! this is the divine order.

*Loss caused by contact with the uninitiated (<term>Paśu</term>):*

->If, in a state of spiritual exuberance, a practitioner of the Kula path looks upon an uninitiated person,<-
->or reads the scriptures of the uninitiated, or associates with their women; || 36 ||<-
->or engages in the company of the uninitiated, or performs the tasks of the uninitiated,<-
->then their religion, wealth, lifespan, fame, merit, knowledge, and happiness are all destroyed. || 37 ||<-

In the state of exuberance, if a <term>Kaulika</term> <note>a practitioner of the Kula tradition of Tantra</note> keeps company with a <term>Paśu</term> <note>literally "beast"; here referring to an ordinary, uninitiated person bound by social conventions and ignorance</note> or reads the scriptures of the <term>Paśu</term> <note>original: Paśu-śāstras</note> or keeps company with an uninitiated woman or copulates with her or follows the ways of the uninitiated, then his own religion, finances, duration of life, merit, knowledge and comforts are all destroyed.

->Whoever, out of affection, greed, or fear, gives the sacred ritual substances<-
->of the sacred circle to the uninitiated, becomes a "beast" of the Yoginīs. || 38 ||<-

One who—out of personal desire, greed, or fear—offers the <term>Kuladravyas</term> <note>sacred ritual substances, often including wine and meat</note> of a <term>Śrī Cakra</term> <note>the sacred ritual assembly or the geometric diagram representing the cosmos</note> to others <note>the uninitiated</note> becomes a <term>Paśu</term> <note>an ignorant "beast"</note> in the eyes of the <term>Yoginīs</term> <note>the fierce female deities who guard the path and punish those who break its secrets</note>.

*Duties of a Practitioner (<term>Sādhaka</term>):*

->One should not engage in verbal disputes, even with an enemy, while within the circle;<-
->one should view them as a father or mother and tolerate whatever they say. || 39 ||<-

In the midst of a <term>Cakra</term> <note>the ritual circle</note> one should not enter into a controversy even with an enemy; instead, treat him as a father or mother and even bear his harsh words.

->Just as the heart rejoices upon seeing a wife, son, or friend,<-
->if one feels such joy upon seeing fellow practitioners, they become a favorite of the Yoginīs. || 40 ||<-

That pleasure which is derived from seeing one's own family members or friends—if that same joy is derived by a person on seeing a fellow <term>Kaulika</term>, then that person becomes a favorite of the <term>Yoginīs</term>.

->From the Creator down to the smallest blade of grass, everything is the lineage of my Guru;<-
->Since I am a disciple of everyone, who on earth is not worthy of my worship?<-
->One who holds this firm conviction becomes beloved by both of Us. || 41 ||<-

One who has such a definite attitude as: "From <term>Brahmā</term> <note>the creator god</note> to the smallest blade of grass <note>original: <term>stamba</term>, which can mean a pillar or a clump of grass, representing the lowest form of life</note>, everyone is for me like the offspring of my <term>Guru</term> <note>spiritual teacher</note> and I am a disciple of everybody; who on earth is not venerable for me," he becomes a favorite of both of Us <note>referring to Shiva and the Goddess</note>.

# Eleventh Chapter 176

->“I am the teacher, I am the elder, I am the knower of truth”—one who is filled with such pride, making this ego their only refuge, can never truly be a <term>Kaulika</term> <note>original: "kaulikaḥ"; a practitioner of the Kula tradition of Tantra who has realized the unity of all things</note>. || 42 ||<-

O Goddess <note>original: "Devi"</note>! With deep devotion, one should speak of the holy Teacher, the Kula scriptures <note>original: "Kulaśāstras"</note>, and the sacred places of worship only after prefixing their names with the honorific title "Sacred" <note>original: "Śrī"</note> and offering a bow. || 43 ||

O my Beloved! Except during the time of <term>Japa</term> <note>original: "japa-kāla"; the meditative repetition of a mantra</note>, one should not utter the personal name of their Teacher. During debates or spiritual practices, one should instead refer to him using titles such as "Holy Lord" <note>original: "Śrīnātha"</note>, "Divine One" <note>original: "Deva"</note>, or "Master" <note>original: "Svāmī"</note>. || 44 ||

O Goddess of the Gods <note>original: "Deveśi"</note>! The sacred lineage of the Teacher <note>original: "Śrī-guroḥ pādukāṃ"</note>, the secret ritual signs, the Root Mantra <note>original: "Mūla-mantraṃ"</note>, and one’s own spiritual lineage should never be disclosed to anyone except one's own disciple. || 45 ||

The oral traditions, the revealed scriptures <note>original: "Āgama"</note>, the sacred lineages <note>original: "Āmnāya"</note>, and the methods of mantra practice—O Beloved, all these are effective only when received directly from the mouth of a Teacher, and never in any other way. || 46 ||

The original book containing the sacred scriptures <note>original: "Śrī-śāstra"</note> should not be recited to others, O Beloved. Such a book should be worshipped daily with devotion and must never be passed into the hands of a <term>Paśu</term> <note>original: "paśu"; literally "beast," referring to an uninitiated person who lacks spiritual awareness</note>. || 47 ||

O <term>Pārvati</term> <note>the Goddess to whom Shiva is speaking</note>! One should cherish and serve the Kula scriptures as one would their own wife, and avoid the scriptures of the uninitiated as if they were the wives of others. || 48 ||

Just as milk kept in a container made of animal hide <note>original: "svacharmastham"; leather bags were considered ritually polluting</note> is unfit to be drunk by the "twice-born" <note>original: "dvija"; those initiated into the higher spiritual life</note>, so too should a practitioner of the Kula path never listen to teachings on duty or religion from the mouth of an uninitiated person. || 49 ||

<meta>This page continues the eleventh chapter of the Kularnava Tantra, moving from the internal discipline of the practitioner toward the social and ritual ethics of the Kula tradition. # In the Kularnava Tantra

->One who hears the sacred conduct of the lineage and one who speaks according to the scriptures—<-
->both of them truly attain the assembly of the Yoginis and the Heroes. || 50 ||<-
<note>original: "yoginī-vīra-melanam"; a "Yogini" is an enlightened female practitioner or deity, and a "Vira" is a "heroic" male practitioner. Their "meeting" represents a high state of spiritual realization and community.</note>

Those who listen to the <term>Kulachara</term> <note>original: "kulācāraṃ"; the specific conduct and rituals of the Kula path</note> and those who speak in accordance with the scriptures <note>original: "śāstra"</note> both attain the direct presence of the assembly of Yoginis and Heroes.

->O Lady of the Kula! Those who have no faith in this sacred duty of the lineage<-
->will not be released from hell even until the final cosmic dissolution. || 51 ||<-
<note>original: "saṃplavam"; refers to the Pralaya, the periodic destruction of the universe in Hindu cosmology.</note>

O <term>Kuleshvari</term> <note>original: "kuleśvari"; the Goddess as the sovereign of the Kula lineage</note>! Those who have no faith in this <term>Kuladharma</term> <note>original: "kuladharme"; the sacred path and laws of the Kula</note> are unable to free themselves from Hell even at the final dissolution of the universe.

### *Five types of the Teacher's Wife:*

->The married, the supported, the purchased, the beloved,<-
->and the one joined through desire—these are the five types of the Teacher's wives.<-
->Like the Teacher himself, all these wives are to be honored and never transgressed. || 52 ||<-
<note>original: "guru-yositah"; the wives or female consorts of the Guru. The text emphasizes that they hold the same sacred status as the Guru himself.</note>

The married wife <note>original: "ūḍhā"</note>, the woman supported or kept <note>original: "dhṛtā"</note>, the woman acquired through payment <note>original: "krītā"</note>, the woman bound by ties of love <note>original: "samāhṛtā"</note>, and the woman attached through sexual desire <note>original: "kāmaratā"</note> are the five kinds of wives of a Teacher <note>original: "Guru"</note>. Like the Teacher himself, all these are inviolate and venerable.

### *Prohibited Women:*

->One should not desire the Teacher's power-consort, the wife of a Hero, a young maiden, or one under a vow;<-
->nor should one desire a woman with missing limbs, a deformed woman, or a hunchback. || 53 ||<-

One should not harbor desire for the Teacher’s female counterpart <note>original: "guru-śaktiṃ"</note>, the wife of a Hero-practitioner <note>original: "vīra-bhāryāṃ"</note>, a virgin <note>original: "kumārīṃ"</note>, a woman bound by sacred observances <note>original: "vrata-dhāriṇīm"</note>, a woman missing a limb <note>original: "vyaṅgāṅgīṃ"</note>, a woman with a physical deformity <note>original: "vikṛtāṅgīṃ"</note>, or a hunchback <note>original: "kubjām"</note>.

->One’s daughter, sister, granddaughter, daughter-in-law, or even one's own beloved wife<-
->should not be desired in the presence of the Teacher, nor should one engage in union with another. || 54 ||<-

Daughter, sister, granddaughter, daughter-in-law, and even one's own beloved wife should not be looked upon with desire in the presence of the Teacher, nor should one engage in physical union with others in his sight.

### *Venerable Women:*

->One should worship women clothed in black, dark-complexioned women, maidens, and the slender-waisted;<-
->the charming and the youthful should be worshipped with the mindset that they are deities. || 55 ||<-

Women dressed in black <note>original: "kṛṣṇāṁśukā"</note>, dark-complexioned women <note>original: "kṛṣṇavarṇā"</note>, charming women <note>original: "manoharā"</note>, and young virgins <note>original: "kumārīञ्च"</note> should be worshipped as if they were embodiments of the Divine <note>original: "devatā-dhiyā"</note>.

->One must never, even once, use force against a Kula-yogini;<-
->within the sacred circle, O Beautiful Lady of the Kula, desire only those who are self-moved. || 56 ||<-

The <term>Kula-yogini</term> <note>original: "kula-yoginīm"; a female practitioner or priestess within the Kula tradition</note> should never be taken by force. Inside the ritual circle <note>original: "cakra-madhye"</note>, O <term>Kula-sundari</term> <note>original: "kula-sundari"; Beautiful Lady of the Kula</note>, one should only seek union with those who are themselves moved by spiritual passion or desire.

<summary>This page outlines the ethical code regarding women within the Tantric community, defining which women are to be venerated as divine embodiments and establishing strict rules against coercion and improper conduct in the presence of the Guru.</summary>
<keywords>Kulachara, Guru, Kula-yogini, Cakra, Kuladharma, ritual ethics, veneration of women, spiritual lineage</keywords>

# Chapter Eleven

->Raw meat, a pot of wine, an elephant in rut, one who bears the signs of spiritual success,<-
->a mango tree and an Ashoka tree, and young girls caught up in play; || 57 ||<-
<note>original: "siddhiligiṇam"; one who displays the outward signs of having attained "Siddhi" or supernatural/spiritual powers. In the Tantric context, items like meat and wine are often ritual substances (Sudha) rather than mere food.</note>

->A solitary tree, a cremation ground, a gathering of women,<-
->and a woman dressed in red—upon seeing these, one should bow with devotion. || 58 ||<-
<note>The color red is sacred to the Goddess (Shakti), and the cremation ground is considered a powerful site for meditation where the illusion of the ego is destroyed.</note>

### Things to be venerated when seen:

Raw meat, <term>Sura</term> <note>original: "surā"; a type of consecrated wine or spirit used in ritual</note>, a <term>Kumbha</term> <note>original: "kumbha"; a ritual pot or jar representing the womb or the universe</note>, an elephant in heat, one bearing the marks of spiritual attainments, the Ashoka tree, virgins engaged in play, a cremation ground, a group of women, and a red-robed lady—all these, when seen, should be worshipped with devotion.

->The Guru’s consort, the Guru’s son, the senior and junior teachers of the lineage,<-
->the scriptures of the Kula philosophy, the sacred ritual substances, and the practitioners of the path; || 59 ||<-
<note>original: "kula-dravyani"; the "Kula substances" are the materials used in Tantric ritual, often classified as the "Five M's" (Makaras).</note>

->Those who inspire, those who indicate the path, the speakers, the seers,<-
->the teachers, the awakeners, the Yogis, the Yoginis, and those who take the form of the perfected ones; || 60 ||<-
<note>original: "siddhirūpakān"; individuals who embody the state of a "Siddha" or perfected master.</note>

->A young girl, a maiden, or a woman who is naked or intoxicated—<-
->none of these should be condemned, despised, laughed at, or insulted. || 61 ||<-

->One should not speak unpleasantly or untruthfully to any practitioner of the lineage.<-
->A woman of the Kula should never be called "ugly" or "dark." || 62 ||<-
<note>original: "kṛṣṇeti"; literally "black." This instruction prohibits making disparaging remarks about the physical appearance of women within the sacred community, emphasizing their inherent divine nature over physical traits.</note>

### Prohibited actions:

The consort of the Guru, the son of the Guru, senior or junior <term>Kaula Sadhakas</term> <note>practitioners of the Kaula path</note>, the scriptures of the Kula philosophy, the sacred ritual substances, those who inspire, those who point the way, the representatives, seers, teachers, and preachers of the Kaulas, the <term>Yogis</term>, the <term>Yoginis</term>, perfected persons, a young girl, a maiden, or a woman who is naked or out of her mind—none of these should ever be condemned, derided, or disregarded. One must not address them harshly or speak untruthfully. A lady of the lineage should never be insulted for her appearance or skin color.

->One should not judge whether the actions of the devoted "Heroes" are right or wrong.<-
->One should not gaze at a woman who is naked, out of her mind, or whose breasts are exposed. || 63 ||<-
<note>original: "vīrāṇām"; the "Vira" or Hero is a practitioner who has reached a level of stability where they can engage with traditionally "polluting" substances without spiritual harm. The text warns against judging their unconventional behavior.</note>

->One should not engage in intimacy with a woman during the day, nor should one gaze upon her genitals.<-

The actions, whether performed or omitted, of the devoted "Heroes" should never be scrutinized, and one should never look at a naked, insane, or bare-breasted woman. Never engage in sexual union with a woman during the daylight hours, and never stare at her private parts.

->Whatever women there are in the world, they are all born from the Mother-Lineage.<-
->The Yoginis of the lineage become enraged by the mistreatment of women. || 64 ||<-

->Even if a woman commits a hundred offenses, one should not strike her even with a flower.<-
->One should not count the faults of women; one should only proclaim their virtues. || 65 ||<-

### All women are like Mothers:

Every woman in this world should be treated as a manifestation of the Divine Mother. The <term>Yoginis</term> <note>female deities or enlightened spirits</note> are angered by any offense against women. Even if a woman has done wrong many times, a practitioner must not strike her, even with something as light as a flower. Do not dwell on the shortcomings of women; instead, speak only of their good qualities.

<summary>This page outlines the ethical code of the Kula tradition, listing sacred objects to be venerated and prohibiting the disparagement of practitioners and women. It establishes that all women are manifestations of the Divine Mother and must be treated with absolute respect, regardless of their actions or appearance.</summary>

<header>In the Kularnava Tantra</header>

...should be treated like mothers. Outraging the modesty of women angers the <term>Yoginīs</term> <note>original: "yoginī"; semi-divine female spirits or powerful female practitioners who guard the secrets of the Tantra</note>. Even if a lady commits a hundred crimes, she should never be struck, not even with a flower. The faults of women should never be counted, and their virtues should always be spoken of publicly.

->The Kula Yoginis always reside within the Kula trees;<-
->one should not eat from their leaves, but rather worship them with special care. || 66 ||<-

### *About the Sacred Kula Trees:*

The Kula Yoginīs <note>The "Kula" refers to the lineage or "family" of the tradition, and these trees are considered their earthly dwellings.</note> always reside on <term>Kula-vṛkṣas</term> (sacred trees of the lineage). Therefore, one should not use the leaves of such trees as plates for food, and they should be given special worship.

->One should neither sleep beneath the Kula trees nor cause any disturbance there;<-
->upon seeing them, one should bow with devotion and never, ever cut them down. || 67 ||<-

One should neither sleep under the Kula trees nor create any disturbance or impurity beneath them. On the contrary, upon seeing or even hearing about such trees, one should salute them with deep devotion and never do them harm.

->The Shleshmataka, the Karanja, the Nimba, the Ashvattha, and the Kadamba;<-
->the Bilva, the Vata, the Udumbara, and the Tamarind is remembered as the ninth. || 68 ||<-

The nine sacred <term>Kulavṛkṣas</term> are:
1. **Śleṣmātaka** <note>original: *Cordia latifolia*; often called the Bird Lime tree</note>
2. **Karañja** <note>original: *Pongamia glabra*; the Indian Beech</note>
3. **Nimb** or **Nīma** <note>original: *Azadirachta Indica*; the Neem tree, known for its medicinal properties</note>
4. **Aśvattha** <note>original: *Ficus religiosa*; the Sacred Fig tree</note>
5. **Kadamba** <note>original: *Nauclea Cadamba*; the Burflower tree, associated with Lord Krishna</note>
6. **Bilva** <note>original: *Aegle marmelos*; the Bael tree, sacred to Shiva</note>
7. **Vaṭa** <note>original: *Ficus Indica*; the Banyan tree</note>
8. **Uḍumbara** <note>original: *Ficus glomerata*; the Cluster Fig tree</note>
9. **Tintidi** <note>The Tamarind tree</note>

->Penance, ritual suicide from a cliff, renunciation, and the taking of formal vows;<-
->going on external pilgrimages—these five a Kaula practitioner should avoid. || 69 ||<-

### *Five actions and five sins prohibited for Kaulikas:*

A <term>Kaula</term> <note>A follower of the Kula path, which emphasizes internal realization over external Vedic ritual</note> is prohibited from these five actions:
1. **Prāyaścitta** (performing traditional orthodox penance)
2. **Bhṛgupāta** (the act of committing suicide by leaping from a high precipice, once a radical form of religious sacrifice)
3. **Sanyāsa** (taking the vow of traditional monastic renunciation)
4. **Vrata-dhāraṇa** (adopting rigid external religious observances)
5. **Tīrthayātrā** (going on external pilgrimages to distant holy places)

<note>In the Tantric view, the body itself is the most sacred site; therefore, wandering to external temples or performing harsh physical penances is seen as unnecessary for one who has the internal secret knowledge.</note>

->The murder of a Hero, drinking for mere pleasure, and violating the wife of a Hero;<-
->stealing the ritual goods of a Hero, and associating with those who do so;<-
->these are declared the Great Sins for practitioners within the Kula lineage. || 70 ||<-

The five "Great Sins" (<term>Mahāpātaka</term>) for a <term>Kaulika</term> are:
1. **Vīrahatyā**: The murder of a <term>Vīra</term> <note>original: "vīra"; literally 'hero,' referring to an advanced Tantric practitioner who has mastered his passions</note>.
2. **Vṛthā-pāna**: Drinking wine for the sake of intoxication or pleasure rather than as a consecrated ritual substance.
3. Copulation with the wife of a fellow practitioner (Vīra).
4. Stealing the **Vīra-dravyas** (ritual substances or sacred objects belonging to a practitioner).
5. Association with those who commit the four acts listed above.

<header>Chapter Eleven</header>

->Knowledge of Truth is the essence of Shaivism, as the mastery of poisons is to the Garuda tradition;<-
->astrology finds its core in the study of eclipses, while the Kaula path is defined by restraint and grace. || 71 ||<-

### *Speciality of the Kaulas: 1. Restraint and 2. Kindness:*

The essence of the <term>Shaiva</term> <note>The path dedicated to the god Shiva.</note> path is the Knowledge of Truth; of <term>Gāruḍividyā</term> <note>A traditional science or lore involving protection against snake bites and poisons.</note>, the capacity to neutralize poison; of Astrology, the capacity to predict Eclipses and other celestial events; and of the Kaula path, it is the power of <term>Nigraha</term> <note>Discipline or the power to punish/restrain evil.</note> and <term>Anugraha</term> <note>Divine grace or kindness.</note>.

->Those who mock the Deities, the Guru, and the scriptures,<-
->the thieves of knowledge and betrayers of their teacher, shall be reborn as a Brahma-rakshasa. || 72 ||<-

### *Sinful actions:*

One who ridicules the <term>Devatā</term> (Deity), the <term>Guru</term> (Teacher), or the <term>Siddhācāra</term> <note>The perfected conduct or established customs of the lineage.</note> of the <term>Shastras</term> (Sacred Texts), who plagiarizes knowledge, or acts as an enemy to their Guru, becomes a <term>Brahma-rakshasa</term> <note>A powerful, malevolent spirit or "ghost" of a learned person who led an unholy life or misused sacred knowledge.</note>.

->O My Beloved! Those who distort the words of a Guru, who disregard the heroic practitioners,<-
->who use harsh words against the Guru, who defeat a hero in a quarrel,<-
->and who doubt the scriptures of the lineage—they too become Brahma-rakshasas. || 73 ||<-

O My Beloved! Those who twist the teachings of a Guru, who insult the <term>Vīras</term> <note>original: "vīra"; literally "hero," referring to advanced spiritual practitioners in the Tantric path.</note>, who speak contemptuously to their teacher, who attempt to defeat a master through argumentative debate, or who speak ill of the <term>Kula-shastras</term> (lineage scriptures) also become <term>Brahma-rakshasas</term>.

->He who treats with contempt a Guru who has bestowed even a single syllable,<-
->after wandering through a hundred births as a dog, shall be born as a social outcaste. || 74 ||<-

One who defies a Guru who has given them even the <term>Ekākṣara</term> <note>A "single-syllable" mantra, often considered the seed of all spiritual power.</note>, will wander through a hundred different animal species (including dogs) before ultimately being born as a <term>Chāṇḍāla</term> <note>A social outcaste, representing the lowest spiritual and social status.</note>.

->O Goddess, one should not hesitate to strike down those<-
->who speak ill of one's mother, father, spouse, brother, relative, son, or the lineage. || 75 ||<-

### *No sin in defending the lineage against slander:*

Those who condemn one’s mother, father, wife, brother, relative, children, or the family/lineage should be dealt with severely and without hesitation.

->O Queen of the Lineage! For the sake of the Guru, the Deity, or the Kaula practitioner,<-
->or for the sake of the scriptures and the spiritual law of the lineage... || 76 ||<-
->...O Goddess, having stopped a slanderer, or even if one loses one's own life,<-
->whoever gives up their life—which is so difficult to surrender—merges into Supreme Shiva. || 77 ||<-

O <term>Kuleshvari</term> (Queen of the Lineage)! For the protection of the Teacher, the Deity, a fellow practitioner, the <term>Kulāgama</term> (lineage tradition), or the <term>Kuladharma</term> (spiritual law), whoever dies while defending these from a slanderer merges into <term>Parama Shiva</term> <note>The Supreme Consciousness or Ultimate Reality.</note>.

<summary>This page details the severe spiritual consequences of disrespecting the Guru or the Kula lineage, warning that such betrayals lead to rebirth as a malevolent spirit or low-status animal. It concludes by praising the merit of those who sacrifice their lives to defend the honor of the lineage and its teachers.</summary>

->Where the death of a single wicked person leads to the<-
->welfare of many, the killing of that wicked person is a meritorious act. || 78 ||<-

<note>original: "एकस्मिन्निधनं यत्र प्रापिते दुष्टचारिणि..."</note> 
> Where the death of one bad person results in the well-being of many, the destruction of such a person is considered a virtuous deed.

->The events surrounding the Shri Chakra, whether auspicious or inauspicious,<-
->must never be disclosed; this is the command, O Supreme Goddess. || 79 ||<-

### **Affairs of the Shri Chakra are Secret:**
<note>original: "श्रीचक्रकृतवृत्तान्तं..."</note>
> Whether favorable or unfavorable, the internal affairs and rituals of the <term>Shri Chakra</term> <note>The "holy wheel" or sacred geometric diagram used in worship, representing the Goddess and the universe.</note> should not be revealed to the outside world. O <term>Parameśvari</term> <note>Supreme Goddess.</note>, this is the divine decree.

->Discussions of the Kula-dharma in the presence of the uninitiated, O Beloved,<-
->should never occur, just as the Vedas are not recited before those outside the fold. || 80 ||<-

<note>original: "कुलधर्मप्रसङ्गश्च पशूनां पुरतः प्रिये..."</note>
> O My Beloved! The subject of <term>Kula-dharma</term> <note>The sacred law, duties, and traditions of the Kula lineage.</note> should never be discussed with <term>Paśus</term> <note>Literally "beasts"; refers to the uninitiated or those bound by worldly limitations who lack spiritual insight.</note>, just as the <term>Vedas</term> <note>The oldest and most authoritative Hindu scriptures.</note> were traditionally not recited before a <term>Śūdra</term> <note>Historically, the laboring class; used here as an analogy for those not prepared for high-level sacred knowledge.</note>.

->The sacred seats, the scriptures, the traditions, the practitioners and their conduct,<-
->and the ritual substances—O Goddess, do not speak of these near the uninitiated. || 81 ||<-

<note>original: "पीठक्षेत्रागमाम्रायं..."</note>
> The <term>Pīṭha-kṣetra</term> <note>Sacred geographic sites or energy centers.</note>, the <term>Āgamas</term> <note>Sacred tantric texts.</note>, the <term>Āmnāya</term> <note>The traditional transmissions of the lineage.</note>, the specific sciences, the conduct of the <term>Kaulikas</term> <note>Followers of the Kaula path.</note>, and the <term>Kula-dravyas</term> <note>The specific physical substances used in tantric rituals.</note> should not be described to the <term>Paśus</term>.

->Just as one protects wealth and grain from thieves, O Beloved,<-
->so must the Kula-dharma be protected from the uninitiated. || 82 ||<-

<note>original: "यथा रक्षति चौरेभ्यो..."</note>
> O My Beloved! Just as a person guards their money and supplies from thieves and intruders, the sacred Kula-dharma must be carefully shielded from the <term>Paśus</term>.

->A Kaula at heart, a Shaiva in appearance, and a Vaishnava in public—<-
->in this way, O Goddess, hide the path like the water inside a coconut. || 83 ||<-

<note>original: "अन्तः कौलो बहिः शैवो..."</note>
> One should be a <term>Kaula</term> <note>An initiate of the inner tantric path.</note> in one’s heart, appear externally as a <term>Śaiva</term> <note>A devotee of Shiva, often more ascetic in appearance.</note>, and behave as a <term>Vaiṣṇava</term> <note>A devotee of Vishnu, typically more conventional or public-facing in their devotion.</note> when among the general public. In this manner, O Goddess, the Kula path should be kept hidden, just as water is concealed within the shell of a coconut.

->All aspects of the Kula-dharma, in all states and at all times,<-
->must be guarded with effort, like a woman hiding a secret pregnancy. || 84 ||<-

<note>original: "कुलधर्मादिकं सर्वं..."</note>
> O Goddess! The Kula-dharma must be kept secret in every condition, always and everywhere, guarded with the same intensity as a woman who keeps the secret of a pregnancy resulting from a forbidden lover.

<summary>This page emphasizes the absolute necessity of secrecy (gopana) within the Kaula tradition, instructing practitioners to maintain a conventional public persona while keeping their inner rituals and identity hidden from the uninitiated.</summary>

<header>Eleventh Chapter</header>

-><note>original: "वेदशास्त्रपुराणानि स्पष्टानि गणिका इव। इयन्तु शाम्भवी विद्या गुप्ता कुलवधूरिव।।"</note><-
->The <term>Vedas</term>, <term>Śāstras</term>, and <term>Purāṇas</term> <note>These are the primary categories of Hindu scripture: ancient hymns, philosophical treatises, and mythological histories.</note> are public and accessible like common women, but this <term>Śāmbhavī-vidyā</term> <note>Literally the "Science of Shiva"; the internal, secret knowledge of this specific tantric tradition.</note> is kept hidden and modest, like a daughter-in-law within the privacy of her home. || 85 ||<-

The Vedas, Śāstras, and Purāṇas are evident like common women, but this Science of Shiva is secret like a daughter-in-law.

-><note>original: "सुगुप्तकौलिकचारमनुगृह्णन्ति देवताः। वाञ्छासिद्धिं प्रयच्छन्ति नाशयन्ति प्रकाशकान्।।"</note><-
->The deities show grace and grant desired <term>Siddhis</term> <note>Spiritual powers or perfections.</note> to those who keep their <term>Kaula</term> conduct <note>The specific tantric practices and lifestyle of this lineage.</note> well-hidden; however, they destroy those who boastfully disclose it. || 86 ||<-

The Deity shows kindness and bestows desired spiritual powers toward well-hidden Kaula conduct, but destroys those who disclose it.

-><note>original: "कुलेशि कुलशास्त्रज्ञाः कुलपूजापरायणाः। ये त्वां रहसि सेवन्ते ते तिष्ठन्ति तवान्तिके।।"</note><-
->O <term>Kuleśī</term> <note>The "Mistress of the Kula," a title for the Goddess.</note>! Those who know the sacred texts of the lineage and are devoted to the <term>Kula-pūjā</term> <note>The lineage-specific worship rituals.</note>, serving You in secret, obtain a place in Your presence. || 87 ||<-

O Goddess of the Kula! The knowers of the lineage scriptures and those devoted to the lineage-worship who serve You quietly obtain residence near You.

-><note>original: "गुरुं प्रकाशयेद्धीमान् मन्त्रं यत्नेन गोपयेत्। अप्रकाशप्रकाशाभ्यां नश्यतः सम्पदायुषी।।"</note><-
->A wise person should openly honor their <term>Guru</term> <note>Spiritual teacher.</note> but must guard their <term>Mantra</term> <note>The private sacred sound-formula given during initiation.</note> with great effort. Revealing what should be hidden, or hiding what should be honored, leads to the destruction of one's wealth and lifespan. || 88 ||<-

The wise should disclose the Guru and effortlessly keep the Mantra a secret. Disclosing what should not be disclosed, and vice versa, destroys both wealth and length of life.

-><note>original: "सर्वाचारपरिभ्रष्टः कुलाचारं समाश्रयेत्। कुलाचारपरिभ्रष्टो रौरवं नरकं व्रजेत्।।"</note><-
->One who has fallen from all other spiritual paths may still find refuge in the <term>Kulācāra</term> <note>The "Kula way of life" or tantric discipline.</note>; however, one who falls from the Kula path itself descends into the <term>Raurava</term> hell <note>One of the most terrifying of the traditional Hindu hells.</note>. || 89 ||<-

One degraded from other paths can take shelter in the Kula path; but those degraded from the Kula path go to the Hell named Raurava.

-><note>original: "शास्त्रेषु निष्कृतिर्दृष्टा महापातकिनामपि। कुलभ्रष्टस्य देवेशि न दृष्टा निष्कृतिः क्वचित्।।"</note><-
->The scriptures offer ways of purification even for those who commit the most heinous sins, but O Goddess, no remedy is seen anywhere for one who abandons the Kula path. || 90 ||<-

The ways of upliftment for even great sinners are prescribed in the scriptures, but the ways of upliftment for those degraded from the Kula are not seen anywhere.

-><note>original: "कुलधर्मं समाश्रित्य..."</note><-
->O Beloved, if one takes refuge in the <term>Kula-dharma</term> <note>The sacred law and duties of the Kula lineage.</note> but fails to follow its practices—living instead with reckless behavior—that great sinner will be plagued by calamities, sin, disease, poverty, conflict, and fear. || 91-92 ||<-
->They will face the wrath of the <term>Yoginīs</term> <note>Semi-divine female spirits or guardians of the tantric mysteries.</note> and stumble at every step. || 92 ||<-
->Lost is their honor, their vitality, and their wisdom. Despised and hated by all, they wander from land to land, distressed and alone, suffering failure in all their endeavors. || 93 ||<-
->Even there, the <term>Śākinīs</term> <note>Fierce female spirits who protect the Kula path.</note> who guard the path will devour them; for in ancient times, I myself gave them the authority to do so. || 94 ||<-

Taking the shelter of the Kula-dharma, if one does not follow its practices, then such a great sinner of reckless behavior is tormented by calamities, sin, disease, poverty, quarrel, and fear. They face the anger of the Yoginis and stumble at every step. Their honor is lost, they are devoid of vitality, and possess a wicked mind. Censured and hated by all, overwhelmed and abandoned, they wander from country to country, always meeting with failure in their work. Even there, the Shakinīs who protect the Kula path devour them; for in the past, I myself gave them that power.

<summary>This page outlines the necessity of secrecy in the Kaula path, comparing its hidden nature to a modest family member versus public scriptures. It warns that while the Kula path can redeem sinners from other paths, betraying the Kula path results in total social and spiritual ruin, including the wrath of guardian spirits like Yoginis and Shakinīs.</summary>

Therefore, O Devi! Persons of good conduct alone become the favorites of the <term>Yoginīs</term>, and those who do not follow the practices of the four <term>Vedas</term> <note>The most ancient and foundational scriptures of Hindu tradition.</note> are destroyed by them.

->One who knows the essence of the <term>Pādukā</term> alone is restrained by good conduct. Through good conduct, one attains divinity and the meeting of Yoginīs and <term>Vīras</term>; by acting to the contrary, <term>Kaulikas</term> fall into the state of animals. || 66 ||<-

**Wrongs which bring the downfall of the Kaulika:**

One who treats the <term>Pādukā</term> <note>Literally "sandals"; here referring to the feet of the Guru or the Goddess as the source of grace and authority.</note> alone as the essence is governed by good conduct. Only by good conduct can one obtain the meeting of <term>Yoginī-Vīra</term> <note>The spiritual assembly of goddesses and perfected male practitioners.</note>. By doing anything to the contrary, a <term>Kaulika</term> <note>A practitioner of the Kula path.</note> takes birth in the animal world.

-><note>original: "आज्ञासिद्धिमदं कौलमनाचाराद्विनश्यति। आचारपालनात् सत्यमाज्ञासिद्धिर्भविष्यति।। ६७।।"</note><-
->This Kaula path, which bestows the perfection of command, is destroyed by bad conduct; by protecting one's conduct, the perfection of command will truly come to pass. || 67 ||<-

This is proved by the rules ordained: that a Kaulika is destroyed by his bad conduct, while by adhering to the good, he obtains <term>Ājñāsiddhi</term> <note>The spiritual power where one's spoken word or will becomes reality.</note>. This is the Truth.

-><note>original: "नाभिषेको न मन्त्रो वा न शास्त्रपठनादिकम्। कारणं कुलधर्मस्य सदाचार: कुलेश्वरि।। ६८।।"</note><-
->Neither consecration, nor <term>Mantra</term>, nor the reading of scriptures is the cause of the <term>Kuladharma</term>, O Mistress of the Kula—good conduct alone is the cause. || 68 ||<-

**Importance of Good Conduct:**

O <term>Kuleśvari</term> <note>Mistress of the Kula; the Goddess.</note>! Neither ritual consecration, nor the chanting of <term>Mantras</term>, nor virtuous deeds like reading the <term>Śāstras</term> <note>Sacred legal or philosophical treatises.</note> are the true basis of <term>Kuladharma</term> <note>The specific duty and spiritual law of the Kula tradition.</note>. Good conduct is the only cause.

-><note>original: "परा श्रीपादुकातत्त्वत्रयाचारादिवासना:। यो वेत्ति समयी स स्यात् कौलिकश्चापि शाम्भवि।। ६९।।"</note><-
->O Śāmbhavī! He alone is a Kaulika and wedded to the <term>Samayācāra</term> who knows the Supreme <term>Śrī Pādukā</term>, the three truths, and the tendencies of conduct. || 69 ||<-

O <term>Śāmbhavī</term> <note>A title for the Goddess as the consort of Shambhu (Shiva).</note>! He alone is a Kaulika and wedded to <term>Samayācāra</term> <note>The internal code of conduct and ritual obligations of the initiate.</note> who knows the purport of the Supreme <term>Śrī Pādukā</term>, the three truths, and the proper modes of conduct.

-><note>original: "तावन्न कौलिको देवि यावन्न समयीकृत:। देहपाते विमोक्ष: स्यात् समयचारपालनात्।। १००।। "</note><-
->O Goddess, one is not a Kaulika until they have been bound by the <term>Samaya</term>. By protecting the conduct of the <term>Samaya</term>, liberation is attained upon the death of the body. || 100 || <note>The verse numbering jumps significantly here in the original manuscript.</note><-

Unless a <term>Sādhaka</term> <note>A spiritual practitioner.</note> follows the <term>Samayācāra</term>, he cannot become a Kaulika. If he follows the <term>Samayācāra</term>, then upon his death, he obtains Emancipation.

<summary>This page emphasizes that ethical conduct (Sada-ācāra) and adherence to the lineage's internal code (Samayācāra) are more vital than ritual or scholarship. It warns of severe spiritual and worldly consequences for those who neglect these behaviors, while promising liberation to the disciplined practitioner.</summary>
