# In the Kularnava Tantra

->The Guru, though himself unattached, acts by the command of Shiva. After assessing the disciple’s fitness for a period of time, he vests them with spiritual authority. [Verse 6]<-

<note>original: "śivājñayā" — by the order or command of Lord Shiva.</note>

***Initiation means Union with Supreme Shiva and Liberation after Death:***

->For the one who is so invested with authority, there is a direct union with <term>Supreme Shiva: Para Śiva, the highest form of the divine</term>. At the end of their physical life, there is eternal <term>Liberation: Mukti</term>—this has been declared by Shankara (Shiva). [Verse 7]<-

->Therefore, O My Beloved! One should strive with all effort to have a Guru belonging to an unbroken <term>Tradition: Sampradāya</term> that originates from the Supreme Shiva Himself. [Verse 8]<-

->To ensure the successful realization of <term>Power: Śakti</term> and for a true success, the Guru must first test the disciple in the prescribed manner. Only then should he communicate the <term>Sacred Chant: Mantra</term>; otherwise, it will be fruitless. [Verse 9]<-

<note>The text warns that spiritual techniques are not just information, but "energy" that fails if the connection between teacher and student is not properly established.</note>

->If one gives instruction improperly and if one receives it improperly, both the giver and the receiver shall, O <term>Goddess: Devi</term>, be cursed within their lineage. [Verse 10]<-

***Without proper testing, both the instructing Guru and the receiving Disciple commit grave errors:***

->If, out of delusion, a Guru and a disciple give and receive instruction without first mutually testing one another, both of them will fall into the state of <term>Goblins: Piśācas, or low-level hungry spirits</term>. [Verse 11]<-

->Likewise, if instruction is given or taken in a way that is contrary to the <term>Scriptures: Śāstras</term>, both the giver and the taker will have to endure the horrors of twenty-one different hells. [Verse 12]<-

<note>original: "narakān ekavimśatim" — refers to the twenty-one hells of traditional Indian cosmology.</note>

## Fourteenth Chapter

->He who imparts an instruction that has not been properly sanctified is a sinner; his <term>Mantra: a sacred word or phrase used in meditation</term> is lost, just like rice seeds sown in the sands. [Verse 13]<-
<note>original: "asaṃskṛtopadeśaśca" — an instruction without the necessary purificatory rites (saṃskāras).</note>

->Knowledge of the Mantra never takes root in one who is unworthy. Therefore, one must proceed only after careful examination; otherwise, it will be fruitless. [Verse 14]<-

***Instructions after the Initiation:***

->After performing the <term>Traditional Initiation: Samaya-dīkṣā</term> and bestowing the <term>Sacred Footprint: Samaya-pādukā, a specific mantra representing the lineage authority</term>, the <term>Guru: spiritual teacher</term> shall seat the disciple close to himself and utter the Mantra, and not in any other way. [Verse 15]<-

->The wisdom that is imparted to a good disciple who is excellently devoted represents the true essence of the sacred scriptures; this knowledge should be understood as whole and undivided. [Verse 16]<-
<note>original: "akhanḍitam" — without gaps, segmentation, or missing parts.</note>

->Whatever knowledge is imparted to bad or undevoted disciples becomes impure, just as cow's milk becomes defiled if kept in a container made of dog-skin. [Verse 17]<-
<note>original: "śvadhṛtā" — a bag or vessel made of dog-hide. In the cultural context of the text, this represents the height of ritual impurity, rendering the "milk" of wisdom undrinkable.</note>

->If, out of a desire for money, fear, greed, or similar motives, one initiates someone who is unworthy, they incur the curse of the Deity, and the act itself becomes fruitless. [Verse 18]<-

***Method of Testing a Disciple:***

->The Guru should test the disciple through their knowledge and their conduct with great effort, for a period of one year, six months, or three months. [Verse 19]<-
<note>original: "saṃvatsaraṃ tadarddhaṃ vā tadarddhaṃ" — literally a year, its half (6 months), or its half (3 months).</note>

<summary>This page warns of the spiritual dangers of improper initiation, likening unsanctified instruction to seeds wasted in sand and comparing wisdom given to the unworthy to milk defiled by a dog-skin vessel. It mandates a testing period for disciples of up to one year to ensure they are deserving of the Mantra.</summary>

### Chapter Fourteen, Page 227

->Devotion occurs at the beginning, O Goddess, for those who come for the sake of <term>initiation: dīkṣā</term>;<-
->but later their hearts are scattered, and they are called "competent in the beginning." [28]<-
<note>original: "Ādiyogya" — refers to a student who starts with great enthusiasm that quickly fades.</note>

Those in whom there is devotion at the outset when they come for initiation, but whose enthusiasm cools down soon, are the disciples called competent in the beginning (*Ādiyogya*).

->Those who arrive when the time for initiation is at hand, lacking both specialized and general knowledge,<-
->but whose obstacles are destroyed by devotion, are remembered as "competent in the middle." [29]<-
<note>original: "Madhyayogya" — refers to those whose devotion blossoms during the process of training.</note>

Those who arrive when the time for initiation is at hand and have neither special nor any knowledge, but whose past obstacles are destroyed by devotion, are known as those competent in the middle (*Madhyayogya*).

->Those who lack devotion at the outset, who are moderately devoted in the middle,<-
->but whose devotion is fully matured at the end, they are "competent at the end."<-
->They are known as those of supreme knowledge; thus instruction is of three kinds, O Beloved. [30]<-
<note>original: "Antayogya" and "Jñānīs" (possessors of wisdom).</note>

Those who have no devotion at the outset, who have devotion in the middle, and whose devotion is fully grown at the end are the disciples called competent at the end (*Antayogya*) and known as the best seekers of wisdom.

**Three Kinds of Instruction:**
O My Beloved! Instruction (<term>Upadeśa: spiritual teaching</term>) is of three kinds: that of <term>action: Karma</term>, of <term>righteousness: Dharma</term>, and of <term>knowledge: Jñāna</term>.

->Just as an ant slowly and gradually reaches the fruit at the top of a tree,<-
->so too is the instruction of action remembered to take a long time. [31]<-
<note>original: "Karma-upadeśa" — This refers to the slow path of achieving spiritual results through repetitive rituals and physical works.</note>

Of these, the instruction of action proceeds slowly like the ant which takes a long time to reach the fruit at the top of the tree, proceeding slowly and slowly.

->Just as a monkey on a branch reaches the fruit by leaping with effort from branch to branch,<-
->so too, O Beloved, is the instruction of righteousness. [32]<-
<note>original: "Dharma-upadeśa" — The path of moral and religious duty, which moves in stages or leaps of progress.</note>

O My Beloved! The path of righteousness is like the pace of a monkey which strains, jumping from branch to branch to reach the fruit.

->Just as a bird quickly alights directly upon the fruit,<-
->so too is the instruction of knowledge described, O Queen of the Kula. [33]<-
<note>original: "Jñāna-upadeśa" — The direct path of realization; "Kulanāyike" is an address to the Goddess.</note>

O Queen of the Kula! The instruction of knowledge is like that of the bird which flies straight and rests on the fruit quickly.

->Known as "by touch," O Goddess; known as "by sight," O Great Goddess; and "by thought,"<-
->Initiation is remembered to be of three types, free from the exhaustion of rituals. [34]<-

**Three Kinds of Initiations without Rituals:**
Initiation is of three kinds: Initiation by touch (*Sparśa*), Initiation by sight (*Dṛksaṃjñā*), and Initiation by thought (*Mānasa*)—all these three are performed without the need for complex rituals or physical exertions.

### From the Kularnava Tantra

->Just as a bird nurtures its young slowly with its two wings,<-
->so is the <term>initiation: dīkṣā</term> and instruction through touch described, O Beloved. [35]<-
<note>original: "sparśa-dīkṣā" — initiation through physical contact.</note>

O My Beloved! Initiation and instruction by touch is likened to the slow nourishing of its young by the bird with the warmth of its wings.

->Just as a fish nourishes its offspring through sight alone,<-
->so is the initiation and instruction through sight, O Supreme Goddess. [36]<-
<note>original: "dṛg-dīkṣā" — initiation through the Guru's gaze.</note>

O <term>Supreme Goddess: Parameśvari</term>! Initiation and instruction by sight is like the nourishing of its young by the fish through its seeing alone.

->Just as a tortoise nourishes its children through thought alone,<-
->so is the mental initiation and instruction through thought. [37]<-
<note>original: "mānasa-dīkṣā" — initiation through the mind or meditation.</note>

Initiation and instruction by thought is like the nourishing of its young by the tortoise by only thinking of them.

->A disciple becomes worthy of grace according to the <term>descent of power: śaktipāta</term>;<-
->where this power does not fall, spiritual perfection is not born. [38]<-
<note>In Tantric tradition, "Śaktipāta" is the moment a Guru's spiritual energy is transmitted to the student, often described as an act of divine grace.</note>

The disciple receives the Guru according to the impact of the <term>Power: Śakti</term> (<note>original: "Śaktipāta"</note>); where there is no impact of Power there is no fulfilment.

->Through ritual, letters, subtle energy, touch, speech, sight, and thought,<-
->initiation is declared to be of seven kinds, O Goddess, and it grants liberation. [39]<-

->***Seven kinds of Initiation which give Liberation:***<-

O <term>Goddess: Devi</term>! The initiations giving liberation are said to be of seven kinds: 1. Initiation through ritual, 2. through letters, 3. through <term>subtle energy: kalā</term>, 4. through touch, 5. through speech, 6. through sight, and 7. through thought.

->The names are Samayā, Viśeṣā, Sādhikā, Putrikā,<-
->Vedhakā, Pūrṇā, and the Master’s initiation called Nirvāṇa. [40]<-
<note>These represent a hierarchy of spiritual stages, from the "Samaya" (probationary) to "Nirvāṇa" (the final liberation).</note>

The special names of initiations described in the previous verse are: 1. Samayā, 2. Sādhikā, 3. Putrikā, 4. Vedhakā, 5. Pūrṇā, 6. Caryā, and 7. Nirvāṇa respectively.

->Ritual initiation is said to be of two types, involving the fire-pit and canopy;<-
->accompanied by the ritual jar and other tools, it should be performed by the Guru externally.<-
->O Queen of the Gods, it is performed for the purification of the body according to the previously stated rules. [41]<-

The ritualistic initiation associated with the <term>fire-pit: kuṇḍa</term>, <term>canopy: maṇḍapa</term> and <term>ritual jar: kalaśa</term>, should be performed by the Guru, O <term>Queen of the Gods: Deveśi</term>, adopting the prescribed means for the purification of the body.

<summary>This page outlines the different modes of spiritual transmission, using nature-based analogies (bird, fish, tortoise) to explain how a Guru initiates a student. It further categorizes initiation into seven ritual and meditative types that lead to liberation.</summary>

### Fourteenth Chapter

->Initiation by letters is said to be threefold, using forty-two,<-
->fifty, or sixty-two characters, O Goddess. [42]<-
<note>original: "Varṇa-dīkṣā" — Here, the Sanskrit alphabet is treated as a manifestation of divine energy.</note>

Initiation by letters is threefold depending on whether the letters are 42 or 50 or 62.

->The Guru should place the letters on the body of the disciple and withdraw them<-
->in the reverse order, joining that consciousness to the Supreme Self, O Beloved. [43]<-
<note>original: "pratilomena" — the reverse order, symbolizing the dissolution of the material world back into the divine source.</note>

O My Beloved! Letters shall be placed on the body of the disciple and withdrawn in the reverse order, joining his consciousness to the Supreme Self.

->Having raised those letters again, he should place them once more on the disciple’s body,<-
->in the order of creation and according to the rules, and unite the consciousness. [44]<-
<note>original: "sṛṣṭi krameṇa" — the "order of creation" refers to the standard sequence of the alphabet, symbolizing the manifestation of the soul into a new, purified state.</note>

->A divine state full of supreme bliss is born within the "child" of the Guru.<-
->This is called the Initiation of Letters which, O My Beloved, removes all bonds. [45]<-
<note>original: "pāśa-hara" — "pāśa" refers to the spiritual nooses or bonds (ego, karma, delusion) that tether a soul to worldly suffering.</note>

After withdrawal, the letters are to be laid again on the person of the disciple in the order of creation and as prescribed; so, too, shall the consciousness be directed. The state of Godhood full of delight is born in the child <note>The disciple is often called the "child" of the Guru because initiation is considered a second, spiritual birth.</note> of the Guru. This is the <term>Letter-based Initiation: Varṇamayī-dīkṣā</term> which, O My Beloved, removes all bonds.

->O My Beloved! The Initiation of Cosmic Energies is also threefold,<-
->to be performed according to the sacred rules.<-
->The phase of "Nivṛtti" resides from the soles of the feet up to the knees. [46]<-
<note>original: "Kalā-dīkṣā" — initiation involving the five "Kalās" or functional aspects of the universe mapped onto the human body.</note>

->The phase of "Pratiṣṭhā" dwells from the knees to the navel, O Beloved.<-
->The phase of "Vidyā" extends from the navel to the throat; "Śānti" is beyond that. [47]<-

->It extends from the throat to the forehead; and from there to the top of the head<-
->is "Śāntyātīta." This is described as the gradual expansion of these energies. [48]<-
<note>These five Kalās are: 1. <term>Nivṛtti: Cessation/Restraint</term>, 2. <term>Pratiṣṭhā: Foundation/Installation</term>, 3. <term>Vidyā: Knowledge</term>, 4. <term>Śānti: Peace</term>, and 5. <term>Śāntyātīta: Beyond Peace</term>.</note>

O My Beloved! The <term>Initiation of Cosmic Energies: Kalā-dīkṣā</term> is also threefold to be done as prescribed. Beginning from the base of the feet up to the knee it is <term>Nivṛtti-kalā</term>; from the knee to the navel it is <term>Pratiṣṭhā-kalā</term>; from navel to the neck it is <term>Vidyā-kalā</term>; from the neck to the forehead it is <term>Śānti</term>; from there to the head it is <term>Śāntyātīta</term>. This is the graded spread of <term>Kalā-dīkṣā</term>.

->By the method of the path of dissolution, moving from one station to another, O Beloved,<-
->the knower of the rules joins them properly up to the top of the head. [49]<-

->O Queen of the Kula, this is said to bestow a divine state.<-
->Whether with thirty-eight cosmic energies or fifty, [50]<-
<note>original: "Kuleśāni" — a title for the Goddess as the sovereign of the spiritual lineage (Kula).</note>

->following the order of ritual placement through the paths of creation and dissolution,<-
->having known it from the mouth of the Guru, he should unite and pierce the disciple. [51]<-
<note>original: "nyāsa" — the ritual act of "placing" or "touching" parts of the body to instill them with sacred mantras or energies.</note>

<summary>This page details two specific forms of Tantric initiation: Varṇa-dīkṣā (using the sacred alphabet) and Kalā-dīkṣā (using five cosmic energies mapped to the body). It explains the ritual process of dissolving the disciple's old identity and recreating it in a divine form through the "order of creation."</summary>

# Kularnava Tantra

<page-num>230</page-num>

->The state of Godhood arises, along with the meeting of Yoginis and Viras.<-
->Initiation through cosmic phases is declared to be the remover of the bonds of the tethered soul. [52]<-
<note>original: "pashu-pāsha-apahāriṇī" — "Pashu" refers to the uninitiated soul, often compared to an animal tethered by the "pāsha" (noose or bond) of worldly existence.</note>

O My Beloved! Following the order of withdrawal, the one who knows the sequence joins the consciousness from place to place up to the head. O Queen of the Kula! This induces a divine feeling in the disciple. Alternatively, with 38 or 50 *Kalās* <term>cosmic phases or divine energies</term> in the order of *Tattva-nyāsa* <term>the ritual placement of cosmic principles on the body</term> and with the order of withdrawal and creation known from the mouth of the Guru, one should center and impinge these energies on the disciple. This gives birth to the state of Godhood and the meeting with the *Yoginīs* <term>female deities or semi-divine powers</term> and *Vīras* <term>heroic practitioners</term>. This is the *Kalā-dīkṣā* (Initiation through Cosmic Phases) which destroys the bonds of the tethered souls.

->Meditating on the Guru as Shiva within the hand, one should recite the garland of root-limb mantras.<-
->The Guru should then touch the body of the disciple; this becomes the Initiation by Touch. [53]<-
<note>original: "mūlāṅga-mālinīm" — likely refers to a specific sequence of mantras identified with the "limbs" of the primary deity.</note>

Invoking Lord Śiva in the hand, doing *Japa* <term>meditative repetition</term> of the *Mūlāṅga-mālinī*, the Guru should touch the person of the disciple; this is the *Sparśa-dīkṣā* (Initiation by touch).

->Establishing the mind in the Truth, one should utter the gathered mantras<-
->Which are strengthened by the Supreme Truth; this is called the Initiation by Speech. [54]<-

Securing the mind in the Truth, the Guru shall utter the body of Mantras which are expansions of the Supreme Truth; this is the *Vāg-dīkṣā* (Verbal Initiation).

->Closing both eyes and meditating, with a mind purified by the Supreme Truth,<-
->The Guru should gaze intently at the disciple; this, O Beloved, is the Initiation by Sight. [55]<-

Closing both the eyes and meditating upon the Supreme Truth, with a happy mind shall the Guru gaze well into the disciple; this is *Dṛk-dīkṣā* (Ocular Initiation), O Beloved.

->Through the Guru's mere glance, speech, or even touch,<-
->Knowledge is instantly born; that is considered the Shambhavi Initiation. [56]<-
<note>original: "śāmbhavī-dīkṣā" — Named after Shambhu (Shiva), this is considered a highly potent and direct transmission of spiritual energy.</note>

When by the mere look or speech or touch of the Guru, there is an instantaneous knowledge, that is *Śāmbhavī-dīkṣā*.

->Initiation by the Mind is said to be of two kinds: the Intense and the More Intense.<-

*Mano-dīkṣā* (Mental Initiation), it is said to be of two kinds: *Tīvra* (Intense) and *Tīvratara* (More Intense).

->Knowing the sixfold paths and contemplating them in the body of the disciple, O Beloved, [57]<-
->One should envision the Worlds, Principles, Phases, Letters, Words, and Mantras,<-
->From the knees, navel, heart, throat, and palate, to the top of the head, O Mother. [58]<-
<note>original: "Adhvāns" — The six 'paths' or categories through which the divine manifests in the universe and the human body.</note>

O Mother! Knowing the sixfold *Adhvāns* one shall form in the body of the disciple the *Bhuvana* (World), *Tattva* (Principle), *Kalā* (Phase), *Varṇa* (Letter), *Pada* (Word) and *Mantra*—mapping them from the knee, navel, heart, neck, and palate to the top of the head.

### Vocabulary
*   **Kalā-dīkṣā**: Initiation through cosmic phases or parts.
*   **Sparśa-dīkṣā**: Initiation by physical touch.
*   **Vāg-dīkṣā**: Initiation through the spoken word or mantra.
*   **Dṛk-dīkṣā**: Initiation through the Guru's gaze.
*   **Śāmbhavī-dīkṣā**: A direct, powerful initiation involving the Guru's presence.
*   **Mano-dīkṣā**: Initiation through mental transmission.
*   **Tattva-nyāsa**: The ritual practice of assigning cosmic principles to parts of the body.
*   **Adhvāns**: The six paths or systems of cosmic organization.
*   **Bhuvana, Tattva, Kalā, Varṇa, Pada, Mantra**: The six components of the cosmic paths (Adhvāns).

It also introduces the "six paths" (Adhvāns) used to map the macrocosm onto the disciple's physical body during the ritual.</summary>

<header>Fourteenth Chapter</header>

The wise Guru shall effect the <term>Vedha (a spiritual "piercing" or direct impact of energy)</term> following the method received from the lineage. In a single moment, the disciple who was bound by worldly attachments will have those bonds severed. This is declared to be the <term>Tīvra-dīkṣā (Intense Initiation)</term>, O Sovereign Lady of the Kula, which yields final liberation. [59]

O Goddess! There is also the "Highly Intense" initiation. Merely by the Guru—who is proficient in this spiritual impact—remembering the disciple, the disciple’s sins are instantly severed. This is the <term>Tīvratara-dīkṣā (Highly Intense Initiation)</term>. [60]

O <note>original: "Śāmbhavi" — the female energy of Shiva</note> Goddess of Shambhu! Released from all external activity, the disciple falls to the ground in that very moment. A divine state arises within him, and he comes to know everything. [61]
Whatever occurs at that moment of impact is experienced directly by the disciple; but upon waking, O Sovereign Goddess, he is unable to find the words to describe that supreme happiness. [62]

One who is struck by this spiritual impact is truly <note>original: "Śivaḥ sākṣāt" — Shiva himself</note> Shiva in person and shall never be born again. This is the Highly Intense initiation that releases one from the bonds of worldly existence and grants the very state of Shiva. O Leader of the Kula, I swear this to be true by You! [63]

### Six Conditions of Vedha:

<term>Ānanda (spiritual bliss)</term>, <term>Kampa (trembling)</term>, <term>Udbhava (rising or spiritual rebirth)</term>, <term>Ghūrṇā (reeling or whirling)</term>, <term>Nidrā (meditative sleep)</term>, and <term>Mūrchā (swooning or divine trance)</term>—these, O Sovereign Lady of the Kula, are said to be the six conditions that manifest from the spiritual impact. [64]

O Sovereign Lady of the Kula! These six characteristics are visible at the time of the impact of the <term>Vedha</term>. Wherever the person so struck may be, he is liberated; of this, there is no doubt. [65]

<summary>This page describes the Vedha-dikṣā, a powerful form of initiation where the Guru's spiritual energy "pierces" the disciple, leading to immediate liberation and specific physical-spiritual symptoms like bliss and trance.</summary>
<keywords>Vedha, Tīvra-dīkṣā, Intense Initiation, Shiva-state, liberation, spiritual impact, trance states, Kularnava Tantra</keywords>

->A Holy Guru who performs the <term>Vedha initiation (a direct spiritual impact or "piercing")</term> is rare in this world, O Beloved.<-
->A disciple worthy of such a gift is equally rare; they are brought together only through a fortunate conjunction of spiritual merit.<-
->One should not grant this to just anyone; O Supreme Goddess, this is the command. [66]<-

O My Beloved! It is difficult to find such a Guru who can initiate through the subtle impact of Vedha; it is equally difficult to find a disciple fit for it. It is only by the happy conjunction of merit that such a pairing is obtained. But this initiation should not be given to just anyone. O <note>original: "Parameśvari" — the Supreme Goddess</note> Sovereign Lady! Such is the divine command.

->Having worshipped the <term>Kula-Chakra (the sacred circle of the lineage)</term> according to the traditional rules with the <term>Kula substances (sacred offerings used in Tantric ritual)</term>,<-
->the Guru shall reveal it to the disciple, O Goddess; this is remembered as the <term>Kaulikī initiation</term>. [67]<-

### *Kaulikī Initiation-Method and Glory of Siddhābhiṣeka:*

Duly worshipping the circle of the Kula with the appropriate ingredients of Kula-worship, the Guru shall show it to the disciple. This is, O Goddess, known as the *Kaulikī Dīkṣā*.

->Filling his own mouth with the ritual substance mixed with the nectar of the <term>Pañca-gavya (the five products of the cow)</term>,<-
->the Guru shall sprinkle the disciple with it; this is proclaimed as the <term>Gaṇḍūṣa initiation</term>. [68]<-

Filling the mouth with the substance for worship mixed with the five nectarous products of the cow—<note>original: "Pañca-gavya" — a purifying mixture of milk, curd, clarified butter, urine, and dung</note>—the Guru shall bathe the disciple with it. This is called the Gaṇḍūṣa initiation.

->With <term>wine</term> containing <term>fish</term>, and filled with the <term>five nectars</term>,<-
->or with a conch or a jar similarly filled,<-
->he should then perform the external initiation; this is how it is described, O Beloved. [69]<-

O My Beloved! Then the Guru should perform the external Initiation with <term>Surā (consecrated wine)</term> containing <term>Mīna (fish)</term>, or using a conch-shell or jar full of the <term>Pañcāmṛta (the five nectars: milk, sugar, ghee, curd, and honey)</term>.

->The "fish" is actually the <term>Lambikā (the soft palate or the tongue turned back in yoga)</term>, O Goddess, and the "jar" is said to be the mouth.<-
->One should consecrate the disciple with the mouth full of the nectar of the five cow-products.<-
->This is the <term>Siddhābhiṣeka (Consecration of the Perfected One)</term>, O Parvati, and it is desirable even for the Teacher. [70]<-

"Fish" here refers to the <term>Lambikā (the yogic positioning of the tongue)</term>; the "Jar" is said to be the Mouth. Thus, O Goddess, the Guru should consecrate the disciple with a mouth full of the nectar of the five cow-products—<note>The original verse defines these as: "Milk, curd, and clarified butter, as well as urine and dung: these are the five products of the cow."</note>. This is called the <term>Siddhābhiṣeka</term>, O Parvati, and it is a ritual desired even by the high Acharyas (Teachers).

->The ritual tooth-stick used three times and the offering of a handful of flowers, O Beloved; [71]<-
->The ritual placement of the <term>Veda-kalā (knowledge-aspects)</term> in the conch—this knowledge becomes eight-fold.<-
->The <term>Samaya (the initiate's code of conduct)</term> is represented by the tooth-stick; the <term>Sādhaka (practitioner)</term> is the handful of flowers. [72]<-

->The spiritual son is prepared by the conch-shell consecration, the Awakener by the method of Piercing,<-
->And the Teacher by the Full Consecration; these are proclaimed as the five stages. [73]<-

O My Beloved! The eight rituals consist of cleaning the teeth, offering an <term>Añjali (a prayerful gesture with joined palms)</term> of flowers during the three transitional times of the day (dawn, noon, and sunset), performing the <term>Kalā-nyāsa (ritual placement of divine energies on the body)</term> using water from a conch-shell, and the spiritual knowledge gained through these acts. The five conditions of <term>Abhiṣeka (Consecration)</term> are: the practitioner with the flower offering, the spiritual son with the water of the conch-shell, the <note>original: "Bodhaka"</note> Awakener through the <term>Vedha (the subtle "piercing" or impact of energy)</term>, and the <note>original: "Ācārya"</note> Teacher through the <term>Pūrṇābhiṣeka (the Full or Final Consecration)</term>.

->Those solely intent on the practice of the Kula path, devoted to the Teacher and firm in their vows,<-
->Who are purified by the Full Consecration, are liberated within this very lifetime. [74]<-

### *Praise for those who have received the Full Consecration:*

Those who are entirely focused on the ways of the <term>Kula (the sacred lineage)</term>, who are devoted to their Teacher, steadfast in their spiritual observances, and purified by the <term>Pūrṇābhiṣeka (Full Consecration)</term>—all such individuals achieve liberation while still inhabiting their present physical bodies.

->O Sovereign Lady of the Lineage, those purified by the Full Consecration who pass away,<-
->Obtain a superior rebirth and achieve union with the Divine through the grace of the Teacher, who is Shiva incarnate. [75]<-
->Purified by the Full Consecration, which bestows union with Shiva,<-
->They shall proceed to final liberation; so spoke the voice of the Goddess. [76]<-

O <note>original: "Kulanāyike"</note> Lady of the Kula! Those purified by the Full Consecration who have died will attain a superior birth. They eventually achieve union with <term>Śiva</term> due to the grace of the Teacher, who acts as the very form of the Divine. Purified by this ritual, which grants the gift of divine union, they shall reach liberation. O <note>original: "Śāmbhavi"</note> Goddess! This is the declaration of the Divine.

->A follower of the Kula path who dies without having undergone the Full Consecration,<-
->Is doomed to remain a ghost until the final dissolution of the universe. [77]<-

A <note>original: "Kaulika"</note> practitioner of the Kula path who dies without receiving the <term>Pūrṇābhiṣeka (Full Consecration)</term> is destined to exist as a <term>Piśāca (a restless spirit or ghost)</term> until the great cosmic reset at the end of time.

->Initiation is proclaimed to be of two types: external and internal.<-
->The external is known as Ritual Initiation, while the internal is called Piercing. [78]<-

### *Two Kinds of Initiation and the Glory of Initiation:*

Initiation is further divided into two categories based on whether it is performed externally or internally. The external form is <term>Kriyā-dīkṣā (ritualistic initiation)</term>, and the internal form is <term>Vedha-dīkṣā (initiation through the direct, subtle impact of energy from teacher to student)</term>.

->Purification is described as being of two kinds: inner and outer.<-
->Inner purity is achieved through ritual practice, and outer purity through initiation. [79]<-

Purification is recognized in two ways—the inner and the outer. The inner is achieved through appropriate ritual acts, and the outer is secured through the process of <term>Dīkṣā (Initiation)</term>.

<summary>This page defines the five grades of Tantric consecration (Abhisheka) and emphasizes that only the "Full Consecration" (Purnabhisheka) ensures liberation in this life and prevents one from becoming a restless spirit after death.</summary>

->Through <term>Dīkṣā (spiritual initiation)</term>, which acts as the lamp of liberation, even one born into the lowest station is set free.<-
->Without these two <note>Referring to the light of liberation and the initiation itself</note>, O <note>original: "Kuleśāni"</note> Lady of the Kula, even a <term>Kaulika (a practitioner of the Kula path)</term> is never liberated. [80]<-

->The physical body cannot be truly purified through ritual, nor can one's <term>Karma (the accumulated weight of past actions)</term> be cleansed so easily.<-
->One must have initiation performed for the sake of the inner self, awakening the ageless <term>Kuṇḍalinī (the primordial spiritual energy at the base of the spine)</term> of the lineage. [81]<-

->Though the external rituals may appear identical, these initiations produce different results<-
->based on the spiritual connection and intention between the <term>Guru (spiritual teacher)</term> and the worthy disciple. [82]<-

->Just as the power of poison is neutralized by a <term>Mantra (a sacred sound or invocation)</term> or by medicine, O <note>original: "Kuleśvari"</note> Sovereign of the Lineage,<-
->so does the knower of Mantras instantly sever the bonds of the <term>Paśu (the bound soul, literally 'animal')</term> through initiation. [83]<-

->From this vast and extensive bondage, initiation alone provides liberation by revealing the Supreme State<-
->and leading the seeker to the ancient, divine Abode. [84]<-

# Fifteenth Chapter 236

->In this world, which is filled with suffering, if one desires personal fulfillment, one should perform the <term>Recitation (Japa)</term> of the <term>Sacred Sound (Mantra)</term> through the <term>Five-Limbed Worship (Panchanga Upasana)</term> to attain happiness. [7]<-

*The Five Limbs of the Preparatory Rite (Puraścaraṇa):*

->Daily worship performed at the three transitions of the day—morning, midday, and evening—along with regular recitation, <term>Water Libations (Tarpaṇa)</term>, <term>Fire Offerings (Homa)</term>, and the feeding of <term>Priests (Brahmins)</term>; this fivefold worship is known as the <term>Preparatory Rite (Puraścaraṇa)</term>. [8]<-

->If any of these limbs are omitted, the seeker should perform double the number of recitations as compensation. In the case of physical weakness on the part of the <term>Practitioner (Sādhaka)</term>, one should, for the completion of these limbs, perform them with devotion two, three, four, or even five times the required number. This is because, if these limbs are lacking, the practitioner will not attain the desired fruits. [9-10]<-

->O Goddess, if the priests are well-fed with the four kinds of food <note>original: "annaiś-catur-vidhair"; traditionally categorized as foods to be chewed, sucked, licked, and drunk.</note> and items containing all six flavors <note>original: "ṣaḍ-rasānvita"; these are sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent, and astringent.</note>, then all efforts shall become fruitful. [11]<-

->O <term>Goddess of the Lineage (Kuleśvari)</term>! If, by Your grace, success is achieved even in a single Sacred Sound through this five-limbed worship, then all other Sacred Sounds will also yield their fruits. [12]<-

->The success of a Sacred Sound arises from the potency of the instruction, the grace of the <term>Holy Teacher (Śrī Guru)</term>, and the devotion of the seeker toward the power of the Sacred Sound itself. [13]<-

Innumerable are the Mantras which agitate the mind; but only that Mantra gives fulfillment which is received through the grace of the Guru.

Japa of a Mantra heard by chance or seen by deceit or picked up from a sheet of paper can only lead to disaster.

Those who, seeing the Mantras written in books, practice their Japa commit a sin <note>original: "pātakā"; a heavy spiritual transgression.</note> tantamount to Brahmanicide resulting in disease and misery.

### From the Kularnava Tantra

->One who performs <term>Recitation (Japa)</term> or <term>Worship (Pūjā)</term> without first honoring the <term>Lord of the Lamp (Dīpanātha)</term> <note>original: "dīpanātham". This refers to the Guru or the presiding deity who "ignites" the power of the Mantra.</note>,<-
->The fruit of that action is taken by him, and the practitioner is left only with exhaustion. [31]<-

**Worship of the Lord of Light is necessary:**
If one performs <term>Recitation (Japa)</term> or <term>Worship (Pūjā)</term> without first offering to the <term>Teacher (Guru)</term> who holds the Light, then he steals the fruit and all the efforts of the <term>Practitioner (Sādhaka)</term> go in vain.

->The wise person should avoid a seat made of bamboo, stone, earth, wood, grass, or sprouts;<-
->These bring only poverty, disease, and sorrow. [32]<-

**Rejectable and acceptable Seats:**
The wise shall reject the seat made of bamboo, stone, earth, wood, grass or sprout; such seats only bring poverty, disease and misery.

->A wise person should prepare a seat from cotton, wool, or cloth, or the skins of a lion, tiger, or deer;<-
->These increase good fortune and wisdom. [33]<-

A seat made of cotton, wool, cloth, skin of lion, tiger or deer brings good fortune.

->Sitting in postures such as the <term>Lotus (Padmāsana)</term>, the <term>Auspicious (Svastikāsana)</term>, or the <term>Hero (Vīrāsana)</term>,<-
->One should perform <term>Recitation (Japa)</term> and worship; otherwise, it will be fruitless. [34]<-

Seating himself in <term>Lotus Posture (Padmāsana)</term>, <term>Auspicious Posture (Svastikāsana)</term> or <term>Hero Posture (Vīrāsana)</term> the <term>Practitioner (Sādhaka)</term> should perform his <term>Recitation (Japa)</term> and <term>Worship (Pūjā)</term>; otherwise his efforts would be fruitless.

->Mentally repeating the <term>Sacred Syllable OM (Praṇava)</term> twelve times, maintaining three <term>measures of time (Mātrās)</term>,<-
->One should release the inner breath through the <term>Right Channel (Piṅgalā)</term>; this is called <term>Exhalation (Recaka)</term>. [35]<-

**Method of Breath Control (Prāṇāyāma) and its Fruits:**
Performing mentally twelve times the <term>Recitation (Japa)</term> of the <term>Sacred Syllable (Praṇava)</term> of three <term>measures (Mātrās)</term> one should exhale the breath through the right nostril (<term>Piṅgalā</term>)—this is called <term>Exhalation (Recaka)</term>.

->Repeating the <term>Deliverer (Tāra)</term> <note>original: "tāra". A synonym for the sacred syllable OM.</note> sixteen times, one should fill the body with external air,<-
->Slowly through the <term>Left Channel (Iḍā)</term>; this is known as <term>Inhalation (Puraka)</term>. [36]<-

Repeating sixteen times the <term>Deliverer (Tāra)</term> one should inhale through the left nostril (<term>Iḍā</term>)—this is called <term>Inhalation (Puraka)</term>.

->Repeating the <term>Sacred Syllable (Tāra)</term> twelve times, one should retain the breath in the center;<-
->One should then dry the body with the <term>Seed-Syllable of Air (Vāyu-bīja)</term> <note>original: "yaṁ". A specific sound vibration used in visualization to "dry out" or purify the physical impurities of the body.</note>; this is described as the "drying of the body." [37]<-

Then repeating the <term>Sacred Syllable (Praṇava)</term> twelve times the breath should be retained inside—this is <term>Breath Retention (Kumbhaka)</term>. Then he should dry up the body with the <term>Seed-Syllable of Air (Vāyu-bīja)</term> **Yaṁ**. This is drying up of the impurities of the body.

### Fifteenth Chapter: Page 243

Austerities, pilgrimages, sacrifices, charities, and religious observances are not worth even a tiny fraction of the merit gained from such a practice of breath control.

O <term>Shive (Goddess)</term>! All the sins, whether mental, verbal or physical, are very soon burnt up by only three <term>Pranayamas</term>.

Just as the impurity of ore or metal is burnt away when it is subjected to the heat of the blower, so the sins and distractions of the senses are burnt out by the control of the <term>Prana (Life-force)</term>.

->Whatever actions are performed by one whose soul is purified by breath control,<-
->They all bear fruit without doubt, even if performed without effort. [44]<-

Whatever actions are performed by one who is purified by breath control, they all reach fruition undoubtedly, even if they are carried out effortlessly.

# In the Kularnava Tantra

->He who performs his practice daily according to the path spoken in the Scriptures,<-
->attains the state of the Deity, and perfection in the sacred chant is born. [45]<-
<note>original: "āgamoktena mārgeṇābhyāsaṃ nityaṃ karoti yaḥ...". The "Agama" refers to the body of revealed tantric scriptures.</note>

*Recitation of the sacred chant only with Ritual Placement, etc. :*

He who does this practice regularly in accordance with the directions in the <term>Agama (Scripture)</term>, attains the state of Godhood and acquires perfection in the <term>Mantra (Sacred Chant)</term>.

->O Beloved, for him who recites the mantra with Ritual Placement, Protective Armor, and Meter,<-
->obstacles flee upon seeing him, just as elephants flee at the sight of a lion. [46]<-
<note>original: "yo nyāsakavacacchando mantraṃ japati...". These are specific ritual steps: <term>Nyasa (Ritual Placement)</term> involves touching body parts to "install" the mantra's power; <term>Kavaca (Armor)</term> is a protective mantra; <term>Chandas (Meter)</term> is the rhythmic structure.</note>

O My Beloved! Seeing him who performs <term>Japa (Recitation)</term> of the Mantra as prescribed with Nyasa, Kavaca, and Chandas, obstructions flee like elephants at the sight of a lion.

->That foolish soul who recites the mantra without performing the web of Ritual Placements,<-
->is harassed by all obstacles, like a fawn by tigers. [47]<-

But if someone foolishly does the Mantra-japa without taking the precautions of Nyasa, etc., he is harassed by all the obstructions like an infant deer by the tiger.

->The rosary is said to be of two kinds: the "constructed" and the "unconstructed."<-
->The "constructed" is fashioned from gems; the "unconstructed" is the Alphabet itself. [48]<-
<note>original: "akṣamālā dvidhā proktā kalpitā'kalpiteti ca...". The term for rosary, <term>Aksha-mala</term>, literally means "garland of eyes" or "garland of letters."</note>

*Two kinds of rosaries and the fruit of recitation with them :*

Rosaries are said to be of two kinds: 1. Constructed (Imagined) and 2. Unconstructed (Unimagined). The Constructed is made from gems and the Unconstructed from <term>Matrikas (the "Mother" letters of the alphabet)</term>.

->Because it consists of the letters from "A" to "Ksha," it is called an Aksha-mala.<-
->The best knower of mantras should count in both forward and reverse orders. [49]<-
<note>original: "ādikṣāntākṣavarṇatvādakṣamāleti kīrtitā...". In the Sanskrit alphabet, "A" is the first letter and "Ksha" is the last; together they encompass all sound and creation.</note>

Being constituted from alphabets from *A* to *Ksha*, it is called Aksha-mālā. The knower of Mantra should count the number of recitations on it both in the forward and reverse orders.

->Counting with the fingers yields single fruit; with lines, it is tenfold.<-
->With gems, it is a hundred thousand-fold; with rubies, it is said to be infinite. [50]<-

Counting the number of recitations on fingers yields fruit only once; counting by drawing lines yields fruit ten times; counting by gems yields fruit a hundred thousand times; and counting on <term>Manikya (Rubies)</term> yields fruit an infinite number of times.

->With thirty beads there is wealth; with twenty-seven, there is nourishment;<-
->With twenty-five, there is liberation; and with fifteen, for magical rites.<-
->With fifty beads, O Mistress of the Kula, all perfections are declared. [51]<-
<note>original: "triṃśadbhiḥ syāddhanaṃ puṣṭiḥ saptaviṃśatibhirbhavet...". The "Mistress of the Kula" (<term>Kuleshani</term>) is a title for the Goddess to whom the text is addressed.</note>

With a rosary of 30 pieces one gets wealth; with that having 27 pieces one gets health <note>original: "pusti," implying nourishment or well-being</note>, with that having 25 pieces one gets liberation, with fifteen pieces one succeeds in <term>Abhichara (Magical Rites)</term> <note>referring to rituals intended to influence or subdue others</note>. With fifty beads, O Mistress of the Kula, all perfections are attained.

# Fifteenth Chapter

...and with that, having fifteen beads, one attains the fruits of the sacred charms. And, O <term>Kuleshani</term> <note>original: "Kuleśāni," a title for the Goddess meaning "Mistress of the Kula/Family lineage"</note>! With a rosary having fifty beads, one obtains all possible fruits of practice.

->Through the thumb, liberation is reached; the forefinger is the destroyer of enemies.<-
->The middle finger should be known as the giver of wealth; the ring finger is for rituals of peace.<-
->The little finger is well-known for the power of immobilization and attraction. [52]<-
<note>original: "aṅguṣṭhena ca mokṣaḥ syāt..." This verse explains the "mudra" or finger positions used while counting beads on a rosary, where each finger corresponds to a different spiritual or worldly goal.</note>

### *Rule for using fingers in Recitation:*

One attains liberation from using the thumb; the destruction of enemies by using the first finger; wealth by using the middle finger; the success of pacifying rituals by the third (ring) finger; immobilization of opponents by the small or fourth finger; and the power of attraction by the use of all the fingers together.

->The most excellent knower of sacred chants, having first made a ritual resolve,<-
->should sit upon a stable seat and, after reciting, offer the fruit to the Goddess. [53]<-
<note>original: "etajjapiṣyāmityādau saṅkalpya..." A <term>Sankalpa</term> is a formal statement of intent made before beginning a ritual to "anchor" the spiritual energy toward a specific goal.</note>

Taking a vow (<term>Sankalpa</term>) for the performance of a specific number of <term>Japa</term> (recitations), the master of the sacred chants should sit on a stable seat and perform the recitation. Then, he should offer the spiritual fruit of that recitation, along with water, to the <term>Devi</term> (the Goddess).

->Loud recitation is called the lowest; whispered is remembered as the middle;<-
->Mental recitation, O Goddess, is the best. Thus, recitation is said to be of three kinds. [54]<-

### *Three kinds of Mantra-recitation:*

Recitation done aloud so that others may hear is the lowest form; recitation done in low tones (<term>Upāṁśu</term>), where only the lips move, is the middle form; and O Goddess, recitation performed entirely within the mind (<term>Mānasa</term>) is the best. Thus, the acts of recitation are of three types.

->Too clipped a pronunciation causes disease; too extended causes the decay of ascetic merit.<-
->When a sacred chant is joined letter-to-letter indistinctly, it does not bear fruit. [55]<-
<note>The text warns against rushing the chant (clipped) or dragging it out too long (extended), both of which drain the <term>Tapas</term> or spiritual heat generated by the practice.</note>

If the repetition is too clipped, it causes disease; if it is too drawn out, it causes the decay of <term>tapas</term> (spiritual merit); and when the letters are pronounced indistinctly and blurred together, the <term>Mantra</term> (sacred chant) does not bear fruit at all.

->He who remembers a hymn of praise mentally, or recites a sacred chant aloud,<-
->both are fruitless, O Goddess, like water held in a broken vessel. [56]<-
<note>original: "manasā yaḥ smaret stotraṃ vcasā vā manuṃ japet..." In Tantric tradition, a <term>Stotra</term> (hymn) is meant to be voiced to vibrate the air, while a <term>Mantra</term> is an internal seed meant to be kept secret and mental. Reversing these roles ruins the efficacy of the practice.</note>

Mental remembrance of a hymn of praise and the verbal repetition of a sacred chant are both useless, much like trying to hold water in a broken vessel.

->At the beginning, there is the impurity of birth; at the end, there is the impurity of death.<-
->Joined with these two impurities, a sacred chant does not bear fruit. [57]<-
<note>original: "jātasūtakamādau syāt..." This refers to <term>Sūtaka</term> (ritual pollution). In this context, it is a technical term for certain "blocks" or "impurities" inherent in mantras that must be removed through specific purification rituals before the mantra becomes "alive" and effective.</note>

### *Mantra free of two impurities alone is fructifying:*

A sacred chant entails the impurity of birth at its beginning and the impurity of death at its end. So long as it is associated with these two ritual impurities, a sacred chant does not produce results.

## In the Kularnava Tantra

->Having mentally removed the beginning and end, one should repeat the sacred chant.<-
->A chant liberated from the two impurities is the giver of all success. [58]<-
<note>original: "sūtaka," usually meaning ritual impurity from birth or death. In this context, it refers to specific technical defects or "impurities" at the start and end of a mantra that must be removed through mental focus.</note>

Therefore, one should remove these two impurities of the <term>Mantra</term> <note>a sacred sound or phrase used in meditation</note> before its <term>Japa</term> <note>the meditative practice of repeating a mantra</note> because thus stripped of its two impurities and repeated mentally the Mantra becomes all-fructifying.

->The meaning of the chant, the consciousness of the chant, and the womb-seal—he who knows them not,<-
->even with a billion repetitions, for him success does not arise. [59]<-

->*Mantra is infructuous without a knowledge of its Meaning:*<-

If one does not know the meaning of the Mantra, the <term>Mantra-caitanya</term> <note>the "consciousness" or living energy of the mantra</note> and the <term>Yoni-mudrā</term> <note>original: "womb-seal," a ritual hand gesture or internal state that connects the practitioner to the source of the mantra's power</note>, then even a hundred crore <note>a crore is ten million; a hundred crore is a billion</note> of its Japa would not lead to success.

->Chants whose seeds are asleep, O Beloved, will not grant fruit.<-
->Those joined with the consciousness of the chant are remembered as the givers of all success. [60]<-

->*Mantras devoid of their Potency are infructuous:*<-

Mantras whose potency is asleep do not yield fruit. Mantras alive with their conscious power alone have been said to be all-fructifying.

->Chants bereft of consciousness are said to be merely letters.<-
->They grant no fruit at all, even from millions or billions of repetitions. [61]<-

Bereft of this consciousness the Mantra remains a mere collection of letters. Even millions of repetitions of such a Mantra yield no fruit.

->Whatever true form first appears when the chant is uttered properly,<-
->that fruit is worth hundreds, thousands, millions, or billions of repetitions. [62]<-

The Truth that manifests when the Mantra is thus articulated properly is worth the fruit of hundreds, thousands, millions and billions of repetitions.

->The piercing of the knots of the heart and throat, the expansion of all limbs,<-
->tears of joy, hair standing on end, the intoxication of the body, O Mistress of the Kula!<-
->and suddenly, faltering speech—of this there is no doubt. [63]<-
->When the chant, joined with consciousness, is uttered even once in this way,<-
->where such signs are seen, that is called the lineage tradition. [64]<-

When a Mantra alive with consciousness is articulated even once, the knots of the heart and the throat snap <note>referring to the "granthis" or psychic blockages that prevent the flow of spiritual energy</note>, all limbs increase, tears of joy rush to the eyes, there is <term>horripilation</term> <note>goosebumps or hair standing on end, a sign of intense spiritual fervor</note>, the body is intoxicated and speech becomes tremulous. When such signs are there one can be sure that the Mantra has been handed down by Tradition <note>original: "pāramparyaṃ," the unbroken oral transmission from Guru to disciple</note>.

<summary>This page explains that a Mantra is more than just sounds; it must be purified of ritual impurities and "awakened" with conscious intent to be effective. It describes the physical and emotional symptoms, such as tears and horripilation, that prove a practitioner has successfully activated a Mantra through authentic tradition.</summary>

->Now the ten purificatory rites are told, which remove the defects of mantras, O Beloved.<-

*Ten purificatory rituals of Mantra:*

### *Consideration of Siddha, etc. Cakras:*

These verses <note>original: ślokas</note> are written in a coded language <note>a system called "bhuta-sankhya" where common concepts represent numbers</note> and describe the **Akathaha Cakra** used to determine if a <term>mantra</term> <note>a sacred sound-formula</note> will be effective for a specific <term>sadhaka</term> <note>spiritual practitioner</note>. The names such as "Indra" given in the verse actually denote the numbers to be placed in the various houses of the grid. 

For example: Indra = 1 <note>as the first among gods</note>, Agni = 3 <note>referring to the three sacred fires</note>, Rudra = 11 <note>the eleven forms of Shiva</note>, Graha = 9 <note>the nine planets</note>, Dṛk = 2 <note>the two eyes</note>, Veda = 4 <note>the four sacred Vedas</note>, Arka = 12 <note>the twelve solar months</note>, Dik = 10 <note>the ten directions</note>, Şaḍa = 6 <note>the six seasons</note>, Aşṭa = 8 <note>the eight-fold nature</note>, Şodaṣa = 16, Manu = 14 <note>the fourteen progenitors of humanity</note>, Bāṇa = 5 <note>the five flower-arrows of the god of love</note>, Abdhi = 7 <note>the seven mythological oceans</note>, Tithi = 15 <note>the fifteen days of a lunar fortnight</note>, Trayodasa = 13. 

These figures are to be placed one each in the sixteen houses of the grid. Then all the letters of the alphabet should also be placed in various houses as shown in the grid (see page 257) from which should be determined the category of a mantra, whether it is **Siddha** (Perfected), **Sādhya** (To be Accomplished), **Susiddha** (Highly Effective), or **Ari** (Hostile)¹. Each of these categories is further sub-divided into four:

*   **Siddha**: Siddha-Siddha, Siddha-Sādhya, Siddha-Susiddha, Siddha-Ari.
*   **Sādhya**: Sādhya-Siddha, Sādhya-Sādhya, Sādhya-Susiddha, Sādhya-Ari.
*   **Susiddha**: Susiddha-Siddha, Susiddha-Sādhya, Susiddha-Susiddha, Susiddha-Ari.
*   **Ari**: Ari-Siddha, Ari-Sādhya, Ari-Susiddha, Ari-Ripu <note>Ripu is another word for Ari, meaning enemy</note>.

->Siddha-Siddha is perfected by repetition; Siddha-Sadhya by double the amount.<-
->Siddha-Susiddha by half the repetition; Siddha-Ari kills one's kinsmen. [81]<-
->Sadhya-Siddha comes through great hardship; Sadhya-Sadhya is useless.<-
->Sadhya-Susiddha comes through worship; Sadhya-Ari kills those of the same lineage. [82]<-
->Susiddha-Siddha by half the repetition; its Sadhya is as previously stated.<-

A **Susiddha-Siddha** mantra provides results by performing half the number of repetitions usually required; a **Susiddha-Sādhya** bears fruit with the standard prescribed number of Japas; a **Susiddha-Susiddha** bears fruit by its mere adoption; and the **Susiddha-Ari** destroys one's own family.

An **Ari-Siddha** <note>'enemy-perfected'</note> destroys one's sons, an **Ari-Sādhya** destroys the wife, an **Ari-Susiddha** destroys the entire clan, and an **Ari-Ari** destroys the very <term>Ātmā</term> <note>the soul or inner self</note> of the <term>Sādhaka</term> <note>the spiritual practitioner</note>.

->The Ascendant, wealth, brothers, relatives, sons, enemies, and spouses;<-
->Death, virtue, actions, gains, and losses—these are the twelve zodiac signs. // 60 //<-

The technical names of the twelve signs from Aries <note>original: Meṣa</note> to Pisces <note>original: Mīna</note> are: **The Ascendant** <note>original: Lagna</note>, **Wealth** <note>original: Dhana</note>, **Brother** <note>original: Bhrātṛ</note>, **Relative** <note>original: Bandhu</note>, **Son** <note>original: Putra</note>, **Enemy** <note>original: Śatru</note>, **Spouse** <note>original: Kalatra</note>, **Death** <note>original: Maraṇa</note>, **Virtue** <note>original: Dharma</note>, **Work** <note>original: Karma</note>, **Income** <note>original: Āya</note>, and **Expense** <note>original: Vyaya</note> respectively. ->The wise should count from one's own zodiac sign to the sign of the mantra;<-
->If the zodiac sign and constellation are unknown, count from the sign of the first letter of the name. // 61 //<-

The wise practitioner, using the Zodiac Wheel, should start counting from the house of his own zodiac sign (that is, from the house in which the alphabet denoting his sign occurs) to the house in which the letter representing the sign of the Mantra is found. In case one's own zodiac sign is unknown, the counting should be started from the house in which the first letter of the personal name occurs and proceeded to the house of the letter representing the Mantra's sign.

->Starting from the first letter of the name until the first letter of the mantra,<-
->divide by three and separate by the vowels; then do the same in reverse. // 62 //<-
->Calculate which is the "Greater" and which the "Debt"; if the mantra is the "Debtor," it is the best of mantras.<-
->If the seeker himself is the "Debtor," he must first chant that mantra because he is the one in debt. // 63 //<-

In these verses has been described the **Debtor-Creditor Grid** <note>original: Ṛṇi-Dhanī Cakra</note>. (The method of construction of this grid can be seen in the *Encyclopedia of Yoga* referred to earlier). If by counting on this grid according to the prescribed procedure, the numerical value of the Mantra happens to be greater than the figure of the practitioner <note>original: Sādhaka</note> (called the "target number" <note>original: Sādhyāṅka</note>), then the Mantra would be called the "Debtor" <note>original: Ṛṇi</note>. If it is less, the Mantra would be called the "Creditor" <note>original: Dhanī</note>. 

In other words, if the practitioner's number is greater, then the Mantra is a "Creditor," and if it is lesser, the Mantra is a "Debtor." In case both the figures are equal, then the mantra is called "Non-Debtor" <note>original: A-Ṛṇi</note>. See page 258 for the Diagram <note>original: Cakra</note>.

### Chapter Fifteen <note>original: पञ्चदश उल्लासः (Pañcadaśa Ullāsaḥ)</note>

Beginning from the first letter of the name one should proceed up to the first letter of the sacred sound <note>original: Mantra</note>. The figure so obtained should be multiplied by three; then dividing the multiple by seven would give the figure for the practitioner <note>original: Sādhaka</note>. Again counting in the reverse order from the first letter of the sacred sound to the first letter of the practitioner, the figure found should be multiplied by three and then dividing the multiple by seven would give the figure for the sacred sound. In case the figure of the practitioner is less, then the sacred sound would be called a "Debtor" <note>original: Ṛṇi</note>. Adoption of a "Debtor" sacred sound is auspicious.

->Speech-Air, Fire, Earth, Water, and Space: the fifty letters in order;<-
->Five short, five long, those ending in the nasal drop, and those born of junctions;<-

From the letter 'A' to the letter 'Kṣa', the fifty letters have been placed into five groups, each group representing one Element. The groupings are as follows:

There is friendship between Earth and Water, and also between Fire and Air; there is enmity otherwise. The sky is the friend of all the Elements. Adoption of a sacred sound where the letter of the sound <note>original: Mantrākṣara</note> and the letter of the practitioner <note>original: Sādhakākṣara</note> belong to a group which are friends is auspicious. O Mistress of the Kula <note>original: Kuleśvari</note>! The sacred sounds adopted from a group which is an enemy of the practitioner would mean destruction. Therefore, such a sacred sound should be avoided.

# In the Kularnava Tantra

Regarding a sacred sound <note>original: Mantra</note> given by women and those obtained in a dream, there is, O Leader of Mantras <note>original: Mantranāyike</note>, no use for the consideration of their validity on the Energy Wheels <note>original: Cakras</note> mentioned earlier.

### *Obstructive factors in the success of Recitation:*

If the mind be in one place, Śiva in another, Śakti in another and the life-breath in still another, then even a crore <note>ten million</note> of Recitations, O beautiful-limbed one, would be useless.

->If learning is acquired for the sake of debate, and recitation is done for the benefit of another,<-
->If charity is given for the sake of fame, how can there be spiritual success <note>original: Siddhi</note>, O lovely-faced one <note>original: Varānane</note>? // 101 //<-

If the learning is acquired for the sake of debate, Japa is done for the sake of another, gifts are given for the sake of fame, how can, O lovely-faced one, there be fulfilment?

->If pilgrimage is undertaken for the sake of wealth, and austerities <note>original: Tapas</note> are performed for show,<-
->If the worship of a deity is done for selfish purposes, how indeed can success arise? // 102 //<-

If pilgrimage is done for the sake of wealth, austerities for show, worship of a deity for selfish purposes, how indeed can there be fulfilment?

->Those fools who perform ritual placement of sound <note>original: Nyāsa</note>, worship <note>original: Pūjā</note>, recitation <note>original: Japa</note>,<-
->And fire-offerings <note>original: Homa</note> with an unclean body; all their efforts shall be fruitless. // 103 //<-

They are fools who do Nyāsa, Pūjā, Japa, Homa with a body that is unclean; all their such efforts are fruitless.

->O My Beloved! If the ritual is performed by one who remains unclean from the excretion of waste,<-
->Then all recitation and worship, and all other such acts, become impure. // 104 //<-

O My Beloved! If the ritual is done by one who is unclean due to faeces, urine and other leavings, then all Japa and worship, etc., are rendered impure.

->One who performs the meditative repetition <note>term: Japa; the meditative repetition of a mantra</note> while clad in soiled clothing, with unwashed hair, or with a foul odor from the mouth or body, is quickly consumed by the wrath of the deity <note>original: Devatā</note> who feels utter disgust toward the practitioner. // 105 //<-

->One should strictly avoid laziness, yawning, sleep, sneezing, spitting, fear, touching the lower parts of the body, and anger during the time of practice. // 106 //<-

One should avoid laziness, yawning, sleeping, sneezing, spitting, fear, touching the lower limbs and anger.

->The sacred sound <note>original: Mantra</note> does not reach perfection through these six obstacles: overeating, empty babbling, idle gossip, obsession with rigid rules, attachment to <unclear>others</unclear>, and fickleness of mind. // 107 //<-

The Mantra does not succeed where there is excessive food, meaningless talk, gossip, rigidity of rules, attachment to <unclear>another an</unclear> fickleness.

->One should not perform the recitation while wearing a turban or a restrictive cloak, nor while naked, with disheveled hair, or while surrounded by a crowd. Likewise, one must not chant while wearing an impure upper garment, while in a state of ritual impurity, or while walking. // 108 //<-

One should not perform Japa with his turban on, with cloak, naked, hair dishevelled, surrounded by retinue, unclean upper cloth or while impure or while walking.

->During the time of recitation, one should avoid mental dullness, sorrow, idle fidgeting <note>original: tṛṇaccheda; literally "cutting or snapping blades of grass"</note>, arguments, daydreaming, or the passing of internal gas. // 109 //<-

One should avoid during Japa inertia, grief, useless activity, free imagination and passing of wind.

->O Beloved <note>original: Priye</note>! A practitioner should perform the recitation while being peaceful, pure, moderate in eating, and sleeping upon the bare ground. One must be devoted, self-controlled, free from the influence of dualities <note>note: dualities such as heat and cold, or pleasure and pain</note>, steady of mind, silent, and self-restrained. // 110 //<-

*Conditions conducive to success in Japa :*

One should be calm, clean, limited in food intake, sleeping on the ground, devoted, in full control, free from duality, steady of mind, silent and self-controlled during Japa.

->A person should engage in the practice possessed of qualities such as confidence, spiritual faith, compassion, deep conviction <note>original: Śraddhā</note>, adherence to rules, and firm <unclear>resolve</unclear>. They should also possess contentment, spiritual eagerness, and a commitment to righteousness <note>original: Dharma</note>. // 111 //<-

One should perform Japa with confidence, belief, composure, faith, regularity <unclear>certitude</unclear>, contentment, enthusiasm and like qualities.

### Kularnava Tantra

Success is held in the very palm of the hand of a practitioner <note>term: Sādhaka; a dedicated spiritual seeker or practitioner</note> who is adorned with fragrant flowers, jewelry, and fine clothing. For anyone else, success remains elusive even after ten million repetitions <note>term: Japa; the meditative repetition of a mantra</note>. // 112 //

One should recite the sacred sound <note>term: Mantra; a transformative power-word or phrase</note> with total devotion, with one's life-force dedicated to it, the mind centered upon it, and the soul entirely focused on the goal. While chanting, O Beloved, one should constantly contemplate the deeper meaning of the mantra. // 113 //

When tired of repetition, one should turn to meditation <note>term: Dhyāna; the practice of deep, focused visualization or contemplation</note>; when tired of meditation, one should return to repetition. For the one who unites both repetition and meditation, the mantra reaches perfection <note>original: siddhyati</note> very quickly. // 114 //

Thus, O Queen of the Kula <note>original: Kuleśāni; an address to the Goddess as the sovereign of the spiritual lineage</note>, I have described to you in brief the characteristics of the preparatory rites <note>term: Puraścaraṇa; the preliminary practices required to awaken the power of a mantra</note>. What more do you wish to hear? // 115 //

->Thus, in the glorious *Kularnava*, the Great Mystery and Gateway to Liberation,<-
->the Supreme among all Sacred Traditions, the Work of 125,000 verses, in the Fifth Section,<-
->in the *Urdhvamnaya Tantra*, ends the Fifteenth Chapter,<-
->entitled "The Discourse on Preparatory Rites." // 15 //<-

# CHAPTER SIXTEEN

## The Auspicious Goddess said:

O Lord of the Kula <note>original: Kuleśa; a title for Shiva as the head of the Tantric 'family' or lineage</note>, Ocean of the Nectar of Compassion, O Supreme Lord! I wish to hear about the procedures for rituals performed for the fulfillment of desires. Please speak to me of this, O Supreme Ishvara. **(1)**

## The Lord said:

Listen, O Goddess! I shall explain what you have asked. By merely hearing this, a person becomes skilled in the practical application of these rituals. **(2)**

The practitioner <term>Sadhaka|A dedicated student or practitioner of a spiritual discipline</term>, possessing a purified heart and following the rules previously mentioned, should recite the Supreme Mantra of the Sacred Palace <note>original: Śrīprāsāda-parā Mantra</note> five hundred thousand times, my dear. **(3)**

**The Results of Chanting and Fire Offerings**

O Goddess, one should then perform a fire sacrifice <term>Homa|A ritual where offerings are made into a consecrated fire to convey them to the deities</term> consisting of one-tenth the number of your recitations <note>meaning 50,000 offerings</note> into a purified fire. Then, perform a libation ritual <term>Tarpana|An offering of liquids, usually poured through the hands, to satisfy and 'satiate' the deity</term> of one-tenth that amount using milk, water, and Shali rice. **(4)**

With fragrances, flowers, unbroken rice grains <term>Akshata|Whole grain rice, often dyed with turmeric or kumkum, symbolizing wholeness and abundance</term>, ornaments, wealth, and clothing, my dear; **(5)**
And with various delicious foods, drinks, and beautiful materials intended for the fire, one should satisfy the Circle of Yoginis <note>Yoginis: A group of powerful female deities in the Tantric tradition who represent different aspects of cosmic energy</note> as extensively as one’s wealth permits.

In this way, through ritual placement <term>Nyasa|The practice of 'placing' parts of a mantra or a deity onto specific parts of the body through touch and visualization</term>, chanting <term>Japa|The meditative repetition of a mantra</term>, meditation, fire sacrifice, worship, and libations; **(6)**
The practitioner <note>original: Mantri; one who possesses or wields a mantra</note> attains success and becomes, in essence, the Great Shiva himself.

# IN THE KULARNAVA TANTRA

->Then, O Mistress of the Kula, for the desires of one’s own mind,<-
->The wise one should perform these practices with this mantra for enjoyment and liberation.<-
->For one who has perfected the mantra, the six rituals succeed without a doubt;<-
->They never succeed for one who has not attained perfection, and such a person may incur the deity’s curse. (7–8)<-

*A practitioner with a Perfected <term>Siddha Mantra|A mantra that has been "awakened" or mastered through rigorous repetition and ritual</term> obtains success in the Six Rituals:*

O Mistress of the Kula <note>original: Kulanāyike; a title for the Goddess as the leader of the Tantric tradition</note>! Thus with ritual placement <term>Nyāsa|The practice of "placing" mantras or deities on specific parts of the body</term>, recitation <term>Japa|The repetitive chanting of a mantra</term>, meditation <term>Dhyāna|Visualized meditation on the deity’s form</term>, fire sacrifice <term>Homa|A ritual where offerings are made into a consecrated fire</term>, worship, and libation <term>Tarpaṇa|Satiating the deity with liquid offerings</term>, the Mantra becomes fruitful and the practitioner <term>Sādhaka|A dedicated student or practitioner</term> becomes like the Supreme Shiva <note>original: Para Śiva</note> Himself. Only then should a wise practitioner start the spiritual practice <note>original: Sādhana</note> for the fulfillment of his heart’s desire with this mantra (the *Mantra of the Supreme Sacred Palace* <note>original: Śrī-prāsāda-parā Mantra</note>). With a perfected mantra, the six Rituals (the *Six Magical Acts: <term>Māraṇa|Death-inflicting</term>, <term>Mohana|Delusion</term>, <term>Vaśīkaraṇa|Subjugation</term>, <term>Uccāṭana|Expulsion</term>, <term>Stambhana|Immobilization</term>, and <term>Śānti|Peace/Healing</term>*) definitely succeed. A non-perfected mantra never gives success and, on the other hand, a practitioner of such a mantra receives the curse of the Deity.

->For those who perform rituals for specific desires, there is no world beyond;<-
->The success of the ritual is their only reward, and nothing else, O Beloved. (9)<-

*No Liberation for a practitioner of the six rituals:*

O My Beloved! Those who perform spiritual practice for the fulfillment of selfish motives through the six rituals <note>original: Ṣaṭkarmas</note> do not reach spiritual liberation. They, however, succeed in their magical experiments, and this alone is their fruit, nothing else.

->From a single procedure, two fruits are never seen anywhere;<-
->O Mistress of the Gods, therefore one should worship the deity without desire. (10)<-

One can never obtain two fruits <note>meaning both worldly power and spiritual liberation</note> through only one medium. Therefore, O Mistress of the Gods <note>original: Deveśī</note>, the worship of the Deity should be performed with a selfless spirit.

->Through fire sacrifice, libations, mantras, and specific placements and meditations,<-
->One should perform the six rituals for the protection of oneself and others. (11)<-

*Pacification of the faults of the experiments with Circle Worship <term>Cakra-pūjā|A central Tantric ritual involving a circle of practitioners or a geometric yantra</term>:*

One should perform his own and others' six rituals with ritual placement, fire sacrifice, libation, meditation, and mantra, etc.

->At the end of the ritual, one should perform the Circle Worship according to the rules;<-
->One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, accompanied by placement and meditation,<-
->To pacify the faults of the ritual and for the sake of self-protection.<-
->Otherwise, one does not obtain the fruit and receives the deity’s curse. (12–13)<-

For the pacification of the faults of the experiments and for his own safety, one should, at the end of the experiments, perform <note>The instructions for the concluding rites likely continue on the following page</note>

<summary>This page outlines the necessity of mastering a mantra (Siddha) before attempting the Six Rituals of magic. It warns that while these rituals can fulfill worldly desires, they do not lead to spiritual liberation, and requires practitioners to perform Cakra-pūjā to atone for ritual errors.</summary>

# SIXTEENTH CHAPTER

Circle worship <term>Cakra-pūjā|A ritual performed within a circle of practitioners or involving sacred diagrams</term> and one hundred thousand <note>original: lakh</note> mantra recitations <term>Mantra-japa|The repetitive chanting of a sacred formula</term> must be performed according to the prescribed procedures; otherwise, the desired results will not be obtained. On the contrary, the practitioner <term>Sādhaka|A dedicated spiritual aspirant</term> would receive the curse of the Deity.

->One should perform rituals only after knowing the lunar day, the day of the week, the lunar mansion, the planetary alignment, the month, and the fortnight,<-
->as well as the Lord of the Lamp and the various Clan-Charts. (14)<-

*Things to be known before resorting to the Experiments:*

After knowing the Lunar Day <note>original: Tithi</note>, the Day of the week <note>original: Vāra</note>, the Star <note>original: Nakṣatra</note>, the Alignment <note>original: Yoga</note>, the Month <note>original: Māsa</note>, the Season <note>original: Ṛtu</note>, the Fortnight <note>original: Pakṣa</note>, the Lamp-Lord <note>original: Dīpeśa</note>, and the Tortoise Chart <term>Kūrma Cakra|A diagram used to determine the stability of a site or the direction of success</term>, one should bring his ritual to fruition.

->One should master the mantras only after understanding the Seer, the Meter, the Deity, the ritual placement on the body, meditation, and worship,<-
->along with the Seed-syllable, the Power, and the Pillar. (15)<-

The Seer <term>Ṛṣi|The sage to whom the mantra was first revealed</term>, the Meter <term>Chanda|The rhythmic structure of the mantra</term>, the Seed <term>Bīja|The core syllable containing the mantra's essence</term>, the Power <term>Śakti|The creative energy of the mantra</term>, the Pillar <term>Kīlaka|The 'pin' or 'lock' that must be removed to release the mantra's power</term>, the Deity <note>original: Devatā</note>, the placement of the mantra on the limbs <term>Aṅga-nyāsa|A ritual where the practitioner touches parts of their body while reciting syllables to 'place' the deity within themselves</term>, the Visualization <note>original: Dhyāna</note>, and the Worship <note>original: Pūjana</note> should all be known before starting the spiritual practice <note>original: Sādhanā</note>.

->Knowing the compatibility of sons, relatives, and wives, the favorableness of the zodiac sign and social class,<-
->the friendship of the elements, and the rising and setting of the stars, one should begin the practice. (16)<-

Knowing the compatibility of one's family <note>original: Putra, Bāndhava, and Strī</note>, the favorableness of the Zodiac Sign <note>original: Rāśi</note> and Social Class <note>original: Varṇa</note>, the friendship of the Elements <note>original: Bhūtas</note>, and the rising and ending times <note>original: Udaya-anta</note>, one should start his spiritual practice.

->One should perform the rituals only after knowing the non-difference between Mantra and Wisdom, their sleeping and waking states,<-
->and whether the mantras are male, female, or neutral in gender. (17)<-

The fundamental identity of the Mantra and the Wisdom <note>original: Vidyā</note>, their states of sleep <note>original: Nidrā</note> and waking <note>original: Bodha</note>, and their male, female, or neuter genders—all these should be known before starting the spiritual practice.

->The wise know the consciousness and the birth-impurity of letters and words;<-
->after knowing the short, long, and extra-long vowels, one should begin the mantra practice. (18)<-

Only after knowing the specific letters <note>original: Varṇa</note> of the mantra, the repetition of words <note>original: Padadvita</note>, the inherent consciousness <term>Caitanya|The 'life-force' of a mantra that must be awakened</term>, the ritual impurity <term>Sūtaka|The 'birth-impurity' of a mantra that requires purification before use</term>, and the various vowel lengths—short, long, and extra-long <note>original: Hrasva, Dīrgha, and Pluta</note>—should one start his ritual.

->Understanding the five purifications, the posture, breath control, the ritual placements, and the rosary,<-
->as well as the flaws, the cleansing rituals, and the hand gestures, one should perform the rituals. (19)<-

The Five Purifications <term>Pañca-śuddhi|The cleansing of the self, place, materials, mantra, and deity</term>, the Posture <note>original: Āsana</note>, Breath Control <note>original: Prāṇāyāma</note>, Ritual Placement <note>original: Nyāsa</note>, the Rosary <note>original: Akṣamālā</note>, the potential flaws of a mantra, the methods for purifying mantras, and the hand gestures <term>Mudrā|Symbolic hand positions used to channel energy</term> should also be known before beginning the ritual.

->In the same way, after knowing the seat, the binding of the directions, the binding of the energy channels, and their proper connection,<-
->the deity, the timing, and the hand gestures, one should bring the ritual to fruition. (20)<-

In the same manner, after mastering the seat, the protective binding of the directions <term>Digbandha|A ritual act to seal the space against negative entities</term>, the control of the energy channels <note>original: Nāḍī</note>, the connection of the elements <note>original: Tattvasaṅgati</note>, the Deity, the appropriate time <note>original: Kāla</note>, and the hand gestures, one should complete his ritual.
